# llmx - Development Status

## ROCm Q8_0 decode steps by row width, DeepSeek-V4.1 query and window in one call, one-entry routed calls without grouping (2026-11-11, DSDEV121 proposal, F2DEV review, DSDEV122, branch perf/q8-decode-steps on main 12b84ea73, rebased onto main 4eaa874bd over perf/routed-decode-wide; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** the int8 class's one-column Q8_0 decode on ROCm closer to its read floor at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 shapes, every output the bits main gives.

**Done:**
- `q8_0_half_one<R, NS>` builds by row width (`kernels/int16.hip`): a row under two spans of blocks (64 on a 64-lane wave) loads one step at a time (`kNarrowSteps`, `llmx_q8_0_half8_1s1` and `_1r2s1`), since it cannot fill a second step a load and the steps it holds cost registers (71 against 39 VGPRs at one row, 3 against 5 waves a SIMD); at two rows a wave a row of the profile's `q8_decode_four_steps_from` blocks (256 on the MI50) loads four (`llmx_q8_0_half8_1r2s4`).
  A step count changes how many blocks a lane loads ahead, never its blocks, their order or the tree, so every build gives the one-row build's bits; the rule reads the row width, the output count and the type, never the call's columns.
- The four-step width is a measured knee, a `DeviceProfile` value without a flag: at 192 blocks 25600 rows gained 2.4% and 2560 rows (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's `ssm_out` and `attn_output`) lost 2 to 3%; 256 blocks (DeepSeek's `attn_output_b`) and 384 (Qwen3-8B's down) gain.
- `window_attention` (`arch/deepseek4.hpp`) projects the query latent and the window key in one `matmul_group` call on generated rows.
  A prompt keeps two calls: the tile splits its sums by the call's outputs, so a prompt group is not the bits of its projections alone (both backends, 5120 and 6144 wide at 17 rows); the indexer's weights projection stays apart, BF16 in the real file.
- Routed half-block Q8_0 calls of at most one entry an expert take the one-column build an entry with no grouping launch where that build fills its steps, under two spans of blocks (`llmx_q8_0_routed_half8s1`) and from four (`routed_half8`); between, the grouped build's two steps measured faster (Qwen3-30B-A3B's 2048-wide gate and up at 2 tokens: 85.0 us grouped, 91.8 us per entry).
  The other routed Q8_0 builds, the 16-bit and odd-block forms and the other types keep their break-evens.
- Checks: `q8_decode_bits` holds every one-column int8 build to the host's one-row sum at rows of 8 to 257 blocks, 63 to 65 and 254 to 257 among them, and at outputs on both sides of `q8_decode_two_rows_from` at 2560 and 4096, with the expected build witnessed; groups of 1280 and 512 rows and a third of 1024 against their projections' calls at 1 and 2 columns on ROCm, 1280 and 512 on Vulkan in f16 and int8; `experts_grouped` witnesses `routed_half8s1` and `routed_half8` on Q8_0 rows 1280 and 4096 wide.

**Measured** (one MI50, default clocks, production kernels through the backend, 200 calls a cell, best of 5, ABAB, both arms built in the same container, us a token over the calls each model makes; every output hash main's):

| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1 token: q_b, idx_qb, out_a, out_b, wkv, q_a+kv | 8977 | 8033 |
| the same at 2 tokens | 8832 | 8647 |
| Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0: qkv, gate+up, output | 984 | 844 |
| Qwen3-8B Q8_0: down | 2657 | 2613 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: ssm_out, attn_output (unchanged builds) | 1256 | 1258 |
| routed Q8_0 decode, 1 token: Flash-Next down, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3-30B-A3B shapes | 221 | 203 |

Per call at one token: DeepSeek q_b 75.2 to 61.3 us, out_a 58.3 to 49.3 (no grouping launch), out_b 60.6 to 59.9, idx_qb 13.8 to 12.6; Qwen3-0.6B output 227 to 200; the query and window rows in one call 16.7 us against 13.5 and 9.4 in two (DSDEV121's harness, same card), 0.25 ms a token over 40 layers beside the table's 0.94 ms.
Vulkan: the deepseek4 call is the only change, 17.7 us for the pair against 19.6 and 12.4 in two.

## ROCm MXFP4 decode lane: two lanes a block, the quarter order's bits (2026-11-11, DSDEV113 then DSDEV118, branch perf/routed-decode-wide on main 12b84ea73, rebased onto main 4eaa874bd under perf/q8-decode-steps; DSDEV113's proposal of 06:17, F2DEV's review of 06:24, DSDEV118's results of 07:08 and 09:59, COORD's ruling to land the MXFP4 lane alone; DSDEV124 gated it; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** MXFP4 decode rows, dense, routed and grouped, faster on ROCm with main's bits, so DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's routed experts decode faster with no re-baseline.

**Done:**
- MXFP4's row lane (`MXFP4Lane`, kernels/int16.hip) takes two lanes a block, a lane the nibbles of one half of the 16 bytes, so 16 values from one scale decode, one five-word gather and one index step, where the quarter form took four lanes of 8.
- A lane keeps one accumulator a quarter (`row_chains`), each chained over the blocks its quarter lane chained, on a cluster of half the lanes (`row_cluster`); the two trees' sums are added in the lane (`store_cluster_pairs`), the quarter tree's last level, so every output keeps main's bits.
- Its grouped build of 8 loads 2 columns a step (`G8Step`), since 4 held 121 VGPRs, two waves a SIMD, and took 1654 us gate+up at 16 rows against the 2-column build's 1155; 1 column a step took 1304, and one row a cluster 1865 at 4 columns and 1475 at 2.
- `mxfp4_decode_bits` (backend-rocm) holds dense rows of 1 to 16 columns, routed, g2, g4 and g8, f16 and int8, 32 to 5120 wide, to a host emulation of the quarter order bit for bit; `types` passes on an MI50.

**Measured** (one MI50, default clocks, int8, a scratch harness over the production kernels at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's expert shapes, 5120 into 2x2304 and 2304 into 5120, 6 experts a row, main / branch / DSDEV113's re-baselining half form interleaved, 3 rounds, us a call):

| call | gate+up main / branch / half | down main / branch / half |
|---|---:|---:|
| routed, 1 row | 227 / 174 / 175 | 151 / 111 / 134 |
| routed, 6 rows | 1366 / 998 / 1028 | 872 / 611 / 752 |
| g2, 1 row of 16 experts | 284 / 212 / 218 | 193 / 140 / 174 |
| g4, 6 rows | 990 / 740 / 806 | 667 / 472 / 616 |
| g8, 16 rows | 1714 / 1155 / 1092 | 1145 / 746 / 860 |

Every branch output hash equals main's.
Counters at 1 row (gate+up, down): VALU active cycles 20.3M and 13.0M on main, 13.2M and 8.2M on the branch; VALUBusy 88% and 84% to 74% and 71%; MemUnitBusy 65% and 58% to 60% and 54%.
On Vulkan at the same shapes, same card, main's routed MXFP4 decode takes 262 to 272 us for gate+up and 215 us for down at 1 row, below this ROCm rate; it is a later step of its own.

**Landing gates** (DSDEV124, one MI50, the head's code at 949e8296 on main 12b84ea73, against main's build of 12b84ea73):
- Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M on rocm:0: greedy ids over 64 tokens and logits over 1400 positions are main's, in int8 and auto.
- The scratch harness's 60 hash cases (MXFP4, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_0, Q5_1 and IQ4_NL; dense, routed and g8; 1 and 16 rows; f16 and int8) are main's.
- CTest 84 of 84 on an MI50; the suite on rocm:0 passes every component but `docs` and `dead-code`, which fail in the container only because the worktree's git directory is not mounted there, and pass on the host.
- No Vulkan code changes, so neither the Vulkan suite nor the Radeon VII check applies.
- At the stacked head with perf/q8-decode-steps (LAND26, 9b53dcfda on main 4eaa874bd), against main's build of 4eaa874bd made the same way: greedy ids and top-8 logits are main's for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4 over ten MI50s on ROCm int8 and Vulkan (64 ids and 1400 logit positions of a short prompt, 64 ids and 512 positions of a 15032-token prompt), and on rocm:0 under auto and int8 for Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M (64 ids, 1400 positions) and a synthetic MXFP4 qwen3moe file of random blocks (width 1024, 16 experts of 768, 4 used; 64 ids, 1400 positions).
  The stack's other gates and its timing round against main are in the perf/q8-decode-steps block above; the change lands by fast-forward after the Radeon VII check.

**Left:**
- The lean `k_rows` loop (proposal item 2), every type with main's bits, is a step of its own: measured against main's loop it took Q5_0 and Q5_1 about 40% lower at 16 dense columns and Q5_1's g8 45% lower, and was slower on MXFP4's g8 (+42% to +64%, 83 to 114 VGPRs), Q4_K (+5% to +11%, g8 +65% to +75%) and IQ4_NL (g8 +16% to +21%, 16 dense columns +248%), wherever the compiler then hoisted per-column 64-bit addresses.
  So it is a per-build choice, which needs its own rule and review.

**Gotchas:**
- The bits hold because the quarter tree's last level pairs the quarters 2t and 2t + 1 that one lane now holds, and the levels above pair lanes that differ in the block index alone; IEEE addition commutes, so the in-lane add is that level.
- docs/ROCM.md has no MXFP4 lane text, so only docs/src/backends-rocm.md changes.

## DeepSeek-V4.1 narrow decode ops on ROCm and Vulkan (2026-11-11, DSDEV114 to DSDEV117, branch perf/narrow-decode-ops on main 12b84ea73; F2DEV's review of DSDEV114's proposal, 05:03; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** the DeepSeek-V4.1 ops that run a row or a few at decode, and grow with depth, take their time from the work they do rather than from serial lanes, with every output's bits unchanged.

**Done:**
- `model_format_qdq` and `model_format_pack` take a lane a value: on ROCm each block's amax a shuffle reduction over its lanes, on Vulkan over shared memory in the CPU's order, a pack on Vulkan gathering runs of four blocks' bytes, whole words, in shared memory.
- Vulkan codes a NaN as the CPU does, 0x7F under FP8 and a signed zero under FP4, and reads E4M3's 0x7F and 0xFF back as NaN; main's integer division coded a NaN otherwise and read 0x7F as 480 (the first commit's checks, failing on main's Vulkan).
- `indexer_scores` reads its keys through the code table four blocks of words at a time (ROCm `lut_dot`, Vulkan `FORMAT_DOT` in `model_formats.glsl`, which `sparse_softmax.comp` shares); `stored_dot` goes.
- `route_experts` under sqrt_softplus runs a row on one wave of 64 lanes, each pick an argmax by shuffles, the sum in pick order on one lane as before.
- `topk_rows` and `candidate_blocks` find the picks' least key four bits a round by a radix select over wave histograms instead of bit by bit, and place picks by ballot ranks.
- The window packs its rows straight into the ring under native, a pack a ring run, and the `packed_kv` slot and its copy go.
- `hc_collapse_norm` writes its output's twin beside it, as `rms_norm_rows` does, so the head's product quantizes nothing.
- Not kept: a one-block-a-row decode softmax (item 2), under the 2x F2DEV set at every form tried (64 heads of 640, d 4096, main 86 us: dots 81 to 138 us, norms 24 to 143 us); window ids once a pass, which needs a first-layer-of-key flag in the plan and per-key slots for about 0.3%; the compressor's products straight into the ring, which splits prompt products at ring runs; a shared zero row for `moe_step` (F2DEV's item 1, every MoeStep::zero user); the collapse's sum of squares moved into `hc_coeffs`, which changes bits.

**Measured:** one op a call on one MI50, us, main / branch, every output hash main's (a private bench over the backend libraries):

| op, shape | ROCm main / branch | Vulkan main / branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| `model_format_qdq` FP4, 8192 values (index query) | 41.4 / 3.5 | 45.2 / 12.8 |
| `model_format_qdq` FP4, 8192 x 512 | 1271.4 / 82.0 | 1187.0 / 298.4 |
| `model_format_qdq` FP8, 512 (window) | 22.9 / 3.1 | 39.2 / 7.0 |
| `model_format_pack` FP8, 1 x 512 (window) | 20.8 / 3.3 | 26.5 / 8.6 |
| `model_format_pack` FP4 under E4M3, 1 x 512 (entry) | 8.1 / 3.4 | 23.2 / 8.8 |
| `model_format_pack` FP4, 1 x 128 (key) | 12.0 / 3.3 | 31.5 / 10.9 |
| `model_format_pack` FP8, 512 x 512 | 33.6 / 9.4 | 46.7 / 32.4 |
| `topk_rows` 1 x 512, k 512 | 45.6 / 11.7 | 53.2 / 31.0 |

The minimum of two rounds a cell, arms alternated, in one container a backend (/opt/claude-work/dsdev117/out/ob-R.txt and ob-V.txt).
`sparse_attention_sink` shares the dot with `indexer_scores` and moves within 3%; with `lut_dot` inlined by the compiler's choice instead of forced, ROCm's decode softmax lost 46% (130.2 to 191.2 us at 128 + 512) while `indexer_scores` at 64 x 4096 gained 13% (12437 to 10834 us), so the forced inline is kept.
The window pack into the ring and the collapse's twin have no op cell of their own; the model timings below hold them.

## ROCm Q8_0 decode of 9 to 16 columns: one build a width at two rows a wave (2026-11-10, KRES17 to KRES19, branch perf/rocm-q8-wide-decode on main a5684cab3; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** the int8 class's half-block Q8_0 decode of 9 to 16 columns no slower than main on any shape, with one host rule and the one-column build's bits.

**Done:**
- Main ran 9 to 15 columns on the sixteen-column build, a column past the call skipped by a branch in its loads and products, at four rows a wave.
- `q8_0_rows_half` builds over 8 columns compute every column they hold, a column past the call reading the call's last column and stored by nobody, and sum as 16 columns; one build a width from 9 to 16 (`llmx_q8_0_half8_9` to `_16`), the host taking the narrowest that holds the call (`kHalfWide`).
- Every build over 8 columns takes two rows a wave: at four rows they held 153 to 251 VGPRs and ran one wave a SIMD on an MI50, a 256-VGPR register file (a device with a 512-entry file could run four rows at two waves, unmeasured), and the nine-column build at 251 VGPRs drained its loads 14 times a loop against 10 at ten columns, slower than main at 9 columns on 12 of 17 shapes (8192x5120 291 to 368 us).
  At two rows they hold 99 to 114 VGPRs, two waves a SIMD; a row keeps its lanes and order, so the bits do not change.
- Builds of 1 to 8 columns are unchanged.
- Checks: every column of every width 1 to 16 and 64 equals the one-column build's bits on 17 shapes; backend-rocm passes on an MI50.

**Measured** (one MI50, default clocks, a scratch harness over the production kernels, 17 shapes in input x output, ABAB of main and this branch, us a call, mean of two rounds):

| shape | 9 main / branch | 12 main / branch | 16 main / branch | 64 main / branch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192x5120 | 289 / 183 | 385 / 215 | 500 / 270 | 1966 / 1079 |
| 6144x25600 | 1043 / 644 | 1339 / 761 | 1709 / 945 | 6729 / 3813 |
| 5120x1280 | 61 / 39 | 78 / 44 | 99 / 53 | 418 / 217 |
| 1280x32768 | 455 / 329 | 532 / 397 | 629 / 484 | 2527 / 1929 |
| 2560x512 | 21 / 18 | 25 / 22 | 29 / 25 | 119 / 94 |
| 320x10240 | 101 / 74 | 113 / 87 | 130 / 104 | 530 / 414 |

Every cell of 9 to 16 columns and 64 is faster on the branch, by 12% to 51%, but one sample: 2560x512 at 10 columns measured 18.8 and 40.3 us in its two rounds, and a rerun gave 18.9 and 19.1 against main's 22.4 and 22.3.
Columns 1 to 8 moved -4.8% to +2.0%, their code unchanged.

**Landing gates:** landed stacked on perf/deepseek4-rocm-kernels by LAND24; the gates and timing round of the stack are in that block (DeepSeek-V4.1 ROCm kernels, below).

## DeepSeek-V4.1 ROCm kernels: routed prompt groups by size, sparse prefill (2026-11-09, DSDEV62, DSDEV67 and DSDEV68, then DSDEV78, DSDEV80 and DSDEV82, branch perf/deepseek4-rocm-kernels on main 298a94a65 and rebased on a5684cab3 to land, carrying perf/deepseek4-rocm-mxfp4 43174a802 and perf/deepseek4-rocm-mxfp4-2 de5de5da3; F2DEV's review of 19:39, B1 to B4, COORD's rulings of 19:42 and 20:49; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4 prefill and decode on ten MI50s in a layer split on ROCm toward the reference's 642 tok/s at pp16965 and 25.6 tok/s decode, every output the bits it had, one build for each range of a routed group's entries and each class.

**Done:**
- A routed prompt group runs in one build by its entries, each entry the tile's sums in block order in every build: up to 8 MXFP4's thin build (`k_thin`) in the F16 class and the stream (`routed_stream`, main's) in the int8 class, Q8_0's narrow tile in F16; up to 16 the narrow tile; a K-type's mid tile (`k_tile` at 32 rows) up to 32; the 64-row tile past.
  The thin build is the F16 class's alone: the int8 class has no thin build, since the stream now beats the int8 thin build at every entry count on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MXFP4 (owner's ruling of 20:49: one path, no speed given away).
  The stream reads the entries' twin blocks by uniform scalar loads for MXFP4, Q5_0 and Q5_1 (`StreamScalar`), a lane decoding a whole load's blocks once and each entry then running over them, which took MXFP4's stream from 167 to 123 VGPRs; the other types keep the shared-memory staging, where the scalar loads lost (Q8_0 at every entry count, the K-quants from 3 entries, IQ4_NL from 5).
- B1 table (one MI50, gate+up each build launched alone, us a call, hashes equal): 

| entries | DeepSeek MXFP4 5120x2304: main stream | int8 thin (removed) | this stream | Q5_0 2560x640: main | this | Q5_1: main | this |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9790 | 12714 | 9117 | 2139 | 2078 | 2228 | 2041 |
| 2 | 10744 | 13400 | 9427 | 2348 | 2164 | 2350 | 2114 |
| 3 | 12099 | 12630 | 9847 | 2462 | 2210 | 2358 | 2117 |
| 4 | 13322 | 13470 | 10325 | 2677 | 2285 | 2534 | 2168 |
| 5 | 15294 | 13778 | 11350 | 3024 | 2374 | 2859 | 2275 |

| 7 | 18077 | 16048 | 13244 | 3496 | 2668 | 3298 | 2522 |
| 8 | 19475 | 17500 | 14201 | 3750 | 2837 | 3542 | 2706 |

  Min of three interleaved rounds against main's stream, every output hash equal, int8 gate+up, us a call (/opt/claude-work/dsdev85/out/sc; the removed thin build's column from /opt/claude-work/dsdev82/out/e7); the staged types (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0) keep main's loop written out and compile to main's instructions and registers (`llvm-objdump` of int16dot and of the build against main's, exact diff 0), and IQ4_NL differs only in its table's PC-relative offset; a first version that called a lambda for an entry's terms rescheduled them (Q6_K 871 lines reordered), so Q6_K is main's kernel.
  Tests passed on one MI50: backend-rocm moe and deepseek4, and backend-vulkan --deepseek4.
  Measured and not kept: scalar loads with the blocks decoded one at a time (MXFP4 at 82 VGPRs, 13775 and 14425 us at 7 and 8 entries, but the K-quants up to 1.9 times slower), the scale and twin sum read from memory instead of staged (MXFP4 at 1 entry 14512 us), half-superblock batches for the K-quants (170 VGPRs, still slower from 3 entries), `waves_per_eu(2)` (spills from 6 entries), two-block loads and entries split over waves.
- Thin cutoff: `kThinRows` 8 is kept for MXFP4 in F16: thin builds of 12 and 16 rows lost to the narrow tile from 9 entries (10 entries 72158 and 57104 against 47535 us) and the 16-row one cost 1 to 8 entries (8 at 37126 against 23876 us); on Q4_K the thin build (about 9.7 ms from 3 entries) lost to the narrow tile (6318 to 7122 us), so it is MXFP4's alone.
- Forced-path check (B2): `routed_builds_witness` in backend-rocm `moe` launches each build alone (`rocm_route_only`) over a sentinel output and requires it to write exactly the groups of its range among groups of 4, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17, 32 and 33 entries, each the bits of the call of every build, for MXFP4, Q4_K and Q8_0 in f16 and int8; `experts_quads` adds 32 entries and MXFP4 at 65 blocks a row.
- Prompt sparse attention: from `kSparseWideRows` rows `llmx_sparse_softmax_g` (`kSparseSoftmaxHeads` heads a block, the queries staged once for them) and `llmx_sparse_columns64`; fewer rows, decode's, keep the one-head kernels; every output keeps its chain.
  `kSparseWideRows` is 8: one MI50, 64 heads of 512, 4096 entries, three rounds against main, 1 row 57.3 against 57.5 us at k128 and 159.5 against 158.0 at k640, 8 rows 25 percent faster, 16 rows 33 to 40, 120 rows 49 to 54, every hash main's; at 7 rows both arms run main's kernels and differ by 4.5 percent, a layout effect.
  `kSparseSoftmaxHeads` is 4: 8 heads a block was 8 to 14 percent slower at 16 rows and 0.3 to 5 percent faster at 120 and 512, and the planner's slices are small.
  The grouped softmax's head width is no longer a literal 512: it runs while its heads' queries fit the shared memory its own arrays leave (`DeviceCaps::shared_bytes`, which ROCm and Vulkan now report and only ROCm reads until Vulkan thin-mid rebases, less the kernel's static size read with `hipFuncGetAttribute`), staged in dynamic shared memory; on an MI50 four heads take up to 3424 values beside the kernel's 10376 bytes; `sparse_head_budget` in backend-rocm `deepseek4` holds the widest head that fits and one block wider to their builds and to the rows called alone.
- Decode keeps main's one-head pair, `llmx_sparse_softmax` and `llmx_sparse_columns`, unchanged below `kSparseWideRows` rows, which a first version had replaced and lost 10 to 15 percent at 1 row.
- Earlier measurements carried (DSDEV62 and DSDEV67): thin up to 4 entries at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash expert shapes, f16 gate+up, 1 entry 38645 to 13132 us and 4 entries 38979 to 14089 us; mid tile 17 entries 106549 to 61431 us and 32 entries 115157 to 66586 us; ten MI50s, `--ubatch 512`, pp2048 512.0 to 710.0 and pp16384 571.3 to 641.9 tok/s, tg32 level; thin taking 1 to 16 entries was not kept (16 at 116436 against the narrow tile's 51317 us).
- Sparse bench of DSDEV67 (64 heads of 512, 4096 entries, us): 120 rows base 2235/7872 to 1195/3681 at k128/k640, 512 rows 9385/33406 to 4620/15551, 1 row unchanged (the base kernels).

## Vulkan routed MXFP4: a 16-column float tile build (2026-11-09, DSDEV58 to DSDEV61, branch perf/vulkan-mxfp4-routed on main 298a94a65; VKMX1's finding of 04:54, DSDEV58's proposal of 05:13, F2DEV's reviews of 05:40, items 1 to 9, and of 07:28, R1 and R2; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** routed MXFP4 prompt products on Vulkan read the experts' weights at more than a quarter of the card's bandwidth when experts hold few entries each.

**Done:**
- MXFP4 always takes the float tile, whose 64 columns left an expert of a few entries reading its whole weight for mostly empty columns: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's gate and up read at 26 GB/s on one MI50.
- `routed_call` sends a call whose entries average 16 or fewer an expert (`kNarrowCols`) to `matmul_tile_mxfp4_narrow`, a thread a row over every column of a run of 16 entries (`shaders/matmul_tile_narrow.glsl`, 256-row workgroups, `kNarrowFloatRows`).
  The narrow build takes the height the 64-column grouping gives, since the tile's rows decide which sums are wide, so its outputs are the 64-column build's bits (F2DEV's item 1).
- The MXFP4 tile decodes through the doubled E2M1 table, fetches the next stage during the current one and gathers each stage's scale range in its loop; the BF16 build shares it.
- `check_routed_mxfp4_narrow` holds both builds to an ascending fma or the wide sum over wide rows (scale bytes 0, 1, 64, 189, 200), wide inputs, and calls at the cut (128 entries over eight experts) and one past it (F2DEV's item 2).
  It runs on experts of 160 rows and of 8192 rows, whose narrow calls must take `matmul_tile_mxfp4_narrow_tall` by name, with wide rows in each workgroup's second 128 rows (F2DEV's R1).
- Both narrow builds have 84 VGPRs, 48 SGPRs, no spills, no scratch and 3 waves a SIMD on an MI50 under RADV, as the 64-column tall build has.
- Known, not this branch (F2DEV's item 6): the wide decision depends on the tile's height, which follows the call's entries, so an MXFP4 output that takes the wide sum is not batch-invariant on main either.
- Not taken: a refusal of files with wide scale bytes (F2DEV's item 7), and IQ4_NL, which routes on the integer narrow tile (item 8, a separate branch after a profile).

**Microbenchmark** (`llmx-moe-kernel-bench`, a scratch tool, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash expert shapes 5120 into 2304, 384 experts, 6 a row, one MI50, default clocks, ABBA main e899036de vs this branch before the rebase; every output hash equal to main's), gate and up in us:

| entries an expert | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 185.6k (26 GB/s) | 33.1k (145 GB/s) |
| 8 | 189.1k | 45.3k |
| 16 | 193.6k | 67.8k |
| 17 (64-column build) | 195.5k | 141.6k |
| 32 (64-column build) | 208.8k | 146.4k |
| average 8, four experts at 96 | 194.0k | 48.9k |
| average 16, four experts at 128 | 198.8k | 72.2k |
| dense 4096x5120 over 512, bf16 / f32 | 4782 / 4899 | 3493 / 3363 |

The 64-column tile's thread layout cut to 16 columns (DSDEV59's variant d) read at 92 GB/s at 1 to 8 entries and was 4% faster at 16; the thread-a-row build kept here is 1.2x to 1.6x faster at 1 to 8.

**Ten cards** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4, ten MI50 layer split on Vulkan, default clocks, `--cpus 8`, nr_throttled 0 in every run; main 1227b7871 and the rebased branch built the same way; `bench --p 2048 --n 32 --r 2 --ubatch 512`, ABBA):

| tg32 tok/s | 16.46 / 16.02 | 16.28 / 16.13 |

`logits` over a 1400-token prompt at `--ubatch 512` (top 8 every position) gives main's bytes (md5 67056081 in both arms).
A pp2048 profile of the branch on vulkan:0 gives `matmul_tile_mxfp4_narrow_tall` 1856 of 2698 ms (69%), so the routed tile is still the prompt's largest cost.
Decode does not take the tile, so tg32 moves within its noise.

- `llmx-backend-vulkan-test --routed` (397920 routed MXFP4 outputs through both builds) and `llmx-mxfp4-vulkan-test` (577 cases, 703574 outputs) pass.
- Byte identity against main on vulkan:0, 32 files: the MXFP4 and IQ4_NL raw-block fixtures, dense and qwen3moe, prompts at `--ubatch` 64 and 512 and greedy ids, and the Qwen3-0.6B MXFP4 file.

## ROCm frees beside the devices (2026-11-09, PRE4, branch perf/rocm-defer-free on main e899036d; PDEV1's item 1 of 2026-11-07, F2DEV's review of PRE3b at 06:48, item 6; lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

**Goal:** no free that drains a device on the pass path of any thread, in the one owner of dropped ROCm memory (`Graves` in `rocm_backend.cpp`).

**Done:**
- Microbench on one MI50 (gfx906, ROCm 7.2.1, 3 repeats): `hipFree`, `hipHostFree` and `hipFreeAsync` of `hipMalloc` memory each hold their caller until the queued work has run (200 ms queued: 201.0, 201.5 and 200.5 ms); with the stream idle `hipFree` takes 0.04 to 0.19 ms from 16 MiB to 4 GiB; `hipMalloc` does not wait (0.1 ms).
  `hipMallocAsync` with `hipFreeAsync` does not wait but the pool keeps the memory (31510 MiB free before the free, after it and after a synchronise), which the fit would read as used, so it was not taken.
  A second thread's `hipFree`, `hipHostFree` or `hipStreamSynchronize` while the first keeps the stream fed leaves the feeder's `hipEventRecord` at 0.01 to 0.07 ms, its `hipEventQuery` at 0.00 to 0.03 ms and the device's gaps as with no second call (1.84 against 1.85 ms over 200 kernels); a second thread's `hipEventSynchronize` on an event the feeder queries holds the query 12.8 ms.
- Profile (main with every allocation and drop of 1 MiB or more and every free timed, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, four MI50s): on layer-4 pp2048 the first run with a new slice plan freed 28 buffers in 700 ms on the recording threads, at 1149 tok/s against 1564; they are the backend's twins and split-K partials grown for the larger slices (`take_twin_slot`, the split tile's partials), so any split meets it on a plan change.
  A server taking prompts of 516, 2313, 9205, 748 and 14772 tokens freed 84, 164 and 132 buffers in 1.8, 3.2 and 4.3 s inside the 2313, 9205 and 14772-token prompts, the first of each size, and none in repeats.
- The fix: `record` and `wait` free nothing; a thread the backend starts last in its constructor and joins in its destructor takes each grave whose covering ticket is recorded, synchronises the stream and frees it, woken by `record`. An allocation HIP refuses waits for the graves under recorded tickets to be freed (`Graves::settle`), which waits for the whole stream, and is tried once more; it records nothing, since `alloc` may run beside the recording thread. A grave now lives until the stream has run past it and what was queued then, instead of until the next record or wait after its ticket retired.
- After F2DEV's review (08:30, PRE5): `memory_available` settles the recorded graves before it reads and `sync` records a ticket for drops since the last one, so the fit's readings after `sync` (`build_fitted`'s `before`, `after` and `short_by`) count dropped memory as free; `memory_available` is read only by placement, never on a pass.
  `backend-rocm` now also reads the memory at once after `sync`, with no polling, for drops under a ticket and after the last one, and with the device filled requires an allocation the device refuses to take a buffer dropped under a ticket with about 200 ms of copies still queued, and one with nothing dropped to still be refused.
  On main it fails four checks (submission after a drop 180.2 ms, wait 182.7 ms, a drop after the last submission still held after `sync`, the allocation refused with 581 MB free and work queued); on the branch the whole test passes.
  Rechecked on the reviewed fix, layer-4 pp2048 as below, four processes an arm alternated ABBA ABBA (main the same binary as below): mean main 1437.5 and the branch 1556.8 tok/s, slow runs 6/20 and 0/20, first runs 1481, 1492, 1495, 1495 against 1549, 1549, 1548, 1549, fast medians 1556.8 and 1558.3, nr_throttled 1 and 4.
- `backend-rocm`: the new check fails on main (submission after a drop 179.3 ms, wait 182.3 ms) and passes on the branch, the whole test passing.
- Timing, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ROCm on four MI50s (renderD132-135) at default clocks, bench pp2048 five runs a process, eight processes an arm alternated ABBA ABBA, --cpus 8, slow below 0.9 times the pooled median:

| cell | main mean tok/s | branch mean tok/s | slow main / branch | first runs main | first runs branch | fast median main / branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| layer-4 pp2048 | 1440.6 | 1543.0 | 7/20 / 0/20 | 1327, 1149, 1148, 1397 | 1547, 1544, 1407, 1547 | 1557.4 / 1557.2 |
| 2x2 pp2048 | 1462.3 | 1455.8 | 0/20 / 1/20 (1308, a second run) | 1459, 1467, 1465, 1475 | 1449, 1468, 1467, 1468 | 1460.1 / 1467.4 |

  nr_throttled over all processes: layer-4 3 and 4, 2x2 3 and 8. Three of main's slow runs are not a process's first (1174, 1175, 1176 at 6 slices); the profile saw no free in later runs, so they are not attributed here.
- Server, layer-4, one fresh server a run alternated main, branch, branch, main, prompt tok/s of the first 2313 and 14772-token prompts: main 905 and 918, 1367 and 1021; branch 1060 and 1089, 1653 and 1660; the repeated 14772-token prompt 1694 and 1688 against 1690 and 1690.
- Greedy ids: 64 tokens after a 2.5k-token prompt are the same on main and the branch, layer-4 and 2x2.

**Landing gates:** run once on the stacked head 5e4eef071 with perf/prefill-pipeline-flow below this branch, all passing, including layer-4 pp2048 and the server's first prompts against main; recorded in (A ROCm ticket some thread synchronises on reads as not done, below).
Lands by fast-forward together with perf/prefill-pipeline-flow, as that branch's two commits and then this branch's failing test and fix.

**Gotchas:**
- Only a stream synchronise may wait on the thread: an event synchronise there would hold the recording thread's `done` queries (12.8 ms in the microbench, PRE3b's slow mode).
- Vulkan's `vkFreeMemory` does not wait for the device (F2DEV, 2026-11-07), so Vulkan keeps freeing a ring slot's buffers as the slot is reopened.

## A ROCm ticket some thread synchronises on reads as not done (2026-11-09, PRE3 then PRE3b, branch perf/prefill-pipeline-flow on main ed9780218; PRE3's proposal of 2026-11-08 22:46 with F2DEV's review of 23:28, items 1 to 7; lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

**Goal:** remove the layer-split prompt's slow mode on ROCm, where about one prefill in five ran at 1186 instead of 1552 tok/s on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next layer-4.

**Done:**
- `RocmBackend::done` reads a ticket whose event some thread is in `hipEventSynchronize` on as not done without asking HIP, which holds such a query until the work ends; `wait` counts itself in and out of the slot around the synchronise, before it retires the ticket, so a reused slot never sees a stale count.
  `Backend::done`'s comment and `docs/src/backends-backend.md` say that done may read not done for a retired ticket while another thread is still in `wait`; every caller (the completion lanes, hold's first-chunk choice, the history and service polls) asks again or waits.
- Cause, from stamps of every query over 3 ms, HIP frees over 2 ms and each stage's record per chunk (diagnostic builds, not landed): on main the recording thread's query of the last stage's ticket blocks about 545 ms at the start of every prefill and 125-160 ms three more times, about 980 ms a pass, fast runs included, so the block alone costs nothing visible.
  It makes the recording thread late, so on the first prefill after the warmup's slice plan the graves of that plan's buffers retire while it is still recording, and its next record frees them: 7 hipFree calls, 625 ms, each draining a device mid-pass, chunk 1 done at 1202 instead of 707 ms.
  With the fix the thread records a whole pass in about 50 ms with no query over 3 ms, and the same frees (one call, 684-969 ms) fall on the completion lane after all work is issued.
- The frees themselves remain; the hipFree deferral (PDEV1's item 1, F2DEV's review of 2026-11-07 22:26) would remove them on any thread.

**Timing** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL `--dtype int8`, `-ctk f16 -ctv f16`, four MI50s renderD128-131, ROCm, default clocks, `--cpus 8`, bench `--r 5` a process, ABBA ABBA, 20 runs an arm a cell; clean builds of detached worktrees, main `llmx 0.1.0+ged9780218f62`, this change at 6e78d226; slow = below 0.9 x the cell's pooled median, fixed before measuring; nr_throttled 5-12 in the L4 pp2048 processes of both arms, 0-12 at pp16384 L4, 0 on 2x2):

| cell | main mean tok/s | this change mean tok/s | main slow runs | this change slow runs | fast-run median main / this change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| layer-4 pp2048 | 1479.1 | 1563.5 (+5.7%) | 4 of 20 (1186-1188, each process's first run) | 0 of 20 | 1552.0 / 1563.9 |
| layer-4 pp16384 | 1953.1 | 1951.9 | 0 | 0 | 1953.1 / 1953.0 |
| 2x2 pp2048 | 1456.1 | 1498.9 (+2.9%) | 0 | 0 | 1473.8 / 1507.6 |
| 2x2 pp16384 | 1538.8 | 1533.8 | 0 | 1 (1370) | 1553.5 / 1553.8 |

Part of the layer-4 pp2048 gain is the first prefill's frees moving off the pass: the slow runs go from 4 of 20 to 0 of 20, while the fast-run medians differ less (1552.0 against 1563.9).
The 2x2 pp2048 difference follows the slice counts each process chose (main 4-10, this change 4-5), and the one 2x2 pp16384 slow run is unexplained (no diagnostic run at that size).
The speed gate stays open: the reference gives 2615 tok/s on layer-4 and 1939 on 2x2 at pp2048.

## ROCm routed prompt stream (2026-11-09, PRE2, PRE2b, PRE2c then PRE2d, branch perf/rocm-moe-prompt-stream stacked on perf/rocm-hc-mix-rows over main 4b5f9236d; F2DEV's reviews of 2026-11-08 22:20, B1 to B3, and of 2026-11-09 02:50, B1 and B2; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** a routed MoE prompt group of few entries reads its expert's weights once at full bandwidth on ROCm, with the routed tile's bits.

**Done:**
- `routed_stream` (kernels/int16.hip), for every twin type (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_0, Q5_1, IQ4_NL, MXFP4, Q8_0) on the 8-bit twin: a group of up to kStreamRows (8) entries is one wave, a lane one output that reads its weight row once as whole 16-byte loads and decodes it in registers, the group's twin rows staged in shared memory.
  `RocmBackend`'s routed-tile branch launches the three builds over the groups and each group runs in one by its entries: the stream up to 8 (8-bit twin only), the narrow tile up to 16, the 64-row tile past; no build above 8 entries changed.
- Each entry takes the tile's integer block sums and float terms in block order, so an entry has one result whichever build its group takes; no K split (one part, as the tile), no flag and no profile number.
- Past kLeanWords (48) words a lane load, Q6_K's 210-byte superblock, the entry loop skips the entries past the group instead of leaving it, which took Q6_K's stream from 256 VGPRs and 124 bytes of scratch a lane to 206 and none; Q5_0 reads its halves from the words by shifts (`StreamDecode<rq::Q5_0>`), which took its 56 bytes of scratch away.
  Taken by every type, the skipping loop cost Q4_K 548 to 505 GB/s at 1 to 4 entries, Q5_K 416 to 361 at 5 to 8 and MXFP4 170 to 156 at 1 to 4 (mb/m1.txt under /opt/claude-work/pre2d), so only the loads that spilled take it.
- Microbenchmark (one MI50, mb/r16.txt and r17.txt under /opt/claude-work/pre2): 0 differing outputs against main's tile and narrow builds for all 8 types at group sizes 1 to 65 and on real routing, the entry alone the entry in its group in every case.
  GB/s main to branch at 1-4 / 5-8 entries: Q4_K 209 to 554 / 193 to 373, Q5_K 180 to 572 / 171 to 416, Q5_1 247 to 439 / 220 to 332, Q8_0 450 to 519 / 421 to 469, Q6_K 250 to 532 / 227 to 364 (mb/m1.txt, with the skipping loop; 340 / 218 before it), MXFP4 98 to 169 / 94 to 149 (182 to 392 / 169 to 265 against main 1227b7871, whose MXFP4 decode reads aligned words; mb/m3.txt), IQ4_NL 133 to 185 / 129 to 165 (the same against 1227b7871), Q5_0 242 to 464 / 227 to 334 (mb/m2.txt under /opt/claude-work/pre2d, with its shifts; 281 / 238 before them).
  The tradeoff: at 9 to 16 entries every group runs in the narrow tile and the stream's launch is all early returns, which costs Q8_0 5 to 7% there (640 by 2560 389 to 365 GB/s, 2592 by 640 424 to 396) and the other types up to 3%.
  That cost is the launch's grid, a wave for every 64 outputs of every group, not its registers (Q8_0 at 99 VGPRs instead of 153 lost the same), and the host cannot size the grid without reading the groups back; on mixed routing (`real`) Q8_0 is +3 to +8% at 640 by 2560 and level at 2592 by 640.
- backend-rocm `moe`: `experts_quads` now requires the stream in int8 and not in f16 and holds every entry of groups of 1 to 33 to the entry routed alone, bit for bit, for all 8 types, at inner sizes 2560 and 768 for the K-quants and 2560, 640 and 800 for the others, which end the stream's last chunk full, at half a chunk, short and with a one-block tail, and the routed class check counts the stream among the tile builds; it passes on one MI50.
- A static_assert holds that every twin type has its stream, since the 8-bit routed tiles leave it the groups of up to 8 entries.

**Timing** (LAND13's landing round on the stacked head of this branch and perf/rocm-hc-mix-rows: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ROCm on four MI50s at default clocks, `--cpus 8`, nr_throttled 1 to 3, host load 11 to 21; main 4b5f9236d against the head, `bench --p P --n 1 --r 3`, ABBA, 2 rounds, 12 runs an arm; per-run tok/s in /opt/claude-work/land13/out/ab):

| cell | main | head | delta | Vulkan main c319438bc | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| layer-4 pp2048, fast mode | 1554.5 (7 runs) | 1749.6 (8 runs) | +12.6% | 1715 | 2615 |
| layer-4 pp2048, slow mode | 1185.7 (3 runs) | 1257.2 (4 runs) | +6.0% | | |
| layer-4 pp16384 | 1953.9 | 2077.6 | +6.3% | 2331 | - |
| 2x2 pp2048 | 1494.5 | 1548.7 | +3.6% | 1581 | 1939 |
| 2x2 pp16384 | 1550.2 | 1616.8 | +4.3% | 1714 | - |

Layer-4 pp2048 is bimodal in both arms: every slow run is the first of a process's three, and main has two more between the modes (1392.2 and 1437.2), so each mode is compared within itself; the all-run means are 1439.0 against 1585.5 (+10.2%).
Greedy replies are main's text in the 2x2 server cells (one user with MTP, and four users without drafts, perf/rocm-hc-mix-rows's block).
The Vulkan column was measured on main c319438bc (PP16's baseline), not on 4b5f9236d.

- ISA at the landed head: no stream build uses scratch (VGPRs q8_0 153, q4_k 248, q5_k 249, q6_k 206, q5_0 164, q5_1 168, iq4_nl 164, mxfp4 167).
- Landing gates: the ones listed in perf/rocm-hc-mix-rows's block (CTest with backend-rocm `moe` and `twins`, suites, identity on the CPU, vulkan:0 and rocm:0, hosted run); no Radeon VII check, as the change is ROCm only and the Windows build compiles it out.

**Left:**
- The 16-bit twin keeps the narrow tile for groups of 1 to 16: the stream was built and measured for the 8-bit twin only.
- Q5_1, which spills in neither loop, was faster with the skipping loop too (5 to 8 entries 366 to 436 GB/s at 2592 by 640, mixed routing 303 to 322); a loop chosen by type rather than by spilling is left open.
- Vulkan: the routed narrow tile on runs of 1 to 8 entries is measured, and a stream build there is a follow-up branch if it pays.

## Multi-row hyper-connection mix on ROCm (2026-11-09, MTP5, branch perf/rocm-hc-mix-rows on main 4b5f9236d, landed stacked under perf/rocm-moe-prompt-stream; MTP4's item 4 of 2026-11-08; F2DEV's review of 01:12; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** verify and multi-user decode rows mix their hyper-connection streams in one launch, as a decode row does, with each column's bits the one-column launch's, so verify rows equal decode rows; the chain stays only for the shapes the launch does not take.

**Done:**
- `RocmBackend::hyper_mix` takes generated rows (every run of extent 1) in launches of up to 8 columns: `llmx_hc_mix` for one column, unchanged, and `llmx_hc_mix8` for 2 to 8, from one template (`hc_mix<C>` in kernels/int16.hip) whose phases run the columns one after another on the weights a wave already holds, with a block an inject output of each column.
  Unrolling the columns spilled 267 VGPRs at 4 columns and made the launch slower than the chain (89 us against 77 at 4 rows); rolled, `llmx_hc_mix` spills 39 VGPRs into 120 bytes of scratch a lane as main's does, and `llmx_hc_mix8` 46 into 144 bytes, neither more than that scratch.
- `backend-rocm twins` (`hyper_mix_bits`): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 13 and 16 rows at four shapes, out, the normed streams, the low rows, the gates and the inject gates bit for bit against the chain and against each column launched alone, and out's twin through a product; it counts the `llmx_hc_mix8` launches a call, one a chunk of 8 rows and one for a last chunk of 2 to 7 (none at 1 row, 2 at 13 and 16).
- Microbenchmark (rig-only bench mode of the backend test, one MI50, the Flash-Next shape 4 x 2560 streams of low rank 320 with inject gates, us a call):

  | rows | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | chain | 49.8 | 61.1 | 72.9 | 77.3 | 130.7 | 202.9 |
  | fused | 30.9 | 39.7 | 49.3 | 57.0 | 87.0 | 173.8 |
  | one-column launch a row | 30.9 | 61.9 | 92.9 | 123.8 | 248.5 | 494.8 |

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ROCm 2x2 on four MI50s at default clocks, one user, MTP draft-max 3, `--cpus 8` with nr_throttled 0, a fresh server an arm in turn, three rounds, greedy 256-token replies, tok/s of the runs after the warm one (host load 20 to 24 from other work):
  perf/mtp-draft-price 724b32941 78.5/80.5/76.9, 77.7/80.6/80.9, 75.3/75.3/78.7 (mean 78.2); this branch 87.3/84.8/84.0, 80.8/84.3/83.5, 81.1/84.1/85.4 (mean 83.9, +7.3%); the reference build measured 92 to 96 on this cell.
  Every reply of both arms, warm ones included, is main's text (sha256 10eb8235), so verify rows mixed in the multi-column launch change no token.
- Layer-4, the same cell (nr_throttled 5 to 10 in every server of both arms): perf/mtp-draft-price 67.4/65.4/66.7, 66.8/65.5/67.0, 65.2/67.3/64.8 (mean 66.2); this branch 74.2/70.2/72.7, 71.3/70.7/71.7, 70.8/70.2/71.6 (mean 69.3, +4.6%); every reply main's text.
- `llmx_hc_mix` against main's: the index math of one column is guarded by `C == 1`, the VGPR, SGPR, spill and scratch counts are main's (128 VGPRs with 39 spilled, 120 bytes of scratch a lane, 17 SGPRs spilled), and the instructions differ in scheduling and in the argument's layout (3587 against 3593), so a drafts-off decode A/B against the parent head holds it.
- Drafts off, the same 2x2 cell, three fresh servers an arm (host load 18 to 26): perf/mtp-draft-price 63.0/63.1/59.3, 61.2/52.2/59.3, 63.0/61.5/59.7 (mean 60.2); this branch 62.1/62.1/62.1, 58.0/62.0/61.7, 61.2/61.2/62.4 (mean 61.4); every reply main's text, so the one-row launch keeps its speed.
- rocprofv3 on the stage-0 device, generate of 48 tokens at draft-max 3: the chain's six launches at 4 columns take about 92 us a mix (27.5 + 23.0 + 18.6 + 10.6 + 6.6 + 5.3), `llmx_hc_mix8` 68.0 us, and `llmx_hc_mix` 39.5 against 38.8 at one row.

**Landing gates** (LAND13, at the stacked head of this branch and perf/rocm-moe-prompt-stream on main 4b5f9236d; that block gives the table):
- Fresh ROCm and Vulkan builds; ROCm CTest 84/84 with backend-rocm in full, `twins`, `moe` and `deepseek4` on one MI50; the CPU suite and the suite on rocm:0 pass; docs and dead-code pass; hosted run 42588340137 8/8 green.
- Byte identity against main for Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and the tiny MoE fixtures on the CPU, vulkan:0 and rocm:0.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ROCm 2x2, four users without drafts (the 2 to 8 column launch): main 186.2, head 204.4 tok/s, every reply main's text; one user with MTP draft-max 3, three fresh servers an arm alternated: main 80.4, head 83.2 tok/s (one head run of 68.1; medians 80.7 and 84.8), every reply sha256 10eb8235.
- The Windows build.bat binary compiles the ROCm backend out (no hc_mix or routed_stream kernel names in it).

**Left:** the Vulkan backend has no fused mix at any row count (the chain at every width, so its verify rows already equal its decode rows), and a fused Vulkan mix is a design of its own, since Vulkan gives no co-residency for grid barriers.
On ROCm the fused launch is 30.9 against the chain's 49.8 us at one row and 57.0 against 77.3 at four, 0.5 to 0.9 ms a stage pass of 12 layers, the size of what a Vulkan fused mix could take; Vulkan's own chain is not yet measured at these widths.

**Gotchas:** the launch's grid grows by a block a stream for each column with inject gates, so its residency is checked a build and a column count; the bench mode stays out of the tree.

## DeepSeek-V4.1 decode speed: serial kernels spread, MXFP4 expert rows and sparse attention as two kernels (2026-11-08 to 2026-11-09, DSDEV52 to DSDEV56, branch perf/deepseek4-decode on main ed9780218; DSDEV52's plan of 2026-11-08 19:42; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's decode on ten MI50s in a layer split, ROCm and Vulkan, with every kernel the bits it had on main: the per-token kernels that ran on one lane or one thread spread over their workgroups, the expert MXFP4 rows faster, and sparse attention split so each kept row is decoded once for all heads.

**Done:**
- Serial kernels, ROCm and Vulkan in their backend owners (`kernels/f32.hip`, `shaders/hc_coeffs.comp`, `shaders/hc_collapse_norm.comp`, `shaders/indexer_scores.comp`): `indexer_scores` a lane a (position, head) dot with the head sum's chain on one lane over shared memory; `hc_coeffs` its Sinkhorn rounds on hc * hc lanes, each entry's row and column sums in the CPU's order, its loads batched; `hc_collapse_norm` the CPU's chains with batched loads, on ROCm 1024 lanes with the row staged in shared memory.
- MXFP4 expert rows: ROCm reads each block's scale and nibble words raw from the aligned words around it and widens the nibbles by byte selects of the E2M1 table held in registers (`KRaw<MXFP4>`), and MXFP4, a type with no min, skips the twin sum and widens its bytes to 16 bits by byte selects, while IQ4_NL keeps main's form, its term `ds * isum` the value of the old `fmaf(ds, isum, -(0 * xsum))`; Vulkan's one-column MXFP4 chunk takes two rows a cluster where the transposed reduction holds the cluster (`column_builds`).
- `sparse_attention_sink` as two kernels on both backends over a scratch the backend grows, a chunk of rows of at most 32 MiB at a time: a softmax kernel a (row, head) keeps the named rows that name something in name order, forms each kept row's score on its own lane from the row's aligned words and a shared table of the E4M3 and E2M1 values, and writes p by kept row and head, the denominator with exp(sink - max) and the kept rows; a columns kernel decodes eight columns of the kept rows once into shared memory for every head, a lane a head and two columns (docs/src/backends-rocm.md, docs/src/backends-vulkan.md).
  Every score and output is the CPU's multiply-add chain over the same rows in the same order, so the result is the one-kernel form's bit for bit.
- Microbenchmarks on one MI50 at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's shapes (64 heads of 512, a 128-row FP8 window and 512 FP4 entries), output hashes equal to the one-kernel form at every position and at 64 rows:

  | kernel, us a call | position 96 | position 16384 | 64 rows at 2048 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | ROCm one kernel / two kernels | 475 / 58 | 1440 / 116 | |
  | Vulkan one kernel / two kernels | 668 / 96 | 1586 / 259 | 60262 / 4927 |

- Ten MI50s, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4, layer split, `--lookup-storage file`, default clocks, `--cpus 8`, nr_throttled 0 to 2 (tok/s):

  | backend | main tg32 | branch tg32 | branch pp2048 | branch pp16384 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ROCm | 9.81, 9.79 | 21.20, 21.17 | 512 | 575 |
  | Vulkan | 6.39, 6.39 | 16.40, 16.91 | 172.8 | 304.3 |

  main's figures are its landing record's (`--r 3`); the branch's are `--p 64 --n 32 --r 2` at `--ubatch 64` and `--ubatch 512` for the prompts.
  Vulkan with the two sparse kernels against the branch's one-kernel shader, the same slot, head then branch then branch then head: tg32 14.48, 14.61 to 16.40, 16.91, pp2048 91.9 to 172.8, pp16384 122.9 to 304.3.
  No matched mx fork figure: its loader reads the whole 411 GB MXFP4 set, lookup tables included, at about 250 MB/s on one thread, and an attempt with `--repack 0` had put nothing on the cards after 13 minutes; with repacking at `-ub 512` it failed to place a 35.5 GB repacked buffer on device 0.

- Forced-path checks (`tests/deepseek4_checks.hpp`, run by `backend-rocm` and `backend-vulkan`): `hc_coeffs` at hc 16, `indexer_scores` at 64 and 300 heads, and `check_sparse_shapes`, `sparse_attention_sink` at 160-wide heads in every stored format (four-block runs and a tail), 65 heads, 600 named rows and 140 rows of 1024 named rows over 64 heads, past one scratch chunk on both backends.
  ROCm's `sparse_attention_sink` stays held to 1e-5 against the CPU, not its bits: its exponentials are `expf`'s, and the bit check failed by one ulp (0.0846442953 against 0.0846443027) on the first pooled case.
- Identity: greedy ids of the 64-token chat prompt on the real file equal main's on ROCm (md5 83aacc46) and Vulkan; the tiny deepseek4 fork fixture's greedy ids and `logits` rows equal main's on `rocm:0` and `vulkan:0`, f32 and default caches; `backend-rocm` and `llmx-backend-vulkan-test --deepseek4` pass.
- Identity after the review fixes, branch against main built the same way: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4 on ten MI50s, 1489 prompt tokens at `--ubatch 512` (three passes, each over two or more sparse scratch chunks), `logits --last 1400 --top 8` the same bytes on ROCm and Vulkan.
  On one MI50, ROCm and Vulkan: the suite's MXFP4 and IQ4_NL raw-block fixtures (dense tied, untied and qwen3moe MoE, contexts 16 and 128, prompts at `--ubatch 64` and greedy ids), Qwen3-0.6B MXFP4 and Qwen3-0.6B IQ4_NL (632-token prompt rows at `--ubatch 512` and 48 greedy ids) are main's bytes.
  Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL holds IQ4_NL only in `per_layer_token_embd`, a lookup no matmul reads, so it reaches neither the ROCm widening nor the MXFP4 builds.
- Landing gates (LAND12 and LAND16, rebased on main e899036de, both arms built the same way from exported trees, `llmx 0.1.0+unknown`; the change lands by fast-forward):

  | ROCm, one MI50 | main | head | delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | IQ4_NL, six ABBA pairs | 245.03, 244.91, 245.42, 227.57, 233.29, 225.59 (mean 236.97) | 242.94, 243.95, 222.40, 231.39, 217.42, 214.75 (mean 228.81) | -3.4% |

- Further decode work: a Vulkan decode profile of the branch (the last, before the two sparse kernels, gave Q8_0 one-column rows 31 percent and MXFP4 rows 27 percent of a card's time); ROCm `mxfp4_routed16` is VALU-bound (89 percent busy, about 127 VALU an iteration of two rows).

**Gotchas:**
- Measured and not kept: a wave-uniform row base with 32-bit offsets for ROCm MXFP4 rows (gate+up 251 to 257 us), a one-step weight prefetch in ROCm's one-column Q8_0 rows (32768x1280 66 to 86 us), Vulkan's columns kernel staging p through shared memory (139 to 349 us at 16k), 1024-thread and 512-thread sparse attention blocks, q in shared memory for the ROCm scores, ROCm k_rows load unroll and four rows a cluster, and q_a with kv as one group call (ROCm's group differs from separate products at four columns).
- Scores of a sparse attention bench whose window values dwarf the entries hide the entries entirely (every output hash the same at any entry count); the bench's scales were set so both sources count.

## Drafter head split over a tensor group (2026-11-09, VKH1 to VKH4, branch perf/drafter-head-split on main e899036de; VKH1's proposal of 02:41 approved by F2DEV at 02:45 with changes 1 to 6; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** a group's draft step reads its share of the drafter's output head, not the whole 675 MB on every member, and every member still picks the id one device's `argmax_rows` gives.

**Done:**
- The drafter's `output` role shards by vocabulary rows as the target head's does (`blocks::shard` in `qwen4exp` and `qwen35`), and `blocks::draft_head` is the one head step of both modules: one device's logits and `argmax_rows`, or on a group the member's rows and `Backend::argmax_part`.
- `Model::draft_record` owns the exchange: in phase 2 each member writes (largest logit, -inf counted; its id as a float value; a NaN or +inf flag) at its slot of a row of zeros, `Collective::sum_in_place` sums 3W floats a row, and `Backend::argmax_pick` gives every member the same id: the invalid id where a flag is set or the largest is not finite, else the largest, ties to the lowest id, then the prior id's rule.
  An id is a float value, exact below 2^24 (`kExactIds`), never an integer's bits, which a device flushing denormals would lose; x+0 keeps finite values, inf and NaN, and -0 to +0 is harmless under strict >.
- `Model::draft_logits` reads a row from the members' slices into a host row at their offsets, so tests read the whole vocabulary at width 2 as before, and member 0 no longer writes R*V floats a step into host-visible memory.
- `Model::ensure` makes the group's collective for ceil(rows*3W/sum_width) rows where 3W exceeds a tiny fixture's summed row; the fit counts a member's logits of its own rows (`footprint`).
- The ROCm `llmx_argmax_part` flags a +inf largest as the CPU and Vulkan do.
- Tests: `qwen35-ops` on the CPU and `backend-vulkan`/`backend-rocm` (`qwen35_checks.hpp`) split the argmax rows into 2 to 4 slices, ties across a slice end, a half of -inf, signed zeros, -inf with a NaN, and require argmax_rows' ids with and without prior ids; `server-spec`'s injected chain failure fires in `argmax_pick` too.
- Focused runs on the rig (split builds of this tree): `qwen35-ops`, `qwen4exp-mtp` (CPU groups at widths 2 and 4), `server-spec`, `arch-qwen35`, `arch-qwen4exp`, `placement`, `backend-vulkan`, `backend-rocm`, and `qwen4exp-mtp` on Vulkan and ROCm groups of width 2 over 2 and 4 cards (1305 and 1307 checks), all rc 0.
- Timing (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8 with the Q8_0-v2 MTP head, draft-max 3, four MI50s at default clocks, `--cpus 8`, host load 17 to 30, a cardlock per cell; main and the branch built the same way, `llmx 0.1.0+unknown`):

## Lookup reads started at pass formation (2026-11-09, DSDEV64, DSDEV65 then DSDEV70, branch perf/lookup-early-reads on main 4b5f9236d; COORD's task B of 2026-11-09, the "Never wait" principle; F2DEV reviews)

**Goal:** a pass's lookup-table rows (DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's per-layer embedding) are read while the stages before their layer run, so a lookup layer's stage no longer waits for its rows; one owner, the pass, for both architectures.

**Done:**
- `Model::start_lookups` (passes.hpp) computes every lookup layer's ids as the pass is formed (`begin`) and starts its `WeightRows` read into a scratch the `Pass` owns (`Pass::lookups`), so passes in flight never share one.
  The preceding ids come from the committed tail where the token stage holds everything the pass follows, else from the tail the sequence's last formed pass leaves (`Sequence::formed_tail_`), which is what a pipelined prompt chunk needs.
- `Model::start_lookup` stays where the stage begins as the check: it computes the ids from the stage's own snapshot, keeps the early read where they match and starts the read again where they do not, and counts the read kept, restarted or late (`Model::lookup_reads`, printed by `generate --verbose` and in the health's `passes.since_start`).
- The fit counts a pass's host lookup rows and their ids once a pass in flight, the larger of `slots` and the used stages (`split_layers`); `tests/placement.cpp` holds the exact sum.
- No new reader, store, thread or flag; `finish_lookup` and the device rows buffer are unchanged.
- Tests: `arch-deepseek4 --gguf` runs 320 tokens in five passes formed ahead on two CPUs cut at layer 1 with the Engram tables read from the file: kept 10, restarted 0, late 0 and the serial slices' last row; with one early id spoiled, kept 9, restarted 1 and the same row.
- Measured on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4, ROCm int8, ten MI50s at default clocks, `--lookup-storage file` with both Engram shards on a 4K-record ZFS dataset, the 2070-token wiki prompt and 16 tokens, a process a cell, one warm cell then ABBA twice, `--cpus 8`, nr_throttled 0 to 2, every cell flagged contended by ZFS reads: pp main 410.2, 412.6, 422.7 and 373.8, the branch 424.0, 423.3, 423.5 and 423.7 tok/s (404.8 to 423.6 on the means, +4.6%; 411.4 to 423.6 on the medians, +3.0%); tg 19.82 against 19.81; greedy ids the same in every cell.
  An earlier run at main e899036de, before 4b5f9236d rewrote DeepSeek's per-token kernels and with the shards at 1M records, gave pp 80.96 and 85.36 against 90.48 and 92.39 tok/s (+9.9%).
- Byte identity against main e899036de with the tables read from the file (`--lookup-storage file`): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8 on four MI50s under ROCm, layer-4 and 2x2 at `--ubatch 64` so the prompt runs as chunks in flight, generated ids and logits rows the same; the tiny deepseek4 fixture's logits rows the same on the CPU and on rocm:0.
  Flash-Next has no CPU leg: a CPU run is one stage holding its one lookup layer (layer 1), so its read starts as that stage begins on main too, and the CPU path of `start_lookups` and `start_lookup` is held by the deepseek4 fixture's CPU leg and `arch-deepseek4 --gguf`.
- Measured on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ROCm on four MI50s at default clocks, `--lookup-storage file`, one warmed 2006-token prompt and 16 tokens, a process a cell, ABBA after a warm cell, `--cpus 8`, nr_throttled 0 to 2, every cell flagged contended by ZFS reads: 2x2 pp main 1149.8 and the branch 1148.6 tok/s over six each (-0.1%), tg 61.82 and 61.32; layer-4 pp 632.7 and 636.8 over four each (+0.6%), tg 51.32 and 51.57; every branch cell kept every early read (26 and 30, none restarted or late) and gave main's greedy ids.
  With its one lookup layer in the first stage, the early read starts about when main's does, so neutral is the expected result.
  An earlier run that fed each cell a different prompt never read before showed 2x2 at -27%; its main cells alone differed by 12%, and the same prompt warmed shows no difference.
- The same Flash-Next cells on Vulkan, two an arm after a warm cell: 2x2 pp main 726.5 and 728.0, the branch 727.6 and 736.4 tok/s (+0.6%), tg 27.26 against 26.86; layer-4 pp 847.4 and 838.0 against 848.2 and 832.1 (-0.3%), tg 26.60 against 26.31; every early read kept and greedy ids main's in each placement.

**Left:** server cells with the counters on DeepSeek-V4.1, which feat/deepseek4-serving serves (its Left). Landing gates: the stack's, in (Drafter head split over a tensor group, above); every timing cell there reads its lookup rows from file.

**Gotchas:**
- A start that throws at formation (an id the table refuses, or bad_alloc) is swallowed there and thrown again by the stage's own start, so `begin` still refuses nothing it did not refuse before.
- The formed tail is used only where the token stage (the first stage with a history layer) has not committed the pass ahead, so a split whose first stage holds the first Engram layer always takes the committed path.

## Draft price outliers (2026-11-08, MTP3, MTP4 then MTP5, branch perf/mtp-draft-price on main ed9780218; MTP2's finding of 19:24 and 19:35, F2DEV's reviews of MTP2 items 1a to 1c and of this branch at 22:26; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** every fresh MTP server drafts at the depth its measured passes give, as one drafting at the cap does (75-83 tok/s on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ROCm 2x2, one user), stable across fresh servers, within the one price owner.

**Done:**
- 1a: why a stage cell reads about a whole pass, from a print-only build (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 2x2, one user, medians from the pass's formation): at 1 row stage 0's recording begins at 0.02 ms and stage 1's at 2.35 ms, stage 1 is seen retired at 15.70 ms and stage 0 at 16.77 ms, the pass taking 15.78 ms, alike at 2 to 4 rows.
  Stage 0's ticket reads as retired only after the last stage ends, so stage 1 never sees its upstream end (`ServiceRecord::measure`) and runs from its recording start, and both cells hold about the whole pass: their sum priced 1 to 4 rows at 29.1, 40.3, 49.0 and 54.3 ms for passes of 15.8, 21.6, 26.1 and 29.1.
  `ServiceRecord::measure` now ends a stage at the time its device was held by the stage's own submissions (`Backend::busy_ms` from the device's last ticket before the stage, `Backend::last_ticket`, so the draft chain and uploads between stages are not counted) after the stage's start, or at its recording's end if later, and measures a pass's stage only after its stage before: on the same cell the cells read 8.5 to 9.3 ms (stage 0) and 7.4 to 7.8 ms (stage 1) at 1 row and 15.0 to 18.8 and 14.1 ms at 4 rows, summing to the passes of about 16 and 29 ms (`device_stage_end`).
- 1c: with the cells summing to the pass, `PassTimes::server_ms` is the table's price plus the reconciled passes' mean difference, the host's time; the line through the reconciled passes that scaled overlapping cells was dropped in review (F2DEV N3), since nothing overlaps once the stage ends at its device time.
- 1b: `PassTimes::pass` skips a width's first pass and bounds a pass at `spec::kOutlier` (2) times the known line's prediction, `reconcile` and `PriceTable::observe`'s decode cells bound a measure the same way, and `draft_depths` gives every request its cap only for an unknown line, not for a known line clamped at a slope of 0.
  A server's first pass of 487 ms had set the slope to 0 and the cap for about 280 passes.
- Chain host time (F2DEV item 2, measured only): `Model::draft_record` medians 0.64 ms recording, 1.32 ms waiting for the devices and 0.00 ms reading the ids back over 194 chains, so the wait is about two thirds.
- `sampler` passes with `outlier_passes` (first pass, stall, clamped slope) and `device_stage_end`.

- Timing (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ROCm on four MI50s at default clocks, `--cpus 8`, nr_throttled 0 to 3, a fresh server per arm in turn, greedy 256-token replies, tok/s of the runs after a warm one):

## DeepSeek-V4.1 decode speed: tables sized by the budget and the router rewritten (2026-11-08, DSDEV50 and DSDEV51, branch perf/deepseek4-router-and-tables on main c319438bc; DSDEV49's proposal of 16:55 with F2DEV's CHANGES of 16:53, items 1 to 11; lands by fast-forward as two commits)

**Goal:** the position tables and position-sized arena slots of every architecture cover the positions the KV budget reaches, sized inside the fit's search, so a prompt pass of 512 rows fits beside DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on ten MI50s; and the `sqrt_softplus` router on Vulkan and ROCm runs a workgroup a row instead of one lane, bit-identical to the one-lane kernels, which cost about 98 of the 239 ms a token on the ten-card decode.

**Done:**
- (a) `ModelPlan::table_steps` and `ModelPlan::position_slots` declare what grows with the positions; `footprint` sizes them at `covered_positions` of the candidate budget, so `fitted_kv`'s search sees them; the model sizes them at the context capped at its pool's tokens once the pool is made (`Model::positions`), and passes, drafts and images past that are refused.
  Every architecture's rope tables are declared per position (qwen3, qwen35, qwen4exp, deepseek4), and deepseek4's index scores slot at its least ratio.
  `Scheduler::request_limit` and the row classes of `Model::host_identity` read `Model::positions`, the one figure of what a request may hold.
  `arch-deepseek4` `positions` holds the fit on the tiny fork fixture: a device too small for the whole context's tables holds a budget between half and the whole with tables to match, a prompt past it is refused, and a smaller device is refused by the placement.
  `arch-qwen35-fit`'s checkpoint case now finds its room at the three quarters of the budget where the fit tries checkpoints, since the tables there are smaller than at the whole budget.
- (b) `shaders/route_sqrt_softplus.comp` and ROCm's `llmx_route_sqrt_softplus` take a workgroup a row: scores into shared memory, each pick an exact argmax over (score + bias, id), the sum in pick order on one lane.
  `ds4::check_routing` runs on `backend-vulkan` and `backend-rocm` over 1 to 600 rows, 1 to 1024 experts and k 1, 6 and 256 with ties and non-finite rows; picks may differ from the CPU's only at near ties within 1e-6 relative, since the device's exp and log round apart from libm's.
- Evidence, binaries built the same way from detached rig worktrees of main c319438bc and the branch (Vulkan image `mxxm/llmx-dev:vulkan`, ROCm `rocm-gfx906:7.2.1`), default clocks, `--cpus 8`:
  - Byte identity against main, greedy text and ids and `logits` rows: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and the tiny deepseek4 fork fixture on CPU, Vulkan and ROCm; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4 on ten MI50s on Vulkan and ROCm (256 logits rows of the excerpt, 64 chat tokens); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on four MI50s on Vulkan and ROCm (64 tokens).
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 MXFP4, ten MI50s, `--ubatch 64 --lookup-storage file`, `bench --p 64 --n 32 --r 3`, two rounds an arm, main then branch each round (tok/s):

    | backend | main pp64 | branch pp64 | main tg32 | branch tg32 |
    |---|---|---|---|---|

## MoE routed step clears its own partial rows (2026-11-08, MEGA24 and LAND8, branch perf/moe-step-clears-partial on main 24fcabf04; MEGA24's research/moe-step-clears-partial 4058a62c1, F2DEV's approval of 2026-11-08 12:25; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** remove the zero copy before every routed part of a tensor group.

**Done:**

  `Step::zero` now hands the member's zero row (kept by the runtime) to `blocks::moe_step`, which passes it as `MoeStep::zero` on a group; the CPU, Vulkan and ROCm steps already start from that row, so qwen3moe and qwen35moe keep their bits.

## Automatic KV pool built again with fewer tokens when a device's reading overstated its room (2026-11-08, WIN2 and WIN3, branch fix/vulkan-pool-headroom)

**Goal:** `llmx serve` without `--kv-tokens` starts on a card that other processes share, rather than failing with VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY on the Radeon VII under Windows.

**Done:**
- Cause, measured with a standalone allocation probe on the Radeon VII (AMD driver, Windows, a browser holding part of the card): the heap is 16.90 GB and its budget read 16.04 GB (95%) until this process's usage passed 12.9 GB, then 13.30 GB, where allocation stopped, and 16.04 GB again after freeing; the fit read the 16.04 GB once and backed a pool past the 13.3 GB the card held.
- `build_fitted` (model/place.hpp) is the one owner of building a planned model, called by `place_model` and by the loader's lookup-table path, which before built once with no retry (the `deepseek4` suite component's `serve` on vulkan:0 failed on main with an out-of-memory error for 1 MiB).
  With an automatic budget, a build that runs a device out of memory or leaves a device holding KV below `scratch_reserve(0)` is given up and the same placement built again, at most twice, with fewer KV tokens: the bytes the device's reading fell, or the reserve it was left below, in whole blocks at the KV bytes a block takes on that device (`kv_block_bytes`).
- Vulkan caps the budget by the one it stated when the heap was last full (`Device::ceiling`, noted at an out-of-memory result and at a reading within the fixed reserve), so the reading's fall survives the given-up build's free, and `sync` drops retired slots' buffers so that build frees its memory before the next reading; the loader clears its upload plan before the first build and as a build is given up, before the reading, so the weights a streamed load mode recorded are not counted in the fall.
- ROCm: `hipMemGetInfo` states other processes' memory in every reading, so it needs no ceiling and a correct reading never builds twice.
- Test first: the placement test's overstating device (3 MiB of 16 MiB hidden, failing and oversubscribing allocations, 3 MiB of weights held by its adopt hook until the placement drops them, as the streamed load modes hold theirs) fails on main and passes here.
- F2DEV's review (2026-11-08) found the given-up build's weights still held at the reading, so the fall counted them and a real 8B model was cut past zero; the hook now drops them before the reading, and an explicit `--kv-tokens` reads no device.

**Gates** (head ed0719c6a, `llmx 0.1.0+ged0719c6ab93`; the tree that lands differs by this STATUS block):
- The placement test fails on main 87a3760a3 with the test commit (the build runs out of memory) and passes here; with the reading taken before the weights were dropped it left 5.6 MB of a 3 MiB overstatement unused.
- Radeon VII, Windows, AMD driver, `serve` without `--kv-tokens` in the default load mode: Qwen3-8B Q8_0 failed on the review's head 6d7931789 (binary `g39ba70765f8f`, the same code) with "the KV budget of 41536 tokens ran a device short once built, and no smaller budget fits", and started 2 of 2 times here at 23104 KV tokens; the synthetic F32 model started 3 of 3 times (main failed with VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY).
- CTest on Windows (fresh Release build with Vulkan ON, rebased on 49fde43de) 101 of 101; on Linux with an MI50 100 of 100.
- The suite on the CPU under Windows passes, 48 components.
- Suite `--only server,deepseek4` on an MI50 under Vulkan passes; placement is held by its CTest above.
- Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 greedy, 128 tokens: the text is byte-identical between main and here on the CPU and on vulkan:0 of an MI50.
- Idle MI50 (Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, `serve` without `--kv-tokens`, two runs, built from the head): Vulkan 273664 KV tokens and ROCm 274368, as on main.
- Hosted run 42442980128 on ed0719c6a green; the head that lands, differing by this block, takes its own run on gate/vulkan-pool-headroom.
The change lands by fast-forward.

**Gotchas:** a heap's ceiling is kept for the device's life, so a Linux card that really filled and then had memory freed by another process reads the lower figure until llmx restarts.

## ROCm fused MoE step over generated rows (2026-11-07, RDEV69, branch perf/rocm-moe-rows on main 49f753824; MEGA10's finding of 2026-11-07 19:36 from research/rocm-moe-rows d5be5e828; lands by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** the fused MoE step (`RocmBackend::moe_step`, `fused_step`) takes every count of generated rows its kernels can, not one row alone, so an MTP verify step and a decode of several sequences take three launches a routed layer, each output the bits of the base's ops.
- **Done:** `fused_step` takes rows whose runs are all of extent 1 while rows * k is below the gate type's int8 grouped break-even times the experts (`TwinKernels::groups`, the rule `routed` groups by, now one function for both); from there the base reads each expert's gate and up rows once for all its entries, which outweighs the fused step's fewer launches; at Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 10 of 512 experts and Q4_K's or Q5_K's 1.25 that is up to 63 rows.
  `llmx_moe_step_route` takes each row of h on its own in the one-row order and routes the rows on its last block's four waves; `llmx_moe_step_up_<type>` takes the shared expert of each row as the first block rows; `llmx_moe_step_down_<type>` a block row a row.
  The gate+up has a lean build (shared rows a row a wave, two steps a load) and a wide one (`_w`, two rows a wave, four steps a load); `step_up_kernel` takes the wide one where the grid fits the compute units at that build's occupancy, which the device reports at the first step, and the lean one elsewhere.
  The research switches (rows, build and overlap counter) and the study's bench are not carried.
  `llmx-backend-rocm-test` `moe_rows_bits` (in `twins` and the full run): 1 to 4 rows and the last two counts below the break-even are the three fused launches with no twin launch, and at 1 row and the last with h's twin not kept the route launch makes it, and the first count past it the base's, by the launches, every output the base's bits, at 10 of 512 experts with both routed widths and at 6 of 128, both gate+up builds taken.
- **Gates** (main 49f753824 and the branch built alike from detached trees on the rig, four MI50s, renderD132-135, default clocks):
  The gates ran at 503fb370, whose src/ tree is the head's: the head differs from it only in this STATUS block, docs/TESTS.md, docs/src/backends-rocm.md and tests/backend_rocm.cpp (`moe_rows_bits`' unkept-twin arm and launch counts), so the timing, identity, CTest and suite evidence carries forward, and the test reran at the head with `twins`, `moe` and the full run passing, as did `docs` and `dead-code`.
  Builds: ROCm build of llmx, llmx-rocm and llmx-backend-rocm-test rc 0; `llmx-backend-rocm-test` full, `moe` and `twins` PASS on one MI50; CTest 84 of 84 on the ROCm build and 81 of 81 on the CPU build; the suite on rocm:0 rc 0.
  Identity against main on rocm:0, `generate` 64 greedy tokens and `logits --last 4`, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M at auto and int8: 8 of 8 files the same; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8 tg64 ids equal between main and branch on both layouts, and the MTP ids equal the plain ids.
  Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, int8, tg64 ABBA (n10 each, tok/s median, four MI50s, default clocks), against the owner's castagna-veloce gate (2026-10-25):

  Every cell stays below the castagna gate, so the speed gate is open and recorded, not met.
  Radeon VII on the stack at c64031305a1d: its `server` component fails with VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY for 8192 bytes in two runs on the shared desktop card, with Firefox holding about 4.8 GB of it, and fails identically on main 27697a85e (the auto pool fit overshoots on a shared desktop card, fixed separately on fix/vulkan-pool-headroom); COORD records the Radeon VII suite at 47 of 48, and this run covered only the `server` component, so it is not marked PASS on the Radeon VII.
