## Prefill pipeline priced a stage at a time (2026-11-08, PDEV1 to PDEV8, branch perf/prefill-pipeline rebased onto main 8e344fcbb, measured on perf/device-handoff bf5806fcb; F2DEV's review of 2026-11-07 23:39, items 1 to 9)

- **Goal:** a pipelined prompt cut by each stage's own cost, so a heavy stage sets the slices around it and the light ones are not planned as its copies.
- **Depends on:** the ROCm crossings ordered on the devices (perf/device-handoff, landed as d05eb6c2a): `busy_ms` starts a ROCm submission after those waits.
- **Done:** `Backend::busy_ms(a, b)`, the device time submissions a+1 to b held the device from their first operation after their waits on other devices, on the CPU (span from the first dispatch, write or copy to the submit), ROCm (timing ticket events and a ring of start events) and Vulkan (a timestamp pair a submission wherever the queue keeps timestamps, read without waiting).
  `run_chunks` gives each chunk's busy time a stage, its slowest device's; `SlicePeriods` fits a line a stage and band through them and calibrates the fixed costs by the prefills' wall times, each residual scaled by the cells on the plan's critical path and averaged over a true window, so the fit through departure times is gone and one planner remains.
  `prompt_cut` scores the equal cuts and then cuts growing or shrinking by a ratio (`kSliceRatios`, 0.8 to 1.2) from first slices around the best equal cut's (`kSliceSteps`, 16 a doubling), keeping the server's increment bound on each cut's first slice; `SlicePeriods::cut` plans one cut and follows it.
  Choosing only among equal cuts again for every slice, as before, ended a 96-row prompt over stages of 1.0 and 0.25 ms a row 4.4% after the best found, and a 2048-row prompt whose last stage costs twice the fixed cost 4.6% after it; the one cut reaches the best found in the first and 1459 against 1527 ms in the second.
- **Constants from the simulation** (2048 rows, 2, 3, 4 and 8 stages, a heavy first or middle stage or a light first one, 2% noise a slice, 5% of slices stalled 30 ms, handoffs of 1 and 5 ms, eight seeds of eight prefills, scored by the plan's finish at the true costs against the best cut found by search and hill-climbing):
  `kCalibrationWindow` 4 and `kCalibrationShare` 0.5: windows 2, 4, 8 and unbounded and shares 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 give means within 0.25% of each other and the same minima on every shape; learned lines reach 97.8 to 99.4% of the best found on average and 89.8 to 97.7% at worst. A stall's sample leaves the mean after the window; the share holds what one stall can move.
  `kSliceRatios` 0.8 to 1.2: ratios 0.6 to 1.5 give the same plans, learned and from the true lines (98.5 to 99.9%).
  Not covered: stalls perturb only the measures, so a plan's robustness to them is unscored; a 2048-row prompt stays in band 0; the cost has no depth term.
- **Left:** `SlicePeriods::observe` drops the wall residual of an unpriced prefill (`if (finish.empty() || !n) return;`), so a prompt whose first bands have no line never calibrates their fixed costs.
- **Item 1 of the review dropped:** the stage-ordered free of a mid-prefill slot (b55427fde) had no measured use: at matched slice counts layer-4 pp2048 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next was within 2 tok/s of main (15 slices: 1438.0 and 1438.2 against 1436.9 to 1439.9 tok/s; 14 slices: 1403.9 to 1412.6 against 1413.8), so it lands only with a workload that shows the stall it removes.
- **Tests:** `server-passes` holds `prompt_cut` against the path enumeration and the equal cuts, and `SlicePeriods`' per-stage lines and calibration; `placement`'s `pipelined_cut_follows_stage_lines` cuts a prompt over two timed CPU stages within 2% of the best cut found; `backend-group`, `backend-rocm` and `backend-vulkan` check `busy_ms` positive below wall time and a wait or the host's 50 ms left out.
  Focused results at 2c8dfa416 on the Linux MI50 machine: `server-passes` and `placement` pass; `placement` on bf5806fcb with only the test and its timed stages ends its cut at 288 ms against the best 280 and fails, the branch reaches 280.
  `busy_ms`: `backend-group` passes on the CPU; `backend-rocm` counts 5.9 ms of copies busy in 6.8 ms wall and the reader 0.032 ms behind 51.96 ms of the sender's copies; `backend-vulkan` counts 10.19 of 10.47 ms, 0.006 ms queued behind, 0.014 ms across a 50 ms host gap.
- **Measured** (tok/s, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, `--dtype int8`, pp2048 and tg128, four MI50s at default clocks, ABBA against bf5806fcb with 3 repetitions a run, host load 20 to 63; slices are the cut's count in each repetition; castagna-veloce figures as the gate):

  | cell | base runs | branch runs | base mean | branch mean | change | castagna gate |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | ROCm 2x2 pp | 1368.5 (slices 7, 9, 9), 1457.4 (4, 4, 4) | 1466.3 (5, 5, 4), 1468.9 (5, 5, 5) | 1412.9 | 1467.6 | +3.9% | 1939 |
  | ROCm layer-4 pp | 1483.5 (14, 14, 14), 1397.4 (4, 4, 4) | 1428.4 (6, 6, 6; one repetition 1177.2), 1497.8 (5, 6, 6) | 1440.4 | 1463.1 | +1.6% | 2615 |
  | Vulkan 2x2 pp | 1537.3 (4, 4, 4), 1567.4 (5, 4, 5) | 1570.5 (5, 5, 5), 1559.0 (5, 5, 5) | 1552.3 | 1564.7 | +0.8% | |
  | Vulkan layer-4 pp | 1723.7 (8, 8, 10), 1708.8 (8, 9, 9) | 1701.9 (7, 7, 7), 1715.2 (7, 7, 8) | 1716.3 | 1708.5 | -0.5% | |

## ROCm crossings ordered on the devices (2026-11-07, XDEV1, XDEV6, XDEV7, branch perf/device-handoff on main 49f75382; F2DEV's approval of 21:44 on 574c9f31; lands by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** a layer split's crossing from one ROCm device to another without the host: the receiving stage's queue waits for the sender on the devices and copies the rows itself, so the host neither waits for the sender's ticket nor writes the rows (AGENTS.md, Principles).
- **Done:** `Backend::handoff` and `Handoff` (`begin`, `sent`, `take`, `taken`, `serves`) in `backends/backend.hpp`, null by default; `RocmHandoff` in `rocm_collective.hpp` keeps the order by 64-bit counters in coherent host memory that `hipStreamWriteValue64` and `hipStreamWaitValue64` write and wait for; `Model` asks each sender's readers once at load and `send`, `receive` and `stage_waits` choose per pair, a reader of another backend keeping the host path; a pipelined prefill takes its slice times at completion, so the slicing prices see four slices where the old code saw one.
  A HIP event waited for on another device's stream held the caller until it completed, so events are not used (docs/src/backends-rocm.md).
  F2DEV's changes are taken: a count advances only after the flush that issues it returns, the host-order invariant is in the `Handoff` contract, and the first copy's cost is once a device pair, so `ensure` primes nothing.
- **Measured** (tok/s, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, `--dtype int8`, four MI50s at default clocks, ABBA twice against main 49f75382, castagna-veloce figures as the gate):

  | cell | main | branch | change | castagna gate |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2x2 pp | 1429.6 | 1450.5 | +1.5% | 1939 |
  | 2x2 tg | 57.47 | 60.86 | +5.9% | 79.5 |
  | layer-4 pp | 1404.9 | 1408.3 | +0.2% | 2615 |
  | layer-4 tg | 44.24 | 48.26 | +9.1% | 52.3 |

  The pp changes are inside the run-to-run noise.

## A ROCm group sum waits for a late peer (2026-11-08, GRP1, branch fix/group-sum-timeout on main 18792d249; SRV1's finding of 01:42; lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

- **Goal:** a request never fails because one member of a tensor group reached its sum late: SRV1 saw 2 of 6 drafts-on 2x2 cells on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL `--dtype int8` end with "gave up waiting for its peers" after the 1 s device-clock bound.
- **Done:** a witness build timed every sum's host issue per member and recorded device events around each member's sum.
  Over 32 drafts-on 2x2 cells, 24 of them beside a container keeping 2 CPUs busy, the host issued every member's sum within 20 ms of its peers', and one cell still gave up, on rocm:2 of stage 1: the late member was alive and its stream reached the sum over a second after its peer's.
  Since the host issues every member's sum together and each depends only on work issued before it, an alive peer always comes, so the serving sums no longer carry a deadline: a member waits until its peers come, a peer sets the abort word, or the host sets the collective's cancel word, read once a device-clock millisecond, which the collective sets where a member's launch of the sum throws, then turns conservative.
  The one-second bound stays in `join`'s probe alone (`kProbeTimeoutMs`), where peer writes that never become visible are what it looks for.
  Vulkan's collective waits on semaphores without a deadline, so it has no such class.
  `backend-rocm` gains a check whose peer launches 2.5 s late, which fails on main with NaN and the fault and passes here, and its dropped-launch check becomes a launch HIP refuses, cancelled within 0.5 s.
  Gates on the rig, default clocks, `--cpus 2` for builds and tests and `--cpus 8` for the timing and serve containers (`nr_throttled` 0 in every one): the fix was built and tested at 512f30544 on main 49fde43de, and the head that lands, 4317f0bad on 18792d249, differs from it by the rebase and the update of the `sixteen` check below.
  `llmx-backend-rocm-test` and the `--only server` component on `rocm:0` pass at 512f30544.
  CTest at 512f30544 failed `backend-rocm-sixteen` with a segfault in 3 of 3 runs after `backend-rocm` (main passes in 2 of 2): its hand-built kernel call lacked the kernel's new `tick` argument and its peer table the `cancel` word, so 4317f0bad passes both.
  CTest at 4317f0bad, built the same way (`--version` numerics a657d0dfb98a25d6, sha256 3f3496777e64b726), passes 84 of 84 with `backend-rocm-sixteen` after `backend-rocm` at 0.41 s; the documentation commit that lands changes no source.
  Six drafts-on 2x2 serve cells on 512f30544 beside a container keeping 2 CPUs busy, each the first after warm-up, ended with no give-up at 67.0 to 72.4 tok/s.
  Timing, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL `--dtype int8` 2x2 tg128 and Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 at `--tensor-width 2` tg128, renderD132-135, host load 14 to 27, A B C C B A twice, in tok/s:

| arm | binary `--version` numerics, sha256 | Flash-Next 2x2 | Qwen3-0.6B width 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main 49fde43de | faad78e485f17802, ede132c948ee0d86 | 63.46 | 310.3 |
| head 512f30544 | d3c5c1a035a378bc, fcda84d53cff2130 | 62.71 (-1.2%) | 310.4 (+0.0%) |
| layout control (main with an unused kernel in f32.hip) | 1042691fa95608b9, d527a47e9aceb36c | 62.00 (-2.3%) | 287.5 |

  All three were built from archives of their trees the same way (`--version` 0.1.0+unknown); the 0.6B runs vary by about 8% within an arm, and the head is inside the band the control gives on both models.
- **Left:** the device-side cause of the second-long lag of one member's stream, which the witness dump did not catch in 24 cells; the hosted run at the head that lands.

## ROCm fused linear-attention decode step (2026-11-07, RDEV64, branch perf/rocm-delta-step on main 49f75382; MEGA6 to MEGA8's study, research/rocm-megakernel-delta 09a109773, lifted into the decode loop; lands by fast-forward)
- **Goal:** a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next linear-attention layer's decode step as one ROCm launch beside one product group, bit-identical, at any layout of the model over any devices.
- **Done:** `Backend::delta_step` (`DeltaStep`) owns a linear-attention layer's step up to its output product, and qwen4exp's `linear_attention` is that call and its output product.
  Its base runs the qkv product, the gate, alpha and beta group, `causal_conv_silu`, `gated_delta_rule` and `gated_rms_norm`, the calls the layer made before, so the CPU and Vulkan backends run what they ran.
  `RocmBackend::delta_step` runs the qkv and gate products as one group only when every run has extent 1 (decode rows; rocm_backend.cpp:704-712 at d6acbfa8d), since a prompt's or a verify's rows take the tile, whose split follows the group's total outputs, so they keep the base's two products, and then `llmx_delta_step` (kernels/f32.hip) where `delta_holds` holds, the base otherwise: K and V heads multiples of 4 up to 128, V heads any multiple of the K heads, at most 8 rows a view, 64 views and 4096 (view, K head) counters, four conv taps, F32 alpha and beta (`kDeltaHead`, `kDeltaRows`, `kDeltaViews`, `kDeltaCounters`, docs/src/backends-rocm.md).
  The kernel writes the alpha and beta slots as the base does, which the study's kernel did not, so a retract's rerun reads the products' rows it saved; `exact_row` is `exact_sum` and its store, and the kernel takes `exact_sum` for alpha and beta; the study's experiment switches, its multi-block form and its V-head counters are gone.
  `llmx-backend-rocm-test delta` (`delta_step_bits`) holds every slot, both state slots and the output's twin to the base's bits at the tensor-width shards 48/16, 24/8, 12/4 and 6/2 and other head widths, 1 to 8 rows over histories 0, 1, 2 and 100, one view and three with a verify, f16 and int8, and checks which build ran.
- **Measured** (tok/s, tg64 on four MI50s at default clocks, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ABBA main, branch, branch, main, the mean of the two runs of each build; Vulkan and gate from the decode loop's step 0 on the same cards):

| layout | main 49f75382 | branch | delta % | Vulkan | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x2 | 55.33 | 60.67 | +9.7 | 53.6 | 79.5 |
| layer-4 | 43.39 | 46.19 | +6.5 | 50.5 | 52.3 |
| tensor width 4 | 54.89 | 57.87 | +5.4 | none | none |

The runs in order main, branch, branch, main were 2x2 56.43, 61.33, 60.01, 54.23, layer-4 43.04, 44.99, 47.39, 43.73 and tensor width 4 53.31, 61.03, 54.70, 56.47, each of three runs with a spread of 0.04 to 2.85.
The host's load average over the timing window was 5.9 to 30.9 (mean 15.6), with other jobs on cards outside the four timed, so the figures are one noisy round and the tensor-width-4 cell, whose branch runs differ by 6.3, is the least certain.

## ROCm decode loop (2026-11-06, RDEV42, branch perf/rocm-decode-loop rebased onto main b8d18801c; the owner's fast loop for ROCm decode, reviewed and gated once at each batch's end; lands by fast-forward)
- **Goal:** ROCm decode of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8 over four MI50s toward Vulkan's, a profiled bottleneck at a time, each fix bit-identical: the replay (F2DEV's review re:rocm replay, 15:37), the twin keep, then the kernel levers.
- **Done:** fix 1, the host-to-host copy. On 2x2 the head's member logits sit in host-visible memory and are copied into the rows every member wraps; HIP makes any copy between two host memories on the host once the stream has drained, behind a 50 ms kernel 50.1 ms in every form of the call (kinds Default, HostToHost, DeviceToDevice, host or device pointers), while a copy from device memory into the same pages took 0.01 to 0.04 ms and neither 8000 queued kernels nor 2000 queued copies ever held a call 1 ms. `RocmBackend::copy` now copies between two host memories with `llmx_copy` on the stream, so the bytes are the same and the host does not wait.
  Steps 1 and 3 of the replay: every launch, copy and zero fill is held in the backend's record and issued in order every `dispatch_chunk` held operations (the profile's 64 until the cadence is measured; a submission opened with nothing running issues its first 8 at once, warm 2x2 tg64 medians 57.2 / 55.2 against 54.7 / 54.2 without it), at every submission and before a host wait that could cover held work; a tensor group flushes all its members before each sum and once its launches are held; a ring wrap submits only into a slot read since the last submission, so a stage's chunks follow its operations alone.
  The twin keep (F2DEV's review re:rocm stream ops, 15:49): two twin slots, the newer first, a new twin taking the slot not holding the newer and a twin read becoming the newer; `forget_written` the one owner of forgetting them, copies and the producers through `launch_writing`; `group_rms_norm` four values a thread where its operands lie on 16 bytes, one a thread at any other offset, the same bits.
  The hyper-connection mix (fix 2) is one `Backend::hyper_mix` call, which ROCm runs for a decode row over 8-bit activations as one persistent launch, `llmx_hc_mix`, with grid barriers behind a residency gate; its barrier counters sit at offset 0 of its scratch, so a launch on scratch a wider mix used reads zeros there, and its residency query sets its device first, since HIP finds the module's function through the calling thread's device (without it, a layer split's first decode token segfaulted inside HIP).
  The fused MoE step (from the megakernel study, research/rocm-megakernel cd05bd275): `RocmBackend::moe_step` launches `llmx_moe_step_route`, `llmx_moe_step_up_<type>` and `llmx_moe_step_down_<type>` directly where `fused_step` holds, three launches a step instead of 13, every output the base's bits (`llmx-backend-rocm-test twins`, `moe_step_bits`); the study measured 2x2 tg64 47.4 -> 52.6 tok/s and layer-4 38.4 -> 43.0 on Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8.
- **Measured** (tok/s, tg64 on four MI50s, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL int8, ABBA main, branch, branch, main, the mean of the two runs of each build, ids equal to main's; Vulkan and gate from the loop's step 0 on the same cards):

| tok/s | before (main b8d18801c) | after (branch ded11218f) | Vulkan | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x2 | 43.88 | 56.78 | 53.6 | 79.5 |
| layer-4 | 36.48 | 44.44 | 50.5 | 52.3 |

- **Gates** (2026-11-07, tree ded11218f, both arms built the same way from clean clones in the ROCm 7.2.1 image, branch `llmx 0.1.0+gded11218f98c`, main `llmx 0.1.0+gb8d18801ce45`): ROCm and CPU-only builds rc 0 (a "errors 1" from grepping the build log is `system_error` in a GCC warning about `tests/weight_rows.cpp`, not a compile error); `llmx-backend-rocm-test` twins and the full run pass, with `moe_step_bits` on its five shapes; CTest 84 of 84 on the ROCm build and 81 of 81 on the CPU build; `docs` and `dead-code` pass.
  Byte identity against main: Flash-Next on four MI50s, greedy ids and logits the same on 2x2 and layer-4; on the CPU (`--load-mode mapped`) Flash-Next 16 greedy tokens equal on both arms.
  The device suite (`--device rocm:0`) and the Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 CPU identity are carried forward from a4bc8650a, whose delta to ded11218f is F2DEV's five review changes (the fused step's down-type and ff condition, `h` in host memory refused and its twin kept, the step's limits 512 experts, 10 picks, 2560 in and 640 ff, the `moe_step_bits` shapes, and rocm_backend.cpp stored with LF), none of which reaches the device suite's components or the 0.6B CPU path.
  Timing: the runs of each build per placement are in the table's means (2x2 main 43.07 and 44.69, branch 56.30 and 57.25; layer-4 main 36.53 and 36.42, branch 43.63 and 45.24, three runs each); the host load average (1 minute) peaked at 28.4 during the rounds, recorded every 20 s beside the runs.
  The branch lands by fast-forward.
- **Left:** the cadence sweep and the twin trace (twin8 calls a token at 0 on both placements); step 2 (HIP graphs, with the server guard); the kernel levers; the between-token idle.

## DeepSeek-V4.1 on the devices: steps 8, 9a and 9b (2026-11-06, DSDEV40, DSDEV41 then DSDEV42, branch feat/deepseek4-devices on feat/deepseek4-cpu 2e8a1e6fe; steps 8 to 9b of docs/DEEPSEEK4.md, built as a batch with one review at its end)
- **Goal:** DeepSeek-V4.1's layer ops on Vulkan (step 8) and on ROCm (step 9b), and MXFP4 weights on ROCm (step 9a), each held to the CPU, so the tiny deepseek41 model runs on one MI50 under either backend.

## ROCm decode one-row exact products (2026-11-06, RDEV35, branch perf/rocm-decode-f32 stacked on perf/rocm-decode 81bc6bb3f, now on main e30a8cba9; RDEV35's proposal re:rocm decode f32 approved by F2DEV at 08:24 with three changes; gates scored by RDEV38; lands by fast-forward)
- **Goal:** the one-row exact products on ROCm at the weights' bandwidth with the bits of the block-an-output kernel they replace, the largest kernel cost left in Flash-Next decode.
- **Finding (kernel trace, Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, four MI50s, int8, pp16 and 64 one-row passes, base 81bc6bb3f):** per card and token on 2x2, router F32 2560->512 24 x 53.4 us, hc inject F32 10240->4 48 x 20.7, ssm_alpha/beta F32 2560->24 36 x 7.6, shexp gate F32 2560->1 24 x 7.5, indexer BF16 2560->512 6 x 53.7 and 2560->128 6 x 7.4: 3.09 ms a card; layer-4 1.63 ms a card. The block-an-output kernel waited on every load of a lane's chain (vmcnt(0) before each fmaf), so a 2560-wide row took 10 memory round trips and a 10240-wide one 40.
- **Done:** `exact_wave` in `kernels/f32.hip`, one body for `llmx_matmul_<type>` and the routed F32 class's `llmx_routed_<type>`: a wave an output, lane t holding the block kernel's chains J t to J t + J - 1 (J = 256 / warpSize) in the same unit order, block_sum's pairs folded by shuffles from level 128 to J and in registers below it; F32 and BF16 rows load four weights a step where aligned, a batch of steps issuing its loads before its products behind a scheduling barrier; `exact` and the `part` bodies are gone. `exact_rows` holds it to the blocked build at widths 100, 2560, 2561 and 10240, and `moe` the routed entries to the dense one-row product, bit for bit.
- **Batch:** 64 bytes of a lane's weights a batch (`kBatchBytes`; F32 4 steps, BF16 8 on gfx906), then halving batches. `rates exact` under the kernel trace, median GPU us, batch of 2 / 4 / 8 F32 steps: router 2560x512 10.7 / 11.2 / 19.0, one block (10240x4, 2560x1) 8.3 / 6.2 / 6.4, the 24-output shapes 8.7 / 6.8 / 6.7; base 55.2, 10.7 and 11.2. BF16 2560x512 at 8 steps 7.8 against 53.9.
- **Registers (both code objects, scratch 0 in every exact build):** gfx906 F32 51 VGPRs, BF16 80, Q8_0 35, Q4_K 44, routed F32 49; gfx1151 (J = 8, F32 2 and BF16 4 steps a batch) F32 49, BF16 82, Q4_K 145. An unrolled scalar chain had taken Q4_K to 248 VGPRs and 140 bytes of scratch on gfx906, so the scalar steps are not unrolled.
- **In the model (same trace, renderD133-136, base retraced there):** one-row exact products a card and token, base / branch: 2x2 3.10 / 1.21 ms (router 1279 / 310 us, the one-block inject and gate 1190 / 613, 2560->24 272 / 206, BF16 362 / 93), layer-4 1.59 / 0.63 ms. The one-block calls stay latency, a 10240-wide row's 40 steps in 10 batches from cold memory (8.5 us a call); splitting a chain over more waves would change the sum.
- **Gates (fresh ROCm builds from detached worktrees, base e30a8cba9 `llmx 0.1.0+ge30a8cba951b` against the branch's code at f09d771d4 `0.1.0+gf09d771d48dc`, MI50s at default clocks, the machine monitored throughout, other jobs on other cards):**
  Byte identity against e30a8cba9: all 68 cells equal by `cmp`, each file without its timing lines: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on the CPU at 1 and 4 threads, greedy and logits; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M on one card at `--dtype` auto, int8 and f32, greedy, seeded, logits batched and per token and perplexity batched and per token; Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL layer-4 and 2x2 at int8 and auto (greedy, logits and perplexity, batched and per token) and at f32 (logits and perplexity, batched and per token), where every product of every type takes the changed kernel.
  The base ran on renderD128-131 and the branch on renderD133-136, all MI50s.
  The HF cells are unchanged, since every output is the base's bits.
  CTest ROCm 82/82; `llmx-backend-rocm-test` types, moe, twins, qwen35 and attention PASS; device suite on rocm:0 every component PASS or SKIP but docs (the comment below), reference-generator and raw-blocks, the last two failing because the ROCm image lacks numpy, which `--require-tools` asks for (reference-generator's read-back of the tiny deepseek41 files, raw-blocks' numpy form), raw-blocks passing in a numpy image; docs and dead-code PASS once the `exact_rows` comment was cut to two sentences, which the docs check had found a wall.
  Timing round base, branch, branch, base (base 81bc6bb3f, the code of e30a8cba9), Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on renderD133-136, `bench --p 512 --n 64 --r 5 --ubatch 512`, tok/s as the mean of the two runs a side:

  | cell | base tg64 | branch tg64 | change | base pp512 | branch pp512 | change |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | layer-4 int8 | 31.50 | 36.42 | +15.6% | 966 | 938 | -2.9% |
  | layer-4 auto | 29.32 | 34.23 | +16.7% | 827 | 786 | -4.9% |
  | 2x2 int8 | 35.27 | 39.58 | +12.2% | 1078 | 1082 | +0.4% |
  | 2x2 auto | 34.59 | 39.09 | +13.0% | 897 | 898 | +0.1% |

  tg64 runs base / branch / branch / base: layer-4 int8 31.54 / 36.38 / 36.47 / 31.47, layer-4 auto 29.41 / 34.27 / 34.19 / 29.24, 2x2 int8 36.11 / 40.53 / 38.63 / 34.43, 2x2 auto 33.76 / 38.50 / 39.67 / 35.43.
  A prompt reaches the changed kernel only in a call of one row (`nbatch > 1` takes `llmx_matmul_rows_<type>`), so the pp512 cells measure no change of their kernels: on layer-4 int8 the two base runs alone differ by 6.1% (996 / 936), the branch level with the second at 935 and 942, and on layer-4 auto the branch's first run holds one slow repetition (573 tok/s), its per-repetition median 821 against the base's 837 (-1.9%).
- **Left:** F2DEV's review and the landing.
- **Gotchas:** without the scheduling barrier the scheduler sinks each load to its fmaf and the batch buys nothing (ISA read with `asm.sh` on the rig); 128 bytes of weights in flight a lane over 512 waves made the router slower than unbatched loads.

  The group sum, remeasured on the traces after step 1 (2x2 int8 ub320, 1201 sums a card, one clock): the later starter's time is 161 us a sum on rocm:0+1 and 263 on rocm:2+3 (181 and 165 before), and the start skew grew from 574 and 918 ms to 913 and 848 ms, rocm:0 and rocm:2 now the earlier in 1131 and 1154 of 1201, so with the exact products gone the first card of each pair waits for its partner's heavier rest; that lateness is the collective's and the split's to remove, not this branch's.
- **Left:** on ROCm a pass's end is seen up to a period late (the last stage's record ends come in pairs, found by the landed fix/prompt-slicing), which the scheduler's retirement and time to first token pay too; whether the device or the HIP runtime holds it is not told apart.
  No hosted runner has a ROCm device, so the ROCm checks are the rig's hand checks above.
- **Gotchas:** the exact rows build needs `__launch_bounds__`: without it the compiler capped it at 64 VGPRs and spilled, and it ran no faster than the one-row kernel.
  On ROCm the pipelined slicing varies run to run (one branch run of 2x2 auto ub512 took 225 slices at 217 tok/s, where its other nine took 4 to 42 at 632 to 1182); the chooser is the runtime's (`model/slicing.hpp`), its fix the landed pipelined prompt slicing (fix/prompt-slicing), not this branch's, and the rates above are read beside their slices for that reason.
  The delta rule's 96 workgroups a call (65 against Vulkan's 45 ms a card) is recorded as a finding for perf/rocm-decode.

## DeepSeek-V4.1 steps 4-7: the module opened and run on the CPU (2026-11-05 to 2026-11-06, DSDEV10 to DSDEV39, branch feat/deepseek4-cpu on main 5a8c5676c; steps 4 to 7 of docs/DEEPSEEK4.md, DSDEV10's proposal of 15:49 and DSDEV12's of 20:14 approved by F2DEV with the changes recorded below, all taken; lands by fast-forward as two commits, the runtime and then the module)

**Goal:** `src/model/arch/deepseek4.hpp` reads a `deepseek41` file's configuration, refuses every key, value and tensor it does not read by name, plans the fork layout's tensors and its per-layer place among the shared caches, and refuses the architecture by name as the plan's last check until step 7 runs the math (docs/ADDING-AN-ARCHITECTURE.md, order of the work, step 3).

**Done:**
- The module, namespace `deepseek4`, and the registry line `{"deepseek41", deepseek4::open_v41, backend::Dtype::bf16}` with no `normalize_drafter`; the page docs/src/model-arch-deepseek4.md. arch-boundary holds `deepseek41` to the module and the registry.
- Layouts by key: `engram.layer_ids` is the fork's; upstream's `ple.layers` is refused as "inference: unsupported metadata deepseek41.ple.layers", a file holding both by a text naming both, and one with neither as missing `deepseek41.engram.layer_ids`; the last refusal is "inference: unsupported architecture deepseek41, whose math is not implemented yet".
- Change 1, one `check_config` every reader calls: the source rules of model.py at 1bae0e10 (a compressed layer's KV source at or before it at its ratio, every KV source an index source, the candidate source an index source whose later index sources share its ratio, a positive block size and count with a source, ascending distinct ids inside the block count, no source without a ratio), Engram's lengths, offsets, table rows, pad id and token map range, and the allocation bounds; the plan carries the per-layer table (`layer_table`), held on the tiny file to F2DEV's eight rows.
  `attention.compress_ratios` takes a tail of zeros of any length past the blocks: the 1017 file's first shard header, read again with `llmx info` on 2026-11-05 at 19:03 rig time (headers only, under the provenance of docs/DEEPSEEK4.md, as DSDEV10's read at 15:5x was), holds 43 entries for 40 blocks and no key counting DSpark's stages among its 74 entries (53 of them `deepseek41.*`).
- Change 2, the role kinds `role_fits` takes: sinks, the router's bias and the hyper-connection bases and scales are norm roles and the mixes tables; `engram_embed` gathered with `Lookup{engram_embed, 24}` (6 on the tiny file), `engram_wkv` one matrix until step 5, `engram_q` and `engram_k` matrix roles; every layer `Cache::none` with no token history, so the footprint of step 4 counts no cache; the residual `hyper_connection.count` x `embedding_length` with `embed_copies` the stream count, `context_length` from the file, two rope tables of context x rotary width and the ones table, slot 0 alone, whose other widths the math sets in step 7; steps 5 to 7 give every layer its entries and move the refusal to the first pass (below).
  The two rope tables are model.py's: the window layers' at `rope.freq_base` without YaRN and the compressed layers' YaRN rope at `attention.compress_rope_freq_base` (model.py:681-690 at e5decd76); their values are step 6's.

## Live health item's first-token time (2026-11-06, FIXDEV1, branch fix/health-first-token on main 2e8a1e6f, tests and docs only; lands by fast-forward on 2e8a1e6f)

- **Goal:** the `server` component stops failing on a fast machine: hosted macOS run 42230254764 read a live item with `published_tokens` 4 and `first_token_ms` 0.
- **Done:** the test was wrong and the server right: `first_token_ms` is in whole milliseconds (`src/server/scheduler.hpp`), so a first token under 1 ms reads 0 while tokens are published.
  `tests/server.py` now requires 0 only before a token is published and no longer requires the first-token time of a replying item to be above 0; docs/USAGE.md says the field is in whole milliseconds.
  No failing-test-first commit: a first token under 1 ms cannot be made deterministically through a live server, so the branch is one commit.
  Gates: CTest 81 of 81 and the suite's `docs`, `dead-code` and `server` components on the CPU in a container of 2 CPUs on the rig, the real-model pass skipped for want of its fixture, and the hosted run at the head that lands.
- **Left:** nothing; F2DEV approved at 20:49 with this entry as the one change.

## The quick newcomer's long-prompt bound follows the chunk search (2026-11-05, PDEV17 then PDEV18, branch fix/server-passes-newcomer on main 1df72137d, tests only; lands by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** `server-passes-cpu`'s `short_newcomer` holds on any machine: on a slow hosted runner (run 41965354179, job 127040987113, a shader-only branch) and once under TSan a pass between two steps of a reply held 96 prompt rows beside the quick newcomer, against the bound of its whole 85-token prompt.
- **Done:** the 96 rows were the long prompt's, not the newcomer's: its due chunk beside the unmet objective is the price search's (`PriceTable::chunk_rows`), and since a slice alone pays a 70 ms stage past the 62.5 ms chunk budget, only the newcomer's rides, priced as the pass less the replies' price, can be within it.
  The test machine reads rides of 16, 32 and 37 beside the long prompt too; what follows the machine is which of them are priced, since a ride is recorded only where its pass outlasts the replies' price.
  Where all three are priced at both stages, the 16-row ride's remainder overwrites that cell's alone measure as its last, cells of 16, 32 and 48 are within, and the search's next probe is twice 48, 96, the figure the hosted runner gave; on the test machine the 16-row cell keeps its alone measure and the due chunk is 16.
  The check now holds the long prompt's rows in each pass between two steps of a reply to what the search can give it then, a step or twice the largest slice the newcomer has read in steps, at most 192, still far below the ubatch or the 241-row and larger cuts it reads alone once the replies end; the newcomer's own rows need no bound.
  No failing-test-first commit: ten runs on the test machine at 2, 1 and 0.25 CPUs and beside busy loops all read the same table, and forcing the other one needs a hook into the scheduler's price table, which the product has none of.
  Gates: CTest `server-passes-cpu` on the CPU (Linux and Windows), `docs` and `dead-code`, and the hosted run at the head that lands.
- **Left:** nothing; F2DEV approved at 11:04 with one change, the Done text's account of which rides the test machine reads, made.

## Pipelined slicings test made deterministic (2026-11-05, PDEV16 then PDEV17, branch fix/placement-slicings on main bc1a58efa; lands by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** `placement`'s `pipelined_slicings_match` passes on any machine: on the hosted windows-2022 runner (run 41948650911) it failed "the pipelined prompt was read in one slicing only", since whether its priced prefills chose another slicing than the first followed the periods that machine measured.
- **Done:** each split's check now opens with a second fresh split read at ubatch 5, and a fresh split's first prompt must take the cut without prices exactly, five slices at ubatch 3 and three at 5, so two slicings are checked whatever the timing, and the priced prefills that follow are still each held exact to one backend.
  No product hook: the cut without prices is the slicing owner's own rule for a model that has measured nothing (`infer::prompt_slice`).
  The failure cannot be forced before the fix without a hook into `Model`'s measured periods, which the product has none of; it needs every priced prefill to choose the unpriced cut of ubatch 3.
  Gates, all passing: CTest `placement` three times on Windows (MSVC, fresh build directory) and four on Linux, 1150 checks, `docs` and `dead-code`, and the hosted run at the head that lands.
- **Left:** nothing; F2DEV approved at 08:03 with one change, the leftover check of two slicings removed, since the fresh cuts now hold it.

## Routed narrow tile: column quads past a run's entries skipped (2026-11-04, KDEV4, branch kdev/routed-quads on main 2c463d721, rebased onto a3cb5d0a7 and a359b94e3, B2 of KDEV's castagna gap kernels, proposal of 20:40 approved by F2DEV at 20:47 with changes and to land at 21:31; lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL prompts at 2x2 int8 faster with the same bits: at a 320-row chunk an expert averages about six entries, so the 16-column narrow tile computed mostly empty columns (main 091a4cc6b --profile, per card a chunk: routed gate+up 39.5 ms and down 19.9 ms, against 22.2 and 13.3 for the reference).
**Done:** `matmul_tile_q.comp`'s narrow build gives each 64 threads one column quad over every row (rows lane and lane + 64), rotated by workgroup since wave w of a workgroup runs on SIMD w, and a quad holding no entry of the run skips its dots; the narrow decision, its runs and the profile are unchanged, and every output keeps its integer block sums, float terms and block order.
Tests: `check_routed_quads` (explicit counts on every quad edge and an empty expert, each entry against itself alone, every type the narrow build takes in int8 and f16), the tensor-width-2 routed shapes and the tile's driver statistics in the occupancy report, a hash of `check_routed_narrow`'s entries, and the `--routed` mode.
Step 0, one MI50 under RADV, `--routed` in the order a b c e d d e c b a twice, median of 4, ms (a main with the test, b the change, c rows at stride MROWS, e without the rotation, d an 8-column bound):

| shape (512 experts, 10 a row, picks over every expert) | a | b | c | e | d |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q4_K int8, 2560 into two 320-row projections, 320 rows | 2.310 | 1.982 (-14.2%) | 1.991 | 2.205 | 1.889 |
| Q5_1 int8, 160 into 2560, 320 rows | 1.296 | 1.211 (-6.6%) | 1.227 | 1.278 | 1.100 |
| Q4_K / Q5_1 f16, 320 rows | 4.034 / 2.250 | 3.479 / 2.122 | 3.431 / 2.114 | 3.655 / 2.181 | 3.417 / 1.982 |
| Q4_K / Q5_1 int8, 1024 rows | 4.539 / 1.408 | 4.314 / 1.345 | 4.375 / 1.388 | 4.431 / 1.400 | 5.487 / 1.688 |
| filled tiles (picks over 80 experts), every shape, against a | - | -3% to +4% | -3% to +3% | -4% to +2% | 0% to +67% |

The rotation carries the gain (without it a third remains), the row stride does not; the 8-column bound gains more at six an expert but loses up to 67% where tiles fill. Driver statistics: the int8 narrow builds keep 64 VGPRs and 4 waves a SIMD, the f16 ones go from 104 and 96 to 108 and 100 VGPRs at 2 waves in both.
Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL pp2048 ub320 2x2 int8 (renderD129/130/134/135, a b b a, `--r 3`): main with the test (`llmx 0.1.0+g263ba45757fb`) 1470.96 and 1471.86, the change (`llmx 0.1.0+g25494aa1beb8`) 1508.84 and 1506.08 tok/s, +2.5%; decode never takes the tile.
Machine activity: load average 11 to 36 from others' work, recorded at each run's edges only, with no per-process monitor, a limitation of this measurement.
The rule set at 20:40 (-15% on both routed shapes at 320 rows) is missed on the down and by 0.8 points on the gate+up; it lands on the measured end-to-end gain, and the recovery work is a 64-row narrow build (MROWS 1, where `qtile` now forces `kTileRowsTall`), which shortens a workgroup's path rather than relying on co-resident waves.
Gates at 2607288b8 on main 2c463d721, the head that lands differing from it only by two shortened test comments: `llmx-backend-vulkan-test` whole on an MI50 under RADV rc 0; CTest 97/97; the suite's `dead-code` PASS and `docs` PASS after the comments were shortened; Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 byte identity against main (renderD129/130/134/135, tensor width 2, layer shares 1,1, ubatch 320, a 1660-token prompt), main `llmx 0.1.0+g2c463d7218cb` against the change `llmx 0.1.0+g2607288b856d`: the last 4 logits rows identical in int8 and in f16, and 64 greedy tokens identical in both, only the timing and load lines differing.
The Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver builds it and `--isa` gives rc 0, stating that the device takes the float tile and so has no narrow routed build; the hosted run on gate/kdev4-routed-quads at 3cd4a4e7e on main 2c463d721 was green in all 8 jobs (41917287640).
Rebased onto a3cb5d0a7 (pipelined prompts) without a conflict in code, the build and CTest ran again at that head, and onto a359b94e3, which touches no `src/` file, with the hosted run at the head that lands.
It lands by fast-forward as two commits, the test and the change.
**Gotchas:** on the MI50 under RADV int8 routed calls never take the 64-column build (`qtile_narrow_per_expert_8bit` is every count), so `check_routed_narrow`'s int8 cells compare the narrow build with itself; its entries hash holds a build to main's.
The narrow decision (`routed_call`) follows the call's average entries over the experts it can touch, so a run's build follows its neighbours, safe only because both builds give the same bits; ROCm's narrow build chooses per group and puts the entries lane-minor, so its mirror (RDEV) puts them on the wave-uniform axis in quads, rotated, as here.

## Server startup order under a mapped load (2026-11-05, PDEV16 then PDEV17, branch fix/server-mapped on fix/placement-slicings c7246fb5c on main bc1a58efa; lands by fast-forward after it)

- **Goal:** the `server` component passes under `--load-mode mapped`, where it failed on main every run (RDEV21's finding): its startup check expected `weights` after `allocate`.
- **Done:** the test was wrong and the server right: a mapped load warms its weights before the model is fitted and built, since the model adopts each weight as it resolves it (`src/inference/load.hpp`), and docs/SERVER.md already said they come before `allocate`.
  The check now expects devices, metadata, weights, fit, allocate and ready under a mapped load and the weights after `allocate` otherwise, and reads the weights phase by its name; docs/SERVER.md adds that the warm also comes before `fit` for a model without lookup tables.
  The failing test is main's own, so the branch is one commit.
  Gates, all passing: `python tests/run_tests.py --only server` in the auto, mapped and direct load modes on the CPU and on one MI50 (`--device vulkan:0`) of a Vulkan build, the real-model pass skipped for want of its fixture, `docs` and `dead-code`, and the hosted run at the head that lands.
- **Left:** nothing; F2DEV approved at 08:03.

## ROCm weight types for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (2026-11-04, RDEV2 to RDEV7, branch feat/rocm-types on main 091a4cc6b, main since 840b96ec7, rebased at landing; RDEV's proposal re:rocm flash-next of 08:36 with its amendment, approved by F2DEV at 08:39 with seven changes)
Goal: steps 0 to 3 of the ROCm Flash-Next plan (docs/ROCM.md, Flash-Next on ROCm, plan of 2026-11-04), landing A: a ROCm layer split checked against one card, the 2x2 memory fit settled, the weight types Flash-Next and its drafter read, the qwen35 layer ops and the routed experts on the ROCm backend for every caller.
Done, step 0: passed (Qwen3-8B Q8_0, MI50s under ROCm 7.2.1, wiki excerpt, 8 decode steps, ubatch 64, f16 cache): `llmx-split-check`, which takes named devices (`rocm:1`), over rocm:0,1 and rocm:0..3, `--dtype` auto and int8, bit-identical to one card, passes in flight included.
Per-card fit: hipMemGetInfo gives 31.949 of 31.984 GiB free on each of the four cards, the figure the Vulkan fit of production's 2x2 placement reads (pair A 19.90 GiB weights, 6.00 cache, 3.37 activations and scratch; pair B with the head and the MTP drafter 21.75, 6.86, 3.37), so the shared fit places Flash-Next on ROCm as it does on Vulkan, with the IQ4_NL lookup table (26.8 GiB) on the host.
Done, step 1: `kernels/quant.h` reads every ROCm block layout, its sizes and the IQ4_NL grid from `src/quant/types.hpp`; the descriptor table `kTypes` in `rocm_backend.cpp` (exact product, embedding, routed exact product, twins) is `supports_type`; Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_0, Q5_1, BF16 and IQ4_NL run exactly into F32 sums; all but BF16 have twins (16- and 8-bit row builds of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 columns, a 64 by 64 tile), BF16 keeping the exact kernel in every class; `rocm_take_launches` names the kernels a call launched.

ROCm is faster or level at 1 and 16 columns and 1.1 to 2.3 times slower at 64, where its row builds stop at 16 columns and a call takes four launches; step 8 owns that.
Step 3 written: `route_experts` (a row a block of 64, one reduction tree through shared memory, Vulkan's order), `matmul_experts` and `matmul_experts_add` with each entry through its type's one-column body over its expert's rows (`llmx_routed_<type>` exact, `routed16`, `routed8`, `routed_half8` on the twins), the down slots joined in slot order by `llmx_moe_combine`, and the base `moe_step`; `llmx-backend-rocm-test moe` holds them (docs/src/backends-rocm.md) and passes on an MI50 (renderD130); its first run found the down sum one F32 unit off where HIP contracted the slot's product into the add, which `__fmul_rn` does not stop; every ROCm kernel now compiles with `-ffp-contract=off` (F2DEV's change 1 of 13:02) and writes a fused multiply-add as `fmaf`, the `_rn` intrinsics replaced by plain operators.
The rule (F2DEV, 13:46): a kernel's order (op boundaries, tiles, splits, merges) follows the Vulkan design and every multiply-add accumulation is written as `fmaf`, attention's online softmax sums, the per-row score dot and the merges' `L` and `A` among them; the flag makes the bits hold between ROCm's own builds, and across backends ROCm is held to the CPU's bound and HF. The per-row attention's pinned bits are now 0x6dd90927b3b484a2 / 0x2abdc799a2845129, neither the contracted build's old pins nor the unfused ones, so the old contracted build did not fuse exactly these sites.
Attention rates (`rates`, one MI50, renderD130, b a a b, 9c03e938a's kernels against the fmaf head, us): per row after 4096 tokens 93.9 / 93.1 against 101.9 / 92.7, 16 rows 757.8 / 761.8 against 766.0 / 765.6, after 16000 tokens 267.2 / 270.4 against 268.6 / 268.5; the tile over 512 rows 477.0 / 475.1 against 489.0 / 482.1, after 4096 tokens 6043.6 / 6040.7 against 6043.9 / 6065.6; the per-row cells are back within noise of 9c03e938a (they were 1.5-3% slower unfused).

Routed rates (`rates`, one MI50, renderD130, 512 experts 10 a token, gate and up 2560x640 together and down 640x2560, the grouping's launch included, medians of five interleaved, two runs agreeing within 1%; grouped over one-column): Q8_0 f16 0.83 / 0.81 / 0.80 / 0.78 / 0.72 / 0.65 / 0.56 / 0.20 at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 rows / a 512-row prompt, int8 0.56 / 0.54 / 0.53 / 0.51 / 0.47 / 0.42 / 0.36 / 0.10 (down alike, 0.46 to 0.07 in int8); Q4_K 0.96 / 0.99 / 1.01 / 0.99 / 0.93 / 0.84 / 0.72 / 0.41 f16 and 0.96 / 0.99 / 1.00 / 0.99 / 0.92 / 0.83 / 0.72 / 0.30 int8; Q6_K f16 1.05 / 1.06 / 1.07 / 1.03 / 0.96 / 0.86 / 0.75 / 0.39, int8 0.96 / 0.97 / 0.98 / 0.96 / 0.89 / 0.80 / 0.69 / 0.37.
The crossover is one break-even a routed build (type by activation width), `TwinKernels::group_from` beside the build table in `rocm_backend.cpp`: a call groups from that many entries an expert on average (entries >= ratio * n_expert), measured on gfx906 at Flash-Next's shapes only.
`rates routed` measures it: every twin type's one-column build (a routing of 1025 experts, past the grouping's 1024, over the same ids and weights) against the build the call takes at 1 to 64 generated rows, and each build's break-even, where gate and up and the down together (where the type fills both) win or are level within 1% at every larger count; where an entry is nonzero the build the call takes is the one-column build itself and the tool prints "unmeasured here", so a nonzero entry is re-derived by building with it at 0.
On one MI50 (renderD130, 0a0a17f4f's tree with every entry at 0, at 1-64 rows, medians of five interleaved; a build of the next tree ran pinned to other cores meanwhile) it is 0 for Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_0 and Q5_1 in both widths, Q6_K int8 and IQ4_NL (IQ4_NL int8's gate and up lose 0.6 to 2.6% at 1 to 8 rows and its down wins 11%, 5% together at 4 rows); Q5_K, measured here first, loses 10 to 15% in block-int16 to 16 rows (1.04 there, wins from 32), 1.3 to 2.6% in block-int8 to 4 rows (level at 8), so 1/2 and 1/8, between the last losing count and the first winning one; Q6_K block-int16 keeps 1/4 (1.03 at 8 rows, 0.97 at 16).
`rocm_set_group_from` is gone; the moe check keeps the one-column build below a nonzero break-even through Q6_K block-int16 at 4 rows of 300 experts, and passes on an MI50.
The tiny MoE fixture passes on rocm:0 (`run_tests.py --only moe --device rocm:0`, renderD129, CPU-expert and streamed placements included): F32 logits at most 7.5e-7 from HF against the 2e-5 bound and NLL 4e-8 against 1e-5; the Q8_0 gated model at most 2.24e-4 against 0.127, every greedy id HF's.
Closed by ROCm routed decode (2026-11-05, below): the one-column routed builds' deficit against g2 at one entry an expert was the routed call's copy in scratch, which every routed and grouped build kept and the dense rows did not; without it the Q8_0 one-column routed build is level with g2 in block-int8 and faster in block-int16, and every type's break-even is measured again there.
Routed prompt tile: a prompt's routed rows from its build's tile extent group by expert through `llmx_moe_group` in groups of up to 64 entries, each group a block row of the type's routed tile (`llmx_<type>_routed_tile16` and `_tile8`, the prompt tile's 64 by 64 design over its expert's rows, never split, each entry's blocks summed in order), Vulkan's routed_call tile branch; `experts_tile` in `llmx-backend-rocm-test moe` holds every twin type in both widths and both roles: the grouping and the tile's two builds alone launched from the role's extent (both builds launch on every tiled call, so the launches cannot show which ran a group), the row builds one row below it, the two extents different row classes, for gate and up (an up of 200 outputs, a partial output tile) each entry the same bits at extents 2T and T and beside generated rows, the generated rows their one-column bits, unwritten entries, and every seventh entry within (blocks + 8) F32 epsilons of the sum of |w*x| of its one-column product, and for the down (`matmul_experts_add`) each row the same bits at 2T, T and beside generated rows, the generated rows the row builds' bits, and every seventh row within (blocks + 8 + k) F32 epsilons of the weighted sum of |w*x|.
Narrow routed tile: a group of up to 16 entries takes the routed tile's narrow build (`llmx_<type>_routed_narrow16` and `_narrow8`, `TwinKernels::routed_narrow`), the same 64 outputs and staging over 16 rows, a thread 4 outputs by 1 row where the 64-row build takes 4 by 4, so a column sums the same blocks and words in the same order and gives the 64-row build's bits; both builds are launched over the grouping and each group runs in the one its size picks, the other's workgroups returning at once, so the choice needs no constant and a call's bits do not depend on it. `experts_tile`'s ids give the call at extent T groups of 1, 7, 15, 16 and 17 entries whose experts are one group of more than 16 at 2T, and every call groups of both builds (`tile_groups_cover`), so its bits across extents are the witness that the narrow build ran and gave the 64-row build's bits, at the five gate and up builds of extent 128 (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_0, Q5_1 in f16, two projections and the 200-wide partial output tile) too. Expert 0 takes five of expert 1's entries in the first half, so the whole 256-row call at T = 128, whose other experts all hold more than 16 entries, still launches a narrow group.

Against the 64-row build alone (r18-tile.txt, the same build with no narrow build), the tile's own time at 10 entries an expert drops 1.8 times (Q8_0 gate and up f16 at 512 rows 14449 to 8244 us, the Q8_0 down 7779 to 4419, Q6_K's 768-wide down 13170 to 6188), and gate and up, which lost on the 64-row build below 192 to 512 rows (Q8_0 f16 1.67 at 32 and 1.06 at 384, Q4_K 2.41 at 32), now win from 32 or 128.
The tile's extent is a routed build's entry by role beside `group_from`, `TwinKernels::tile_from[role][width]` (gate and up, then the down; block-int16, then block-int8), the first measured extent from which that role's call wins or is level within 1% at every larger extent; the call knows its role (`matmul_experts` is gate and up, `matmul_experts_add` the down): 32 for every build and role but gate and up in block-int16 of Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_0 and Q5_1, 128 (1.03 to 1.12 at 32).
`row_class` counts the tile extents a prompt's extent reaches over every routed build, so each set of builds on the tile is a class and a choice still follows the rows' prompt.
Next lead for the tile: a group of 17 to 63 entries runs on the 64-row build with rows to spare; cutting such groups into narrow ones of 16 would keep the bits (the builds' sums are the same a column) and may win where an expert's entries average past 16, which Flash-Next's 512 experts 10 a token reach only past 819 rows a prompt.

Done, step 5 part 2: `sparse_attention` on ROCm with no second attention body. The per-row body (`attention_vec` in `kernels/f32.hip`) takes its head width as a template parameter, 128 or 256 (lanes DIM / 8 a stream), and a sparse flag that reads each row's selected ids in place of its positions, skipping ids outside the causal prefix and giving zeros for a row of none; the chunk body (`attention_chunk`) and both merges take the same flag, the chunk body for widths other than 128 and 256 (the shared test's 8). The per-row build splits a row's ids in chunks of the device profile's `sparse_split_ids` (256), the chunk doubling until the merge's 256 splits cover the stride, so a row's splits follow the id stride alone, 9 at Flash-Next's 2051 and 129 at 65537; the chunk build chunks by the stride. ## ROCm decode steps 2 to 6 (2026-11-05, RDEV27 to RDEV34, branch perf/rocm-decode on main 1fd20cc87, rebased onto 99df4418e; RDEV27's proposal of 20:25 as amended at 20:27, approved by F2DEV at 20:34 with six changes on the 13:35 design of the `k_rows` layout and its four changes; lands by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** ROCm decode of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL over four MI50s toward Vulkan's (50.48 layer-4 and 53.63 2x2 tg64 at int8), the kernel families of RDEV27's profile (rig llmx-rdev27-20261105/p1-*): twin launches, the router, the delta rule, the Q8_0 decode rows and the K-type row layout.
- **Done**, every step inside `src/backends/rocm/` and its test, no flag, no env, CPU and Vulkan untouched; steps 2 to 5 keep every value's bits, step 6 moves only the K-type decode rows' F32 order (the class, integer block dots exact with F32 sums, unchanged):
  (2) The stream and gate ops (`group_rms_norm`, `silu_scaled`, `mix_streams`, `sigmoid_mul`, `gated_rms_norm`) write their output's twin beside it (`twin_at`), and a product's twin is kept for the next product of the same activations, which exact products, routers and the grouping keep unless they write its input (`launch_writing`); test `twins` (producer and stream twins, a kept twin after the buffer grows and after a copy, write or host read).
  (3) `llmx_moe_route` reduces by the 64-pair tree, xor shuffles below the wave's width and shared memory at or above it, so a 32-lane wave gives the 64-lane bits; the test's reference is a host function of that tree (`route_host`).
  (4) `llmx_gated_delta_rule_short`, 4 tokens a stage where every view holds at most 8 rows, as Vulkan chooses; both builds bounded to 256 threads and two waves a SIMD, since unbounded they kept their state rows in 304 bytes of scratch (127 VGPRs and no scratch now).
  (5) Q8_0 decode in the half-block order: the one-column build's tail steps skipped in loads and products, a 64-lane wave's halves as two rows for rows of at most 16 blocks (`half8_1p`), two rows a wave from `q8_decode_two_rows_from` output rows (`half8_1r2`); the stream ops' twin map read in place (it was 124 bytes of scratch).
  (6) The Vulkan row layout in `k_rows`, one body for the dense, routed and grouped builds: a row a cluster of lanes (`row_cluster`, Q4_K and Q5_K capped by the profile's `k45_row_lanes`, whose comment names both backends), each type's `KRaw` naming its `Lane`; the old layout is the quarter form (`QuarterLane`, four lanes a block through the type's own `KRaw`, int2 twin loads at int8), taken by IQ4_NL alone and by Q5_0 and Q5_1 where it fills the cluster's steps fuller (`row_form`, one lane on a tie).
  The form rule's measurement, `rates routed`, renderD137, 10 of 512 experts, one generated row, us a call, the rule's form against the other (rig llmx-rdev30-20261105, s6r-repo-* against s6r-flip-*, two runs each, interleaved):

- **Goal:** ROCm decode of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL toward Vulkan's, routed expert products first (the open speed gate in ROCm weight types for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, above: routed products 17000 against 4100 us a token over four MI50s).

Every routed and grouped row build, of every twin type and Q8_0, kept 120 bytes of scratch a lane on gfx906 (llvm-readelf notes of the dot module), the dense row builds none: the routed builds work on a modified copy of `RowCall`, and `row_of`'s three-way select over its `w`, `y`, `start` and `nout` fields compiled to an indexed load, so the copy lived in private memory, stored and reloaded by every wave before its first weight load.
  `row_of` now adds the fields' differences under its two comparisons, the same addresses and so the same bits; scratch is 0 in every build, `q4_k_routed8` 51 to 37 VGPRs, `q5_1_routed8` 59 to 33, `q4_k_routed8_g2` 74 to 52, `q8_0_routed8` 32.

  `experts_grouped` runs every twin type through its grouped builds and its one-column build, each entry against the same one-column product, so the builds give the same bits whichever the break-evens choose.

## Draft price at depth (2026-11-04, SDEV3 and SDEV4, branch sdev2/draft-price-at-depth on main 44c5e56f0; SDEV2's finding and proposal of 2026-11-03 22:39, approved by F2DEV at 22:42 with seven changes and at 2026-11-04 04:09 with four more)

**Goal:** a drafting reply at depth weighs its drafts against fresh prices of the pass it would run: on production's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL over a 2x2 layer split at about 200k tokens, a lone reply drafting took 23-row verifies at about 19 tokens a second where plain decode gives 35.9, because the depth rule read decode cells last measured during old stalls and priced a pass alone as its slowest stage plus a flat offset.
**Done:** a decode cell keeps its band's pass count at its last measure and the depth rule reads only cells measured within spec::kForget's horizon of the band's newest measure (`kPriceHorizon`, 100 passes), an aged width priced on the line through the fresh cells beside it and its mean starting again once measured; past the widest fresh cell the curve goes on at the slope of the two widest fresh cells of that band; no width is read dearer than the cheapest fresh wider cell; a drafting reply takes a plain pass in its band when its plain width has aged; a pass is priced as the larger of its slowest stage and its stages' sum over the replies' passes in rotation (`ServiceRecord::combine`), and its server time is reconciled against that same price (`ServiceRecord::decode_price`).
The slope past the widest fresh cell is beyond the approved list: with the plain price right, a band priced past its widest cell on `spec::PassTimes`' line, which mixes every band, never drafted past 4 rows on a shallow copy, 110 to 160 tok/s against main's 130 to 185.
Change 7, on a fresh server: drafting on the preview build at 203.7k tokens gave 60.2 and 77.4 tok/s against plain 35.9 (SDEV2's arm), so production's 19 tok/s was the stale cells (cause 1), which no fresh server shows; `sampler`'s production case holds the ageing and the plain refresh to it.
Bench, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, four MI50s at tensor width 2 and layer shares 1,1, production's flags but `--ctx-size 262144` without `--yarn` (main has no `--yarn`), a fresh server an arm, greedy, 600 tokens, the request line's rate, the cold request then the one reusing its prompt (tok/s):

| Arm | 203.7k-token wiki chat | 1.9k-token self-repeating prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main 5c77f0d83, drafting off | 39.3 / 40.1 | 45.4 |
| main, drafting on (three servers) | 56.6 / 69.2, 57.3 / 72.0, 56.8 / 70.4 | 165.2 / 185.0, 132.0 / 132.6, 129.1 / 130.1 |
| branch without the slope (two servers) | 59.9 / 76.4, 60.3 / 75.8 | 110.0 / 160.5, 111.8 / 141.9 |
| branch (two servers) | 59.4 / 74.4, 57.9 / 70.9 | 188.7 / 194.9, 171.8 / 184.8 |

Drafting `lookup` and the Q4_K_M MTP head at `--draft-max` 63; the branch feeds about 5 drafts a verify at 200k where main feeds 8, and about 11 on the copy, as main's best server did.
Checks: `sampler` (24636 checks, with a lone pass on two stages, passes alternating one and two in rotation keeping the offset at the host's time, production's aged-cell case and inverted widest cells), `server-spec`, `server-passes` (its 2000 schedules' summary identical to main's), `docs` and `dead-code`.
F2DEV's four of 04:09: past the widest fresh cell the slope is the two widest's where it rises, else the band's narrowest to widest fresh cell's, else those widths fall to the line, so inverted widest cells never price wider drafts flat (`sampler`'s `inverted_widest`); SERVER.md says so; the plain refresh keys on the pass taking no prompt rows (`rows` generated, or all with the plan's order empty), and `form` throws if such a pass took prompt rows, which `server-passes-cpu` runs.
Cross-band check on one branch server (the bench's flags, a build of the head's code before two comments were cut), greedy 600 tokens a request, in order, decode tok/s, stage-0 passes, and the widths the health's recent passes showed (band, rows, count):

## Tensor width 16 (2026-11-03, branch feat/tensor-width-16 on main 840b96ec7; the proposal of 20:43 approved by the reviewer at 20:45 with four changes, the final review of 2026-11-04 10:59 with three, the review of 15:37 with one)

**Goal:** a pure tensor split of up to 16 devices a group (`--tensor-width 16`) on the CPU, Vulkan and ROCm, the member-order sum `t = p0; t += p1; ...; x += t` kept at every width.
**Done:** one limit, `backend::kMaxTensorWidth = 16` beside `Collective`, which the CLI's usage error reads ("at most 16 devices a group"); the CPU's collective already took any width.
Vulkan: `sum_rows.comp` reads its sources as one array binding of 16 through the kernel table's `counts` (`kSumRowsCounts`), its dispatch's list fixed at 18 buffers, and `missing_device_need` refuses a device that binds fewer storage buffers a stage than the kernel binding the most (`kernel_storage_buffers`).
ROCm: `kGroupMembers` is `kMaxTensorWidth`, the kernel's `GroupSignal` (2116 bytes, within the 4096 reserved) and `GroupPeers` (272 bytes, in device memory written once at join and passed by address, so the launch's arguments do not grow with the width) pinned on both sides; no two-shot, which is a later branch with its own measured gain.
Tests: `placement` runs groups of CPU backends at widths 2, 5, 8 and 16 on tiny models each width divides (16 with four KV heads each held by four members), one stage against two bit for bit through prompts, slices, decode, scored rows, two sequences, a recompute by class whole and from a fork, and passes in flight at P = 2, 3 and 4, and against one device within the F32 bound; `backend-group` holds the CPU collective at 5, 8 and 16 members to the oracle of `tests/group_sums.hpp`; the new `vulkan-sum` drives the sum kernel at 1 to 16 sources on one device; the new `backend-rocm-sixteen` runs the fast sum's kernel at 16 ranks on one device; `backend-vulkan` and `backend-rocm` hold every wider group the opened devices form to the oracle; `cli` refuses `--tensor-width 17`; `llmx-split-check` names ROCm devices.
**Gates at this head** (MI50s at default clocks, the free cards renderD129, 130, 134 and 135 and the idle GPU 9 at renderD131, never production's or renderD128):

**Left:**
1. The width-8 check by hand: Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on 8 cards in a window off production, on Vulkan and ROCm, bytes across stages, slices and passes in flight and its HF bounds, which also exercises the imports, files and inbox memory a width-8 group takes.
2. Widths 8 and 16 on devices are not measured here; the cost a sum past width 4 is extrapolated (docs/TENSOR-SPLIT.md, section 4.5).
3. The element-share sum in two shots on ROCm, a separate branch with its own measured prompt gain.
**Gotchas:** the runtime never puts two ranks of a group on one device: `RocmBackend` makes one stream per device and `RocmBackend::join` refuses a device twice, so a real group runs one rank per device, and HIP's hardware queues, which are per device, are never shared between ranks.
Only `backend-rocm-sixteen`, which runs all 16 ranks on device 0 beside the backend's own stream, needs more hardware queues than HIP gives a process by default.
On the ROCm 7.2.1 image here the default in force is 4, measured with N one-block kernels on N streams that meet only when all are resident: with `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES` unset and set to 4 alike they meet at up to 3 streams and give up from 4, and set to 16 they meet at up to 15; HIP documents 4 as the default.
The 16 the earlier comment named was a value set for the test, not HIP's default, so the test sets 32 for its own process and the runtime sets none.

## Vulkan F16 pair widening (2026-11-03, Done, lands by fast-forward)

**Goal:** Improve Vulkan F16 decode while preserving storage, activation, reduction and precision behavior. Weight conversion remains in its existing shader owner. No flags or model representation were added.

Candidate C replaces subnormal integer normalization in the F16 packed row loader with an exact F32 subtraction over normal intermediates, followed by integer bit selection. Scalar rows, embedding and tiles retain the existing integer helper. The host formula covers all 65,536 encodings. The GPU micro screen passed 15 calls with finite and double controls and byte-identical outputs within each weight mixture. The final ISA contains the precise subtraction, with 596 instructions, 29 branches and unchanged registers/spills. Every normal and mixed mean improves versus main; one mixed smaller-row wall mean is 3.87% slower than B. That tradeoff and all samples are retained. The measured main baseline is `19084b489`.

The same-file 12-call model screen, including the reversed block, gives these descriptive means:

| Arm | Prefill (tok/s) | Decode (tok/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 3586.333 | 184.485 |
| C | 3570.945 | 212.390 |
| mx Vulkan | 3087.043 | 226.231 |

C improves decode in all four chronological main/C pairs and has a descriptive pooled gain of 15.13%; prefill changes by -0.43%. Strong background activity and rate drift affect both blocks. These means do not establish or pass an mx performance floor. No samples were removed. F16/BF16 model speeds do not isolate storage type because their files have different parameter counts.

Windows checks passed on Radeon VII: the native backend test covered 68,643,840 kernel outputs and 1,209,244 half-weight checks. The half-weight model component passed 48 CPU and 24 Vulkan capture sets, with 64-token replies and no unavailable formats. These are independent widened-F32 controls, not external HF results. The audited MI50 half-weight suite passed 24 exact comparison sets with 32 capture witnesses and no skips. All 11 qualification commands passed. Main/C full-logit payloads, 64 greedy IDs and generated text matched byte-for-byte on CPU and MI50. Each backend passed all six file-exact HF ranking prompts with top-5 overlap 5/5 and eight NLL checks over the 247-token excerpt. Maximum continuous/window NLL errors were 0.000062857/0.000125923 on CPU and 0.000019743/0.000179058 on MI50, against unchanged bounds 0.01/0.02. All 126 sealed artifacts, source and fixture pins verified. [Qualification audit](benchmarks/half-decode-subtraction-qualification-20261103.json). GPU product checks do not directly verify signed-zero conversion bits or NaN payload preservation.

The exact widening replacement leaves activation arithmetic, reductions and precision unchanged, so the 16K gate is not applicable to this change; an independent review concurs. No precision bounds changed.

**Landing:** The applicable local checks pass, including docs and dead-code. The affected device suite is `half-weights`, supplemented by the native finite/mixed-pair checks and the full Windows Vulkan backend test. The Vulkan runtime and half-weight test body match checkpoint `59d883599`. The landing is rebased onto `23cdacc2a`, whose runtime change is confined to ROCm and whose Vulkan test addition is a separate shared collective oracle. The affected F16 code and tested inputs remain unchanged. Hosted CI compiles the combined tests. The feature edits after its tested checkpoint are documentation and archived evidence. All eight hosted jobs passed at `1efb25bb3af4` in [run 41694164559](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/41694164559). The landing adds only this final documentation and the [hosted evidence record](benchmarks/half-decode-ci-20261103.json), with unchanged runtime, tests and build inputs. It lands by fast-forward after the final documentation check and main check. The mx performance deficit remains recovery work, not a passed reference gate. The Markdown review carries 155 unchanged pages and checks the three changed pages against source and receipts. Historical claims were not revalidated individually. The A/B/C records remain available: [A micro](benchmarks/half-decode-micro-20261103.json), [A model](benchmarks/half-decode-model-screen-20261103.json), [A profile](benchmarks/half-decode-model-profile-20261103.json), [B micro](benchmarks/half-decode-branchless-micro-20261103.json), [B model](benchmarks/half-decode-branchless-model-20261103.json), [B operator](benchmarks/half-decode-branchless-operator-20261103.json), [C micro](benchmarks/half-decode-subtraction-micro-20261103.json), [C model](benchmarks/half-decode-subtraction-model-20261103.json), and [C Windows checks](benchmarks/half-decode-subtraction-windows-20261103.json).

## Attention at depth: the indexer's scoring and sparse attention over grouped heads (2026-11-03, MDEV, branch perf/qsa-depth on main 19084b489, MDEV's proposal of 18:50 with F2DEV's CHANGES of 19:42; lands by fast-forward)

Publication note, 2026-11-04: this change is now on main at `840b96ec7`; hosted run 41806264577 is verified green. COORD reports the MI50 CTest and device suite passed at `834c2016c` before the clean rebase. The checkpoint checklist below records the pre-publication state. Its reported Q2_0 ISA mismatch was subsequently identified as Q2_K and is handled by the separate instruction-checker fix.


- **Goal:** Flash-Next's prompt slices after a deep history spent most of their device time in the indexer's scoring (489 of 1034 ms of a 1024-row slice on one card after 131072 tokens on main d3a652cf9) and then in sparse attention (110 ms), both with the same bits kept.
- **Done:** `kv_index_scores_tile` takes 64 groups and 4 query rows a workgroup, four lanes a group: the group's pooled key stays in registers over the rows, the rows' queries go through shared memory eight heads at a time, more heads taking turns, and each dot is the same tree in the same order, every product formed apart through the width select so none fuses into an add, with a head no wider than 128 adding +0 for step 128's upper slots without forming them.
  `score_rows` no longer refuses more than eight indexer heads.
  The 256-wide sparse attention gains `_g4` builds taking 2, 3 or 4 query heads of a KV head a workgroup when the call's rows give every compute unit a grouped workgroup, and each stream of the sparse builds takes four selected tokens at a time, in the order it took them one at a time.
  The selection is unchanged; its rework is the next branch.
- **Bits:** Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on 2x2 MI50s at production's flags without a drafter (`--tensor-width 2 --layer-shares 1,1 --ubatch 1024 --dtype int8`, f16 cache): every logits row of the last slice, hashed over its raw bytes, and 32 greedy decode steps after it, ids and raw rows, are main's for 1024-row slices after 8192 (the one-workgroup selection), 16384 and 131072 tokens (the wide one), and for slices of 19 and 21 rows after 16384, either side of the grouping crossover of 20 rows; both arms built alike from detached trees with the same scratch patch to `logits --last`.
  `vulkan-index` (scores bit for bit with subnormals, 0 fused multiply-adds in the scoring's ISA), `sparse-attention --device vulkan:0` and `kv-selection --device vulkan:0` pass on an MI50.
- **Crossover:** sparse attention at Flash-Next's per-card shape (12 query heads, 1 KV head, 2051 selected tokens), one head a workgroup against grouped, on one MI50 (60 compute units): grouped 15% slower at 16 rows (0.8 grouped workgroups a compute unit), level at 24 (5% faster after 16384 tokens, 3% slower after 131072), faster from 32 rows on (44 and 45% less time at 1024 rows); the rule groups from one grouped workgroup a compute unit.
  The Radeon VII also has 60 compute units, so the per-unit rule is unmeasured on any other count.
  It is a crossover of speed only, with the bits held by the grouped-against-alone tests, and measuring it again on a different count is open work.
  A scoring span of 16 rows a workgroup measured slower than 4 (202 against 168 ms after 131072 tokens on a contracted prototype), so the span is fixed at 4 and no halving remains.
- **Measured:** the same placement and flags at default clocks, `bench --p 1024 --n 32 --r 2`, main 19084b489 / the branch at 019c30acb (the head's code, its comments and docs aside), rounds main, branch, branch, main, tok/s: pp1024 after 16384 tokens 794.17, 797.23 / 899.47, 896.87 (+12.9%), after 131072 460.77, 462.70 / 613.73, 613.43 (+32.9%); tg32 after 16384 36.84, 33.80 / 39.12, 41.25 (the branch's second run spread 5.57), after 131072 40.91, 40.99 / 42.90, 43.29 (+5.3%).
  `--profile` of one 1024-row slice after 16384 tokens, vulkan:0, ms of device time, main / branch: the slice 581.6 / 511.9, `kv_index_scores_tile` 60.7 / 44.5, sparse attention 108.3 / 55.9 (`_g4`), `kv_index_select_wide` 32.1 / 30.7.
  Another developer's CPU job on all 16 cores ran through part of the round; the cards were held by cardlock throughout.
- **Radeon VII:** the first head failed `sparse-attention --device vulkan:0` there under the AMD driver on Windows: its V16 builds contracted the accumulation into mixed-precision multiply-adds in the one-head build and into converts and unfused multiply-adds in the grouped one, so a row beside others differed from the row alone.
  The sparse builds' sums and products are now `precise`; both builds then hold only converts, multiplies and adds there, and sparse-attention, kv-selection, vulkan-index, CTest (97) and `backend-vulkan --isa` pass on the Radeon VII, as did a scratch sweep of 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 16 query heads a KV head over strides 1 to 515.
  On RADV the change leaves every instruction but each lane's first product, now formed as a multiply-add of +0, which can only turn a -0 product into +0 ahead of the scores' max and exp; the identity above was rerun at the fixed head (4f93c7839) with every case main's bytes, and the MI50 device tests pass again.
  A short round at the fixed head, the same flags with each container held to 2 CPUs, rounds main, branch, branch, main after 131072 tokens, tok/s: pp1024 462.31, 459.11 / 612.76, 614.60 (+33.2%), tg32 41.13, 41.00 / 42.78, 43.21 (+4.7%); host load average 4.8 to 22 from other developers' jobs, cards held by cardlock.
  `backend-vulkan --isa` on an MI50 fails at main 19084b489 and here alike on `matmul_row_q2_dot_2col` against `_16col` (Q2_0's two-row builds), which this branch does not touch.
- **Left:** CTest and the device suite on an MI50 at the landing head, and the hosted run.
  `backend-vulkan --isa` already fails on main on Q2_0's two-row builds, which this branch does not cause.

## Pipelined prompts: one slicing owner and the stage crossings measured (2026-11-04, PDEV2 to PDEV15, Done, lands by fast-forward on main 2c463d721; PDEV's proposal of 2026-11-03 16:45 with F2DEV's reviews of 16:46, 21:15, 03:55, 05:03, 2026-11-04 16:39, 18:18 and the LAND ruling of 21:02)

**Goal:** a prompt's slices on a layer split chosen by one pure function in `model/` (`infer::prompt_slice`) from what remains, the stages' measured cost lines and what is in flight, for `Model::prefill` and the scheduler alike, and the per-chunk stage overhead of the pipelined prefill measured (B).
**Done:** step B measured (devlog RESULT 2026-11-03 17:04): stage 0 is the pipeline's clock and a crossing costs ~1.5 ms a slice, so no device-side handoff is proposed.
`src/model/slicing.hpp` owns the slicing; `Model::prefill` plans each slice after the backlog of those before it, and the scheduler's `server::next_slice` cuts every prompt slice on a split after the passes in flight, its increment at the last stage capped by `kMaxStepGapMs` beside other requests, which changes main's path for prompts that are not alone.
`SlicePeriods` (F2DEV 05:03): every slice is one measure under the band `prompt_slice` reads, a band's line is a least-squares fit of fixed, row and row-by-depth costs, and each priced prefill's wall time beyond the recurrence's prediction calibrates the fixed cost, which the bottleneck period leaves out; before it the line's fixed cost was a fraction of the real one, so 16k prompts took 24-32 slices and layer-4 pp16384 at d16384 lost 2.5% (PDEV4, 05:01).
Checks at the candidate: server-passes with the new `SlicePeriods` tests, CTest (placement's failure test now on fresh models, since a prefill prices its slices sooner), the CPU suite, docs and dead-code.
PDEV11's (c) diagnosis and F2DEV's review of 2026-11-04 16:39 (PDEV12): an uncapped slice beside other ready prompts, admitted prompts with rows left (`others_ready`), is a ubatch, main's cut in a queued load, and alone the prompt's own cut; the capped path is unchanged.
A stage's cost line is `infer::fit_line`, the one least-squares fitter, which `SlicePeriods` also uses, weighted by each cell's measures, in place of the line through the two cells farthest apart: in PDEV11's queued layer-4 run stage 0's 1024-row cell (7 measures, 1124 ms) came from the load's first nine passes, where stage 0 took 1013-2252 ms beside 300-380 ms at stages 1-3, and set the line to 13 ms and 1.09 ms a row against about 29 ms and 0.31 ms.
F2DEV's review of 2026-11-04 18:18 (PDEV13): the cap serves only an arrival admitted at once and an unread admitted prompt with fewer rows left than the slice it would wait behind, min(left, ubatch), least remaining first (`slice_capped`); a reply decoding no longer caps, since a slice there is reached only while no reply waits beside a prompt and the reply's bound is the service rule's chunk (`chunk_plan`).

**Measured** (PDEV13 and PDEV14, devlog RESULT 2026-11-04 20:44 and NOTE 20:45, F2DEV's LAND ruling of 21:02): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on four MI50s at production's serve flags, layer-4 (`--layer-shares 1,1,1,1`) and 2x2, a fresh server a run, M = main 840b96ec7, B = b11819054 (the earlier cap), N = db7c32e1c (this change with a measurement-only slice-path log, removed here), each built the same way from its own worktree, run order M-B-N-N-B-M for (c) and (a) and M then N for (b), at default clocks, cards held by cardlock; no GPU fault in dmesg.

## Q2_0 read-only inference (2026-11-03, Done, lands by fast-forward)

Q2_0 GGUF weights now run on CPU and Vulkan through the existing quant decoder and backend owners. Type 42 stores 64 values in 18 bytes. There is no quantize writer or new runtime flag. F32, F16, BF16 and int8-request fallback policies retain their existing precision rules.

Independent format/operator and tiny HF checks pass, including their unchanged scoped allowances. The pinned 8B file passes short ranking/NLL checks and raw/chat 16K selected-HF checks, each with 512 exact top-1 matches, zero ties and zero misses. TP2 and layer split each pass 150 logit and 12 NLL comparisons. Current-main Q8 CPU/MI50 and Q1 F16/F32 device captures are byte-identical; the clean current Radeon VII native check passes. [HF](benchmarks/q2-tree32-short-hf-20261103.json), [depth](benchmarks/q2-tree32-depth-20261103.json), [split](benchmarks/q2-tree32-split-hf-20261103.json), [identity](benchmarks/q2-tree32-existing-identity-20261103.json), [Radeon](benchmarks/q2-tree32-radeon-20261103.json).

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
