| Decode, tok/s | 125.820 | 132.820 | 129.720 | +2.390% |

All 18 calls remain reported, including the slow activity-overlapped candidate call. The layout control and activity limits are retained; this is an assessed workload tradeoff, not a claim that every phase or sample wins. Existing Q8 MI50 changes are -0.100% prefill/+2.708% decode. CPU's single reversed-order repeat gives -0.499%/-0.753%; six paired-block medians across both cohorts are -0.616%/-0.730%. A small CPU cost remains possible, with no matched Q8 CPU layout control or zero-regression claim. [Matched comparison](benchmarks/q2-tree32-matched18-20261103.json), [layout control](benchmarks/q2-tree32-layout-20261103.json), [both CPU cohorts and disposition](benchmarks/q2-tree32-existing-timing-20261103.json).

Its native tests and all 45 non-docs Python components passed [the isolated macOS retry](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/41660437794) at `61aafe787`, with identical job steps and runtime/test/build source. ## Radeon tiled-attention pairing test control (2026-11-03, test-only cherry-pick e71dad0cc on published main d3a652cf9, branch fix/attention-pair-policy-20261103)

**Cause:** `tile_split_cap_checks` forced `compute_units` to select the attention pairing, then left that fake value active during the following Q8_0 projection of the attention output. The projection could therefore use different tile/reduction geometry across the equality arms. The test now overrides the capability only for attention and restores the real value before Q8_0 matmul. It retains strict byte-for-byte equality for the complete outputs. No runtime code changed.

**Evidence:** a clean Radeon VII build at published main `d3a652cf9d7c1477e6d456d74d8d1d4a5d44aadf` reproduced `tiled attention 100 rows after 2118 tokens, whole and cut into pieces of one tile, one and two rows a lane: differs`. The corrected test passes on the patch branch under the same Radeon VII environment. The 20,000-token/1252-part double-reference case remained within `1e-4`, with its short-prompt identity check passing. Retained pretest counters (`scratch/q2-attention-main-control-20261103/gpu-postpatch-pretest-summary.json`) show Radeon VII max engine use 0.495%, dedicated usage 1,380,859,904 bytes, and local usage 452,861,952 bytes; free VRAM was not recorded. This is local Radeon evidence, not MI50 coverage.

**Checks:** `vulkan-lifetime` passes on the corrected test (25.54 s); `dead-code` passes with 8 known findings and 19 planted faults, and `docs` passes with zero findings and 21 planted faults. These focused checks used the fresh local Windows Vulkan build.

**Hosted validation:** the scoped Vulkan job `125854912591` in GitHub run `41617620774` passed at `b9ed033f424c07b7ca3cfbe32dd6ca7a406e9c5b`. The final documentation update records that result and clarifies the Q8 projection control in `docs/TESTS.md`; the tested source is unchanged. This is a test-only correction, with no Q2 runtime changes and no claim of Q2 performance, model or HF qualification. The change lands by fast-forward after final documentation checks; the merge adds no commit.

## ROCm tensor groups: the collective (2026-11-03, DDEV, branch feat/rocm-collective on main d36458312; docs/ROCM.md step 4, DDEV's proposal of 08:12 approved by F2DEV at 08:20 with six changes; gated, F2DEV's CHANGES (1) of 14:15 applied)

**Goal:** tensor groups on ROCm through the one `Collective` interface, on the one-shot peer-write algorithm of the proposal, with the bytes of the Vulkan collective; ROCm `join` returned nothing before, so a ROCm tensor group was refused.
**Done:** `rocm_collective.hpp` implements `partial`, `sum_into`, `sum_in_place` and `wait` (docs/src/backends-rocm.md), with F2DEV's six changes: the second meeting kept and two sums in flight tested with `wait(1)`; an atomic abort-word load and a one-second wait on the device's wall clock; a sum that gives up leaves NaN, throws once on its backend and turns the collective conservative for every later sum; epochs skip 0 on the wrap, tested from 0xfffffffc; the Vulkan sum's order held to one oracle with signed zeros, tails and residuals (`tests/group_sums.hpp`, shared with `backend-vulkan`); an acquire fence for every thread after each meeting; the signal block in `scratch_reserve`; no fine-grain prerequisite, `join` probing each group once and printing fast or conservative and why.
Every launch now makes its device current, since HIP finds a module's function through it; without it a second device's launch failed with hipErrorInvalidHandle. `wrap_host` registers host memory for the head group's logits rows, and so the loader streams ROCm weights through its read ring's registered pages as it does Vulkan's.
Its first form took the contract's lifetime wrong: a dropped view's `hipHostUnregister` waited in the graves past the caller's free, HIP keys a registration by address, so the next memory mapped there read as already registered and was taken as a view of the stale registration (a single-device `generate` faulted the GPU on a copy out of it), and a view of memory another device registered lost it when that device's view dropped (`--tensor-width 4` aborted in HIP, "Memobj map does not have ptr").
Now one registration per address counts its views across devices, the last view dropped waits for its stream and unregisters at once, and a second span at a registered address is refused, so the caller writes through staging (`backend-rocm`'s `host_views`); HIP takes a second registration of a span and drops it at one unregister, so the count must be the backend's.
**Measured** (rig `ddev/ar/out/gall` at 4d8d358ce and `out/gfin` at 1c1546dcb, renderD129,130,134,135, MI50, default clocks, one harness and image, HIP libraries of the reference's closure, 20 KiB sum, one call timed to every rank's completion, 120 warmups, 100 calls, three interleaved rounds; us p50 / p95):

| Width | reference (fine-grain set) | llmx, fine-grain set | llmx, unset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W2 | 41.0-41.1 / 43.1-43.4 | 32.7-33.9 / 45.3-48.4 | 32.0-34.4 / 34.0-50.6 |
| W4 | 76.9-77.5 / 78.6-81.5 | 70.2-75.9 / 97.0-125.4 | 67.1-70.5 / 72.3-108.0 |

Gate g100/g101 at the rebased head (rig `ddev/ar/out/g100`, `g101`, renderD129,130,134,135, MI50, default clocks, no dmesg event in any phase): the single-device `generate` that faulted runs clean; backend-rocm passes on four MI50s (fast at widths 2, 3 and 4, conservative, two sums in flight, a sum whose peer never launched giving up in 1.0001 s, the epoch wrap, wrap_host, `host_views`); CTest; docs and dead-code clean.
Qwen3-8B Q8_0, 256 greedy tokens: ROCm at widths 1, 2 and 4 and Vulkan at widths 1, 2 and 4 give the same bytes.
Qwen3-8B Q8_0, `bench --p 512 --n 128`, tok/s, two rounds:

| --- | --- | --- |

The loader's registered path on one ROCm device against main's staging, same runs: read 1.60/1.57 s and upload 1.06/1.15 s against read 1.20/1.07 s and upload 2.07/1.91 s, so 2.66/2.72 s against 3.27/2.98 s, and it is kept.
**Left:**
1. ROCm width 4 prefill (851 tok/s) is below width 2 (1470) and Vulkan width 4 (1309): profile the prompt's sums at width 4 against width 2 with rocprofv3 (`ddev/ar/gprof2.sh`).
2. F2DEV's two added checks (one view dropped then a copy through the other; member 0 dropped then member 1 copying and the last drop unregistering) pass on the branch and on the unfixed tree too: HIP 7.2 copies through memory a dropped view unregistered as pageable memory, so only the second-span check fails there; the fault itself needs freed memory remapped under a stale registration, which faults the GPU, so no test provokes it.
3. F2DEV's note (not blocking): dropping a registered view waits for its whole stream under the graves lock; waiting only for the view's last copy would do.
4. Open single-call cells (first support): p95 at W2 and W4 and p50 at W4 with the fine-grain setting against the reference; recovery is step 6: one sum per replayed graph, concurrent member launches, and the meetings' cost, measured in the same harness with kernel timestamps against host time.
**Gotchas:** a fast sum's two phases must take the same units in the same blocks, or a block's meeting does not cover the rows it reads (the prototype's reduce took other units than its push); each member's zero fill of its signals must finish before any peer signals into them, so the collective drains its members once it is made; `sync` and the collective's `wait` record without the failure check (`record`), so a group fault is never swallowed.

## The job between a long conversation's turns names only live requests (2026-11-03, SDEV, branch fix/server-resume-cache-flake on main d3a652cf9, the coordinator's FINDING of 17:52; tests only)

- **Goal:** `server-resume-cache` passes on any allocator and any load, its case "a job that fits only between a long conversation's turns" waiting on events and never on time.
- **Cause:** the case told a job's pass from a turn's by the address of each request it sent, and let the handles of finished turns go, so a request freed by then could give its address to the job, whose passes then read as the test's own: the second turn, sent at the job's first pass, was never sent, and the case failed "the second turn sent at the job's first pass within a minute", as the hosted macOS job did in runs 41633439705 and 41657333944.
  glibc gives a block back to the arena of the thread that took it, so on Linux the turns sent from the test's thread take those addresses and the job, made on the scheduler's thread, does not; an allocator whose free blocks any thread takes next, as macOS's does, can hand one to the job.
- **Done:** the case holds every handle until the scheduler stops, and the 300 ms it gave the job to start again between two turns is now the event it stood for: the turn has left the scheduler's active requests; the round that does so looks at the waiting jobs only while no request is queued, so a turn sent first makes it skip the check, which can hide a restart from `started == 1` but never fail the case.
- **Evidence (rig, CPU, the case alone):** under an allocator shim that keeps one free list of blocks from 1 to 64 KiB for every thread (LD_PRELOAD), main d3a652cf9 fails 20 runs of 20 with the hosted message, and the fix passes 20 of 20; on one core beside three busy loops at nice 19, with the shim, main passes 10 of 10, since the order its threads free and take blocks in moves, and the fix passes 20 of 20; on one core under starvation without the shim main passed 30 of 30, so time alone did not make it fail.
- **Shim:** the allocator shim is `/opt/claude-work/sdev-rcf-shim` on the test machine.
- **Left as they are:** the case's other wall-clock checks, `queued < 5000` against a 10 s reader chunk and `last_ms < 20000`, keep about twice their margin; either becomes an event wait if it fails on a hosted runner.
- **Gates (CPU, rig, the commit's tree):** CTest 78 of 78 (`server-resume-cache` 149 s); the suite's `docs` and `dead-code` pass; `llmx-server-resume-test cpu-cache` 5 runs in a row pass.
- **Left:** review by F2DEV and the hosted run, which lands it by fast-forward.

## ROCm many users (2026-11-03, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-many-users on main 7a46dd672, after perf/rocm-f16-decode-dot landed; DDEV's proposal of 02:28 and F2DEV's review of 02:30)

**Goal:** ROCm decode of 2 to 16 sequences nearer Vulkan's on one MI50; on main Qwen3-8B Q8_0 int8 x16 gave 311 tok/s against Vulkan's 551, and the 0.6B 1579 against 2867.
**Cause** (rocprofv3 kernel trace against Vulkan's profile, Qwen3-8B and 0.6B Q8_0, 16-token prompts and 32 tokens, rig `ddev/rocm/p82`): launches per step and their gaps were level with Vulkan's at 8B; the time was in the row builds, which reduced every (row, column) by its own six-level wave sum, R * C * 6 shuffles a wave, more than the products on the 0.6B's short rows.
**Done:** every row build reduces its R * C sums by one transposed xor tree (`wave_sums` in `kernels/int16.hip`), each level halving the values a lane holds, own plus partner as the butterfly adds them, so every sum keeps its bits; each sum is written by its own lane, which takes its row's output from the wave's rows held in scalar registers, never reading the call's arguments again.
A 32-lane wave (gfx1151, compile coverage) folds the int8 class's 64-sum sixteen-column builds in two parts of 32, each part the same tree, so `warpSize / NV` is never 0; on a 64-lane wave that branch folds away.
A build of one column group issues its weights' and twin's loads before a scheduling barrier: without it the compiler put the scale loads behind a wait on the twin's, which cost the one-column F16 build 11% and the four-column build 22% on the 8B; the wider builds keep their order, which measured 3 to 5% faster for them than the barrier.
F16's sixteen-column build loads its twin four columns at a time, where it took eight: per call on the gate and up projections 757 against 829 us on the 8B (main 776) and 1297 against 1335 on the 14B (main 1400), one group of sixteen 1801 (rocprofv3, renderD131, rig `ddev/rocm/p94`).
The half-block order takes sixteen columns in one launch at four rows a wave (127 VGPRs on the dot module, two waves a SIMD), where it took two launches of eight.
Rows a wave follow the call's rows (`row_build`, replacing the fixed `waves_rows` table): the builds of two to eight columns take four rows once a call launches the profile's `row_four_waves_per_cu` (8) waves a compute unit at four rows and two below it; F16's one- and sixteen-column builds take two at every count, the int8 builds of sixteen columns four, the int8 quarter layout's one-column build two, and the half-block order's one-column build keeps its stepped one-row build; only those builds are compiled.
**Sweep** (rocprofv3, renderD131, synthetic Q8_0 rows 1024 to 12288, widths 1024, 3072, 4096 and 12288 and for the int8 quarter layout 1312, 3104, 4128 and 12320, 1 to 16 columns, every build at R 1, 2 and 4, 20 calls each, rig `ddev/rocm/rsw1` and `rsw2`): a threshold from 1.5 to 3 waves a SIMD keeps every pair within 0.0 to 1.7% of the best R summed over its cells, 4 or more loses 1 to 4%, so the profile takes 2 a SIMD; four rows at F16's sixteen columns lose 10 to 35% at every count and two rows at int8's lose up to 45%; the int8 two-column builds took one row, 7.7% (half-block order) and 18.4% (quarter layout) over the best.

## The --isa screen passes over instructions scheduled inside an address division (2026-11-03, VDEV, branch fix/isa-division-window on main 7a46dd672, the coordinator's ask of 07:2x after MDEV's finding; tests only, lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

**Goal:** `llmx-backend-vulkan-test --isa` on an MI50 under RADV fails `matmul_row_q4_dot_16col_grouped` against its wide build; the build is right and the count rule is wrong.
**Done:** RADV places instructions inside the address division's sequence (`v_mbcnt_hi_u32_b32 v0, -1, v0` between its first multiply and its reciprocal), so the screen's five-line window missed one division and counted its two normalizing multiplies; every grouped build of 8 and 16 columns of the two-row families carried 2 multiplies too many, the Q4 16-column one first in the list.
`float_ops` now keeps the division's own instructions in the window and the registers other instructions name between them, and excludes a matched sequence only where neither of its two registers is among them, so an instruction that touches the sequence still breaks it; three planted cases in `check_float_ops` hold that (an unrelated instruction inside, one writing a sequence register, one naming a range over it), the first failing on main.
**Gates:** on one MI50 (renderD130) the failing test at 5b9b66efe fails `check_float_ops` with its own message; at the fix `llmx-backend-vulkan-test` passes as CTest runs it, and with `--isa` every grouped build matches its wide build; on the Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver) `--isa` passes, 27 grouped builds the same as their wide build; `docs` and `dead-code` pass.
**Left:** with the grouped check passing, `--isa` on the MI50 now stops at the next check, which the first failure had hidden: the two-row builds of other rows (`matmul_row_q2_dot_2col` against `_16col`), and an offline replica of that rule over the same disassembly fails it for every family steps 2 and 4 of the wide decode plan added (Q2_K, Q3_K, the IQ types, TQ, Q1_0, MXFP4, F16 and BF16 values), where the 16-column four-row build is not whole copies of the 8-column two-row build's rows; those builds' decode columns are bit for bit the columns alone, so this is the count rule against the driver's code shape, and the rule for them waits on the reviewer (the wide decode plan's end gates).

## ROCm wide decode rows (2026-11-02, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-f16-decode-dot on main 672b6d998, after perf/rocm-decode-run-launch landed; the coordinator's ask of 11:5x after DDEV's p74 FINDING)

**Goal:** ROCm decode of 4 to 16 sequences nearer Vulkan's on one MI50; after perf/rocm-decode-run-launch, Qwen3-8B Q8_0 gave f16 x16 142 tok/s against Vulkan's 313, int8 x16 246 against 520.
**Cause** (rocprofv3 kernel trace, Qwen3-8B Q8_0, 16-token prompts and 32 tokens, rig `ddev/rocm/p74`): every column count takes one launch of its row build, and the wide builds were slow per launch, f16 x1/x4/x16 85/206/746 us against Vulkan's 75/95/295 and int8 73/116/422 against 73/82/164.
The sixteen-column F16 build held 195 VGPRs, one wave a SIMD, most of them a 64-bit twin pointer a column; the four-column builds waited on their twin loads.
**Done:** the row kernels take R, the output rows a wave, and G, the columns whose twin loads issue together before their products, per build (`LLMX_ROWS`, `LLMX_HALF`, the host's `waves_rows` following R).
A build wider than its group addresses every column from one 32-bit lane offset, which took the sixteen-column F16 build to 112 VGPRs and two waves a SIMD; in the narrower builds that form measured slower (f16 x1 85 to 100 us, x4 141 to 208), so they keep a pointer a column.
The F16 builds of four columns and more and the int8 quarter-layout builds take two rows a wave in groups of four or eight columns on the dot module; the half-block order's four-column build takes four rows a wave and its eight-column build two, and the half-block order launches eight columns at a time, its sixteen-column build removed: it measured 420 us at one row a wave, 494 at one row with per-column loads, 510 at two rows in groups of four, against 163 for eight columns.
Every column keeps the bits of the column alone, since a column's sum keeps its lanes and order in every build; backend-rocm passes on every variant.

## A request's passes on its request line (2026-11-02, SDEV, branch feat/request-log-drafting on main d1686f69f, the coordinator's ask after production's replies at 291-298k tokens ran at 16-23 and then 64.8 tok/s)

- **Change:** the request line gives, after its rate, `S steps, V verifies, D drafted, K kept, M ms a pass` (docs/SERVER.md, The request line): its passes without drafts, those that verified drafts with the drafts fed and kept, and its time after the first token over its passes after the first, so a slow reply shows whether it kept fewer drafts a verify or waited longer between passes; sat out passes, pauses, resumes and recomputed rows were already on it and stay.
  The counts are `Request`'s own atomics the live view reads (`Request::passes`), filled as tokens are published, so nothing waits on a device; the compatible routes' `timings` carry them as `steps`, `verifies`, `drafted`, `kept` and `pass_ms`.
  The line is now written before the request ends (`Request::stamp_end` takes its end time first), so its reply follows its line; it was written after, and a test reading the line on the reply could see none or the request before's.
- **Tests:** `server`: a completion without drafts gives a step a token, one more where it drew the end of text, and no verify, in `timings` and on its line; the Flash fixture's chat with and without the embedded drafter gives steps + verifies + kept = 64 on its line, verifies only with the drafter, and the line's drafted and kept equal to the server's counts for the request.
- **Gates:** CTest (78 of 78) and the CPU suite pass on the CPU; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 against main on the CPU gives the same bytes for greedy, seeded and chat replies and for the prompt's logits, timing lines left out.
  The change lands by fast-forward.
## A reply that could not grow is not a reply the prompts wait for (2026-11-02, SDEV-E, branch fix/empty-pass-round on main d1686f69f, the coordinator's ask from the uncapped mix check, lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

- **Found:** `tools/server_mix_check.py --uncapped` on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on the CPU of a loaded machine ended two requests with `server: a round with active requests formed an empty pass: a request of 1279 tokens was not ready, 2 active, blocks free 1 of 32`, and the tool then failed on the missing reply (KeyError 7).
- **Cause:** a younger uncapped reply whose growth step the older request's room holds sits the pass out (a stall), but `Scheduler::plan` still counted it among the replies, so the round planned replies beside prompt work. With the replies' pass priced above a step's allowance (the objective unmet, as on a loaded machine) a prompt beside replies reads only once it has gone `kPromptWaitMs` without rows, or rides the replies' pass as the quick prompt, and the older request, resuming or still reading its prompt, got neither: no reply was ready and no prompt was in the plan's order, so the round formed nothing with nothing in flight and its check ended every active request.
- **Done:** the failing test, then `plan` leaves a stalled reply out of the replies, as the pass leaves it out, so the prompt beside it reads as though no reply waited (docs/SERVER.md, The service rule).
- **The failing case first:** `server-resume`, `stalled_beside_prompt`: on four CPU stages of the synthetic Q8_0 model at one pass in flight and ubatch 16, capped X (400 tokens and 4) and uncapped Y (128) fill 7 blocks of 128, the last stage sleeping 50 ms a submission until the first stall; each reply must be its reply alone with a stall and no pause. Main with the test failed it 4 runs of 4 with the empty-pass error (`a request of 16 tokens was not ready, 2 active, blocks free 0 of 7`); the fix passes it.
- **Gates:** see the gate post of 2026-11-02 in the devlog; filled at the landing head.
- **Reviewed:** review requested from F2DEV and the coordinator; not landed.
## The scheduler round's reuse question at a cost that does not grow with holders (2026-11-02, PDEV, branch perf/cache-round-cost on main d1686f69f, the owner's priority one of 2026-11-02)

**Goal:** a request or job waiting for room costs the scheduler round little at any history length; production's 4-MI50 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next fell from 55-65 to 9-20 tok/s at 250k-315k tokens of context while a reread job waited, rounds taking 180-290 ms of server time against 30-90 ms of stage time, every gdb sample of the scheduler thread in `Cache::served`.

**Cause:** `served` compared the asked tokens with every donor, host copy and boundary token by token, a boundary's rows took `holds` over every holder, and `rank` and `host_victims` asked `held_below` for each holder, which copied its history and asked `served` again, so each round of a waiting request redid holders times history, and holder pairs every round.

**Done:** holders keep their tokens as `HeldTokens` (a generation no change reuses and their whole blocks' chained hashes); `served` compares tokens it is asked about with each holder by binary search over the hashes and then the answering holder token by token, asking every holder token by token where that holder shares less, so outputs are those of the token compare; two holders' shared length is remembered by generation (`Cache::common`), so `holds`, `held_below` and the ranks compare a pair once; `Stats::reuse_scans` (health `reuse.scans`) counts holders compared token by token.
A new `server-resume` case holds it: a request waiting 900 rounds for room beside three donors sharing its prompt compares 1805 holders token by token (at most 3 a round allowed); the same tree with `served` forced token by token fails it at 5415.
After review (2026-11-02): `Stats::reuse_scans` is an atomic the stats read from other threads; the pair memo (`PairMemo`) past its cap drops only pairs of generations no donor, host copy or boundary has and sets its cap to twice what stays, where it was wiped whole at 4096 pairs; `enter` and `prefetch` hash the asked history once for all their questions; the question is `reuse_answer` over listed holders, which `server-resume` holds to the token compare in 3000 random trials (prefixes, row classes and states on and off block edges, holders passed over, boundaries without rows, the state rule), with every block hashing to 0 and asked of a holder's own tokens, and the memo to a trimmed donor and to 20000 dead pairs beside a live one.
The hash's mixing is unchanged: a collision costs only the token compare's fallback, which the zero-hash trials hold to the same answers.

**Measured** (CPU microbench on the rig, synthetic: one conversation's 12 host copies, 6 other conversations' and 40 boundaries, kept out of the tree; per call after a warm-up, ms):

| L tokens | asked + served | rank of every boundary | rank of every host copy | host_victims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100k main | 1.082 | 0.188 | 3.971 | 4.411 |
| 100k branch | 0.070 | 0.009 | 0.013 | 0.023 |
| 300k main | 4.092 | 1.647 | 15.601 | 18.534 |
| 300k branch | 0.197 | 0.008 | 0.012 | 0.022 |

What is left grows with the asked history alone: its copy, its hashes and one compare, about 0.2 ms at 300k.

Rounds of `host_victims` and `ranked`, the same microbench with 8 donors, after a warm-up, ms a round and holders compared token by token a round (12 rounds each, all alike):

| L tokens, holders | live pairs | before review | after review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300k, 8 donors, 30 host copies, 70 boundaries | 745 | 0.073-0.084 ms, 0 scans | 0.082-0.153 ms, 0 scans |
| 300k, 8 donors, 100 host copies, 200 boundaries | 5950 | 978-998 ms, about 8480 scans | 0.97-1.05 ms, 0 scans |

At the asked shape the live pairs stay under the old cap, so neither wipes; past it the old memo was wiped inside every round and recomputed about 8480 pairs, which the pruned memo keeps.

**Gates:** on the rig, CPU, in the same image, the tree after review: CTest 78 of 78 pass; `server-resume`, `server-resume-cache`, `server-passes`, `server-passes-cpu`, `cache-scenario`, `cache-scenario-production`, `image-cache` and `kv-cache` pass 5 runs each; `docs` and `dead-code` pass; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `generate --temp 0 -n 128` gives main's text byte for byte; `tools/server_mix_check.py` on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 passes with every phase's ids byte-equal to main's; the new trials fail with the fallback taken out (every block hashing to 0 gave 48 tokens against the token compare's 16). The `--uncapped` mix check and the CPU suite were still running at the push on a machine at load 34 of 16 CPUs (`/zpool1/llmx-pdev/gates-b2.log`); main's own `--uncapped` run in the same conditions ended with requests 7 to 11 getting error events in place of tokens, so that phase is load-bound there and is read against main.

**Left:** a production measurement once landed; the reread job's room rule is SDEV-C's fix/reread-job-room, which touches `prefetch` apart from this change.
## A job never holds room a request needs (2026-11-02, SDEV, branch fix/reread-job-room on main d1686f69f, the coordinator's BLOCKER of 11:19 and the owner's DECISION of 12:01, reworked after XDEV's and F2DEV's review)

- **Goal:** a reread job gives way to any request that needs its room, with or without a pass in flight, is dropped where no room is left, as before, and does not start again only to give way to the next turn.
- **Cause:** production (97899a5e3) held a 257726-token request queued for minutes with nothing in flight while a job's read of a 234560-token conversation from disk straight into the devices held the room it needed; `yield_jobs` gave way only for jobs on the devices, and a stream holds its blocks until it completes.
- **Done:** where the request first in line lacks room, a read only jobs wait for stops (`Cache::yield_reads`) and its blocks come back once its copies retire (`StreamedRead::copied`); a request short of a seat alone stops none; a read of rows the waiter's own history begins with goes on, and the waiter forks it; a stopped read takes no new waiter (`StreamedRead::stopped`); no read starts that would leave the request first in line short of room, a younger request's included (`Cache::takes_room`); a job that gave way looks at the disk again, and is looked at only once it could start; one that finds no room with no request running is dropped, as before (docs/CACHE-PLAN.md, question 2); a job that gave way to a turn continuing a kept conversation, forking every whole block of a donor or host copy, keeps that turn's room free beside it while the conversation is kept, one record a conversation, the record going when no donor, host copy or running request holds its fork or the turn leaves before admission, and asking at most the whole pool (`Request::rooms_`, `Cache::job_spare`).
- **Tests:** `server-resume`'s job read in six arms (paced, copies held on one CPU and on a tensor group of two, the waiter the job's next turn, a waiter short of a seat, a waiter and the next turn arriving in one round), and the job between a long conversation's turns, its second turn sent from the job's first pass so the case no longer races.
- **Gates (CPU, rig, tree exported with LF endings):** CTest 78 of 78; the CPU suite, 46 components pass and `baseline` skipped without its models, `docs` and `dead-code` among them; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `generate` greedy text and `logits` the same bytes as main d1686f69f, and `tools/server_mix_check.py` ids byte-equal to main's; `server-resume cpu-cache` 10 runs in a row pass; `cache-scenario production` reuses main's figures.
  Arms (fix / 88d869199 / main): paced P/P/F, held P/P/F, held_group P/P/F, shared P/F/P, seat P/F/P, same_round P/F/F, between_turns P/P/F.
  `tools/server_mix_check.py --uncapped` on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 fails in its together phase on this branch as on main: requests end with "a round with active requests formed an empty pass" (`Scheduler::run`), a request not ready beside one other with 1 block of 32 free; no job runs there, so it is a scheduler fault apart from this fix, left to its own branch.
- **Left:** review by XDEV and F2DEV.
- **Gotchas:** a job's passes form only with no reply and no client prompt (`Scheduler::plan`), so a job's pass in flight as a turn arrives delays that turn's first token by the passes in flight ahead of it, not its decode rate; the decode slowdown past 240k tokens on production is not explained by jobs.
  A request that attached to a job's read, behind the request first in line, keeps that read, so the first request waits for the whole read; only a read of the first request's own history goes on for it, and the rule against new reads covers reads not yet started (review finding 9, left as it is).

## Two query rows a lane in the 128-wide attention tile (2026-11-02, MDEV, branch perf/tile-two-rows on main 7a46dd672, first built and measured on main 2e77b49ab, step 1 of MDEV's tile-rate plan, approved by F2DEV on 2026-11-01 at 20:53 with step 1b after it)

- **Goal:** at long context the causal attention tile is most of a prompt pass on Qwen3-30B-A3B (80 percent of pp512's device time after 16k tokens); every K and V value a lane reads from shared memory served one query row, so the tile's rate was bound by those reads.
- **Done:** the 128-wide builds of `attention_tile` give each lane rows i and i + 16 of one 32-row tile, two tiles a workgroup (`kAttentionTileRows` 64), each row keeping the operations of a lane of its own in the same order and stopping at its own tile's end; the `_d256` builds keep one row a lane (`kAttentionTileRowsD256` 32).
  A workgroup whose second tile holds no row, a view of 32 rows or fewer or a view's last 32, takes one row a lane as main does (`attention_tile_rows.glsl`, included once for each layout).
- **Bits:** on an MI50, Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M and Qwen3.6-27B Q4_1 give main's logits bit for bit for 345 ids at ubatch 45 and 700 ids at ubatch 100, batched, decode and greedy (`llmx-model-logits`, SHA-256 of each capture); `llmx-backend-vulkan-test --isa` passes on both arms.
- **ISA (MI50, RADV):** the 128-wide builds go from 84 VGPRs and three subgroups a SIMD to 128 VGPRs and two, LDS 18432 to 20480 bytes, no spills; the `_d256` builds stay at 128 VGPRs and two subgroups.

## A request's reasoning_effort reaches the chat template (2026-11-02, SDEV, branch feat/reasoning-effort on main d50b7a2bb, the owner's ask for clients' thinking levels)

- **Goal:** clients that send the OpenAI top-level `reasoning_effort` get the Qwen 3.8 templates' thinking levels instead of a 400, never with the field silently ignored.
- **Done:** on the chat routes and `/v1/tokenize` a `reasoning_effort` string is the template variable of that name, as if given in `chat_template_kwargs` (`Api::add_effort`, called by `template_vars`, the one owner of a request's template variables, so the prompt, the follow-up prefix and the count all see it).
  The template parser records the variables a template reads (`jj::Template::reads_variable`), and `chat::ChatFormat::reasoning_effort` says whether the template reads `reasoning_effort`; where it does not, the field is refused with 400 naming the template.
  The same field in `chat_template_kwargs` with another value, and a value that is not a string, are refused with 400; a value the template refuses comes back as its own error, as before; `/v1/completions` keeps refusing the field, having no template.
  The native `/v1/chat`, which ignored the field before, now honours it the same way.
  `server` holds it on the Qwen 3.8 template (the top-level field renders as the kwargs value, `high` gives the template's refusal), on a tiny template that reads it (every route's count, the three ways of giving it, the conflicts) and on one that does not (refused on both chat routes and `/v1/tokenize`).
- **Gates:** on the CPU, CTest passes and Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 against main d50b7a2bb gives the same bytes for greedy, seeded and chat replies and the prompt's logits.
  The CPU suite passes but for raw-blocks under `--require-tools`, which fails on `numpy is not installed` in the build image, as it does with main's binary there; a first run's arch-boundary finding, a comment naming a model family, is fixed, and arch-boundary, docs, dead-code, server and CTest pass again on the fixed tree.
  The change lands by fast-forward.
- **Left:** the hosted run, F2DEV's review.

## ROCm products join adjacent runs into one launch (2026-11-02, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-decode-run-launch on main d50b7a2bb; the coordinator's ask of 07:21 after DDEV's batched-decode FINDING of 05:18, cause posted with its profile before the code)

**Goal:** ROCm decode of several sequences on one MI50 well above one sequence's total, as Vulkan's is; Qwen3-8B Q8_0 f16 gave about 70 tok/s for four sequences against 66 for one, Vulkan 225-241.
**Cause** (rocprofv3 kernel trace, Qwen3-8B Q8_0 f16, 16-token prompts and 32 tokens, rig `ddev/rocm/p72`): one sequence took 9282 row kernel launches (q8_0_rows16_1, 807.6 ms, 87.0 us each), four sequences 37130 (3153.1 ms, 84.9 us each) and never a four-column build; the products were 77% and 80% of the device time. A pass gives one row run per entry (`model/passes.hpp`), and `RocmBackend::product_twin` launched run by run, so four sequences read every weight four times; four 16-token prompts likewise took 1440 tile calls against 288. Vulkan's `matmul_runs` joins neighbouring runs whose kernel and split match.
**Done:** `product_twin` joins neighbouring runs that are both generated rows, or both prompts of one `split_tiles_of`, into one run of launches; a decode column and a tile row give the same bits in any call, so no bit moves. backend-rocm adds every decode column of 1 to 64 rows given as one run a row, and two prompts side by side, each their bits alone.
**Measured** (one MI50, renderD131, default clocks, main d50b7a2bb / branch 8abb91d04 built alike from tarballs, Vulkan build 34c18feb4, `bench --p 16`, tg128 for one sequence, tg64 for 4, tg32 for 16, total tok/s, medians of three rotated rounds, rig `ddev/rocm/g73`):

## Wide decode for every type, steps 6c and 7: recorded, not built (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness, its own commit on step 5, steps 6c and 7 of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02 with XDEV's amendment and F2DEV's conditions)

**Goal:** step 6c, the draft length chosen by the tokens a verify is expected to keep a millisecond; step 7, more output reuse in the decode builds for verifies of 256 rows and more, only if production chooses such verifies (F2DEV's condition).
**Done:** 6c is already the server's rule, in the form XDEV's amendment (d) asks for, so nothing was built: `spec::draft_depths` takes the depth that gives the most tokens a millisecond from each request's chance of keeping each draft (`spec::Acceptance::keeps`) and the pass cost the scheduler measures as passes run (`spec::PassTimes` and the price table's decode cells in server time), never an offline table; a depth no better than the pass without drafts gives no drafts.
`generate` keeps `spec::draft_length` (the cap, the tokens left and the acceptance's rest): its verify of a long draft runs in passes of the mark's rows and ends at the first pass with a miss (step 6a), so a draft on prose costs at most one pass of 64 rows past its miss, and the CLI has no pass cost it measures to price with.
Step 7 does not run: the server verifies at most 63 drafts a request and 64 draft rows a pass (`kDraftRows`, `draft_max_` clamped to `spec::kVerifyRows - 1`) and `generate` at most 64 rows a pass, so no path verifies 256 rows or more and no DMAX replay can show production choosing them.
**Left:** step 7 comes back only if a later change lets a pass verify more than 64 rows a request; the CLI could price its depth from measured step and verify times if a workload needs it.
**Device gates (2026-11-03, rebased on main 672b6d998):** two findings fixed in their own commits.
Q1_0's one-column calls took the two-row build with the transposed reduction over 32 lanes whatever cluster their width gave, so on an MI50 a 96-wide call left its second row unwritten (`low-bits-vulkan`); that build now reduces as the one-row builds do (`row_tree_cluster`), as on main.
The whole-chunk check counted dispatches by name, and on the Radeon VII a call's chunks share one build's name, so it now counts the dispatches timed.
CTest passes on one MI50 under RADV and the Vulkan CTests on the Radeon VII under the AMD driver; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 logits on the Radeon VII are byte-identical to main's at ubatch 32, 45 and 96 and per token.

## Wide decode for every type, step 5: whole decode chunks in one dispatch, and no Q8_0 build past 32 columns (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness, its own commit on step 4, step 5 of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02 with XDEV's amendment and F2DEV's conditions)

**Goal:** a Q8_0 decode build past 32 columns, measured first and built only if it gains 10 percent or more at 64 to 256 columns (F2DEV's condition).
**Done:** measured first on one MI50 (renderD130, RADV), `--decode-rates Q8_0` on the Flash-Next shapes and the 27B down projection, four candidate builds against step 4, interleaved, medians of two runs each (before / candidate time).
32 columns in registers, 4 rows (`{32, 4, 2, tree, 1}`): int8 0.71 to 0.86x at 256 and 1024 columns on every shape; f16 1.02 to 1.07x on the large shapes and 0.86 to 0.92x on `hc_down`.
32 columns in registers, 2 rows: 0.53 to 0.85x everywhere.
32 columns in registers, two groups (64 a dispatch): f16 1.08 to 1.16x at 256 and 1024 (attn_qkv 1.16x, ssm_out and the 27B down projection 1.08x), but int8 0.67 to 0.88x and every shape 0.44 to 0.63x at 32 columns.
16 columns, four groups (64 a dispatch): 1.00 to 1.03x at 256 and 1024 on int8 and f16, and up to 1.66x at 64.
So no Q8_0 build past 32 columns gains 10 percent on int8, which production runs (`--dtype int8` on Flash-Next), and the one f16 gain would be an f16-only rule; none is built.
The gain at 64 columns came from the call's split instead: `for_each_column_chunk` put every whole chunk but the last in one dispatch and the last in a second, so a call of exactly two widest chunks (64 Q8_0 columns, 32 of the 16-column builds) ran two dispatches one after the other.
It now takes every whole chunk in one dispatch once there are two, and a rest, if any, in the narrowest build that holds it; a call of one chunk keeps the remainder path, where `filling_build` may spread a Q8_0 chunk of 2 to 8 columns.
Every column takes the build it took before, so the bits do not change; it is host code alone, and all 330 SPIR-V modules are byte-identical to step 4's (`cmp`).
`backend-vulkan` adds `check_whole_chunks`: Q8_0 and Q4_K decode calls of 64 and 256 columns run one product dispatch and 65 columns two, on a timed backend. The whole `backend-vulkan` passes on the MI50 (6 such calls witnessed); `dead-code` and `docs` pass.
Identity: `--decode-columns Q8_0,Q4_K,Q5_K,Q6_K,Q4_1,Q4_0,IQ4_XS,Q3_K,MXFP4`, every width to 1024, plain, residual, grouped and routed: 1,840,976 f16 and 1,840,976 int8 columns equal to the same columns alone.
Rates (`--decode-rates` over the same nine types, b a a b, step 4 against step 5, medians over six shapes and both activation widths, time before / after): at 32 columns Q4_K and Q5_K 1.22x, Q4_1 1.13x, Q4_0 1.09x, the others 1.06 to 1.07x and Q8_0 1.00x (one chunk for it); at 64 1.01 to 1.06x; at 256 1.00 to 1.01x; the largest cells are the small-row shapes, Flash-Next `hc_down` (320 rows) 1.9 to 2.2x at 32 and 64 columns and `shexp_gate` (640 rows) 1.9x at 32.
Examples, int8 (us, before -> after): Q4_K `shexp_gate` 2560x640 at 32 columns 59.3 -> 30.8, at 64 50.7 -> 45.5; Q4_K `hc_down` 10240x320 at 64 122.3 -> 61.6, at 256 228.6 -> 171.9; Q8_0 `hc_down` at 64 116.3 -> 67.4, `ssm_out` 6144x2560 at 64 189.6 -> 172.9.
Cells at 1, 8 and 16 columns, whose dispatches and modules are unchanged, read 0.77 to 1.66x in single cells with both runs of an arm agreeing (Flash-Next `hc_down` at 13 to 90 us), the harness's noise on identical work.
Whole model, one MI50, `bench --p 16 --n 32 --r 3 --seqs S`, b a a b against step 4, decode tok/s medians at S = 1 / 32 / 64: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 f16 422 / 2731 / 2721 -> 424 / 2647 / 2944, int8 421 / 3680 / 3828 -> 419 / 3698 / 4124; Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M f16 328 / 1478 / 1664 -> 331 / 1573 / 1759, int8 341 / 1676 / 1911 -> 344 / 1784 / 1979; Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M f16 82 / 310 / 335 -> 81 / 329 / 337, int8 92 / 387 / 418 -> 92 / 409 / 423.
The 0.6B f16 x32 median is one noisy run (2556 +- 54, the other 2739), where Q8_0 takes one chunk and nothing changed.
Greedy ids, 300 tokens, step 4 against step 5 on the MI50, f16 and int8: the same ids on all three files (6 of 6).
**Left:** F2DEV review; the plan's end gates (the Radeon VII, CTest on a device).
**Gotchas:** a call of exactly one widest chunk must keep the remainder path, or a Q8_0 device whose widest build holds 8 columns loses `filling_build` for its 8-column calls.

## Wide decode for every type, step 4: family A in the two-row body, and NVFP4's column loads (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness, its own commit on step 2, step 4 of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02 with XDEV's amendment and F2DEV's conditions)

**Goal:** the two-row decode builds for the F32, F16 and BF16 rows, a 16-column build among them, and the NVFP4 row kernel's wide build no slower a column than its one-column build.
**Done:** NVFP4, diagnosed first from the driver's statistics and disassembly on one MI50: the eight-column build used no scratch and 24 registers, but its column loop ran under the column count's branch inside the eight-value loop, so each of its 64 activation loads a step was a lone dword load followed by a wait (67 `buffer_load_dword`, 88 `s_waitcnt`, 72 branches), where the one-column build loads two vec4s.
The fix is small, so it is in this step: the eight weights of a step are decoded first, then each column loads its eight values as two vec4s and takes the same eight `fma` in the same order, so every column keeps its bits.
`matmul_row_two.glsl` takes the value rows (`LLMX_VALUES`, the plain, F16 and BF16 modules): each lane's vec4 steps in the one-row build's order and form (`acc += dot(w, x)`), a scalar loop where a row is not a multiple of four; `row_kernel_builds_two_rows` lists `matmul_row_f32`, `matmul_row_wf16` and `matmul_row_wbf16`, so they take the 2, 4, 8 and 16 column builds up to the profile's `row_decode_cols`.
Their calls stay in one dispatch (`is_values_row`, `for_each_column_chunk`): the fewest chunks that give two busy workgroups a compute unit, each in the narrowest build holding it, or in the one-row wide build where only its rows a workgroup give that, which keeps the old choice for few rows (Flash-Next `hc_down`, 320 rows); `filling_build` keeps the Q8_0 builds alone.
Grouped routed calls of value rows stop at 8 columns, as the K-quants do: at 1024 entries over 10 experts of 2560x640 the 16-column grouped build took 21.0 / 25.6 / 19.2 ms (F32 / F16 / BF16) against the 8-column one's 15.9 / 15.6 / 12.5.
Plain calls keep the 16-column build, which beat an 8-column cap at every count from 16: F32 2.0x, F16 1.4x and BF16 2.0x less time at 64 to 1024 columns (medians over five shapes).
SPIR-V: only the family's modules changed (`matmul_row`, `matmul_row_preserve`, `matmul_row_f32_only`, `matmul_row_wf16`, `matmul_row_wbf16`, `matmul_row_nvfp4`, `matmul_row_nvfp4_preserve`); the other 323 modules are byte-identical to step 2's build (`cmp`), the `moe_step_*` modules that share the one-row body among them.
Identity (one MI50, renderD130, RADV): `--decode-columns F32,F16,BF16,NVFP4`, every width to 1024, plain, residual, grouped and routed: 815,600 f16 and 815,600 int8 columns equal to the same columns alone.
Rates (`--decode-rates F32,F16,BF16,NVFP4`, b a a b, step 2 against step 4, medians over six shapes and both activation widths, time before / after): at 16 columns F32 1.67x, F16 1.76x, BF16 2.31x, NVFP4 4.87x; at 64 2.33x, 2.17x, 2.54x, 5.83x; at 1024 2.66x, 2.43x, 2.92x, 6.21x; one column level (0.99 to 1.01x), and no int8 cell below 0.95x.
Examples, int8, 27B ffn_down 17408x5120, 8 / 64 / 1024 columns (us): F32 1564->1054 / 12638->4093 / 184443->64954; F16 1495->818 / 11558->3914 / 182117->61909; BF16 1443->872 / 12015->3339 / 174007->53080; NVFP4 8530->1534 / 75752->12915 / 1277743->202840.
Whole model, one MI50, `bench --p 16 --n 32 --r 3 --seqs S`, b a a b against step 2, decode tok/s medians at S = 1 / 8 / 32 / 64: Qwen3-0.6B BF16 340 / 1007 / 1155 / 1181 -> 340 / 1238 / 2234 / 2349; Qwen3-0.6B F16 231 / 820 / 938 / 1014 -> 231 / 1029 / 1632 / 1856; Qwen3.5-0.8B NVFP4 259 / 191 / 200 / 221 -> 258 / 846 / 972 / 1085, so NVFP4 now scales (x64 / x1 0.85 -> 4.2).
Greedy ids, 300 tokens, step 2 against step 4 on the MI50: the same ids on all three files.
`check_f32_filling_builds` had run on the backend without timestamps, so it reported itself unwitnessed and checked nothing; it now runs on a timed backend and holds the value rows' chunking (one dispatch, one chunk for the largest call, the one-column build for the smallest) and every column to the same column alone.
**Left:** F2DEV review; the plan's end gates (`--isa` on the MI50 and the Radeon VII for the new builds, CTest on a device, byte identity and HF on the files); NVFP4 keeps its one-row builds, two-row NVFP4 builds being a further step if a file needs them; F16 decodes its halves with the software conversion and so gains less than BF16.
**Gotchas:** the plain module also serves Q8_0 rows of odd block counts (`matmul_row`), which never take a two-row build; the first cell of each shape in `--decode-rates` (the f16 one) can read up to 30 percent slow in both arms, so the int8 cells are the cleaner comparison.

## Wide decode for every type, step 2: families B and C in the two-row body (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness, its own commit on step 6b, step 2 of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02 with XDEV's amendment and F2DEV's conditions)

**Goal:** the two-row decode builds (2, 4, 8 and 16 columns, the transposed reduction, chunks side by side) for every quantized type on the integer dot outside the Q4 and K-quant families.
**Done:** `matmul_row_two.glsl` takes three more families, each with its one-column build's per-block dot, scale, add and contraction: the lookup types (IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS, IQ3_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ2_S, IQ2_XS, IQ2_XXS, IQ1_S, IQ1_M, TQ1_0, TQ2_0, Q1_0) through `lookup_group`, which hands a lane each 32-value group whatever block holds it (256 values in IQ4_XS and the TQ types, 128 in Q1_0, XDEV's amendment), so a type such as Q2_0 plugs in by its group decode with no second body; Q2_K and Q3_K with eight lanes a block and `k23_term`; MXFP4 with its integer dot and combined-scale range check.
A build with `LLMX_PRESERVE_F32` keeps its sums `precise`, as the one-column build does.
A product the one-column build repairs is flagged per row and column; a cluster holding one reduces by the butterfly, which carries the flags, and recomputes those rows with the one-column build's own repair (`lookup_float_twin`, `k23_float_twin`, `mxfp4_wide`), so the transposed reduction runs only where nothing is flagged.
`row_kernel_builds_two_rows` lists the new kernels, so their plain calls take the two-row builds and their grouped routed calls follow `grouped_variant`; Q1_0's two-row one-column build is now the family's variant 7 and its transposed reduction runs at its 32-lane cluster (`kLowBitsRowLanes`).
The Q4 and K-quant shaders' text is unchanged under the preprocessor: their 35 SPIR-V modules are byte-identical to step 6b's build (`cmp` of every `matmul_row_{q4,q5,q50,k,k4,k5}*` module).
Identity (one MI50, renderD130, RADV): `--decode-columns` on the 15 new types, every width to 1024, plain, residual, grouped and routed: 2,156,416 f16 and 2,156,416 int8 columns equal to the same columns alone.
Rates (`--decode-rates`, b a a b, the branch before the step against the step, medians, us): the new types' 180 cells a column count at 16 columns 2.16x median (up to 4.61x), at 64 2.68x (up to 4.25x), at 1024 2.92x (1.41 to 4.03x), at 1 column 1.01x; the routed shape keeps the one-column build per entry to 64 tokens and gains 1.5-1.6x from 256 through the grouped two-row builds.
Examples, int8, 27B ffn_down 17408x5120, 1 / 16 / 64 / 1024 columns: IQ4_XS 338->334 / 2466->884 / 9537->3238 / 150594->50144; Q2_K 245->222 / 2283->761 / 8821->2826 / 138831->43715; MXFP4 155->151 / 2100->678 / 8190->2488 / 129920->38382; IQ2_XXS 343->304 / 3614->855 / 12056->3012 / 174060->46086.
The Q4 and K-quant families' 588 cells: median 1.000, 0.78 to 1.14 at the extremes, all in cells of 9 to 113 us (same modules, so noise).
Whole model, one MI50, `bench --dtype int8 --p 16 --n 32 --r 3 --seqs S`, b a a b, decode tok/s at S = 1 / 8 / 32 / 64: Qwen3-0.6B IQ4_XS 269 / 714 / 860 / 926 -> 266 / 817 / 936 / 1055 (+14 percent at 64); IQ4_NL 281 / 738 / 894 / 964 -> 282 / 826 / 974 / 1099 (+14); IQ3_S 298 / 756 / 895 / 997 -> 292 / 860 / 995 / 1163 (+17); IQ2_XS 287 / 711 / 867 / 979 -> 288 / 801 / 962 / 1139 (+16). One sequence takes the one-column build as before (0.98-1.00x; the IQ3_S run of 287.5 beside 297.4 is its spread). On a 0.6B file the matrices are a smaller share of a pass than on the 27B shapes above, so the whole-model gain is below the kernel's.
The 6b ids check after the bounded argmax rows: Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M greedy, 300 tokens, main d50b7a2bb drafts off against the step with lookup at 63 drafts on the MI50: the same ids.
**Left:** F2DEV review; the plan's end gates (`--isa` on the MI50 and the Radeon VII for the new builds, CTest on a device, byte identity and HF on a family-B file); the K23 grouped cap at 8 columns is the K-quants' measurement, not re-measured for Q2_K and Q3_K.
**Gotchas:** a repair flag cannot ride the transposed reduction, whose lanes end holding different values, so a flagged cluster takes the butterfly; the flag reduction is a shuffle over the cluster, since the vote extension is not among the row kernels' required features.

## Wide decode for every type, step 6b: device argmax for verifies (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness, its own commit on step 6a, step 6b of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02 with XDEV's amendment and F2DEV's conditions)

**Goal:** a verify whose draws are plain argmax reads only its rows' ids, which the output device takes, rather than copying every row of the vocabulary to the host and taking the argmax there.
**Done:** `BatchEntry::argmax` asks for a row's argmax alone; a pass all of whose wanting entries ask so, on one output device that is not the CPU and implements `argmax_rows`, writes its logits rows into device memory (`ExecContext::argmax_logits`) and its ids into host-visible memory (`Model::argmax_buffers`, allocated once at the rows a verify takes and refused for good where the device cannot hold them).
`infer::plain_argmax` is the one rule: temperature 0, no repetition, presence or frequency penalty and no id masked by `ignore_eos` (XDEV's amendment, b); `generate` steps a verify with it (`Model::step(ids, n, argmax)`) and accepts through `infer::accept_ids`, which takes a row's id where the device gave one and draws a row whose largest logit is not finite or that holds a NaN from the row itself, read back (`Model::logits`), so every pick is `accept`'s.
The CPU keeps its rows on the host, where they are already and where a draw reads only up to its first miss, and so does a tensor group's head.
The fit counts those rows and their ids on the head's device where the path can be taken (`DeviceBudget::argmax`, set for a backend other than the CPU that implements `argmax_rows`; `Footprint::argmax_per_row`, off a tensor group), as many as a verify takes (`argmax_rows`: a mark's rows, or one for a step) and at most the logits rows it fits: 64 rows of a 248320-token vocabulary are 60.6 MiB; `Model::argmax_buffers` allocates that count and leaves a pass reaching past it on the host path; `placement` holds a device one byte short of them refused, at the logits rows and at the verify's rows, and the CPU not counted.
Only a model whose passes take argmax is charged for them (`ModelOptions::argmax_passes`, which `generate` and `chat` set and `serve` does not, `argmax_rows` giving 0 without it, so `Model::argmax_buffers` keeps such a model on the host path); `placement` holds a server's mark of 64 rows charged none, a verify's 64 and a step's 1.
The scheduler does not take the path yet (below), and the review found a server charged a mark's rows of logits for it, about 64 MB of KV at `--draft-max` 63 on a 248k vocabulary.
Profile, Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M (248320 tokens) on one MI50 at renderD130, greedy lookup at `--draft-max` 63, 18 verifies of 64 rows each all kept, three interleaved runs an arm, medians (ms): before, the step that waits for the pass 35.35 and the host's draw of the 64 rows 6.03 (0.094 a row), 41.4 a verify; after, the step 1.58 (it no longer waits) and the accept with its wait 33.75, 35.3 a verify (-15 percent). The head's write to device memory plus the device argmax take no longer than its write to host memory did, so the saving is the host's draw. Generation 561, 556, 565 -> 598, 602, 603 tok/s (+7 percent).
Identity against main d50b7a2bb drafts off: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M, greedy and seeded at temperature 0.8, 300 tokens, the branch drafts off and lookup at 3, 63 and 255 drafts, on one MI50 and on the CPU: 32 of 32 runs give main's 300 ids (the `--verbose` ids line).
Checks: `spec` adds `device_argmax`: the CPU backend's `argmax_rows` over 64 rows of 37 logits on few levels, with a NaN first and later, an infinity, nothing above negative infinity, half negative infinity and signed zeros, then 2000 verifies of random drafts kept or missed and random ends, `accept_ids` on those ids against `accept` on the rows (rows, last pick and every pick); `plain_argmax` refusing a penalty, presence and frequency penalties, `ignore_eos` and a temperature; the dense model's verify on one CPU keeping its rows and on CPUs playing a device over 1 and 2 stages keeping them on the device, each id the host argmax of the same rows and each row read back their bytes; and the rounds of the dense model on CPUs playing a device over 1 and 2 stages, every greedy run through argmax passes, against the run without drafts. `spec`, `sampler` and `server-spec` pass on the CPU.
**Left:** the plan's follow-up step, the scheduler's argmax passes: a pass whose wanting requests are all plain argmax without log-probabilities and without `on_retire` asks the same; not small enough to fold in here, since the draws run on the sampling pool and read `pass_logits` (which refuses an argmax pass), so the ids and the read-back of a row whose id says nothing must be taken on the scheduler thread first, and only a device reaches it, so its test is a device case in `server-resume`; the plan's end gates.
**Gotchas:** `Model::step(ids, n, true)` returns null once the rows stayed on the device, and `Model::logits(i)` then reads a row back, valid until the next call; the device returns the vocabulary size for a row with a NaN anywhere, where the host's scan takes a NaN only as its first score, so such a row must be drawn from the row and never from the id.

## Wide decode for every type, step 6a: drafts past 63 (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness, its own commit on step 3, step 6a of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02 with XDEV's amendment and F2DEV's conditions)

**Goal:** drafts of up to 1023 tokens (`spec::kMaxDrafts`) with no pass, mark or logits allocation of more rows than one verify pass, every token, draw, end and history those of the run without drafts.
**Done:** a verify pass feeds at most the model's mark rows (`Model::mark_rows`), which the commands set to `spec::verify_rows(--draft-max)`, at most `spec::kVerifyRows` (64), the rows the fit counts for the mark's saved inputs, the drafter's chain and the pass's logits.
`generate` verifies a longer draft in passes of those rows, each its own mark and retract; a pass takes the rest only where every draft before it was kept and its pick equals the rest's first draft, which it feeds as its last pick, so the rows sampled, the picks, the generator's draws, the last pick and the bonus token are one verify's (XDEV's amendment, a), and a miss ends the draft in its pass. The passes of one draft are one verify in the record.
A proposer on the model's devices drafts at most one pass (its chain's rows are the mark's); lookup drafts up to `--draft-max`. The server keeps 63 drafts a request a pass (`kDraftRows`), its `draft_max_` clamped so its mark and logits rows match what the command fitted, and `serve --draft-max` takes 1 to 63, refusing more as a usage error rather than taking fewer than asked (`drafts_flag`, F2DEV's review); `bench --drafter` times one pass, so its `--draft-max` stays 1 to 63.
So no allocation grows with the draft (XDEV's amendment, c): a 1024-row Flash-Next verify's logits alone would be 1.0 GB (248320 x 4 B a row), and the drafter's chain logits as much again a mark slot (`Footprint::drafter_cache`).
Checks: `spec` on the CPU, on the dense, routed and hybrid models over 1 to 4 stages with 32-row marks (31 drafts a pass): drafts of 32, 63, 64 and 100 with misses at the first draft, at 30, 31, 32, 62 and 63 and at the last, greedy and seeded at temperature 1.5 with a penalty, with and without an end token, prompts of 10 and 129 tokens, a verify past one pass witnessed by the record (`Run::deepest` above 31); limits of 31 to 100 tokens and a stop text in a later pass under 100 drafts; lookup shown the reply drafting 100.
**Left:** the chunk is 64 rows until a measurement of the mark and logits memory on Qwen3.6-27B-MTP and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next picks another (F2DEV); step 6b (above) keeps a greedy verify's logits rows on the device; the plan's end gates (CTest, the CPU suite, Qwen3-0.6B identity, `spec` and `split` on a device, drafts on and off at 1, 63, 64, 255 and 1023, a Flash-Next DMAX replay only where a production gain is claimed).
**Gotchas:** a pass's last row samples the pick that the rest's first draft is checked against, and that draft is fed as the next pass's last pick, so a whole draft feeds and samples exactly the rows of one verify; carrying the rest without that check would feed a draft no row confirmed.

## Wide decode for every type, step 3: grouped routed builds wide (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness, its own commit on step 1, step 3 of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02, taken before step 2 in F2DEV's order)

**Goal:** a routed call of many generated tokens, such as a verify of hundreds of drafts on a mixture-of-experts file, reading each expert's rows once a run in the wide decode builds rather than the one-row 8-column grouped build.
**Done:** the Q4 and K-quant families' grouped runs take their two-row builds of 4, 8 and 16 columns (variants 8, 9 and 10, `kRowGroupedByWidth`), each the plain build of its shape reading its columns through the grouping, so a column keeps the one-column build's bits; `grouped_variant` gives a call the narrowest that holds its entries an expert on average, wherever `column_builds` gives the kernel's plain calls the two-row builds, and the one-row grouped build elsewhere, so Q8_0, F32 and the other types are unchanged; `moe_group.comp` groups the entries in runs of the build's columns.
A grouped run stops at its entries (`GROUPED && c >= ncols`), where a plain chunk keeps computing every column its build holds.
Identity (one MI50, renderD130, RADV): `--decode-columns Q4_0,Q4_1,Q5_0,Q5_1,Q4_K,Q5_K,Q6_K`, every width to 1024 in plain, residual, grouped and routed calls (8 experts, 2 a token, so 8 tokens on take the grouped builds, 4, 8 and 16 columns in turn), 1,265,856 columns equal alone in each of f16 and int8.
Rates (`--decode-rates` on those types, m c c m twice, main's kernels against the step; ms, routed Flash-Next shape 2560 into 640, 512 experts, 10 a token):

| type, dtype | 256 tokens | 1024 tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K int8 | 2.33 -> 1.34 (1.74x) | 8.74 -> 4.61 (1.89x) |
| Q5_K int8 | 3.59 -> 1.68 (2.14x) | 14.04 -> 5.52 (2.54x) |
| Q6_K int8 | 5.86 -> 4.08 (1.44x) | 21.12 -> 12.30 (1.72x) |
| Q4_0 int8 | 2.89 -> 1.74 (1.66x) | 11.87 -> 5.45 (2.18x) |
| Q4_1 int8 | 2.93 -> 1.75 (1.67x) | 11.44 -> 5.34 (2.14x) |
| Q5_0 int8 | 6.23 -> 2.67 (2.34x) | 24.37 -> 7.53 (3.24x) |
| Q5_1 int8 | 5.10 -> 1.86 (2.75x) | 19.69 -> 5.79 (3.40x) |
| Q4_K f16 | 3.84 -> 2.39 (1.61x) | 15.20 -> 8.50 (1.79x) |
| Q5_K f16 | 4.53 -> 2.55 (1.77x) | 18.22 -> 8.78 (2.08x) |
| Q6_K f16 | 6.31 -> 5.62 (1.12x) | 23.87 -> 17.05 (1.40x) |

Q4_K int8 at 1024 tokens is 3.64 TMAC/s against 1.92; below 103 tokens (entries under two an expert) every call keeps the one-column build per entry, unchanged.
The 490 plain cells of the table keep their builds, median ratio 1.000; the outliers, 0.65 to 1.06, are each type's first one-column cell.
**Found** (scratch build forcing each grouped width, ms, int8, 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024 tokens, so 2.5 / 5 / 10 / 20 entries an expert): without the stop a run computed every column, so the 16-column build cost the same at 128 to 512 tokens (Q4_K 3.07, 3.09, 3.12) and the 4-column build won even at 1024 (Q4_K 5.12 against 6.16); with the stop the narrowest build holding the average wins or ties for Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0 and Q5_1 (Q5_0 2.05 / 2.66 / 3.84 / 7.53), while the K-quants' 16-column build with the stop was slower than their 8-column one at every count (Q4_K 8.01 against 4.79 at 1024, Q6_K 18.17 against 12.30, Q5_K 8.38 against 5.72; f16 likewise), so their grouped builds stop at 8 columns.
**Left:** F2DEV review; the plan's end gates (`--isa` on the MI50 and the Radeon VII, byte identity on a mixture-of-experts file, Flash-Next 2x2 verify timing); step 2's types join these builds there.
**Gotchas:** a grouped build's waste follows the runs, not the call: every touched expert has a partial run, so the width follows the entries an expert, not the call's width.

## Wide decode for every type, step 1: the identity and rate harness (2026-11-02, VDEV, branch test/wide-decode-harness on main d50b7a2bb, step 1 of VDEV's plan "wide decode, all types" of 2026-11-02, approved by XDEV with amendments and by F2DEV with conditions; tests only)

**Goal:** the gate and the baseline for the later steps: every weight type's decode columns held to the same column alone, and a per-type rate table at real shapes.
**Done:** `check_decode_columns` runs every weight type the device decodes at each of 1 to 64 columns (plain and output-head calls), the residual add and grouped calls at the narrow widths, and 8 experts routed 2 a token over 1 to 64 tokens; F32, Q4_1, Q4_K and Q8_0, one type a row family, also run 65, 96, 127-129, 255-257, 511-513, 1000, 1023 and 1024 columns in every call kind (F2DEV's grid).
The test's `matrix` gives every remaining type (Q2_K, Q3_K, the IQ types, NVFP4) bytes below 0x3c, which keep every half, E4M3 and packed scale finite.
Focused cells (XDEV): `llmx-backend-vulkan-test --decode-columns [TYPES]` runs only these cells, every width for the named types; `--decode-rates [TYPES]` prints, never asserts, us, TMAC/s and the builds that ran at 1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 256 and 1024 columns on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's shapes and Qwen3.6-27B's 17408 x 5120.
One MI50 (renderD130, RADV): the default cells pass, 1,853,048 columns in each of f16 and int8, in 78 s; the rate table takes 159 s.
Rate baseline, int8, TMAC/s at 1 / 64 / 1024 columns: Flash attn_qkv 2560x10240 Q8_0 0.24 / 5.03 / 5.35, Q4_K 0.41 / 4.07 / 4.37, IQ4_XS 0.18 / 0.50 / 0.51, Q3_K 0.23 / 0.51 / 0.52, MXFP4 0.42 / 0.60 / 0.61, F32 0.19 / 0.70 / 0.71; 27B ffn_down Q4_1 1.04 / 5.54 / 5.90; every type outside the Q4/Q5/K families and Q8_0 stays near 0.4-0.8 TMAC/s from 8 columns on.
Routed Flash shape (2560 into 640, 512 experts, 10 a token): every type keeps the one-column build per entry to 64 tokens and takes the grouped build from 256, Q4_K 0.39 / 1.16 / 1.91 and Q8_0 0.59 / 0.70 / 3.47.
