## ROCm F16 decode rows, two rows a wave (2026-11-01, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-f16-two-rows on main fb2e379d2; the f16 decode plan posted to F2DEV and XDEV at 2026-11-01 20:5x, probe 2 kept by p71)

**Goal:** the F16 class's decode products of Qwen3 Q8_0 on one MI50 toward Vulkan's with the same bits; 8B tg128 F16 was 68.3 tok/s against Vulkan's 77.5, the products 1.39 ms of the 1.7 ms a token gap (rig `ddev/rocm/p66`).
**Done:** every 16-bit twin build of the quarter-layout row kernel (`q8_0_rows` in `kernels/int16.hip`, `R` rows a wave) takes two output rows a wave: each lane's twin load and scale serve both rows, and each row keeps its lanes and its sum order, so its bits are the one-row build's; the host launches a wave for two rows in that class; the int8 class keeps one row.
**Found** (probes on the one-column build, same bits each, tg128 F16 medians, main / probe): four steps of loads ahead (56 VGPRs) lost, 8B 68.2 -> 65.2; two rows won, 8B 68.3 -> 70.2, 14B 38.0 -> 39.6, 0.6B 372 -> 382, its product 83.0 -> 80.5 us a call; four rows lost, 8B 65.4; two rows on aligned words and `alignbyte` lost against two rows on 16-bit loads (p71, renderD131: 8B 63.4 against 70.1, 0.6B 353 against 364, 14B 37.9 against 36.8 within spread), 84.2 us a call.
**Measured** (one MI50, renderD131, default clocks, Qwen3 Q8_0, main be0dbed72 / branch 6c1382597 built alike, tok/s; rig `ddev/rocm/g66` three interleaved rounds with Vulkan, `ddev/rocm/g66b` three base-head-head-base rounds):

| cell | main | branch | change | spread main / branch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8B f16 4 sequences tg64, total (g66b, 6 runs) | 65.81 | 70.59 | +7.3% | every round faster: +8.6%, +6.1%, +6.9% |
| 8B f16 tg128 (g66b, 6 runs) | 62.02 | 65.76 | +6.0% | every round faster: +9.0%, +4.4%, +4.5% |
| 8B f16 tg128 (g66) | 67.09 | 68.42 | +2.0% | 4.6% / 7.3% |
| 14B f16 tg128 (g66) | 35.80 | 37.76 | +5.5% | 11% / 10% |
| 8B f16 pp512 (g66) | 865.2 | 859.7 | -0.6% | 2.3% / 3.2% |
| 14B f16 pp512 (g66) | 483.0 | 478.5 | -0.9% | 3.0% / 4.2% |
| 0.6B f16 tg128 (g66) | 374.5 | 371.3 | -0.9% | 0.7% / 1.5% |
| 0.6B f16 tg128 (g66b, 6 runs) | 335.9 | 332.2 | -1.1% | 23% / 25%, rounds -0.5%, +4.5%, -6.9% |
| 0.6B f16 pp512 (g66) | 8763 | 8761 | -0.0% | 0.3% / 0.3% |
| 8B int8 tg128 (g66) | 70.98 | 70.82 | -0.2% | 0.4% / 0.7% |
| 0.6B int8 tg128 (g66) | 363.7 | 364.7 | +0.3% | 2.2% / 0.5% |

The 0.6B and 14B decode cells are wide: the machine's load rose from 12 to 24 during g66b, which a host-bound 0.6B step feels, and 0.6B is at most about 1% slower, within its spread; g66's ordered rounds favoured the first arm of a round, which g66b's base-head-head-base order cancels.
The gain is in the kernel's own time (83.0 -> 80.5 us a call, timestamps), not host code, so the code-layout band of the single host translation unit does not apply.
Registers (gfx906 resource usage, plain and 16-bit-dot modules alike, main / branch, VGPRs and waves a SIMD): rows16_1 35/46, 7/5; rows16_2 46/62, 5/4; rows16_4 70/89, 3/2; rows16_8 118/141, 2/1; rows16_16 60/80, 4/3; no scratch; the rows8 builds keep their VGPRs.
**Identity:** device byte identity against main on Qwen3-8B Q8_0 (256 tokens) and Qwen3-14B Q8_0 (128 tokens) at f16 and int8, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 16k raw and chat-template sequences at f16, and Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on the CPU; backend-rocm passes, with every decode column of 1 to 64 generated rows the column alone, bit for bit, in both forms on rows 4096, 1280 and 1312 wide, the residual add and a group of three, and a decode group of 41, 104 and 63 rows equal to each projection alone, which takes the odd row a wave's second row falls past; CTest 80/80; docs and dead-code clean; the suite on rocm:0 passes but for reference-consumer, half-weights, moe and vision, each the ROCm backend refusing an op the branch does not reach (group_rms_norm, F16 and BF16 weights, routed_experts, layer_norm); int8's dense f16 HF logit errors 0.00011 and 0.00013, the same bits as main.
**Gates after the rebase:** builds of main fb2e379d2 and the head pass, and CTest passes 80/80 on the device; reviewed by F2DEV; the change lands by fast-forward.
The suite on rocm:0 fails reference-consumer, half-weights, moe and vision on main fb2e379d2 and on the head alike, measured with both built the same way: each is the device refusing an op it lacks (routed_experts among them), which the components should report as SKIP through `common.device_lacks_kernel` rather than FAIL; that skip path is the follow-up.
**Gotchas:** four sequences on ROCm decode barely faster in total than one (about 66 against 62 tok/s at 8B, Vulkan 225-241 for four), on main and the branch alike: the cause was one row kernel launch per sequence (ROCm products join adjacent runs into one launch, above).

## The sampler's row scans in lanes of eight (2026-11-01, SDEV, branch perf/sampler-scan on main 2e77b49ab, plan A of SDEV's sampling post of 20:45, approved by F2DEV at 20:53)

- **Goal:** a code reply's verify on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 samples about 10.6 rows a round on the scheduler's thread, 2.15 ms a round, nearly all of it greedy's scalar maximum over 248320 logits, about 5% of a one-user code reply; scanning the row in vector lanes with the same result should take most of that off.
- **Done:** `detail::argmax` takes greedy's maximum, and the best score of a draw over every token, in two sets of eight AVX2 lanes and a scalar tail, with the scalar loop's rule unchanged: ties to the lowest id across lanes and tail, a NaN only as the first id taking part, that first id for a row with nothing above negative infinity, the masked id passed over.
  The heap pass of a top-k or nucleus tests eight scores at a time against the worst score it holds and the ones not below it again one by one, so the kept set is the same.
  The CPU backend's `argmax_rows` keeps its own rule, the invalid id for a NaN anywhere or a row without a finite score, which the embedded drafter reads, so the two scans stay apart.
  `sampler` holds both scans to scalar ones on rows whose sizes are not multiples of the lanes, with leaders, ties, NaN and infinities at the first id, the last lane of a block and the tail, and 4000 random rows with masks; planted faults (a tie to the higher id across lanes, a prefilter dropping equal scores and NaN, the masked id read in the lanes) each fail it.
- **Measured (CPU microbench of `infer::sample` on the rig's EPYC, 248320 scores a row, 11 rows a round, main 2e77b49ab / branch, us a row, two interleaved runs):** greedy cold 176-177 / 60-61, warm 155-159 / 35; greedy with the end masked cold 173-176 / 61; top-k 40 top-p 0.95 at 0.8 cold 157-158 / 77-79, warm 144-146 / 48; penalty 1.1 cold 224 / 100-108; a row's read floor cold 60, warm 17.
- **Measured (card A/B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 on four MI50s, main 2e77b49ab / branch, medians of 6 interleaved runs, decode tok/s):** one user code 266.4 / 277.3 (+4.10%, spreads 1.3% / 3.3%), seeded code 267.8 / 278.4 (+3.94%, spreads 0.8% / 0.5%), prose 60.9 / 60.8 (-0.16%, spreads 8.2% / 5.6%), four users' sum 80.5 / 80.4 (-0.11%, spreads 2.9% / 9.0%) and wall 326.9 / 328.5 s (+0.47%); the code cells gain outside the spread, the others are level, and every reply is the same bytes in every run and arm.
- **Gates:** CTest and the CPU suite pass on the CPU, raw-blocks without `--require-tools` where the image has no numpy; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 against main on the CPU gives the same bytes for greedy, seeded, full-row sampled and chat replies and for the prompt's logits, timing lines left out.
  The change lands by fast-forward.
- **Left:** the hosted run; plan B, a verify's rows sampled in parallel, waits for these numbers.

## Tree drafting closed at step 1: no single rule and no branch clears the spread (2026-11-01, SDEV, plan-tree-drafting reopened by the owner on 2026-10-31, step 1 approved by F2DEV at 12:19 with XDEV's point of 12:18, docs only)

- **Question:** step 0 (2026-10-31) found history forks worth a look on code edits and copies: at a lookup miss, another earlier occurrence had proposed the right token at 0.49 and 0.53 of misses. Step 1 prices, offline, whether a better single choice of occurrence (no extra rows) or one branch at the first point where occurrences disagree (extra rows on every pass that carries it) pays, by the rule set before it ran: build a single rule if it reaches 70% of the tree's gain, close if neither clears a main/main spread of about 2%.
- **Replay:** each recorded reply of step 0 (23 cases in six types a model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 and Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 over two MI50s) token by token: a history draft wherever the last 8 tokens occur earlier, its length by match bucket at production's mean depth (20, 20, 40, 63), else the case's next recorded MTP verify. Each verify is priced by measured decode cells: Flash-Next from production's stage 1 at band 5 (doubled for its two stages), the 27B from both stages of a two-card rig run at band 0, each made non-decreasing in rows; four users run four rotations of a type's cases, one verify each a pass, the pass priced at their summed rows. Production keeps no token ids, so it enters only as a weight: history drafts are 10% of its verifies (68.6k of 671k since start on 2026-11-01).
- **Rules:** main (`Lookup::convincing`, the furthest backward match); a, the latest occurrence; b, the furthest match without the stop at 32; c, the most frequent continuation; d, the occurrence the last kept verify followed; O, an oracle that picks the occurrence keeping most; T, main plus one branch at the first divergence point from the latest disagreeing occurrence (at most 32 rows, within 63); Tg, T gated by a per-request fork-hit average from a shadow check against the branch's price; TO, T with the branch moved to the trunk's actual miss and its best occurrence (an upper bound at T's row cost).
- **Result** (ms a token against main, positive faster):

| model, users | a | b | c | d | O (oracle) | T | Tg | TO (oracle) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flash-Next, 1 | -1.13% | +0.05% | -1.73% | +0.05% | +0.49% | -0.94% | -0.06% | -0.82% |
| Flash-Next, 4 | -1.52% | +0.08% | -1.06% | +0.08% | +0.76% | -0.41% | +0.01% | -0.27% |
| 27B, 1 | -0.86% | +0.02% | -1.75% | +0.02% | +0.93% | -2.53% | -0.32% | -2.20% |
| 27B, 4 | -1.07% | +0.02% | -2.24% | +0.02% | +1.08% | -3.35% | -0.42% | -2.95% |

- **By type, on main's own path** (history draft points, main's misses, then recovered and extra misses against main for a, c and b/d): Flash-Next code edit 137, 45, a 0/15, c 1/8, b/d 0/0; copy 307, 67, a 0/44, c 0/27, b/d 2/0; code write 314, 296, all within 5. The best cell of any non-oracle rule is T on Flash-Next's code edit at four users, +1.8%, and it loses at one user (-1.6%); every other type is within 0.3% for b, d and Tg.
- **Why closed:** neither a single rule nor a branch clears 2% on either model, and the oracles' ceilings (O up to 2.4%, TO up to 2.0% in one cell) are unattainable bounds. Step 0's s of 0.49 and 0.53 was measured against the latest-occurrence rule, which fix/lookup-longest-match replaced: on main's path only 5 of Flash-Next's 45 code-edit misses had another occurrence with the right token, and the latest rule itself adds 15 and 44 misses on code edit and copy while recovering none. No step 2.
- **Reopen if:** a proposer gives several plausible continuations where main's one misses (a draft model's second choice, or a history with many diverging copies), measured by the same replay (rig `sdev/tree/step1.py`, outputs `step1_fl.txt` and `step1_27.txt`).

## The embedded drafter one pass ahead: closed as measured (2026-11-01, SDEV, branch feat/draft-tail 998daca92 on main c92d2d353, kept on gitea, closed by F2DEV's ruling of 12:19 after the profile the owner asked for on 2026-10-31)

- **Goal:** a request drafting from the embedded drafter sits a pass out each round while its chain runs; a draft tail ran the chain's steps after the head of the verifying pass, in the same submission, its drafts serving the next pass where the verify kept every draft and the pick was the tail's guess.
- **Measured** (Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 layer-split over two MI50s, `--drafter embedded --draft-max 63`, greedy, main / tail / tail / main, 2026-10-31 19:25-21:52, every reply the same bytes), decode tok/s: a1 code edit, one user, 36.46, 35.56 against 32.20, 32.86 (-9.7%); prose, one user, mean of four 23.37 against 16.18 (-31%); prose, four users, per request 9.36 against 7.67 (-18%); four code edits at once, aggregate 32.45, 31.66 against 34.63, 20.45.
- **Profile** (per-pass logs): a1 took 231 tail passes, 193 of them 64-row lookup tails, none landing right, 13868 rows against 1478, and each tail pass waited on its chain before it recorded (median 222 ms, the whole host gap); b5 lost (193 s against 159 s) although 1147 of its 1256 landings were right.
- **Why closed:** the tails given whatever they land and their 64-row size are a gate and a cap, but the wait is the design: a tail's pass records only after its chain, serializing what was meant to overlap, and it loses even where tails land right.
- **Reopen if:** the chain can run without delaying the tail's recording.

## Steady drafting is seen by the reply's positions (2026-11-01, SDEV, branch fix/steady-drafting-by-position on main 2a6740508, the coordinator's ask of 04:15)

- **Goal:** the hosted macos-15-intel runner once failed `server-spec` with "steady drafting, the hybrid model with its embedded drafter on one CPU: 0 drafts fed in steady state" (job 124723419632) and passed on a re-run.
- **Found:** a test fault, not a drafting one: `steady_holds` took the scheduler's counters when its reader read the 60th and the 300th token, and a reader starved on a slow machine reads token 60 after the reply has passed 300, so both snapshots are the end's, the window holds no drafts, and the holds check passes without having looked.
- **Done:** the failing test (the reader starts only once the reply has ended, which makes that case certain), then the counters are taken on the scheduler's thread as the first pass retires whose history has reached each end (`Scheduler::on_retire`), so the window follows the reply's positions however late its tokens are read; what it requires is unchanged.

## ROCm prompt tile loads at 32-bit byte offsets (2026-11-01, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-tile-off32 on perf/rocm-tall-w2 9990896f9, which it lands after; step 3 of the global-traffic plan (DDEV 01:18), approved by F2DEV at 01:21)

**Goal:** no 64-bit address arithmetic in the tile's loads with the same bits: the weights' extra word, the twin's words and its scales took a 64-bit shift and add a load, as a pointer indexed by a 32-bit value is widened before its scale.
**Done:** every load of `q8_0_tile` reads at a 32-bit byte offset off a uniform base (`at` in `kernels/int16.hip`), which the existing bound at the tile's launch already covers (`rocm_backend.cpp`: the weights' span plus 64 bytes and the twin's 64 rows and blocks in bytes below 2^32), so every load takes its base from scalar registers and its offset from one vector register.
**Found** (gfx906 code objects of the dot16 build, the main loop, against e50a809d2): tile8_tall 113 -> 110 VGPRs, 949 -> 930 instructions; tile16_tall 98 -> 94, 1588 -> 1566; tile8 82 -> 78, 1107 -> 1070; tile16 85 -> 82, 899 -> 877; every loop load now global_load with an saddr base, none through a 64-bit vector address; no scratch, two waves a SIMD.

## ROCm tall tile weight staging, two threads a row (2026-11-01, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-tall-w2 on main 3418d0b2c; step 2 of the global-traffic plan (DDEV 01:18), approved by F2DEV at 01:21)

**Goal:** fewer weight-load instructions in the int8 tall tile with the same bits: its 128 output rows took four threads a row in two passes, each a quarter block as three 4-byte words, where the Vulkan tile takes two threads a row, a 16-byte load and a word each.
**Done:** a weight row takes 256 / outputs threads (`WT` in `q8_0_tile`, `kernels/int16.hip`), two on the tall build and four on the 64-output one, each its share of a block's quants as one vector load of 4-byte-aligned words (`QWords`) and the word before or after, realigned and stored as before: the same bytes in the same shared-memory words. The twin's staging is unchanged. `backend-rocm` adds a tall matrix 4128 wide, 129 blocks, so a tall tile's rows start on alternating halves of a word, against the 64-output build's bits.

## ROCm block-major twin (2026-11-01, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-twin-major on perf/rocm-tall-stage b0af9f978, which it lands after; step 1 of the global-traffic plan (DDEV 01:18), approved by F2DEV at 01:21)

**Goal:** the int8 tall tile within reach of Vulkan's call time with the same bits: the 8-bit twin's rows lay 4096 bytes apart on the 8B, so a tile stage's 64 rows of block k fell on the same memory channels (knockouts: one X row for every row took the 8B gate,up from 5.62 to 5.02 ms a call, Vulkan 4.99).
**Done:** one layout (`TwinMap` in `rocm_backend.cpp`, its kernel copy in `kernels/f32.hip`) chosen from the call's runs, the consumer each run takes: a generated run row after row as the row kernels read it, a prompt's run block-major, block k of every row of its region together, the rows padded to an odd multiple of 4 (`twin_map`); neighbouring runs of one kernel share a region, and more than eight regions lay every row row after row. The twin is sized from the map; the padding is at most 7 rows a region and sits inside `scratch_reserve`, which the fit leaves out. Producers (`rms_norm_rows`, `silu_mul` from their runs, the per-row attention from its views) write it as the product of those runs reads it, and a product whose runs give another map makes its own; a block's row comes from its number by a multiply and a shift. The tile reads its twin through row and block strides in `TileCall`, under the 32-bit offset bound. Both twins, block-int16 and block-int8, since the one tile reads both. `backend-rocm`: prompt rows at 1, 4, 5, 12, 13, 20, 21, 63, 64, 65, 70 and 129 (512 wide) and 261 and 520 (4096 wide, the tall build) block-major give the bits of the same rows read row after row, a call of four runs of both kernels gives each run's bits alone, and producers given mixed and prompt runs, and attention of a 5-row prompt, give the bits of a product of a copy.
**Found** (probe build d09efa2b5 and 643552644, rocprofv3 kernel traces, pp512, one MI50, renderD131, ms a call): 8B int8 gate,up tall 5.49 -> 5.13 (-6.6%), qkv tall 1.53 -> 1.43, short tile 2.08 -> 1.76 (-15%); 14B int8 gate,up 8.89 -> 8.32 (-6.4%), short 3.01 -> 2.70 (-10%), so the 5120-wide rows gain as the 4096-wide do; F16 8B gate,up 8.08 -> 7.73, short 2.96 -> 2.80. The producers pay for the scattered writes: 8B silu_mul with its twin 0.158 -> 0.200 ms, the norm 0.055 -> 0.061, the product's own twin 0.039 -> 0.050 (first build, with a division a value, 0.217, 0.076 and 0.056).
**Measured at 55515e402** (map-free producer builds) against perf/rocm-tall-stage at b0af9f978 and Vulkan at 98bd6223c on one MI50 (renderD131, CPUs 14,15, default clocks, all built alike from archives, 2026-11-01 03:24-04:08 UTC, rotated interleaved rounds of three runs, three in int8 and six in F16, Vulkan in rounds 1 to 3 on the 8B and 14B, tok/s medians, raw rig ddev/rocm/g61/log.txt; other cards of the machine busy, load 9 to 23, mon.log beside it). tg1 is the decode after each prompt, both depths together; tg128 is 128 tokens after a 16-token prompt. 55515e402 differs from the branch head only in which product the per-row attention's running sum fuses, the same instructions.

Layout never changes a value, so a wrong map shows only as wrong bits against a row-major read, which is what `backend-rocm` compares; the 14B F16 short tile's median is bimodal in both arms (4.5 or 7.1 ms), so read that cell over rounds.

## The tiled prompt attention splits a row's history into parts (2026-10-31, MDEV, branch perf/prompt-attention-split on main c92d2d353, F2DEV's ruling (d) of 09:08 on perf/ts-copy-queue and approval of 15:21)
- **Goal:** a prompt pass at depth fills the card: at 65k tokens of history a 128-row pass of Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 over two MI50s spent 551 ms a card in `attention_tile_d256_kv16_x8` (16 layers), one workgroup per 32-row tile and head walking the whole history (48 workgroups on 60 CUs), against 2921 ms for 1024 rows, where the card is full (RDEV, 09:24). The ceiling is the 1024-row rate, about 370 ms a card at 128 rows, not the 254 ms of a pass without history.
- **Done:** `attention_tile.comp` takes a part index: with nsplit above 1 a workgroup walks the tokens of one part of `DeviceProfile::attention_tile_part` tokens from position 0 and writes each row's maximum, sum and unscaled accumulation; `attention_merge.comp` merges them (a lane takes splits lid, lid + 256, in chunks of 1024 weighed in split order, so no history length is refused) and writes the 8-bit twin in the integer-dot tile's block-major layout (`xquant8_block` takes `major`); `VulkanBackend::wide_attention` runs the tile whole while every row of the call fits one part, else tile and merge, cut over whole tiles where the parts' scratch would pass `attention_scratch_cap_` (64 MiB). `check_tile_split` in backend-vulkan: rows across the first part's end and three parts deep against the CPU, a prompt within one part alone and beside a merged one (output and twin through a projection), and slices of 16 and 32 against the whole prompt; `vulkan-lifetime` sets the cap to one byte through `VulkanLifetimeTest`, so the call is cut into pieces of one tile, and requires the uncut call's bytes, output and twin.
- **Part size (taken on the first build, before the twin fix, which changes no timing path but cut calls' twin layout; one MI50, renderD131, int8, f16 caches, a measurement-only probe forking one filled depth, arms interleaved in one process, medians of 4 rounds, pass ms unsplit -> parts of 1024 (2048, 4096)):**
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M: 16k 128 rows 598 -> 471 (481, 490), 256 1039 -> 757 (916, 938), 512 1912 -> 1500 (1495, 1823), 1024 3662 -> 3009 (2998, 3007); 64k 2154 -> 1462 (1455, 1644), 3667 -> 2929 (2897, 2873), 6732 -> 5848 (5793, 5752), 13217 -> 11693 (11569, 11526); 128k 4238 -> 2863 (2894, 2885), 7206 -> 5690 (5757, 5703), 13006 -> 11400 (11581, 11442), 25668 -> 22796 (23269, 22948).
  - Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1, all 24 heads on the card: 16k 642 -> 603 (603, 613), 1254 -> 1174 (1175, 1175), 2380 -> 2325 (2321, 2316), 4568 -> 4599 (4588, 4578); 64k 1297 -> 1121 (1118, 1114), 2541 -> 2212 (2201, 2198), 4636 -> 4428 (4400, 4393), 8713 -> 8745 (8776, 8745); 128k 2155 -> 1809 (1810, 1804), 4206 -> 3568 (3582, 3569), 7549 -> 7050 (7064, 7054), 13984 -> 14118 (14219, 14111).
  - Every row count reaches the kernel's own rate at that depth; a 1024-row pass of the 27B already fills the card, so there the merge costs 0.4 to 1.0 percent, which no per-batch choice can avoid, since a row past one part always takes the merge. 1024 is best or within 1 percent everywhere and clearly best for the 30B at 16k; it is the profile's value.
- **Bits:** a row whose history and position fit one part keeps main's bytes, the merge of its one non-empty part weighing exp(0) = 1 and its last step the tile's own division; a row past the first part changes numbers (F32 throughout), so it is held to HF.
  Within a part the tile's steps are op for op the unsplit kernel's, the cross-part combine is the decode merge's, and what changes is where the online softmax rescales: unsplit, one running maximum and accumulator cross every part in token order; split, each part starts its own and the merge rescales each part's accumulator once by exp(m_part - M).
  The unsplit order cannot be kept, since each part would need the running state of the part before it, which serializes the parts again.
- **Numerics (MI50 Vulkan, renderD131):** the 16k raw and chat sequences of Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 against DDEV's file-exact f16 HF reference, exact / accepted tie / miss of 512: split f16 raw 512/0/0, chat 512/0/0, int8 raw 505/4/3, chat 502/7/3; main f16 512/0/0 both, int8 raw 509/1/2, chat 505/6/1. The largest HF gap at a miss is 0.25 on both arms, inside the long-context margin of 0.5.
  A first build missed 180 of 512 (f16 chat): a call cut by the scratch cap laid out each piece's twin for the piece's rows; the merge now takes the call's rows and twin layout, and `vulkan-lifetime`'s cut case fails without that and passes with it.
  The qwen35 4096-token windows (baseline_qwen35.py --context 4096 on vulkan:0), NLL delta against HF / bound, main -> split: Qwen3.5-0.8B Q8_0 whole excerpt 0.0038145 -> 0.0038147 / 0.02, windows 0.0033698 -> 0.0033710 / 0.02; Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M 0.0188935 -> 0.0188961 / 0.021, 0.0186932 -> 0.0186951 / 0.025; Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M 0.0262312 -> 0.0262268 / 0.07, 0.0260309 -> 0.0260285 / 0.08; every check of the three files passes on both arms.
  HF on the fixtures: 512-token windows never reach a second part, so their bytes are main's; the baseline component on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 (the qwen3 fixture on the machine) passes with output identical to main's.
- **Identity against main (built the same way from archives):** Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M, generate, logits and perplexity at 512, on the MI50 and the CPU: 12 of 12 the same bytes, as no row there passes one part.
- **Tests (MI50, renderD131):** CTest 94 of 94 at this code; the device suite on vulkan:0 passing at the code before the chunked merge, which gives the same bytes on the 0.6B's 16k raw sequence, generate, logits and perplexity; `vulkan-lifetime`'s case past one chunk fails on that code, where the call was refused, and passes here (largest error 5.0e-7).
- **One card at this code (renderD131, default clocks, main 65744909c against the branch, both built from archives, order main / branch / branch / main, bench pp512 at depth 16384, 3 runs each, tok/s; load 6 to 10 from production and DDEV builds on other CPUs, which ran through the 27B's second branch run):** Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M main 300.63, 287.06; branch 316.08, 314.69 (+7.6 percent). Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 main 228.88, 225.72; branch 227.68, 213.74 (+-4.42), level within the noise, as the probe found a 512-row pass at 16k (2380 -> 2325 ms).
- **Production-shaped cells (GPUs 4-7, default clocks, both arms built the same way from archives, main 65744909c against the branch, order main / branch / branch / main, monitor kept; load 5.5 to 21 from production and other builds on other cards and CPUs):**

## The hc down product's scaled SiLU as the Q8_0 decode kernel's tail: closed as measured (2026-11-01, VDEV, probe 2 of VDEV's 2x2 decode proposals, approved by F2DEV at 2026-10-31 18:33 for the SiLU alone, its second form ruled at 2026-11-01 01:33 and closed by its rule; code kept on gitea branch probe/silu-tail)

**Goal:** a shorter decode step on Flash-Next 2x2 with the same bits, by ending the hyper-connection mix's down product (`matmul` of Q8_0 rows 10240 wide into 320, then `silu_scaled`) in one dispatch.
**The design (on probe/silu-tail):** `Backend::matmul_silu`, by default `matmul` then `silu_scaled`; on Vulkan, where the call takes the Q8_0 decode kernel in one dispatch, a build of it with `LLMX_SILU_TAIL` runs the product as a function and then `silu_scaled.comp`'s scalar code (shared through `silu_scaled.glsl`) and its twin. The decode kernel and `silu_scaled` are both preserving modules, so the bits match by construction. First form: the dispatch's last workgroup made the whole output. Second form: each unit of 32 output rows of each column chunk was made by its own last workgroup, on counters zero between calls.
Checks that passed on an MI50 (RADV), both forms: `backend-vulkan` held `matmul_silu` to `matmul` then `silu_scaled` bit for bit over 2,024,960 values, the output and a Q8_0 product of the twin it leaves, at 1 to 33 decode rows and a 128-row prompt, f16 and int8, ordered and unordered, the tail running in 11 builds. Identity against main on Flash-Next 2x2 with lookup and MTP drafts was the same bytes.
**Measured:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 (four MI50s, GPUs 4-7, CPUs 4-7 and 10-13), production flags (--tensor-width 2 --layer-shares 1,1 --dtype int8, f16 KV), default clocks, `bench --p 64 --n 64 --r 5` with the MTP head at --draft-max 3, 6 runs an arm in ABBA rounds, rig load 12 to 25 from other work. Medians of main e095a0020 against each form:
- First form: tg64 51.73 / 52.90 tok/s (-0.43 ms a token); bench step 21.49 / 21.64 ms (+0.15); 3-draft verify 28.58 / 28.94 ms (+0.37). Rig `vdev/holds/abc`.
- Second form: tg64 51.76 / 52.22 tok/s (-0.17 ms a token); bench step 21.55 / 21.35 ms (-0.20); 3-draft verify 28.79 / 28.92 ms (+0.13). Rig `vdev/holds/abd`.
**Why closed:** F2DEV's rule for the second form was -0.2 ms in every column, the verify included, which production's MTP replies mostly run. Both forms lose on the verify. A tail only for one decode row was ruled out as a second selection rule for a path production rarely takes.

## A tensor group's join summed and injected in one dispatch: closed as measured (2026-11-01, VDEV, probe 1 of VDEV's 2x2 decode proposals, path (a) approved by F2DEV at 2026-10-31 18:33, closed by F2DEV's ruling of 2026-11-01 01:33; code kept on gitea branch probe/join-fusion)

**Goal:** a shorter decode step on Flash-Next 2x2 with the same bits, by making a tensor group's join (the group's sum, then `inject_streams`) one dispatch instead of two with a barrier between them.
**The design (on probe/join-fusion):** below the two-shot size the collective only exchanges the partial rows (`Collective::exchange_in_place`) and each member's join sums and injects them in one kernel (`Backend::sum_inject`, `shaders/sum_inject.comp`, the sum shared with `sum_rows.comp` through `sum_rows.glsl`).
The inject is built preserving and `sum_rows` without float controls, whose subnormal handling Vulkan leaves to the driver, so the fused kernel measures it: `measure_plain_sums` runs `sum_rows` once per device on operands that tell flushed operands from flushed results and either zero, and the rule becomes specialization constant 18, followed add by add in the fused kernel with no branch per element; a device whose answers fit no one rule keeps the two ops and says so once. RADV on the MI50 measures rule 15 (operands and results flushed to signed zeros).
Checks that passed on an MI50 (RADV): `backend-vulkan` (the fused join against the collective's sum and `inject_streams`, 2,004,880 values with subnormal and cancelling partials) and `--isa` exit 0; `vulkan-quantization` (every consistent rule forced and held to a sum written in the test); identity against main on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M on one card and on Flash-Next 2x2 with lookup and MTP drafts. Not run on the Radeon VII.
A variant that also took the norm after the join was slower (49.49 against 51.63 tok/s, one slice a group) and lowered 1/sqrt differently between modules, so it was dropped.
**Measured:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 (four MI50s, GPUs 4-7, CPUs 4-7 and 10-13), production flags (--tensor-width 2 --layer-shares 1,1 --dtype int8, f16 KV), default clocks, `bench --p 64 --n 64 --r 5` with the MTP head at --draft-max 3, three ABBA rounds, 6 runs an arm, rig load 12 to 25 from other work; medians main e095a0020 / probe: tg64 51.73 / 52.24 tok/s (19.33 / 19.14 ms a token, -0.19 ms), bench step 21.49 / 21.35 ms (-0.14), 3-draft verify 28.58 / 28.68 ms (+0.10). Raw data in rig `vdev/holds/abc`.
**Why closed:** -0.14 to -0.19 ms misses the -0.2 ms rule set before the run, and the verify, which production's MTP replies mostly run, is level. A single first sample (-0.44 ms) had overstated it.
**Picking it up:** if the group sum's share of a step grows (more members, wider sums), rebase probe/join-fusion and time it again; the float-mode design above is what keeps it bit-identical on any driver.

The tall staging (cause 2, 20:26-20:43, against dbb6892f6's code at 9fcec1155, 3 interleaved rounds of 3, tok/s medians): staged after the barrier, the 16-bit twin's tall build takes 99 VGPRs where it took 124 and gains, 8B F16 pp512 779.1 -> 785.2 (+0.8), pp2048 712.5 -> 717.9 (+0.8), every run above every base run, 14B 442.1 -> 445.1, 408.6 -> 414.1; the 8-bit twin's tall build in four blocks after the barrier, Vulkan's arrangement (100 VGPRs, 27.6 KB of LDS, 2 waves, scratch 0), loses, 8B int8 -0.9 and -0.8 percent, 14B -0.6 and -0.6, its gate,up 5.73 ms a call against 5.62 (Vulkan 4.99), so the int8 gap is the dot loop, not the staging; an int8 tall step of two blocks after the barrier compiles to 99 VGPRs and was not timed, since the four-block one already lost.
**Done:** the tall build over the 16-bit twin loads its step after the barrier; the int8 builds and the 64-output builds are unchanged. One function holds both, the step's blocks and whether it loads ahead its template parameters (`TileStep`).
**Measured at bfb1db815** against dbb6892f6 on one MI50 (renderD130, CPUs 14,15, default clocks, both built alike from archives, 2026-11-01 00:12-00:28 UTC, six rotated rounds of three runs in F16 and three in int8, tok/s medians, raw rig ddev/rocm/g58/log.txt): Qwen3-8B Q8_0 F16 pp512 780.2 -> 785.5 (+0.7%, every run above every base run), pp2048 713.7 -> 719.1 (+0.8%); Qwen3-14B Q8_0 F16 pp512 442.4 -> 446.1 (+0.8%), pp2048 410.9 -> 414.5 (+0.9%); in each of these three cells five of six branch runs sit above every base run, and the sixth is a run whose own three passes spread by 3 to 19 tok/s, as base runs of the same cells do. int8 and the Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 level: 8B int8 1111.3 / 1110.8, 980.6 / 981.6, 14B 667.6 / 667.6, 600.1 / 599.5, 0.6B F16 7914.0 / 7914.9, 5483.5 / 5485.8, int8 9697.6 / 9790.7 (the bimodal cell), 6337.2 / 6337.2.

## ROCm tall tile (2026-10-31, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-tall-rule on perf/rocm-tile-staging 9612b8b7a, which it lands after; step 3 of the tile staging plan, back as F2DEV ruled at 16:51: a ROCm profile value of the same rule, from a ROCm sweep over Qwen3-0.6B, 8B and 14B with the 0.6B held level)

**Goal:** the int8 and F16 prompt tiles of Qwen3 Q8_0 on one MI50 faster with the same bits, through a ROCm row of the device profile's tile rule (`tile_rows_for`), not Vulkan's MI50 numbers.
**Found:** a sweep with the tile always short and always tall (probe build, never lands; rocprofv3 kernel traces of pp512 and pp2048, renderD130, 17:50 UTC), tall over short a call: Qwen3-0.6B o and down (64 tall workgroups) 1.08, qkv (256) 1.01, gate,up (384) 0.99; 8B o and down (256) 1.03 to 1.04, qkv (384) 0.94, gate,up (1536) 0.96; 14B o (320) 1.06, qkv (448) 0.96, gate,up (2176) 0.94. The tall build pays from about 6 workgroups a compute unit, and on the 0.6B's 1024-wide gate,up, which the trace put at 0.99, the 0.6B pp512 still lost 2.0 percent against a control of the same code that never takes it (5 interleaved rounds).
**Done:** the tall build of the tile (128 outputs, each thread 8 outputs by 4 rows, two blocks a step in both classes; int8 117 VGPRs, 2 waves a SIMD, scratch 0) on step 1's staging, which keeps the 64-output build's inner split so a call's bits do not depend on the build; the MI50's HIP row (`"MI60 / MI50"`, `"HIP"`) sets `tile_tall_per_cu` 6 and `qtile_tall_from` and `qtile_tall_from_8bit` 4096; the 32-bit offset bound now counts the build's outputs. `backend-rocm` checks the two builds give the same bits at 70 rows (both split) and at 520 rows 4096 wide (neither splits, and the whole takes the tall build on 60 compute units), at the matrix's start and inside a partial last tile.
**Measured at 860bace5c** (rtr4) against step 1 at 7733aca06 (rts4) on one MI50 (renderD130, CPUs 14,15, default clocks, both built alike from archives, 19:02-19:20 UTC, three interleaved rounds of three runs, tok/s medians): Qwen3-8B Q8_0 int8 pp512 1088.4 -> 1112.5 (+2.2%), pp2048 963.6 -> 982.3 (+1.9%), F16 pp512 762.6 -> 780.6 (+2.4%), pp2048 697.2 -> 714.4 (+2.5%); Qwen3-14B Q8_0 int8 pp512 652.1 -> 668.6 (+2.5%), pp2048 587.5 -> 600.4 (+2.2%), F16 pp512 429.5 -> 443.8 (+3.3%), pp2048 400.3 -> 412.6 (+3.1%), every branch run above every step 1 run in these eight cells; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, which takes no tall call (trace), int8 pp2048 6347.0 / 6344.3, F16 pp512 7923.5 / 7921.3, pp2048 5490.0 / 5483.6, and int8 pp512 9875.1 / 9578.0 in that round with slow runs in both arms, then alone with a never-tall control in six interleaved rounds of five runs (19:22 UTC) 9867.1 / 9875.1, control 9860.6.
Identity: Qwen3-8B Q8_0 greedy 256 tokens in int8 and F16 and Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 16k raw and chat in int8 and F16, 6 of 6 the same bytes; `backend-rocm` PASS. Traces: 8B takes the tall build in 216 of 432 tile calls a run, 14B in 240 of 480, 0.6B in none.
**ROCm decode row block sizes (item 1, closed as measured, F2DEV 16:51 and 17:56):** the four-step int8 row kernel at 256, 128 and 64 threads a block (61, 73 and 73 VGPRs), a probe harness on renderD130, gives the same hashes on 15 shapes of the 0.6B, 8B and 14B; 64 threads win only on the 8B's 4096-wide gate,up (-2.7%) and head (-2.8%) and lose on the 0.6B (qkv +15%, gate,up +17%, head +22%), the 8B o (+4.5%) and the 14B o and down (+3%, +1%), so no shape cut loses nowhere.
**Left:** review; landing after the tile staging on a green hosted run.
**Gotchas:** the tile rule's column groups are the extent's column tiles, at most eight (`split_tiles_of`), so a check of the tall build needs a matrix of at least 45 tall tiles on a 60-unit device, and a slice compared against it must keep the whole call's inner split.
A 0.6B int8 pp512 cell is bimodal on this card in every arm (runs near 9600 and near 9870 tok/s, some at 7400); compare it over more rounds before reading a few percent.

## ROCm prompt tile staging (2026-10-31, DDEV, branch perf/rocm-tile-staging on main 031c7d38b; the plan of 2026-10-31 16:06 approved by F2DEV at 16:11, steps 1, 2 and 3 in that order, each measured on its own; step 1 done)

**Goal:** the int8 prompt tile of Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on one MI50 toward Vulkan's: 440 ms of device time a pp512 pass against Vulkan's 352 (94 percent of the prompt gap), bit for bit.
**Found:** from the gfx906 code object of the dot module (`llmx_q8_0_tile8`, 83 VGPRs, 3 waves a SIMD) and the RADV disassembly of Vulkan's `matmul_tile_q8i8_tall` (128 VGPRs, 2 waves), per wave and staged step of four blocks: ours 512 8-bit dots, 72 16-byte LDS reads, an LDS wait of 0 after every word's two reads, 20 global loads of which 8 flat, and 4 waits of vmcnt(0) each inside the misaligned weight path's branch, so a step's prefetch ran as four serial round trips; Vulkan 1024 dots, 108 LDS reads with 2 or 3 left in flight, 13 buffer loads issued together and counted down, 2 round trips a step. The dot loop is not the gap; the staging is.
**Done:** step 1: each staging thread loads its quarter of a block as three words, the word before where its eight bytes start on a word and the word after where they straddle one, takes the scale from those words, and realigns them at the store; every load of a step goes out before any is waited for, at block 0 of the tile where out of range with its zero chosen at the store, from 32-bit offsets off the tile's first output and row, so its loads take their base from scalar registers. ROCm buffers are allocated in whole words, since a straddling last block's last word runs past a buffer. Code object: 83 VGPRs, 3 waves, scratch 0, a step's 16 global loads (4 weight pairs, 4 weight words, 4 twin pairs, 4 twin scales) issued before the products and 0 flat, the only branches in the loop the scale stores of a row's first thread, and the waits at the next stage's store and the closing barrier; with 64-bit offsets the same code took 95 VGPRs and 2 waves. The 16-bit build: 86 VGPRs as before. backend-rocm gains a matrix of 65 outputs of 3 blocks adopted alone, whose last block starts on a word, its prompt rows the bits of each row alone and of the same matrix with room after it.
**Measured:** step 1 at 3124b537f (rts1) against the base 502cc5c44 on one MI50 (renderD130, CPUs 14,15, default clocks, 16:18-16:24 UTC, both built alike from archives, three interleaved rounds of three runs, int8, tok/s): Qwen3-8B Q8_0 pp512 1042.5 -> 1086.0 (+4.2 percent), pp2048 927.3 -> 959.6 (+3.5); Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 pp512 9579 -> 9883 (+3.2), pp2048 6236 -> 6356 (+1.9); every step-1 run above every base run. Vulkan on the card earlier the same day: 1294, 1156, 12570, 8470. The tile's device time in the 8B pp512 trace: 422 ms a pass against the base's 440. Identity: 8B greedy 256 tokens at int8 and f16 and the 0.6B 16k raw and chat sequences at int8 and f16 give the base's bytes; backend-rocm passes.
**Steps 2 and 3:** step 2, the next word's LDS reads before the current word's dots, takes 92 VGPRs and 2 waves, and forced to 3 waves spills 20 bytes a lane, so it was dropped unbuilt. Step 3, the tall build on step 1's staging (probe/rocm-staging-tall, with perf/tile-width-rules beside it; staging two blocks, 117 VGPRs, 2 waves, scratch 0), gives step 1's bits and, against step 1 (16:43-16:47 UTC, same card and method): Qwen3-8B pp512 1085.6 -> 1105.8 (+1.9 percent), pp2048 961.1 -> 976.1 (+1.6); Qwen3-0.6B pp512 9844 -> 9319 (-5.3), pp2048 6349 -> 6265 (-1.3); the tile 414 ms a pass against 422 on the 8B and 32.6 against 30.8 on the 0.6B, whose 1024-wide rows take the tall build at the default profile too.
**Left:** step 1 lands on its hosted run (CTest and backend-rocm on an MI50 at the rebased head); step 3 comes back, as F2DEV ruled at 16:51, as a ROCm profile value of `qtile_tall_from` from a ROCm width sweep (Qwen3-0.6B, 8B and a 14B-class width, every pp cell, the 0.6B held level).
**Gotchas:** the tall build (128 outputs, 8 by 4 a thread) on the old staging, tried first on perf/rocm-tall-tile (gitea, record only) and closed by F2DEV at 16:02: same bits and slower in every cell; staging four blocks it took 136 VGPRs, 27.6 KB of LDS and 1 wave (8B pp512 767 against 1044, pp2048 703 against 928; 0.6B 7300 against 9560, 5200 against 6200), staging two 120 VGPRs, 13.8 KB and 2 waves (8B -2.8 and -2.6 percent, 0.6B -5.4 and -3.9, the tile 456 ms a pass against 440). The gap was the inner loop, not the block size.
## Unordered products in qwen4exp, step 1: ops keep their own order while unordered (2026-10-31, VDEV, branch perf/unordered-products on main 1701ac2ed, proposal B of VDEV's 2x2 kernel profile of 2026-10-31 10:44, approved by F2DEV at 10:46, the audit's method at 12:01, in progress)

**Goal:** qwen4exp records its independent products unordered (measured -0.35 ms a decode token on Flash-Next 2x2, ceiling -0.91 with the inject gate product beside the mix's down), which first needs every op to order its own steps while unordered.
**Done:** the audit test in `vulkan-lifetime --queue` (AGENTS.md, Tests); on main it fails on the Radeon VII for a decode product's twin (quantize_x, then matmul_row_q8w), the split integer and float tiles' reductions, and the routed grouping, tile and weighted sum, the grouping also read by the next call that reuses it.
Widened per F2DEV's note of 12:14: on the Radeon VII on main, attention (the split's merge after the per-row kernel, and after the tile beside it) and the routed step (each stage of its unfused sequence, the cleared output's doubling copies among them) fail too; main's one unordered region, the state rerun, is checked clean: the causal conv and the delta rule as `Model::rerun_on` records them, over two layers and two views, and qwen4exp's dilated conv beside its causal one, each one dispatch, pass, as do the row mix and the stream injection.
On an MI50 (RADV) at main 1701ac2ed the same, and the two prompt-product twin cases fail there too (quantize_xw, then the integer tile, which the float tile of the Radeon VII does not read), as does a second split tile reading the first's partial sums; the rerun's conv and delta rule, the dilated conv, the row mix and the stream injection pass.
**Done (change):** the Vulkan backend orders, while unordered, each op's own steps and its scratch across calls in one place (`order_step`, called by `dispatch` and `copy`; `OpSteps` held by the matmuls, the routed products, attention and the routed step); every audit case passes on the Radeon VII, the rerun keeping its one barrier.
qwen4exp records its independent products unordered: linear attention's qkv beside its gate, alpha and beta, sparse attention's q, k, v beside the indexer's q and k, and each part's inject gates beside its mix's down product, into a slot of their own (`hc_inject`), which `join` reads on a group.
**Gates at the head against main 1701ac2ed** (MI50s under RADV, default clocks, both arms built alike from archives, main sha dc5ee15f, branch sha 34387871; raw in rig `vdev/holds/flb`, `ub-mi50.log`, `ub-suite.log`):
- The audit passes every case on an MI50 and on the Radeon VII, the rerun keeping its one barrier and two products after their producer's twin none; `backend-vulkan` passes on an MI50, `--isa` exit 0 on the Radeon VII; CPU CTest 77 of 77; the device suite on an MI50 44 PASS, `baseline` SKIP, `raw-blocks` FAIL only for numpy missing in the image.
- Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 at production flags: byte identity the same (a 3000-byte prompt greedy, a chat reply and a raw reply with lookup and MTP-head drafts at 3 and 7, and a seeded reply with MTP-head drafts).
- Flash-Next 2x2 timing, `bench --p 64 --n 64 --r 5 --drafter <MTP head> --draft-max 3`, ABBA, 6 runs an arm (rig load 20 to 81 from other work, monitored), medians main / branch: tg64 50.81 / 51.78 tok/s (+1.9%, every branch run above every main run), a decode step 22.38 / 21.61 ms (-0.77 ms), verifies of 1, 2 and 3 drafts 25.41 / 24.19, 27.90 / 27.31 and 30.06 / 28.79 ms (the 4-row verify -1.27 ms), pp64 level, the chain of 3 drafts 5.14 / 5.08 ms.
**Left:** hosted run.
**Gotchas:** the test counts a hazard where the backend owes the order: within one op call, or on a buffer the call was not given (twins, partial sums, groupings), whichever call recorded it; a caller's buffers across calls are the caller's promise.
## The tile width rules: the integer tile's tallest height from a measured row width and its routed narrow build to a measured count (2026-10-31, VDEV, branch perf/tile-width-rules on main 17c29ef61, rebased onto main 1701ac2ed, proposal A of VDEV's 2x2 kernel profile of 2026-10-31 10:44, approved by F2DEV at 10:46, in progress)

**Goal:** prompt rows on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 2x2 faster with the same bits: the hc up projection (rows 320 wide, 10240 tall) took the tallest tile at 512 rows and more and ran 2.2 times slower a row than the short tile, and at 1024 rows the routed products left the narrow build at 20 entries an expert.
The probe on main bea3ffdb3 (four MI50s, tensor width 2, int8, pp2048): ubatch 512 1398 to 1484 tok/s without the tallest tile below rows 1024 wide, ubatch 1024 1174 to 1351 with the narrow build to 48 entries an expert as well, one last-logits hash for every arm.
**Done:** the profile's `qtile_tall_from` and `qtile_tall_from_8bit`, the row width from which the integer-dot tile may take the tallest height over 16-bit and over 8-bit activations (`tile_rows_for` takes it as `tall_from`; 0 keeps today's rule), and `qtile_narrow_per_expert` and `qtile_narrow_per_expert_8bit`, the entries an expert up to which its routed calls take the narrow build (16 keeps today's, SIZE_MAX takes it at every count).
The MI50 under RADV takes 768, 2560, 32 and every count; every other device, the Radeon VII among them, keeps today's rule, and so does the float tile everywhere.
`backend-vulkan`: `check_routed_narrow` now calls on each side of both narrow cuts and `check_tile_heights` on each side of both width cuts, per type and dtype, each requiring the same bits on both sides and the build the cut gives (AGENTS.md, Tests).
**The values** come from a scratch tile microbench (never lands; device time of the tile kernels alone, arms rotated every repetition, medians of six; rig `vdev/holds/tbout2`, the first pass with the arms in a fixed order in `tbout`, and on the PC `rvk-tb-*.txt` for the Radeon VII), over Qwen3-0.6B's, Qwen3-30B-A3B's, Qwen3.6-27B's and Flash-Next's dense shapes, a sweep of Q8_0, Q4_1, Q5_1, Q4_K, Q5_K and Q6_K rows 256 to 5120 wide and 4096 or 10240 tall at 256 to 2048 columns, and the routed gate and down shapes of Flash-Next (one card and tensor width 2), Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 16 to 160 entries an expert spread evenly.
- Height, one MI50, int8 (time without the tallest height over time with it, 1024 and 2048 columns): Q8_0 rows 320 wide 0.37 to 0.47, 1024 wide 0.88 to 0.93, 2048 wide 0.97 to 0.99, 3072 wide 1.02 to 1.03; Flash-Next's 2560-wide qkv, gate and out 1.01 to 1.04; Q4_1 crosses at 3072; rows 4096 wide lose 2 to 8 percent with it but take another split without it, so their bits would change, and the cut stays below them.
- Height, one MI50, f16: Q8_0 rows 320 wide 0.62 to 0.83, 512 wide 0.93 to 1.00, 768 wide 1.00 to 1.05, 1024 wide 1.06 to 1.12; Q4_1, Q4_K and Q5_K cross at 768 as well, Q5_1 at 1536.
- Narrow build, one MI50, int8, ms for a layer's gate and down summed, narrow against the 64-column build: Flash-Next 2x2's slices at 40 an expert 7.6 against 8.2, at 160 27.8 against 65.1; Qwen3-30B-A3B at 40 2.80 against 2.67 (the one count where it lost), at 64 4.0 against 4.6, at 160 9.5 against 18.4; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 40 5.26 against 5.24, at 128 14.4 against 23.2. The 64-column build grows faster than its entries at high counts, so the narrow build is taken at every count.
- Narrow build, one MI50, f16: it wins to 32 an expert in every shape and loses from 40 (Flash-Next 2x2's gate slice at 64: 8.0 against 5.5 ms), so the cut is 32.
- Radeon VII (float tile): the tallest height is faster for Q8_0 and the K-quants at every width from 256 (Flash-Next's hc up 1.16 to 1.22) and slower for Q4_1 and Q5_1 at nearly every width (Q5_1 rows 4096 wide 0.45 to 0.66), a finding by type that this branch leaves to its own change.
**Gates at 82fc6cf3f against main 1701ac2ed** (MI50s under RADV, default clocks, both arms built alike from archives, main sha dc5ee15f, branch sha d31e18ff; raw in rig `vdev/holds/abtw1`, `idta`, `twwit`, `fltw`):
- Byte identity: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M on one card, 21 of 21 output files the same bytes (greedy, seeded and lookup-drafted generate in f16 and int8, prompts of about 1400 tokens at ubatch 512 and 2048 in f16 and int8, logits, perplexity, chat, `tools/server_mix_check.py` ids); Flash-Next 2x2 at production flags, prompts at ubatch 512 and 1024 and drafted replies, the same bytes. So it stays a speed change.
- Witness: on 1024-token prompts 0.6B int8 no longer takes `matmul_tile_q8i8_tall`, and 35B-A3B takes the narrow routed builds in f16 and int8.
- `backend-vulkan --isa` exit 0 on an MI50 and on the Radeon VII; the device suite on an MI50 44 PASS, `baseline` SKIP, `raw-blocks` FAIL only for numpy missing in the image.
- One MI50, int8, pp tok/s medians main / branch (rig load 10.5 to 15.5, ABBA, 4 runs an arm, 0.6B 8): 0.6B Q8_0 pp512 13291 / 13278, pp1024 11518 / 12177 (+5.7%), pp2048 8989 / 9392 (+4.5%); 35B-A3B Q4_K_M pp512 1843.5 / 1851.2, pp1024 1886.4 / 2025.4 (+7.4%), pp2048 1824.0 / 1956.6 (+7.3%); 27B-MTP Q4_1 pp512/1024/2048 inside main's range; tg level on all three.
- Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 (four MI50s, CPUs 4-7 and 10-13, rig load 9 to 90 from other work, ABBA, 4 runs an arm): pp512 941.9 / 1008.3 (+7.0%), pp1024 935.1 / 1091.0 (+16.7%), pp2048 at ubatch 1024 1178.5 / 1363.2 (+15.7%), pp2048 at ubatch 512 1403.6 / 1494.8 (+6.5%), every branch run above every main run; tg64 50.5 / 50.3, inside main's spread (42.8 to 51.6).
**Left:** hosted run.
**Gotchas:** both cuts change only which height or build a call takes; every height and both routed builds sum each output's blocks in the same order, and below 4096 values a row no split follows the height, so a row's bits do not depend on the cut, which is what keeps a choice that follows the batch batch invariant.
A tile microbench whose arms run in a fixed order reads the first arm up to 20 percent slow on calls under a millisecond on the MI50 (the memory clock ramps within the repetition); rotate the arms and warm each block.
The narrow cut is an average over the experts a call touches; SIZE_MAX is taken as every count before the product with that count, which it would overflow.
Below 4096 values a row the cut cannot move a call's K split: on the MI50 a call takes the tallest height only at 8 workgroups a compute unit, where the split's target of 4 is already met, and the shorter height doubles the workgroups.
## A reply beside a prompt meets one chunk a stage at every pass count (2026-10-31, RDEV, branch fix/chunk-pass-cap on main c92d2d353, F2DEV's ruling of 13:49 on serving fault 1, lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

- **Goal:** `--passes` follows one rule at every value: while replies and a prompt both wait, a reply's step meets one chunk at every stage, which `chunk_budget` plans by.
- **Found:** the round formed a chunk pass in every free slot, so at P = 2S a reply's step met 2S - 1 chunk passes a stage, each taking the whole budget. Replay (server-passes at the Flash-Next 2x2 prices, one reply planned at two tokens a step beside a 140k-token prompt, two stages, budget 110 ms, objective 250 ms a step) on main: P = 3 two chunk passes, 208 ms of prompt work a step, step 223 ms, prompt 206 s; P = 4 three, 311 ms, step 327 ms (the objective missed), prompt 201 s. Production runs the default P = S + 1, which already met one a stage; its extra 0.73 chunk a step is the reply's host turnaround (RDEV's posts of 13:44 and 14:09), not this rule.
- **Done:** the failing test, then `passes_in_flight` keeps the replies' passes and one chunk pass a stage in flight while both wait (`Scheduler::plan` computes the packed passes first); the replay mirrors it.
- **Figures (replay, after):** P = 3 and P = 4 the same passes and times, 2 chunk passes and 208 ms a step, step 223 ms, prompt 206 s; P = 2 unchanged, one chunk pass, prompt 383 s: at P = S nothing can feed the idle stage with one prompt, which continues only in passes holding it alone (`Model::begin_pass`), so no second chunk of it rides the replies.
- **Tests:** `server-passes` `replay_long_prompt` (fails on main at P = 4 with 3 chunk passes a step) and `passes_in_flight` by hand under overlap; the 2000 random schedules pass; `server-passes-cpu` at P = 1, S, S + 1 and 2S.
- **Left:** the merge gates for server code (CTest, the CPU suite, Qwen3-0.6B byte identity against main, the hosted run); production's P = S + 1 forms the same passes, so no card leg is claimed.

## ROCm decode attention (2026-10-31, DDEV, branch feat/rocm-decode-attn on feat/rocm-decode-rows 1701ac2ed, which it needs and lands after; the plan of 2026-10-31 04:12 approved by F2DEV at 04:15, the probe, change 1 and change 2 in that order; change 1 kept, change 2 not)

**Goal:** the per-row decode attention of Qwen3-8B Q8_0 int8 on one MI50 from 19.6 us a call in the model to the kernel's own time, bit for bit: run alone with its block table, firsts and ends in device memory it takes 9.2 us over a 128-token reply (Vulkan's attention 11.9), and reading them from the pinned argument ring over PCIe adds about 4.5 us a call.
**Done:** the probe: over a 128-token reply's histories the kernel and its merge take 12.6 to 14.2 us a call with their values in device memory, 17.6 to 25.4 in coherent pinned memory and 13.3 in non-coherent pinned memory, but a two-slot ring the host rewrites, as the model's is, takes 20 to 27 in non-coherent and 31 to 43 in coherent memory; one upload of a pass's 1 KiB set costs 3 to 63 us of stream time by an asynchronous copy and 3 to 24 by a copy kernel, and of a 16 KiB set 2 to 24 against 21 to 330, every hash equal. Change 1, the pass values in device memory: attention's table, firsts and ends (one set with a prompt tile's views), the KV write's blocks and slots (one set) and the positions go through `pass_arg`, which the first layer of a pass copies into a ring of device memory by an asynchronous copy on the stream ahead of its launch and later layers find by their bytes; the host compares and never waits for the copy, and a device slot is taken again only once the last launch that read it retires (each slot's lap forgets the sets it held). In the model's kernel trace attention takes 9.84 us a call (19.6 before) and the three uploads 15 us a token; Qwen3-8B greedy at f16 and int8 and the 0.6B 16k int8 raw and chat output are byte-identical to the base, and backend-rocm passes.
**Measured:** Qwen3-8B Q8_0 tg256 at `--dtype int8` on one MI50 (renderD130, CPUs 14,15, 10:07-10:18 UTC, a warm-up then six rounds of five runs in rotated orders, monitor log beside them, host load mean 18.3, max 28.2; rig `ddev/rocm/rdat-1007`): decode-rows 75.14/74.72/74.45/76.96/73.70/76.12 tok/s (median 74.9), this branch 77.45/80.70/75.36/80.28/79.12/80.69 (median 79.7, +6.4 percent), Vulkan 77.56/78.44/76.66/78.40/77.76/77.61 (median 77.7; this branch +2.6 percent). Every run of the branch but one (75.36 +- 4.93) is above every run of decode-rows. The branch gives decode-host's 96 greedy tokens of the 8B at f16 and int8 and its 0.6B 16k int8 raw and chat output byte for byte, and the full CTest passed 79/79.
**Left:** review; landing after decode-rows.
**Gotchas:** change 2 (a build of the per-row attention for each pair of K and V types, both rows of a token loaded before either is widened, 32-bit offsets) changed the int8 decode bits of the 8B and the 0.6B 16k sequences while f16 kept them, because the typed build contracted the V update as fma(acc, corr, w*v) where the base has fma(w, v, acc*corr). With the fused forms written out (feat/rocm-decode-attn-kdis 2ac3a882b) every byte held, but in the same rounds it measured 77.83/79.68/75.22/74.48/75.79/75.14 tok/s (median 75.5), below this branch, so it is not kept here; its gain is at depth (-25 to -34 percent at 1024 to 4096 tokens in the probe), which the deep-history attention work owns. `__launch_bounds__(256)` on this kernel changed its bits in the probe, so it has none.
## A long message's question changed forks a boundary before it (2026-10-31, RDEV, branch fix/tail-boundary on main b45a44d4b, serving fault 2 of the coordinator's decision of 13:25, plan approved by F2DEV at 13:49, the slot step and the tradeoff ruled by F2DEV on 2026-11-01 at 00:12 and 09:33, lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

- **Goal:** a follow-up that differs from a long prompt only in its question, the owner's long chats, forks the hybrid model's state close to the change instead of reading all 140k tokens again.
- **Found:** SDEV's long prompts (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2, production's commit 0c8655f22) are one user message, a 140k-token text and its question; the message boundary falls at the conversation's start and is not kept, and the request's own checkpoint sits at its prompt's last whole block, about 140032, inside the question, which starts near 140000. long_prose and long_think each read 132 s again.
- **Done:** the failing test, then `Cache::admit` sets the boundary `kTailTokens` (1024) before the prompt's end where the last user message starts no further than what the request forked, past the fork and before its own checkpoint; everything after is the boundary's existing path, and `keep_boundary` keeps such a tail boundary only in room no entry holds, ranked with what loses nothing until a request forks it (`Boundary::tail`, whatever the request that kept it reused), so it displaces no other entry; it applies wherever the last user message's start is unknown or at the prompt's start, the raw routes, a first chat turn of one message and a turn after a tool's result included, so each such prompt past about 1.1k tokens on a state model ends a slice at the boundary and copies a state to host memory; taking the room of entries whole on disk instead cost the small-host-tier-and-disk case of `message_boundaries` its boundary forks and 128 tokens of the regenerated turn's reuse, so it does not. A model without a state keeps no boundary, as before. The state at a boundary a request asked for waits in a checkpoint slot of its own, a fork at the checkpoint taken while a slot is free and the request has no token yet (`Request::boundary_seq_`, `Cache::asked_boundary`), and goes to host memory once the first token is out, or is dropped where the request is cancelled or released (`Cache::boundary_out`); without a free slot it is copied at once.
- **Tests:** `server-resume` `edit_tail_of_message`: a 1640-token text and a 60-token question as one message, then the same text with another question, on the hybrid model with a host tier: on main the second reuses 0 tokens; with the change it forks the tail boundary at 640 tokens and gives a fresh model's reply. `tail_boundary_goes_first`: in a host tier of three slabs, a follow-up that forked the first tail boundary keeps its own, its donor takes the third slab, and another conversation's message boundary takes that one's room, so its edit forks it at 256 and a third question still forks the first at 640 (on the ranking of the first review, which kept a reused request's tail at its conversation's rank, the message boundary was refused). `message_boundaries` with a 1 GiB host tier now counts the 2000-token request's own tail boundary beside the turns' six; with the small host tier beside a disk tier the case is main's.
- **Measured** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2, GPUs 4-7 of the Linux MI50 machine, CPUs 4-7, production's flags with a 4 GiB host tier and a private disk directory, default clocks, fresh servers, every reply the same bytes in every arm; raw data in the RDEV scratch, f2leg, f2lone, f2split and f3). Long messages of 140k tokens, one server an arm, main c92d2d353 against the boundary without the slot step: long_prose (the same text, its question changed) reused 0 against 139008 tokens, first token 131.86 against 1.91 s; long_code, long_think (whose thinking render agrees with the held history for one token, so nothing can fork) and a three-turn chat level.
- **Cost:** a lone raw prompt past about 1.1k tokens ends a slice at its tail boundary, and the next slice waits for that pass to retire, since the fork into the checkpoint slot, like the copy it replaced, needs the sequence at rest, so the stages lose one slice of overlap. Warm first token on `/v1/completions`, medians of 8, two a server:

| run (UTC) | arms | 2k (s) | 8k (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-31 18:44 | main c92d2d353 / boundary copied at once | 1.865 / 2.167 | 6.970 / 7.648 |
| 2026-10-31 23:26 | main c92d2d353 / slice end alone (copy skipped, a probe) / boundary copied at once | 1.922 / 2.051 / 2.185 | 6.974 / 7.015 / 7.178 |
| 2026-11-01 03:15 | main 66040b8a1 / with the slot step / slot step and a fork in flight (a probe) | 1.970 / 2.239 / 2.180 | 7.239 / 7.223 / 7.137 |

  The slot step takes the copy off the 8k cell; the 2k cell keeps about 0.27 s (+14%), a known cost F2DEV weighed against the edited question's 130 s (ruling of 2026-11-01 09:33). Forking a sequence in flight gave back only 0.06 s, so it was not built.
- **Left:** CTest, the CPU suite and the hosted run on the rebased head; the long-message leg on it.

## A history draft copies from the furthest match, not the latest (2026-10-31, SDEV, branch fix/lookup-longest-match on main 17c29ef61, the coordinator's question on first-turn code edits from the owner's production report)

- **Goal:** the owner sees lookup boost a first-turn code edit (the file in the prompt) less than follow-ups; find whether it is ours.
- **Found:** the prompt is indexed from the first verify (the scheduler gives `lookup_first` the prompt and the reply). `Lookup::convincing` took the latest earlier occurrence of the last eight tokens; in a long file a later repeat of those eight tokens continues elsewhere than the passage being copied. An offline replay of a 44k-token file (`scheduler.hpp`) copied back with one rename, Qwen3.6-27B tokens, drafts up to 63: latest occurrence 52.5 tokens a verify (839 verifies, 6944 drafts missed), furthest match 60.4 (729 verifies, 113 missed); the same on a 2.8k-token file 31.8 against 33.4; a follow-up repeating the 44k file 53.4 against 61.8, so the latest occurrence costs first turns and follow-ups alike. On the card at a 6.4k-token prompt (Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1, one MI50, main fe2ccacae) a first-turn edit and the same edit as a follow-up ran alike: 66.5-67.9 against 66.7-68.5 tokens/s without thinking, 47.0-47.3 against 46.4-47.0 with it, the reasoning drafted by the MTP head alone.
- **Done:** the failing test (`tests/spec.cpp` `convincing_rule`: a later repeat of the last eight tokens beside the passage whose match runs back twenty), then `Lookup::convincing` takes the occurrence whose match runs back furthest, up to `kLongestMatch`, the latest of equal ones, stopping at the first that reaches it.

## ROCm decode rows (2026-10-31, DDEV, branch feat/rocm-decode-rows on feat/rocm-decode-host dcb738f36, which it needs and lands after, rebased onto main; the plan of 2026-10-31 00:46 approved by F2DEV at 00:47 and 00:55, steps 0, 1 and 2 in that order, in progress)

**Goal:** Qwen3-8B Q8_0 int8 decode on one MI50 past llmx Vulkan's 78.95 tok/s (decode-host 74.12), bit for bit: the decode products are about 1.0 ms a token behind Vulkan's and attention 0.13 ms (step 0, the same one-column calls through each backend on one card).
**Done:** (1) Step 1, the products: the int8 class's one-column build of the half-block order issues four steps of a lane's loads, the weights' five words and the twin's 16 bytes, before any of their products, held together by a scheduling barrier, then each step's products in block order, so every row sums as before; and every lane exchange of the row kernels (the scale handed to the odd lane, the xor tree that folds a row) takes DPP for partners 1 and 2 and swizzles up to 16, a permute only across the wave's halves, the same partners. (2) Step 2, attention, tried and not kept, since none of it was faster (the per-row kernel took 705 us a token before and 708 after on the trace): the per-row and tile kernels' scores, maxima and sums by the same DPP and swizzle exchanges; then also a stream's next token loaded before its current token's math and each stream's weight computed once for the merge. The disassembly held the one-head build's 18 exponentials, 111 fused multiply-adds, 40 multiplies, 24 adds and 16 maxima with the loads ahead, yet the 8B's int8 greedy text and the 0.6B's 16k decode rows changed (its prompt rows held): the compiler fused other products in the reshaped loop, so equal counts do not prove the order. With the math written as the fused operations the one-head build compiles to (`fmaf(part, scale, -mn)` inside the exponential, `fmaf(l, corr, w)`, `fmaf(w, v, acc * corr)`) every byte came back, and the speed did not.
**Left:** review; landing after decode-host, rebased onto main, on a green hosted run. Attention is the next lever (its per-row kernel takes 19.7 us a call against Vulkan's 11.9 for the same design, and the two decode attention kernels 0.90 ms a token against 0.69), which needs a probe of where that kernel's time goes before another change.
**Measured:** on the model, Qwen3-8B Q8_0 tg128 at `--dtype int8` on one MI50 (renderD132, CPUs 12-15, three interleaved rounds of three runs, monitor log beside them): 02:43-02:46 UTC, with CPUs 0-7 of the host 90 percent busy with other jobs, decode-host 71.81 tok/s (71.81/71.76/73.64), step 1 77.30 (77.30/76.54/77.84, +7.6 percent), Vulkan 78.13 (78.13/79.43/78.02); 03:03-03:05 UTC, decode-host 73.15 (73.15/71.68/74.47), step 1 77.78 (77.78/76.86/78.54), step 1 with the attention exchanges 78.58 (75.79/78.58/78.70), Vulkan 79.15 (78.55/79.15/79.28); 03:15-03:17 UTC, quieter, decode-host 73.95 (74.00/73.77/73.95), step 1 with the attention exchanges 78.24 (78.28/78.24/78.04, +5.8 percent), the attention retry 77.98 (77.85/78.25/77.98), Vulkan 79.66 (79.58/79.66/79.73). The branch keeps step 1 alone, which leaves ROCm about 1.8 percent behind Vulkan. The kernel trace of the same run (03:07 UTC, rig `ddev/rocm/prof7-*`): 13.63 ms a token busy before, 12.89 after; the row kernel 11.36 ms before and 10.59 after, by shape 3.90 -> 3.67 ms a token for the 4096-row calls (o_proj and down), and medians of 39.7 -> 37.0 us a call for q,k,v, 143.5 -> 133.0 for gate,up and 861 -> 804 for the head; attention 0.70 + 0.19, norms 0.70, norm_rope_kv 0.32, silu 0.16 ms, unchanged. Step 1 gives decode-host's 96 greedy tokens of the 8B at f16 and int8 and its 0.6B 16k int8 raw and chat output byte for byte, and the full CTest passed 79/79 with it. The settings of step 1, from a probe that times the production kernel's builds on the 8B's decode shapes on renderD129 (one column, int8 twin, outputs hashed, every build below the base's bits; microseconds a call, the lowest of seven repeats, the median of three interleaved rounds; rig `ddev/rocm/rowh-20261031-{a..g}`):

| build | VGPRs | q,k,v 6144 x 4096 | o_proj 4096 x 4096 | gate,up 24576 x 4096 | down 4096 x 12288 | head 151936 x 4096 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode-host (one step a loop, permutes) | 35 | 39.5 | 28.2 | 143.4 | 77.9 | 854 |
| two rows a wave | 41 | 41.8 | 30.0 | 147.9 | 76.5 | 871 |
| 64-thread blocks, one step | 34 | 38.9 | 27.3 | 142.5 | 77.9 | 859 |
| at most 8 waves a SIMD (32 VGPRs, spilling) | 32 | 60.6 | 42.1 | 230.3 | 96.2 | 1388 |
| two steps loaded first, no barrier | 49 | 45.1 | 33.2 | 158.8 | 79.0 | 936 |
| two steps, barrier, DPP and swizzles | 47 | 36.8 | 27.1 | 136.7 | 74.3 | 825 |
| the same in 64-thread blocks | 47 | 36.8 | 26.8 | 135.0 | 74.5 | 815 |
| three steps, barrier | 60 | 38.1 | 28.2 | 140.0 | 73.7 | 853 |
| **four steps, barrier (chosen)** | 63 | 36.4 | 27.0 | 132.7 | 73.4 | 802 |
| six steps, barrier | 83 | 43.3 | 31.5 | 161.0 | 72.6 | 985 |
| eight steps, barrier | 122 | 52.6 | 37.6 | 199.3 | 78.4 | 1212 |

Without the barrier the compiler spread a step's loads to save registers and waited between them, so the loads-first form measured slower than the base or level with it, by the wave cap the compiler was given; with it every cap measured alike, so no cap is set. Four steps hold a row of 4096 in one round of loads and win or tie on every shape; six steps gain 1 percent on down's long rows and lose 20 percent elsewhere, so one setting serves every shape and no shape table is kept. Two waves a row, which would split a row's sum, are not tried.
**Gotchas:** `warpSize` is not a constant in ROCm 7, so a lane exchange chosen by its partner must be unrolled from a constant; `lane_xor` takes its partner as an argument and the loops that call it are unrolled, which the disassembly shows as immediate DPP and swizzle patterns.

## ROCm decode launches and host time (2026-10-30, DDEV, branch feat/rocm-decode-host on feat/rocm-decode-products ecb53a3c0, which it needs and lands after, rebased onto main; the plan of 2026-10-30 22:25 approved by F2DEV at 22:29 with three conditions, in progress)

**Goal:** the rest of a Qwen3-8B Q8_0 int8 decode token on one MI50 beside the products, bit for bit: ROCm's token is 13.8 ms (72.4-73.0 tok/s on quiet CPUs) against Vulkan's 12.5 ms (79.8), the gap nearly all device time in small kernels and their 463 launches against Vulkan's 355, with about 0.13 ms of logits handling between tokens.
**Done:** (1) `norm_rope_kv` is one launch a layer (`llmx_norm_rope_kv`): q's and k's heads normed and rotated in place and k and v written into their KV blocks, the head's math one device function with `llmx_norm_rope` and the rows' blocks and slots one host helper with `kv_write`; the base's ops one at a time where a head is wider than a block or k's rows are not dense. (2) Attention writes the twin the output projection reads (`twin_at`, the norms' and `silu_mul`'s `twin_value`), the per-row kernel at one split and the split merge otherwise, when no row of the call takes the tile kernel. (3) `Model::step(int)` returns its logits row in place, valid until the next pass, as `step(ids, n)` does, instead of a fresh 608 KB vector a step: in a ROCm process each fresh vector was mapped and faulted anew (86 us against 16 under Vulkan). `bench --model`'s decode figure moves by this, so figures before it are not compared across it.
**Left:** review, then landing after decode-products, rebased onto main, on a green hosted run.
**Measured:** tg128 of Qwen3-8B Q8_0 int8 on one MI50 (renderD131, CPUs 8 and 9, three interleaved rounds of three runs, 2026-10-30 23:52-23:54 UTC, monitor log beside it; the host's load was 15-22 from other jobs on other CPUs): decode-products 71.50/72.58/72.06 tok/s (median 72.06), this change 73.80/74.95/73.42 (73.80, +2.4 percent), the same with the grouped attention 72.28/73.48/71.08 (72.28), the Vulkan control 79.08/79.42/74.70 (79.08). The base quoted at the plan was 72.4-73.0. On the final tree (2026-10-31 00:40-00:42 UTC, same card, CPUs and monitor): decode-products 71.84/71.73/71.79 (median 71.79), this change 73.54/74.12/74.27 (74.12, +3.2 percent), Vulkan 78.33/78.98/78.95 (78.95). CTest 79/79 on the card, docs and dead-code pass. The grouped attention's failed check, run once more on its tree with each mismatch printed, differed only at heads 128 wide, ratios 2, 4, 6 and 8 and the 300-token history, where its two tokens in flight run; never at ratios 1 and 3, the 9-token history or heads 256 wide, so the one-head kernel and the chunk kernel hold. Greedy 96 tokens of the 8B at f16 and int8 and the 0.6B on the CPU and under Vulkan are the base's bytes.
**Gotchas:** a dependent tiny kernel costs about 6 us of device time on an MI50 (5.1 in a graph), and a kernel reading one value from pinned host memory 0.9 us more; `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG` changes nothing. The per-row attention taking four query heads of a KV head a block (as the Vulkan `_g4` builds do) loaded K and V once for them but took 24.6 us a call against 17.7 for one head a block, the four heads' registers and serial merges costing more than the loads saved, and was dropped, as the plan's condition asked.

**Goal:** the decode token's norms, activation twins and products off the 8B's decode budget (profdec-20261030: `rms_norm_rows` 1.04 ms a token at 14 us a 4096-wide row, the twins 0.64 ms), bit for bit, by the Vulkan producers' design: a norm and `silu_mul` write the twin of their output beside it, so the product after them makes none.
**Done:** norm rows of up to 8192 values on a block of 1024 threads, the row and its weights loaded at once and each thread scaling and twinning a quarter of a 256-thread block's share, the sum in the plain kernel's order; the block sum's levels inside a wave by shuffles adding the same pairs; `norm_rope` holding a head of up to 256 values a value a thread, its weights and angles loaded with it; the twin rule moved to `kernels/f32.hip` with its producers; the kept twin's tag in the backend, dropped by any other launch, copy, write or allocation and by a product into its input; backend-rocm holds each producer's product to the product of a copy of its output and the drops.
