## The 2x2 targets are kernel work (2026-10-31, RDEV, a device-timestamp profile of main bea3ffdb3, F2DEV's ruling of 10:04, docs only)

**Goal:** record where Flash-Next 2x2's time goes against the final gate's second reference (pp2048 1939 tok/s, decode 79.5, MTP 119), so the owners of each part take it from here.
**Setup:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL over four MI50s as two stages of tensor groups of two, int8, f16 caches, `--lookup-storage file`, default clocks; walls from main, profiles from main plus a timestamp dump that never lands.
**Walls:** pp2048 by `--ubatch`: 128 1185, 256 1445, 384 1439, 512 1402, 768 1370, 1024 1177 tok/s; tg128 49-51 tok/s (20.0 ms a token).
**Prefill model:** a slice costs about 25 ms plus 0.53 ms a row a stage (the 25 ms is the experts' weights read once a slice), and a pass takes (slices + 1) slice times; it predicts four ubatches within 1-2% and puts the best at 6-7 slices, about 1440 tok/s.
1939 tok/s is 1056 ms for 2048 rows, below the 1085 ms of per-row work alone, so no split change reaches it.
**Ranked, prefill (1417 ms at ubatch 256):** per-row product cost, dense and expert tiles, about 0.33 of the 0.53 ms a row (products, VDEV and DDEV); fill and per-slice expert reads about 330 ms at the best slice count; inbox copies 112-125 ms (the cut hides them, perf/ts-copy-queue, held); prompt attention at depth 0 135 ms, about 10 times its flop floor (MDEV); stage 0 heavier than stage 1 by about 45 ms (rebalancing parked by the owner); hyper-connection and norm ops 84-94 ms; sum gaps 16-45 ms.
**Ranked, decode (20.0 ms a token, 12.6 for the target):** kernels about 14 ms over about 1550 dispatches, three times the bandwidth floor of about 2 ms a stage, launch-bound (dispatch count and the small kernels, DDEV); sum exchanges about 4.2 ms, 96 a token at 40 us (the transport's sync-file wait, the collective's owner); inbox copies, sums and injects about 2 ms; host about 1.2 ms.
With every collective cost gone decode would be about 66 tok/s, so 79.5 needs the kernels near 8 ms; MTP 119 rides the same pass cost, a 4-row verify being 39 ms today.
**The server's lone first token** (main bea3ffdb3, production's flags without the disk cache and the image encoder, six fresh servers interleaved, medians of nine prompts): 512 tokens 0.607 s at `--ubatch` 1024 and 0.573 s at 256, 2k 1.888 and 1.635 s, 8k 6.152 and 6.051 s; replies identical at both.
The server cuts a lone prompt on a split into shrinking slices at either ubatch (`lone_slice`), so the bench's 19% gap at 2k is about 6% in the server.
**Split-side probes approved as probes (F2DEV 10:04), each landing only on a measured gain with bits unchanged:** a lone prompt's slices equal and counted from PriceTable's prices in place of `lone_slice`, and the peer's partial read in place with the sum and inject fused; neither closes a target alone.

## Drafts priced by the price table's measured pass cost (2026-10-30, SDEV, branch fix/draft-pass-price on main fe2ccacae, the coordinator's report of production on 2f4f4481 slower than cb374f282, for F2DEV's review)

- **Goal:** production (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2, lookup and its MTP head, `--draft-max 63`) gave 0.053 tokens/ms on 2f4f4481 against 0.059 on cb374f282, on different traffic.
- **Cause:** `spec::draft_depths` priced a pass by a line through the measured passes (`PassTimes`), base plus row times rows, while the measured cost has a step between 7 and 9 rows: band 6 (128k-256k tokens) gave 5 rows 26.4 ms, 6 30.1, 7 29.4, 8 36.2, 9 41.8, 10 41.1, 12 46.6, 17 62.7 (`/v1/health` price table, which predicted 827 s of passes against 823 s measured). A line through 1-20 rows (15.9 + 2.70 a row) prices 7 rows about 5 ms too dear. Offline, with that health's conditional keeps by source, the table's depth against the line's: proposer 6 against 9 (+11% tokens/ms), history 8-15 6 against 9 (+9%), 16-31 6 against 11 (+6%), 32+ 19 against 15 (+12%). cb374f282's rule ran mostly 4-8 rows, before the step (position 8 fed 914), and 2f4f4481 feeds 9-10 rows far more (2816 and 2074).
- **Done:** the failing test (`tests/sampler.cpp` `stepped_price`: a stepped cost in the price table at 1 to 20 rows takes six drafts where the line takes nine; an unmeasured band takes the line; a width between measured cells is priced between them, not at the nearest), then the fix, the price table as the one owner of a width's price (F2DEV's review of 49de4eca3): the scheduler fills `PassCost::rows_ms` from `ServiceRecord::decode_curve`, the slowest stage's measured cell at the deepest decoder's band, the line between two measured cells, 0 outside them, where `spec::pass_ms` continues the nearest measured width's price on the line's slope (F2DEV's edge point), and the line where the band has no cell; `PassTimes` keeps no per-width means, and reconciles the table's stage time with the server's time of each decode pass whose cell was measured (`reconcile`, `server_ms`, the mean difference, which keeps the table's steps; a fitted line flattened them on the card and drafted 3 deep on prose, 6-18% slower); the pass line and the reconciliation take only passes of decode rows alone, as the table keys them, so a one-row prompt slice no longer counts as a decode row; `draft_depths` keeps a request's drafts where their expected tokens pay for `pass_ms(rows + k) - pass_ms(rows)`.
- **First measure:** a decode cell's first measure pays its width's one-time costs, so its mean starts at the second (`PriceTable::observe`), and `decode_ms` and `decode_curve` skip a cell with no price yet; the failing test `first_measure` (`tests/sampler.cpp`): one dear first 2-row pass moved a request kept at 0.6, 0.3 and 0.15 from one draft to three, and a second 2-row pass must price the width. Found on the card: in both price4 arms of pr4b the 2-row cell held 87 and 85 ms from 2 samples whose last measures were 55 and 52 (the first about 97 ms), against base's 55.6 ms from 1059 samples; Vulkan kernel pipelines are made on first use (`src/backends/vulkan/vulkan_dispatch.hpp`), and a 2-column decode pass is the first to need its builds. Priced at 85 ms, two rows looked barely cheaper than three or four, so the proposer drafted 2 to 3 deep on prose (b1 kept 383 of 887 drafts against base's 325 of 551) and never measured 2 rows again.
- **Slice cells** keep forgetting from their first measure: the slice search reads `last_ms`, so an overrun acts at once, and `chunk_ms` and `slice_ms` carry a first-use measure in the mean only until it forgets, which the search's revisits of slice cells bring about.
- **Recorded for the Vulkan backend:** the first pass that needs a kernel build pays its pipeline creation, about 45 to 70 ms on the MI50 (a first 2-row pass about 97 ms against 52 to 55), in a live reply; creating the decode builds at load instead is a separate question, with a startup cost to measure first.

## F32 decode dispatches by workgroup count (2026-10-31, VDEV, branch feat/f32-decode-occupancy, step 2 of VDEV's plan of 2026-10-31 00:55, approved by F2DEV at 03:09; on step 1, feat/q8-decode-occupancy aa8165776 on main fe2ccacae, since it extends step 1's `filling_build` and needs wide-decode's chunks in one dispatch; it rebases when step 1 lands)

**Goal:** an F32 decode call of a few columns over few rows fills the device: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's ssm_alpha and ssm_beta (2560 x 48 each) give 12 workgroups of 4 rows on 60 compute units, and its hc inject rows (10240 x 4) one, so a verify of 6 to 8 rows waited on the 8-column build's serial columns. Every column keeps the one-column build's bits.
**Done:** `VulkanBackend::filling_build` now gives a decode dispatch its build and chunk count (`Fill`); an F32 call is one dispatch cut into as few chunks of at most the wide build's 8 columns as give two busy workgroups a compute unit, else a chunk a column in the one-column build, so a call that fills the device in one chunk, such as the 512-row router, keeps the wide build.
`row_dispatch` gives a plain dispatch's columns to its chunks as evenly as can be, a push constant `longer` naming how many of the first chunks take a column more than `ncols`, so 7 columns go as 4 and 3 in one dispatch with no second dispatch for the leftover; routed and grouped calls are unchanged, and the other kernels' whole chunks are cut exactly as before.
A first version divided the columns by `gl_NumWorkGroups.y` in the shaders; RADV lowers that integer division to float multiplies, which failed the MI50's `--isa` screen on the grouped Q4 dot build, so the host now does the division.
The factor, the bound and the fallback live in that one function beside step 1's; the inputs are the call's rows and columns and `caps.compute_units`.
`backend-vulkan` witnesses F32 calls of 2, 6, 7 and 8 columns over rows halving from 65536 to 4 (one dispatch, the wide build at the largest and the one-column build at the smallest, never back, every column against the same column alone), where 7 columns are cut into 4 and 3 at some height on any device, and adds decode-column cells of F32 rows 2560 wide, 48, 96, 256 and 512 tall.
**The factor.** Device time a call after 100 warm and 100 timed runs, the best of three interleaved rounds, us, the rule against forced chunk counts (c1 is the base's one chunk in the wide build, cn a chunk a column); scratch bench, never landing.
One MI50 under RADV at the final head, 8 columns (6 and 7 columns in brackets, rule against c1):
| matrix (K x rows) | workgroups | rule | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ssm_alpha 2560 x 48 | 12 | 7.49 | 22.37 | 13.77 | 9.14 | 7.56 |
| alpha and beta, one group | 24 | 10.30 | 22.61 | 13.57 | 9.76 | 11.25 |
| hc inject 10240 x 4 | 1 | 13.02 | 64.11 | 35.80 | 21.31 | 13.27 |
| 4096 x 64 | 16 | 11.84 | 24.38 | 14.96 | 10.71 | 11.83 |
| 2560 x 256 | 64 | 16.98 | 25.40 | 17.02 | 17.94 | 22.83 |
| router 2560 x 512 | 128 | 27.19 | 27.30 | 26.77 | 29.88 | 43.32 |
| 2560 x 1024 | 256 | 40.43 | 40.31 | 44.70 | 61.64 | 111.49 |
At 6 and 7 columns: ssm_alpha 7.11 and 7.16 against 18.03 and 20.10; 2560 x 256, cut 3 and 3 and then 4 and 3, 14.65 and 15.58 against 20.45 and 22.86; the router 22.74 and 24.87 against 22.73 and 24.91, and 2560 x 1024 33.63 and 36.97 against 33.59 and 36.97, both keeping their own build.
A factor of 1 would leave 2560 x 256 in its own build (64 workgroups) at 25.40 against 16.98; a factor of 4 would cut the router (128) into two chunks, 26.77 against 27.30 at 8 columns but 14.94 against 13.77 at 2, so 2 takes the large gains and loses nowhere outside noise.
The rule's count is within 10 percent of the best count measured but on alpha and beta at 8 columns (five chunks, 10.30 against 9.76 at c4) and 4096 x 64 (eight, 11.84 against 10.71 at c4).

## Every command fits its KV budget and backs it whole (2026-10-31, MDEV, branch fix/kv-fit-all on main fe2ccacae, F2DEV's ruling of 2026-10-31 05:59 on D1 part one, lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)

- **Seen:** `bench --model` on Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M at 128k on one MI50 measured decode attention at 0.90 ms per 1k tokens of history, twice its 0.45 at 64k.
  The cause was the pool, not the kernel: a command other than `serve` kept the model's context as its budget (163,840 tokens on the context-patched copy) and grew the cache by doubling, and the growth to 1,280 blocks held every layer's old and new buffers at once beside 17.3 GiB of weights, so about 800 MiB of the cache stayed in system memory (GTT 96 to 896 MiB).
  Both readings stand, the 128k one corrected as a bench artifact: 30B decode attention a token at 32k / 64k / 96k / 128k was 16.6 / 30.7 / 44.0 / 120.1 ms with the growing pool and 16.5 / 30.5 / 44.4 / 61.5 ms with a pool of 135,168 tokens backed up front, a flat 0.458 ms per 1k, against the reference's 0.174 (main e14b3eb18 plus a measurement-only probe patch, renderD131, default clocks, f16 caches, int8).
  The earlier table's 128k rows (30B tg 7.7 tok/s, 118.3 ms of attention a token, 0.90 ms per 1k; 27B 0.50 ms per 1k) were read from the growing pool and are bench artifacts; D1's baseline is the up-front pool.
- **Done:** `place_model` fits every request's budget as it fitted a server's (`fitted_kv`): the options' budget, `--kv-tokens` or the model's context, where it fits, else the most whole blocks that do, backed whole as the model is made, so no pass grows the cache and nothing spills; a load where not one block fits is refused by the fit's text.
  `PlacementRequest::fit_kv` is gone; `kv_auto` (a server without `--kv-tokens`) still asks for every block the devices hold.
  A malformed split (share count, a negative share, all zero, more than 16 devices) is refused by `check_split` before the fit, by its own text, rather than read as a budget that does not fit; a request over one device may leave it unnamed.
  Where not one block fits beside the hot rows of a table read from its file, the table holds none, as the lookup choice gave before.
  Only an automatic budget or a split without shares waits for the free memory to stay level (`level_first`); a budget the devices hold is taken at once, and one they cut waits as before.
- **Tests:** `placement`'s `kv_fitted` holds a request naming only its device to the server's cut and backed budget (fails on main); the lookup cases follow the one rule (an explicit device table on a device it does not fit is refused by the fit); the test backend of `load-progress` and `model-validation` keeps its cache in host blocks the CPU's attention reads, since the cache is now backed as the model is made.
- **CPU buffers on zero pages (F2DEV's ruling of 07:11):** backing whole cost the CPU time and memory, since `CpuBuffer`'s value-initialized vector touched every page of the cache: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `generate -n 8 --device cpu --threads 4` took 0.57 to 1.72 s on main and 3.83 to 5.23 s with the cache backed (construct 0.07 s against 2.90 s), at a peak RSS of 0.74 GB against 5.31 GB for the 40,960-token f16 cache of 4.70 GB.
  Every owned `CpuBuffer` now holds `core::HostPages`, the operating system's zero pages, so the backed cache takes address space until passes write it; a count of owned buffers found none below a page (59 on that generate, 33 on Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M, 62 on `bench --seqs 2`, page rounding adding 2.5 to 6 KB), so the rule holds for every one.
  `kv-cache`'s arena failure is now injected through a backend's `alloc`, since CPU buffers no longer pass through `operator new`.
- **Startup at the head (rig, CPUs 12-15, rig load 9.5 to 9.6, interleaved, 6 runs an arm):** the same generate took 0.559 to 0.586 s on main and 0.550 to 0.603 s here, peak RSS 0.736 GB against 0.724 GB.
  Byte identity on the CPU against main: 128 greedy ids, `logits` on a prompt and perplexity over 4 windows of 512 (29.1352) are the same bytes.
- **Speed on the CPU (rig, CPUs 12-15, load 9 to 11 from other work, 40 monitor samples, main, a layout control of main with an unused function appended to `cpu_backend.hpp`, and this tree, six rounds in rotating order, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `bench --p 512 --n 128 --r 3 --threads 4`, medians):**
  | | main | control | this tree |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | pp512 (tok/s) | 215.8 | 214.8 | 218.6 |
  | tg128 (tok/s) | 43.3 | 44.0 | 44.0 |
  The tree sits within the layout band (+1.3 % prompt and +1.7 % decode against main, +1.8 % and +0.1 % against the control); slow samples kept: main's round 3 prompt 160.6 +- 59.4 and round 2 decode 37.2, the control's round 6 decode 29.9. `tests/perf.py` (synthetic): matmul 34.19 / 34.38 / 33.19 GFLOPS, prefill 5666 / 5699 / 5619, decode 5269 / 4907 / 5254 tok/s.
- **Settle wait:** a budget the fit cuts first waits for the devices' free memory to settle, about 5 s on a card and up to 30 s on the CPU, whose host reading moves between reads; a budget that fits is taken at once (docs/USAGE.md). F2DEV accepted it as serve's rule.
- **Checks:** CTest on the rig 76 of 77 at -j4 at the first head, `server-spec` failing once under load with "unequal requests never drafted together" (SDEV's recorded flake), then 6 of 6 alone; at the zero-page head 76 of 77 with `kv-cache` holding the old injection, which passes after its fix; on Windows (VirtualAlloc) 77 of 78 with the same `kv-cache` case, which passes after the fix. The CPU suite passes at the head, baseline skipping without its fixture.
- **Startup on a device (one MI50, renderD131, CPUs 8,9, default clocks, rig load 10 to 17 from other work, both arms built alike with Vulkan, interleaved, `generate -n 8 --device vulkan:0`):**
  | Model | main (s) | this tree (s) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, 40,960-token cache (6 runs) | 0.830-0.968, first 1.447 | 0.822-0.941 |
  | Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M at its 40,960-token context, fits (4 runs) | 6.67-7.45, median 6.84 | 6.74-7.80, median 7.12 |
  | the same at 163,840 tokens, cut by the fit (3 runs) | 7.38-8.35 | 12.50-14.67 |
  A budget the card holds costs about 0.3 s of start on the 30B, the 4 GiB cache backed at load; a budget the fit cuts adds the settle wait, about 5 s, as above.
- **Device legs for landing (F2DEV's approval of 08:23; one MI50, renderD131, CPUs 8,9, default clocks; main fe2ccacae and this head e412c18af each built with Vulkan from an archive of its commit):**
  Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on vulkan:0 is byte-identical to main: 256 greedy ids and their text, `logits` on a prompt, perplexity over 8 windows of 512 batched (29.6012) and over 2 windows per token.
  The suite with `--device vulkan:0` and the 0.6B fixture as `LLMX_BASELINE_GGUF` passes, 46 components, `baseline` within its HF bounds (top-1 6/6, NLL delta 0.0011 to 0.0067), the rest of its fixtures and numpy's checks skipping as not on disk.
  `bench --p 512 --n 128 --r 3` on the same card, interleaved over 4 rounds (rig load 8 to 11): pp512 8908 to 8927 tok/s on main and 8915 to 8926 here, tg128 399.1 to 400.2 against 399.3 to 400.2.
  The Radeon VII leg is not run, as ruled: no device code changed.
- **Left:** the hosted run on the coordinator's gate branch.
- **Startup cost (rig, CPUs 12-15, rig load 16 to 19 from other work, both arms built alike from archives of main and of this tree, interleaved):** Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `generate -n 8 --device cpu --threads 4` took 0.57 to 1.72 s on main (11 runs) and 3.83 to 5.23 s here, peak RSS 0.74 GB against 5.31 GB: the 40,960-token f16 cache, 4.70 GB, is now backed, and the CPU backend's buffer zero-fills it by touching every page (construct 0.07 s against 2.90 s).
  A measurement-only arm whose CPU buffers take the OS's zero pages (`core::HostPages`) instead of a value-initialized vector took 0.56 to 1.42 s at 0.73 GB, main's figures: backing whole then costs address space, not time or memory, until a pass writes it.
  Text and ids are identical in all three arms. The device figures (Qwen3-0.6B and the 30B at its 40,960-token context on one MI50) are owed once a card is free.
- **Open for F2DEV:** the CPU's cost above, with the zero-page buffer or growth whose fit counts the last doubling as the ways out; and on a device a budget the fit cuts waits about 5 s for the free memory to settle, as a server's does, which every such command now pays.
- **Left:** F2DEV's review; the hosted run.
## Long history matches priced apart from short ones (2026-10-30, SDEV, branch fix/draft-long-matches on fix/lookup-longest-match c92d2d353, which it needs and lands after, the owner's production report through the coordinator, for F2DEV's review)

- **Goal:** the owner's forked 225k-token chat on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 drafted history copies to 63 once (5d98a5bf3, 93.5 tok/s, history 32+ kept 529/529 at position 20 and 402/402 at 63) and on its reruns stopped at 12 to 26 (2f4f4481 57.4 tok/s, and 5d98 again), with every position's keep share near 0.97.
- **Cause:** not a frontier shared by sources (each source and bucket prices from its own counts; the proposer stopped at 4 to 8 in the same server where history 32+ ran to 63). The walk measured a match only to 32 tokens, so "32+" held verbatim copies and short coincidences in one acceptance; at a mix keeping 0.97 a position the price rightly stops near 16 to 26.
- **Profile:** Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 code edit (spec_edit, greedy, one MI50), the latest earlier 8-gram's continuation against the reply: kept to 63, matches of 8-15 0.05, 16-31 0.13, 32-127 0.69, 128-511 0.94, 512+ 0.96 (/zpool1/llmx-ldev-scratch/sdev/ab/matchlen on the Linux MI50 machine).
- **Done:** the failing test (`tests/spec.cpp`: buckets 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+, a 600-token copy reported as 128 and a 40-token match as 40, and the copy drafting the same tokens as a match of eight before the same continuation), then the fix: `Lookup::kLongestMatch` 128, `kMatchBuckets` 4, `/v1/health` `by_source` with the new buckets. F2DEV's simplification: 128-511 and 512+ price alike (0.94 and 0.96 at 63, 0.98 and 0.99 at 16), so they share one bucket; a split at 512 comes only if a measurement shows 512+ keeping clearly more. `tests/sampler.cpp` adds the owner's rising profile (0.8 at the first position to 0.99 from the 20th: the current rule opens to 63 from a fresh start and within 200 verifies after 300 short misses) and per-bucket depths (0.97 a position within 26, 0.998 at 60 or more); both pass on the rule as it is, so no change to `Acceptance::keeps` is made. A tail-pooled prior for sparse deep positions was tried in the loop and gained nothing.
- **Cold start (2026-10-31):** on Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 over one MI50 the four buckets lost 12 to 24 percent on long copies on a fresh server and were level once warm, the new 128+ bucket starting as a fresh record and stopping near 32 drafts where 32+ had opened to 63. F2DEV's ruling: a bucket with no verify of its own starts from the next shorter bucket's record (`spec::Record::seed`, through `spec::lookup_first` for the request's and in `Scheduler::propose` for the server's), never over a bucket with its own; `sampler`'s `seeded_bucket` holds a 150-token copy's first verify in a fresh 128+ bucket to 63 drafts beside a 32-127 bucket at 63.
- **Owner evidence:** on production's preview dfdd6ae7 (2f4f4481 with 27a49be13) the owner reports the forked chat's drafts "boost better" than on 2f4f4481 alone.
- **Not in it:** `draft_depths` takes one depth a pass, so in a pass of several requests a weak one is fed that depth or none; per-request depths are a separate change if multi-user runs show it.
- **Card A/B** (Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 on one MI50, `--drafter lookup,embedded --draft-max 63`, greedy, fresh servers, every reply identical across arms), decode tok/s, main against the branch at the seed's code:

| cold prose b1-b5, mean | 17.2 | 17.3 | level |

| warm l1 | 45.3, 46.3 | 48.8, 47.2 | +4.9% |
| warm l2 | 45.5, 46.3 | 49.6, 46.2 | +4.3% |
| warm l4 (aggregate) | 35.9, 35.6 | 42.0, 34.7 | level at best: +7% on the means, one branch run below both main runs, and cold l4 read -5% |
| a1, four runs an arm | 66.24, 63.57, 63.48, 64.44 | 63.60, 63.40, 63.45, 63.41 | inside main's spread (means 64.43 and 63.47) |

## Q8_0 decode builds by workgroup count (2026-10-31, VDEV, branch feat/q8-decode-occupancy, built on main 0e7060da8 and rebased onto main fe2ccacae after wide-decode, where the remainder chunk of a call goes through `filling_build` and the whole chunks side by side keep their build, being wider than 8 columns, step 1 of VDEV's plan of 2026-10-31 00:55 for Flash-Next's verifies of 6 to 8 rows, approved by F2DEV at 00:55; step 2, the same rule for the F32 row builds, is approved as its own branch after this one)

**Goal:** a Q8_0 decode chunk of 2 to 8 columns over few rows fills the device: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 320-row hc_down and shared-expert matrices gave 20 workgroups on an MI50's 60 compute units at the 8-column build's 16 rows a workgroup. Every column keeps the one-column build's bits.
**Done:** three builds of 8 columns with fewer rows a workgroup (`kVecFewerRows`: 8 columns and 2 rows, 8 rows a workgroup; 4 columns and 2 rows in two column groups, 4; 4 columns and 1 row in two groups, 2) and `VulkanBackend::filling_build`, which gives a chunk of 2 to 8 columns the first of its own build and those three whose busy workgroups number at least two a compute unit over 8-bit activations and one over 16-bit ones, else the last; a column group past the chunk's columns is not counted.
The factors and the fallback live in that one function; no profile number and no model rule, only `caps.compute_units` and the activations' width, as the one-column builds already take it.
`backend-vulkan` checks the new builds in the decode-column cells (Q8_0 rows 2560 wide 320, 640, 1280 and 5120 tall, beside the existing ones) and witnesses the choice over rows halving from 65536 to 32 at 2, 5 and 8 columns; the `--isa` screen reads the new builds' names (`_8col_2row`, `_8col_2row_span2`, `_8col_1row_span2`) and holds them to their shapes.
**The factors.** At sustained clocks on one MI50, int8, us a call at 8 columns (the scratch bench of 2026-10-31, rig holds/q8/bench9.txt; the forced builds bit-identical to each column alone at every shape and 2 to 8 columns):
| matrix (K x rows) | own build, workgroups | own | 8x2 | 4x2 two groups | 4x1 two groups |
| 10240 x 320 hc_down | 20 | 28.0 | 19.2 | 17.0 | 17.0 |
| 2560 x 320 shexp/2 | 20 | 10.7 | 11.9 | 7.2 | 8.0 |
| 2560 x 1280 ple_value/2 | 80 | 25.3 (13.1 to 25.3) | 13.1 | 13.9 | 16.0 |
| 3072 x 2560 out/2 | 160 | 21.2 | 22.6 | 25.2 | 32.2 |
| 2560 x 3072 gate/2 | 192 | 25.4 | 23.9 | 26.3 | 34.2 |
| 2560 x 5120 qkv/2 | 320 | 34.2 | 35.8 | 40.6 | 54.0 |
| 320 x 10240 hc_up | 640 | 21.0 | 22.8 | 28.5 | 32.9 |
Below 1.4 workgroups a compute unit the own build takes up to 1.6 times the best; from 2.7 it holds or wins but for gate/2 at 3.2, where 8x2 is 6 percent faster. A factor of 4 would take that 6 percent and lose 7 percent on out/2 at 2.7, so 2 sits between the losses and the holds.
Over the 16-bit twin (f16, rig holds/q8/f16bench.txt), us at 8 columns, own / 8x2 / 4x2 two groups / 4x1 two groups: hc_down (20 workgroups) 32.9 / 23.1 / 24.2 / 30.3, shexp/2 (20) 11.9 / 8.8 / 9.5 / 10.9, Qwen3-0.6B's o_proj 1024 x 1024 (64) 9.0 / 9.0 / 9.2 / 10.9, its down 3072 x 1024 (64) 19.1 / 20.5 / 18.7 / 25.8, ple_value/2 (80) 18.0 / 19.3 / 20.5 / 28.6. A first build at factor 2 for both widths cost Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 f16 4.2 percent at six sequences (1365 to 1308 tok/s, medians of six), so the 16-bit factor is 1; the same 0.6B shapes in int8 gain (o_proj 7.5 to 6.5 us, down 16.0 to 13.4).
**Gates** (MI50s under RADV in the rig's Vulkan image, main 0e7060da8 and this branch built the same way from git archives; Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver on Windows):
- `backend-vulkan --isa` on an MI50 exits 0: 207104 decode columns in f16 and in int8 equal to the same columns alone, 72 calls of 2 to 8 columns in the build their workgroups give, 23 Q8_0 decode builds held to the counts their shapes give, the six new ones among them; rerun without `--isa` after the 16-bit factor, exit 0.
- `backend-vulkan --isa` on the Radeon VII exits 0 at the final selection: 207104 decode columns, 52392 Q8_0 decode columns on the integer dot in each dtype, 72 calls in their builds; on this driver its 17 Q8_0 decode builds, the six new ones among them, are held to their one-column build's kinds of operation, as before.
- Byte identity against main on one MI50: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M, greedy raw, chat and seeded generation, lookup drafts at 32 and at 7 (f16 and int8), logits, perplexity, a two-turn chat and `tools/server_mix_check.py` ids, 12 of 12 files the same at the first head and again at the final one; `bench --seqs 6 --profile` shows the 8x2 build taking 0.6B's o_proj and down in int8.
- Byte identity on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL over four MI50s (tensor width 2, layer shares 1,1, int8, production's flags): three greedy generations of 160, 200 and 160 tokens with lookup and MTP drafts and with lookup alone, the same.
- `run_tests.py --device vulkan:0 --require-tools` on an MI50 (renderD137) at 74e6a893d, built whole from its git archive: 44 components PASS; `baseline` SKIP (no real-model fixture on that tree); `raw-blocks` FAIL only on its numpy form, the Vulkan image having no numpy, after every pure-form check passed (it runs no llmx binary).
- CTest on Windows with the Radeon VII: 94 of 95 under `-j4`; `vulkan-lifetime` failed its hold-release timing (p99 1.09 ms, max 8.9 ms) beside the other tests and passes alone 3 of 3. Docs and dead-code pass.
**The wall gain**, Flash-Next 2x2 at production's flags, `bench --p 512 --n 16 --r 3 --drafter <MTP head> --draft-max 7`, ten runs an arm in five ABBA rounds back to back, mean of the runs' medians and a 95 percent interval on the difference, ms:
| verify rows | main | branch | difference |
| 1 (a step) | 32.87 | 31.92 | -0.95 +- 2.57 |
| 4 | 42.48 | 41.79 | -0.69 +- 0.98 |
| 5 | 47.07 | 45.50 | -1.57 +- 1.16 |
| 6 | 50.44 | 48.59 | -1.85 +- 1.63 (-3.7%) |
| 7 | 53.13 | 51.26 | -1.87 +- 1.67 |
| 8 | 56.17 | 54.08 | -2.10 +- 1.65 (-3.7%) |
Medians of the ten: 6 rows 49.66 to 48.01, 8 rows 56.64 to 53.18. pp512 734.5 against 735.2 tok/s and tg16 44.8 against 45.7, level. These ran with the first build, factor 2 at both widths; Flash-Next runs int8, whose selection the 16-bit factor leaves unchanged.
The rig was loaded throughout by other developers' builds and runs (load average 15 to 123, rig holds/flq-mon.txt, every 5 s); the arms were interleaved within it.
Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on one MI50, `bench --seqs 6 --p 64 --n 256 --r 5`, three ABBA rounds, medians of six tok/s: int8 1480 to 1521 (+2.8%), f16 1366 to 1369 (level) at the final selection.
**After the rebase onto fe2ccacae** (only STATUS conflicted; the Vulkan code and tests are those of the resolution on wide-decode dcf580111, f4fcfefb0): `backend-vulkan --isa` on an MI50 at f4fcfefb0 exits 0 (decode columns in f16 and int8 equal to the same columns alone, 72 calls of 2 to 8 columns in their build, the screen's counts held), and on the Radeon VII at 72d8768f7 exits 0 (1892048 decode columns, 505052 Q8_0 decode columns on the integer dot in each dtype, 72 calls in their build); byte identity against main fe2ccacae on one MI50, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M, the same 12 files as above, 12 of 12 the same.
**Left:** F2DEV review; hosted run; lands by fast-forward as one commit; then step 2 (the F32 row builds' starvation: ssm_alpha/beta 2560 x 48 at 12 workgroups take 29 us at 8 columns against 6.5 at 1).
**Gotchas:** the MI50's memory clock drops to 350 MHz between short bursts at automatic power levels, so a short kernel bench or a single profiled run flips by up to 1.6x: time kernels after 100 warm and 100 timed runs on device time and models back to back.
`pp_dpm_mclk` read every 5 s showed 350 MHz in most samples even on cards at 100 percent busy, so a sampled reading does not show the clock a kernel ran at.
On two columns the own build, 8x2 and the first two-group build all keep 8 rows a busy workgroup, so such a chunk takes its own build or the last.
## A tensor group sums a hyper-connection block, not its four streams (2026-10-30, RDEV, branch perf/ts-block-sum on main e8d413a84, the 2x2 prefill task, plan A approved by F2DEV at 17:36 with four conditions; approved by F2DEV at 23:25 and landing by fast-forward on a green hosted run)

**Goal:** on a tensor group, qwen4exp's members sum the part's 2560-wide block and then each injects the summed block into the four residual streams, as one device does, instead of summing four injected 10240-wide streams, so a sum moves a quarter of the bytes.
**Why (profile of main 06936f48e, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2, int8, pp2048 1097.7 and 1096.4 tok/s, GPUs 4-7 at default clocks):** each card's span of about 1500 ms of a 1879 ms profiled pass is 980-1035 ms of compute and 440 ms of copies into the peer's inbox (192 sums of 512 rows x 10240 floats, 21 MB each, at 9.1 GB/s); waits on the peer are 15-26 ms, the stage handoff under 8 ms and host gaps 4 ms. ubatch 256, 384, 512 and 1024 give 1109, 1099, 1097 and 912-915 tok/s.
**Done:** the profile and the plan; `Collective::sum_in_place` (CPU and Vulkan, `sum_rows` writing over its residual, two shots copying the gathered shares), `ModelPlan::partial` and `Architecture::join`, the runtime's sums through `Model::group_sum` (a stage's two, the drafter's two), the collective and the fit sized by `sum_width`, and qwen4exp writing its block as the partial rows and injecting the sum in `join`.
- **Tests:** `backend-group` and `backend-vulkan` hold the in-place sum to the member-order sum at the width made for and narrower ones, in one shot and two, and refuse one past the reserved floats; the MTP fixture's architecture wrapper forwards `join`.
- **Measured** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, int8, f16 KV, `--lookup-storage file`, GPUs 4-7 at default clocks, CPUs 4-7,12-15, main 06936f48e against 12995fc9e built alike, two ABBA rounds, the second under a monitor log: load average 21 mean and 34 most, renderD130/131 busy with other work throughout):

| 2x2 cell | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| pp2048, tok/s | 1052.5, 1097.7, 1098.3, 1098.5 | 1399.6, 1407.0, 1406.5, 1411.5 |
| pp512, tok/s | 707.8, 718.4, 708.8, 718.0 | 935.9, 937.3, 938.3, 938.7 |
| verify of 15 drafts (16 rows), ms | 83.2, 82.3, 82.3, 83.4 | 76.8, 78.0, 76.8, 77.6 |
| decode at 118k, one reply, tok/s | 34.0, 36.7 | 37.2, 38.4 |
| decode at 118k, seven replies (7-row passes), tok/s | 132.8, 134.2 | 140.2, 143.6 |
| the same, sum_wait a stage pass, ms (stage 0 / 1) | 12.3 / 11.7, 12.1 / 12.1 | 11.7 / 11.5, 11.6 / 11.9 |

Verify of k drafts (`bench --drafter` with the sidecar MTP head, short context), ms, the mean of 4 samples an arm from two ABBA rounds; every branch sample is below every main sample but at 1 and 3 rows, where they overlap:

With drafts (sidecar MTP and lookup, at most 7) at production's flags, interleaved main, branch, branch, main: the 117,876-token prompt, then 256 tokens alone, then seven replies of 128 at once, a monitor log throughout (production's cards about 50% busy over the whole window, in every run):

| run | one reply, s | its tokens and rows a pass | seven replies, s (tok/s together) | rows a pass | stage 0 pass at seven, ms (recording, sum_wait, after) |

| main | 6.37 | 1.35, 1.44 | 7.06 (126.9) | 3.58 | 22.7 (17.3, 11.7, 7.2) |
| branch | 6.51 | 1.24, 1.36 | 6.55 (136.8) | 3.49 | 21.1 (15.8, 11.3, 6.7) |

  - The drafted and kept counts are context, not a measure of either arm: a group's bits differ, so the replies are different text and lookup's matches differ with them. One reply drafted / kept 84 / 66 on main and 75 / 50 and 123 / 99 on the branch; seven replies 123 / 102 and 125 / 102 on main and 25 / 17 and 36 / 26 on the branch.
  - A first, unmatched drafted pair read the branch 25% slower for one reply and 30% slower for seven. It was one branch run whose stage 0 recording outside the sums took 14.0 ms a pass against 5.8 on main, while production's cards were busy during that run only; in the interleaved pairs above it did not repeat.
  - The 118k cells are a server at production's flags without drafts (with drafts the rows a pass differed run to run): a 117,876-token prompt read once, then that prompt and 256 tokens, then seven such replies at once, the stage split from `/v1/health` before and after each.
  - Profile of the branch: a card's span 1162-1186 ms, copies into the peer's inbox 114-124 ms, compute 965-1028 ms; `sum_rows` 5.5 ms a card against 23; the join's `inject_streams` 16.3-16.5 ms a card, as main's inject.
- **Correctness:** CTest 94 of 94 on the MI50 build and 95 of 95 on Windows with the Radeon VII; the tiny qwen4exp fixture's CPU group of 2 against HF, 17 rows, max 5.2e-08 before and after (bound 2e-5); qwen4exp-mtp's group against one CPU 5.96e-08 before and after, drafts on and off equal; Flash-Next on a layer split of 4 byte-identical to main (the last 16 logits rows of a 2753-token text and 64 greedy ids); docs, dead-code and arch-boundary pass.
  - F2DEV's substitute for the Flash HF cells, whose released Q8_0 file and 16k references are gone: f32 dtype and caches, 2x2 main and branch against the layer split of 4, last 512 rows of the restore bundle's 16k inputs. Raw: top-1 510 and 508 of 512, median |dlogit| 0.030 and 0.040; chat: 458 and 457, 0.217 and 0.180. Before any discrete choice flips (rows 1-999 of a 2753-token text) both are 1.7e-5 median, 4.6e-5 p90 from the layer split.
  - Found on the way, not this branch's: on the chat 16k both 2x2 arms part from the layer split by 0.38-0.42 mean |dNLL|. Per-layer dumps of the first rows that part show the residuals equal to 3e-6 until a router near-tie (margins 3e-6 and 8e-6) flips one of the eight experts, which then spreads; the indexer picks every key below its budget there. Main's and the branch's 2x2, which differ only in rounding, part by 0.147 on the chat and 0.022 on the raw input, so the chat input is the more sensitive one, and no group bug was found.
  - The device suite (`run_tests.py --device vulkan:0` on an MI50) passed 45 of 46 components; the one failure was `version`, run on a tree with an uncommitted file, whose build identifier carries the dirty marker, and it passes on the rebuilt clean tree.
**Left:** the hosted run in the coordinator's queue; then plan B (the sum copies left beside a micro-batch's compute on a second queue, and the submission path), a branch of its own.
**Gotchas:** a group's bits change (x + w*(b0 + b1) in place of x + (w*b0 + w*b1)); one device and the layer split keep main's bytes.

## A background job yields to a decoding reply (2026-10-30, MDEV, branch fix/reread-yields on main 06936f48e, the owner's production report through the coordinator, F2DEV's ruling of 19:55, lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix)
- **Seen on production:** a job reading a conversation's next turn ahead took two 16-row chunk passes of about 65 ms for every decode pass of a live reply at 156k tokens of context, and the reply ran at about 6 tokens a second (`rule_replies` 1545 against `rule_chunks` 3273); later a 64-row chunk pass of 131 ms between decode passes of 27 to 33 ms.
- **Cause:** `Scheduler::plan` took the jobs as the prompt work whenever no client prompt waited, so the service rule gave a job the share it gives a waiting user's prompt: on a split every slot past the replies' took a chunk, and a job always passed the wait bound.
- **Done:** a job forms rows only in a round where no reply decodes and no client prompt is read, never rides a replies' pass, and a chunk in flight finishes but continues into no further pass while a reply decodes (`Scheduler::replying`, also out of the round's due test, so nothing spins); `passes.since_start.rule_jobs` counts a job's passes, so `rule_chunks` counts client prompts only. The reread counters were booked right: `reread.now.jobs` counts a live job, one that has read the ids given mid-reply waiting with no rows left for the rest of its turn, and `since_start.jobs` counts completions, which come with the whole turn.
- **Tests:** `server-resume`, `job_beside_decode`: no job rows in a pass formed while the request decodes, at most the chunks in flight, reading once the reply ends, and the mid-reply job live with no rows left and no completion until the whole turn, then completed and gone. The tests commit fails on main with "the job read 1280 rows in 5 passes beside the decoding request". `reprefilled`'s writing cases now hold the job to no rows while the reply is written.
- **Also:** `server-passes`'s random schedules now hold jobs, one request in five, to rows only in a round where no reply decodes and no client prompt is read (5972 job slices over 2000 schedules, none beside a reply or a client prompt).
- **Gates at this source:** CTest 76 of 77 at first, cache-scenario holding the old rule (a job reading a reply's content while it is written); that case now waits for the job between the turns and passes, so all 77 pass. The CPU suite passes; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 byte identity against main in generate greedy, a seeded chat and server_mix_check ids. cache-scenario's reply_reread now lets the job read between the turns, as a user reading the reply gives it, before the next turn forks its 768 rows.
- **Left:** the hosted run; production's same chat showing the reply back at its alone rate while rows_left still falls between turns.

## A draft frontier set by a few early verifies relaxes (2026-10-30, SDEV, branch fix/draft-frontier on fix/draft-depth-censored a3a0f5f4e, the coordinator's decision on the canary's reading, reviewed by F2DEV, lands by fast-forward as two commits after the depth fix)

- **Goal:** the depth fix on production's canary (25b6280ab, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2, `--draft-max 63`) moved the stop from 8 drafts to 20: after 1934 s positions 12 to 20 were fed 1869 to 1812 times and kept 85 to 91 percent, position 21 15 times.
- **Cause (inferred, not yet read off the canary):** a position past the priced depth is fed by no verify, so its chance is whatever the few verifies that reached it early left there; five that reached 21 and missed it price it at 0.44 of position 20, under what a row needs, for good.
- **Done:** the failing test (`tests/sampler.cpp`, `frontier_relaxes`: five verifies keep 20 and miss 21, then 400 keep all 20; the depth fix leaves 21 at 0.444 of 20), then the fix: `spec::Acceptance` weighs each verify 0.99 of the next in the kept and reached counts its chances read, as `spec::PassTimes` does its passes, so the early misses fade and 21 goes back to the chance measured before it; the whole counts stay for reporting (`reached()` beside `drafted()` and `kept()`).
  `/v1/health` gives `drafting.since_start.by_source`: for the proposer and each history match bucket, by position, fed, kept and reached, which shows a frontier directly (docs/SERVER.md, docs/USAGE.md); `tests/server.py` checks they add up to `by_position` and that kept <= reached <= fed.
  F2DEV's review: a closed loop (`tests/sampler.cpp`, `frontier_loop`) runs `spec::draft_depths` on the chances verify by verify against true chances, after the five early misses at 21: kept at 0.99 everywhere, the depth passes 21 within 301 to 343 verifies over eight seeds (bound 400); with position 21 truly at 0.2, 12 to 17 of 2000 verifies feed it (bound 40). `spec::kForget` is one constant for the acceptance and the pass cost; the falling case's bound of 0.25 is explained beside it (0.2 read as 0.239).
- **Before, for the canary (F2DEV's condition):** the current canary 25b6280ab's `by_position` at 1934 s, 1812 fed at position 20 against 15 at 21.
- **CPU checks (rig, CPUs 14-15):** `sampler`, `spec`, `server-spec`, `server-passes-cpu` pass; the suite's `server`, `cli`, `docs` and `dead-code` pass; the failing test fails on a3a0f5f4e with position 21 at 0.444 of position 20.
- **Left:** on the canary (F2DEV's ruling, 18:11): after about a day, `by_source` by position, depths and the kept share past 21, and decode tok/s against 25b6280ab over comparable load, rolled back if positions past 21 keep missing and tok/s drops; the canary's `by_source` confirms the step at the frontier and whether forgetting moves it; probing one position past the priced depth only if it does not.

## Draft positions priced by the verifies that reached them (2026-10-30, SDEV, branch fix/draft-depth-censored on main 06936f48e, the owner's production report through the coordinator, reviewed by F2DEV, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Goal:** production's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 at `--draft-max 63` (`lookup` ahead of the MTP head) drafted at most 8 positions where it kept 15 at `--draft-max 15`, and its replies stayed under 100 tok/s.
- **Cause:** `spec::Acceptance::keeps(i)` was the share of the verifies that fed position i and kept it, the request's own weighed with the server's.
  A verify that missed at position 2 counted as a miss at every later position it fed, and a position past a draft's depth got no count at all.
  Production's health after 12043 s: positions 6, 7 and 8 kept 8130 of 9095, 7826 of 8694 and 7699 of 8506 drafted (96 to 98 percent of the drafts that reached them), position 9 39 of 221 and positions 23 to 63 none of about 80, those being the first verifies, which fed every position before the pass price was known and missed within a few.
  At 3.3 ms a row on a 20 ms pass position 9 pays from a chance of about 0.36; its share gave 0.18, so no request fed it again and the share never moved.
  At `--draft-max 15` the same first verifies fed 15 positions and kept most of them, which is why the cap showed there.
  Refuted: the price table (`PriceTable`), whose rare widths hold outlier means, never reaches the depth; `spec::draft_depths` reads `PassTimes`' line. No other cap is 8 there: decode columns 16 on the MI50 profile, a lone decoder's columns `--draft-max`, 64 draft rows, 64 mark rows.
- **Done:** the failing test (`tests/sampler.cpp`, `censored_depth`: 80 verifies of 63 drafts missing within three, then verifies of 8 kept, priced at 16.7 ms and 3.3 ms a row, held at 8 on main), then the fix: a position's chance given every draft before it was kept, counted over the verifies that reached it (`Acceptance::reached_`), weighed with four verifies at the prior's, which is weighed with four at the chance measured at the last position either reached (one half for the first draft, one where none was reached), and the chance of keeping the drafts up to a position their product; the test's request now drafts 21.
- **CPU checks (rig, CPUs 10-13, 06936f48e against this branch, the same build way):** `sampler` and `spec` pass; `server-passes` passes 2000 schedules; `server-passes-cpu` passes; `docs` and `dead-code` pass.
  `server-spec` passes 10 of 11 runs, 5 alone and 5 beside `server-passes-cpu`; its first run, beside `server-passes-cpu`, failed the Flash split QSA private case on `cpu,cpu` ("unequal requests never drafted together"), which main passed in 13 of 13 runs, 5 of them under the same load; that case drafts 3 a verify on 16 columns with 3 marks, so the order the chances give, the one thing this change can move there, grants every draft either way; at 7e30cb7d0 it then passed 20 runs of 20, each beside `server-passes-cpu` run in a loop, which closes it as F2DEV asked.
- **Before and after on cards (2026-10-30, renderD130, 131, 134 and 135, CPUs 4-7, default clocks, main 0.1.0+g06936f48ec69 against 0.1.0+g6a639e733c2c, both from detached clones, a fresh server an arm, interleaved main, fix, main, fix, greedy, `--drafter lookup,...` at `--draft-max 63`, DMAX's client; raw in /zpool1/llmx-ldev-scratch/sdev/ab):**
  Every reply is identical across arms.
  | Model, task | main (tok/s) | fix (tok/s) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2, spec.hpp edit, 1 user | 174.5, 178.4 | 176.9, 186.9 |
  | Flash-Next 2x2, policy.hpp edit, 1 user | 192.6, 193.2 | 191.6, 189.5 |
  | Flash-Next 2x2, five prose prompts, 1 user | 44.1 to 55.4 | 44.2 to 57.5 |
  | Flash-Next 2x2, four prose users, aggregate | 79.8, 70.1 | 74.7, 70.9 |
  | Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 on two cards, spec.hpp edit after a copy whose history draft misses, 1 user | 38.5, 38.4 | 39.0, 35.9 |
  | 27B-MTP, five prose prompts, 1 user | 15.7 to 28.0 | 16.0 to 23.4 |
  | 27B-MTP, four prose users, aggregate | 33.0, 33.6 | 33.8, 34.1 |
  The lock did not form on main in these fresh-server sessions: main's code edits drafted all 63 positions (Flash: 5660 of 6606 drafts past position 8; 27B: 100 verifies of 63), since the first deep history verifies there kept their drafts, so these runs show parity and no gain; a copy built to miss early (27B, 63 fed, 16 kept) did not lock main either, the pass price being unknown on many passes, which gives each request its cap.
  The gain rests on production's table after hours of mixed load and on the CPU replay.
- **Landing:** F2DEV approved landing at parity as a bug fix; the change lands by fast-forward as two commits, the failing test and then the fix, on a green hosted run.
- **Left:** production runs it as a canary; the coordinator reads `/v1/health` drafted and kept by position past 8 after about a day of real load, and positions past 8 still never fed reopen it.
- **Gotchas:** a record of no verifies keeps every draft at one half, as before, so a new request still ranks above one whose drafts miss; a first version extrapolated one half from the first position and starved such a request in `server-spec`'s column case.
