## Image encodes beside replies, reused images and the image token bound (2026-10-30, RDEV, branch feat/image-no-hold on main 06936f48e, the coordinator's orders of 2026-10-30 and the owner's rulings relayed with them, approved by F2DEV but for the tails' owner, now built; the owner asked for it on production as a preview)

- **Goal:** an image's encode runs as ordinary work between the passes, never under a whole-model hold; a history that forks inside an image encodes nothing; `--image-max-tokens` replaces `--image-max-pixels`; the encoder's time profiled.
- **Done, no hold:** an encode's pieces are items of the thread that records the first stage, which records the embedding's backend (`Cache::encode_piece`, `queue_piece`, `ImageSteps`), behind the passes formed before them and ahead of those formed after.
  The last piece copies the rows on the device into host-visible storage and submits (`VisionEncoder::copy_rows`), and the round takes them once that ticket has retired (`ImageEncode::rows`, `Cache::landed`), looking again a millisecond on (`encode_bound`), as a promotion's copy does; a request waiting on a queued piece or on its rows does not wake the round (`waits_encode`).
  A dropped or failed encode's queued pieces run nothing; a failed piece ends its request with the error.
  Beside replies a replies' pass meets the pieces the chunk budget holds at a piece's measured time, one at least (`encode_pieces`, `Scheduler::piece_ms_`, F2DEV's landing condition), as a prompt takes a chunk beside them: without the hold's drains the pieces came every round, and on four cards a reply fell from 57 to 5 tokens a second while the image encoded.
  A piece's time is what a replies' pass that waited behind pieces took beyond the time the prices predicted for it, or the scheduler thread's own time running them where the first stage records there, whichever is longer, shared among them: pieces that run on that thread run before the pass begins, so the pass's time alone measured them as nothing, and a CPU reply then met every piece at once (image-cache's `pieces` case, whose pieces take longer than the chunk budget, fails without it); a device donor's tails, a few hundred KiB of host memory, are counted nowhere.
  `Vision::encoding`, the mutex that held the encoder for an encode's life, is gone: the scheduler runs one encode at a time and the CLI encodes on its own thread.
- **Done, reused images:** a history forked inside an image, at the last whole block before the image's end, needs only the rows past that block, less than a block of rows.
  A request keeps those rows of each image it is given with rows (`Request::tails_`, `ImageTail`, `Cache::keep_tail`), and each entry holding its history keeps them beside it, the donor, its host copy, counted in the copy's bytes and freed with it, and a promotion (F2DEV's condition: one owner, no second budget); a fork takes its source's, and a sequence takes them as an image's rows from row `MediaRun::from` on (`Model::add_media`, `write_media`), so a follow-up turn or a job forking inside its image encodes nothing while the history is held, and encodes it again once the history has gone (a disk copy keeps none).
  That was production's case of a turn with 15616 of 17037 tokens reused still encoding the image for 58 s: the follow-up forked its first turn's prompt at the last block before the image's end.
- **Done, the flag:** `--image-max-tokens N` on `generate`, `logits` and `serve` (and `llmx-encode-image`), a token count read by the CLI's one count parser with its k and m suffixes; each encoder turns it into its own resize bound (`VisionArchitecture::preprocess(max_tokens)`, for Qwen's N * (patch * merge)^2 pixels of smart_resize's `max_pixels`), the default the encoder's own (16384 tokens, HF's 16777216 pixels, so digests are unchanged); the server's start line gives the bound in tokens.
  `--image-max-pixels` is removed with no alias; production's launch line does not give it, so it needs no change, and any other script giving it must give `--image-max-tokens` (pixels / 1024 for Qwen's encoders).
- **Tests:** `image-cache` `no_hold`: on two devices whose second stage records on its own thread, a reply beside a 24-piece encode keeps its passes between the pieces and the encode stops the stages no times (24 holds on the base); `reused_inside`: a follow-up forking its first turn's history inside its image runs none of its pieces (2 on the base) and gives its reply on a fresh model, and one with another image of the same grid forks nothing and runs its own; `reused_evicted`: with the first turn's history evicted to host memory the follow-up forks the copy and runs none, and with no host tier, the history gone, it forks nothing and runs both, each reply its reply on a fresh model; `job_gives_way` gives its conversation's image no digest, so no rows of it are kept and the job still encodes. `arch-qwen3vl-vision` holds the token bound's conversion and refusals, `cli.py` the flag's refusals and the old flag refused as unknown.
- **Measured, the encoder (Flash-Next's BF16 mmproj, a 4032x3008 image, grid 188x252, 11844 tokens, one MI50, renderD130):** 58.8 s an encode, 91% of it attention (`attention_full_tile_d72`, 53.7 s at about 5.2 TFLOPS, 4 n^2 D a layer over 47376 patches) and 8% the products (5.0 s); what production logs.
  Bit-identical tile changes tried and not kept: 128 query rows a workgroup 86.5 s, 32 rows 73.5 s, keys staged 32 at a time with the softmax still stepping 16 53.6 s (no change); the rows were the same bits each time.
  The cost is the full attention's square in the patches, so the token bound is the lever: at `--image-max-tokens 4096` (4070 tokens) an encode takes 7.4 s, at 1024 (999 tokens) 0.82 s.
- **Measured before the rebase and the pacing, serving (Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M with its BF16 mmproj, a layer split over renderD130 and renderD131, the same image, base 57aceb8a5 and head d8a5d000b each built from a detached worktree):**

| | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| reply alone | 282 tok/s | 285 tok/s |
| reply while the image waits for its first token | 16.0-16.6 tok/s, largest gap 0.20-0.26 s | 17.3 tok/s, largest gap 0.20 s |
| image request, first token | 22.9-24.1 s | 22.6 s |
| holds an image | 338 | 0 |
| second turn of the image's conversation, 11840 of 11902 tokens reused | 20.0-20.1 s, the image encoded again | 0.47 s, nothing encoded |

  Both turns' replies are the same text on both arms. On this placement the hold cost little: each piece is about 55 ms of device work between the replies' passes, so a reply gets about one step a piece either way, above the service rule's 8 tokens a second.
- **Measured, production's placement (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, its BF16 mmproj, renderD130, 131, 134 and 135, production's flags but no disk tier and a 4 GiB host tier, the same 12 MP image beside a reply of 12000 tokens, then a two-turn conversation of the image; base main 06936f48e, the head unpaced 9631aeb92, one piece a replies' pass e9680e043, and priced 2bf7aadeb, each built from a detached worktree; the rig's load average 17 to 19 from other work):**

| | base | unpaced | one piece a pass | priced (landing) | one a pass, 4k | priced, 4k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reply alone | 57.4 tok/s | 68.7 | 54.0 | 65.6 | 66.0 | 37.1 |
| reply while the image waits for its first token | 13.4-13.6 tok/s | 5.0 | 20.8 | 7.8 | 24.1 | 10.0 |
| its largest gap | 1.18 s | 1.17 s | 1.11 s | 1.15 s | 0.52 s | 0.54 s |
| image request, first token | 108 s; 313 s beside a build | 78 s | 128 s | 95 s | 22.4 s | 19.6 s |
| next request with the image, 11840 tokens reused | 60.4-60.6 s, encoded again | 0.60 s | 0.63 s | 0.70 s | 0.79 s | 0.93 s |
| its follow-up turn | 60.5-60.6 s, encoded again | 0.54 s | 0.54 s | 0.58 s | 0.90 s | 1.18 s |

  Priced, the reply holds about the service rule's objective of 8 tokens a second (7.8 at the default bound, 10.0 at 4k) and the image takes the rest: its drafts bring several tokens a step, which widens the step gap the chunk budget is cut from, so the budget holds more than one 55 ms piece.
  The 7.8 is not the estimate lagging at the encode's start: before a piece's time is measured a pass meets one piece, which errs toward the reply.
  It is the objective as the rule holds it, a product objective rather than a guaranteed rate: the gap is cut from the fewest tokens a step among the last eight, and a piece's time comes from the retirements of passes in flight, so the rate settles near 8 and not above it; 2.5% under over 95 s needs no change.
  The priced 4k column's reply alone, 37.1 tok/s against 65.6 and 66.0 in the other runs of this server, is unexplained: no CPU, disk or GPU monitoring was recorded for these runs, and matvec probes on another card (CPUs 12-15, which this unpinned run could share) overlapped them, so it may be contended and is not compared; its other cells are measured beside the encode, as in the other columns.

  Both turns' replies are the same text on base and head; the base's second sample ran beside this branch's build, so its first figures are a contended run, kept as measured.
- **Gates (head 2bf7aadeb, the landing code):** CTest 94 of 94 (rig, renderD130/131), `image-cache` three runs in a row, `server-passes` (`encode_pieces`); the CPU suite, 45 components pass and `baseline` skipped without its models, `docs` and `dead-code` among them; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `generate` ids and `logits` byte-identical to main 06936f48e on the CPU and on vulkan:0 (on e9680e043, whose model code is the same).
- **Flakes under load (Windows PC, F2DEV's ruling of 2026-10-30):** in one round of 50 `image-cache` runs five at a time, run beside MSVC builds, three cases failed once each: `host_tier` ("the host tier with images: 1 promotions and 256 tokens reused, against 2 and 512"), `reused_evicted` ("a follow-up of a history in host memory: 0 promotions") and `disk_tier` ("images on disk: 2 entries after turn 4 within a minute").
  None is a reply differing from its reply alone: the first two fail after every reply matched, and the third is the minute-long wait for the disk entries.
  None recurred without the builds: 50 more runs five at a time at this head, 20 runs one at a time, 400 runs five at a time of the three cases alone on this head and on main 06936f48e, and 50 runs five at a time of main's binary without its `pieces` case (main's own `pieces` failed 25 of 50 at that load, the timing-bound check this branch replaces).
  The likely cause, not confirmed since the failing runs' logs were not kept: these tests admit host copies against the machine's real free memory, which the builds drew down (`Model::host_copy_fits`), as `server-passes-cpu`'s boundary cases did before their fix; the follow-up gives the three cases a fixed host memory through `on`'s `host_memory`, as that fix did.
- **Left:** the hosted run at landing; it lands by fast-forward on main as two commits.
  Not built, by the owner's ruling: the encoder-output cache across chats, and the decode and resize speed-up, about 0.4 s of a 12 MP PNG and 1 s of production's JPEG beside a 7.4 s encode at the 4k bound.

## The quick-newcomer case counts passes between a reply's steps (2026-10-30, TDEV, branch fix/server-passes-cpu-flake on main 06936f48e, tests only, the coordinator's order of 2026-10-30, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

**Goal.** `short_newcomer` in `server-passes-cpu` failed on the hosted macOS runner on every branch and on main: `a reply waited 511.6 to 605.7 ms between two steps beside a quick newcomer beside a long prompt, against the step gap's cap` (jobs 124160912977, 124179102195, 124208863368, 124195078299).
The 500 ms cap is an objective the service rule aims at by measured prices, not a bound the scheduler keeps, as the serving rework's open item records at 670 ms on two MI50s, and a reply's gap there is two or three pass times of two 70 ms stages plus the CPU's work, which a slow runner stretches without the rule letting any more work in.
**Done.** The wall-clock gap is replaced by what the rule decides: between two steps of a reply at most the passes in flight beside its own (2) retire, and none of them holds more prompt rows than the newcomer's whole 85-token prompt, which the long prompt's chunks beside the replies (16 rows in every trace) stay well below.
On the Windows PC the case alone on four cores, two busy loops beside two copies: 50 of 50 runs pass, at most 2 other passes and 64 prompt rows between two steps of a reply, while the old measure passed 500 ms in 5 of 100 cases (largest 790 ms); with six busy loops beside four copies, 50 of 52 pass, the old measure past 500 ms in 25 of 102 cases (largest 3.2 s, the process descheduled whole), the counts unchanged.
The two failures there are an existing check: alone, the newcomer missed 72 and 73 replies' passes between rides, about the 10 s bound in passes, consistent with its 85 rows pricing past the cap at that load so that the rule held it to the bound as it should; the hosted macOS runs never reached that case's checks failing, and holding it would need the newcomer's price taken out of the test's machine, left open here.
**Left.** Nothing: hosted run 41109932122 passed all 8 jobs at 33428ef85, `server-passes-cpu` on macOS among them, and F2DEV approved it.

## Wide decode, steps 1 and 2: a decode call's column chunks in one dispatch, the transposed reduction and four rows in the 16-column build (2026-10-30, VDEV, branch feat/wide-decode on main 9b76ebc36, steps 1 and 2 of the wide decode kernel plan F2DEV approved on 2026-10-30, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

**Goal:** the Q4 and K-quant decode builds at 16 to 64 columns bound by their weight reads rather than by each column's activation loads and reduction, every column keeping its bits.
**Done:** on profiles that set `row_decode_tree` (the MI50 under RADV) the two-row builds reduce a whole cluster through the butterfly's pairs transposed (specialization constant 17, `row_tree_cluster`), and the 16-column build takes four rows (`kRowBuilds`); rows of another cluster width take the one-row builds (`column_builds`), so the two-row builds hold no butterfly.
The `--isa` screen holds builds of other rows to whole copies of a row's weight operations beside the products, takes the transposed reduction's adds and each stored value's off, and lets a grouped build hold its one-column build's counts where the driver keeps its column loop rolled (the K4 wide build, now reached on the MI50 by short rows).
A spec-constant division by a `TREE_CLUSTER` of 0 crashed the AMD proprietary driver at pipeline creation (Radeon VII, exception 0xc0000094 in amdvlk64.dll); the level count now never divides by zero.
Gates so far, one MI50 (renderD129): `backend-vulkan --isa` passes at d17283124 (1,738,272 decode columns equal alone at f16 and int8, 72 pairs of two-row builds); byte identity against main 06936f48e at d56ebd0de (kernel code as now) on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M (generate raw, chat, seeded and lookup at 32, logits, perplexity, two-turn chat, server_mix_check ids) and Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 (greedy with the embedded drafter at 15, lookup at 32, seeded, server_mix_check ids).
Speed, one MI50: synthetic decode calls of 64 columns 1.6 to 1.9 times faster than e4b694175 (docs/VULKAN.md); Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 greedy with the embedded drafter at 15, the same drafts kept, 18.57 to 27.51 tok/s (medians of 3 interleaved runs, 18.32/18.83/18.57 against 27.51/28.30/27.02), plain decode 20.73/20.78/19.97 against 20.73/20.06/19.83.
Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver, Windows): its profile sets no `row_decode_cols`, so these builds do not run there; forced on in a scratch build, two rows with or without the transposed reduction moved Q4_1, Q4_K and Q5_0 calls of 64 columns by -2 to +5 percent, and every Q4/K decode call there runs at 0.14 to 0.30 TMAC/s against the MI50's 2.5 to 5.7, a gap of its own; neither flag is set there.
**Found on the way:** the step 2a figures posted at 17:35 compared against a scratch tree whose 16-column build had four rows under the butterfly, not against e4b694175; against e4b694175 that build's long-row cell was -7 percent at int8 and -1 at f16, not -14 and -24, and its gains smaller than posted. The four-row butterfly had been faster on long rows and slower on short ones, which is what the transposed reduction resolves.
**Rejected:** staging a workgroup's activations in shared memory, four columns a stage: bit-identical, 1.26 times slower at int8 on Q4_1 and 1.06 to 1.08 times faster at f16; probes of the long-row cell (column rotation by workgroup or subgroup, dispatch order with chunks adjacent, lower occupancy, code placement) changed nothing or made it slower.
Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 at production's flags (int8, f16 caches, four MI50s, 37175e178 against main e8d413a84, built alike): greedy replies with the lookup and MTP drafter and without are byte-identical; decode is level, ABBA at a 512-token prompt, the MTP head loaded: a step 29.1/29.6 ms on main against 29.9/28.3, a verify of 6 rows 47.8/48.2 against 48.2/48.8, of 8 rows 53.4/54.2 against 53.7/53.8, and 8 sequences 157.5/154.3 against 155.8/154.0 tok/s. Flash-Next's dense matrices are Q8_0, which keeps its own decode kernel, so at 6 to 8 rows it takes none of the changed builds; the gain is the Q4 and K-quant models' at 16 to 64 columns. The 100k-depth leg was not run for both arms: `bench --depth` refills the history before every draft count and repeat, about 6 minutes a fill on this model (main: pp64 275.4, tg32 39.58 tok/s at depth 102400).
The long-K cell at this head, one MI50 (renderD131), synthetic Q4_1 17408x5120 decode calls, ABBA, the backend's code as main 9b76ebc36 has it (main e8d413a84, whose backend 9b76ebc36 does not change), us per call (main, main / branch, branch): int8 16 columns 423.0, 423.4 / 449.6, 293.8 and 64 columns 1677.9, 1674.2 / 1011.0, 1011.8; f16 16 columns 1036.8, 1039.1 / 590.2, 588.7 and 64 columns 4163.6, 4133.6 / 2169.8, 2159.5. Against main the cell is faster, 1.4 to 1.9 times at 16 and 64 columns; the loss F2DEV accepted was against step 1, e4b694175. At 8 columns f16 is 6% slower (540.8, 538.0 / 572.2, 571.7 us) and int8 within noise (270.8, 294.4 / 395.2, 296.3 us).
The suite on a device at b932cccc4, `run_tests.py --device vulkan:0` on one MI50 (renderD131, RADV): 44 components pass, `baseline` skips (no fixture on that path), and `docs` failed only on the new profile comment's length, shortened since and checked with `docs` on the PC.
**Left:** the hosted run at the head the coordinator rebases.
**Gotchas:** the four-row 16-column build is meant with the transposed reduction; a profile that sets `row_decode_cols` without `row_decode_tree` gets four rows under the butterfly, slower on short rows, so set them together after the `--isa` screen and the decode-column identity.

**Step 1, a decode call's column chunks in one dispatch.**

**Goal:** a decode-class call of more columns than its widest build holds runs its whole chunks side by side in one dispatch rather than one after another, so a matrix of few rows fills the device; each column keeps its bits.
**Done:** `for_each_column_chunk` hands the whole chunks of the widest build to one `row_dispatch` with as many workgroups in y, and `matmul_row.comp` and `matmul_vec_q8.comp` take a plain call's chunk from `gl_WorkGroupID.y`; the arithmetic of every column is unchanged.
backend-vulkan's decode-column identity runs to 256 columns, the residual add and the grouped calls also at 65, 96, 127, 128, 129, 200 and 256: 1,738,272 decode columns equal to the same columns alone, f16 and int8, on one MI50.
On one MI50 with synthetic weights at 256 columns (this branch against 06936f48e, the same build): F32 10240x4 145 against 2039 us, F32 2560x48 83 against 700 us, F32 2560x512 490 to 610 against 869 us (Flash-Next's hc_*_inject, ssm_alpha and ssm_beta and router shapes, 33% of its 256-draft verify), Q4_1 5120x17408 3.08 against 2.92 TMAC/s.
Step 1's gates: the `--isa` screen passes on the MI50 and on the Radeon VII, and Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M and Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 over two cards are byte-identical to main 06936f48e.
**Gotchas:** a plain call's push constant `ncols` is the width of every chunk in the dispatch, so the remainder stays a call of its own.

## A disk write goes on once its copy has landed (2026-10-30, VDEV, branch feat/disk-write-no-wait on the serving landing head ef8e8af41, to rebase onto main once that lands, the coordinator's order of 2026-10-30 under the rule that the GPU never waits for the CPU, in progress)

**Goal:** the disk tier's writes never make the scheduler's thread wait for their copy to host memory, so a request arriving beside an idle write is admitted at once.
**Done:** production on ef8e8af41 counted 18 stage waits after two requests; an instrumented build of ef8e8af41 on GPUs 8-9 (Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 over two devices, a fresh disk directory) placed every one in `DiskTier::write_next`'s wait for the copy (`Model::wait_host`) during the idle writes.
`write_next` now hands back `Wrote::copying` while its copy has yet to land: a host entry's write is asked again next round, and a device donor's copy into the tier's staging slabs is kept and goes to the store from a later round (`DiskTier::write_landed`), the round looking again a millisecond on (`Cache::next_disk_bound`) and no other write starting meanwhile; a staged write cancelled is dropped once its copy has landed, and the stop alone waits for a copy.
`server-resume`'s `arrival_beside_idle_write`, on the dense and the hybrid model over two devices' threads whose slab copies retire 500 ms late, an idle write starting as the first request ends and a second request arriving at once: 0 stage waits and the reply its reply alone, against 3 waits before.
A host entry's write asked while its copy has yet to land is owed (`Cache::owed_`): it counts as in flight and room takes it last, as it does an entry being written (`Cache::written_soon`), so `Stats::disk_in_flight` reads 0 only with no write owed: the hosted run's `server-resume` recorder case on Windows and on the Vulkan job's CPU half took a quiet tier for written while an idle write waited for its copy, so the entry left host memory unwritten and the next steps took other tiers; `owed_write_in_flight` writes 2 MiB after the tier said nothing was in flight before the fix and nothing after
An owed write is also the round's write: before, the round went on to the next entry, so an older unwritten entry's write started while the owed copy waited, and in the recorder case a write of the promoted conversation's own history was then in flight as its follow-up ended, which ranked both its device donors last (`Cache::ranked`), so another donor went to host memory and the conversation was found on the devices at the next step instead of promoted (3 of 15 recorder runs under load on Windows, and 2 of 25 with only the first half of the fix).
Now `Cache::owe` ends the round's search at an owed write, each round asks the owed write again before any other (`Cache::write_owed`), since a promotion between rounds can rank the entries another way, and the turn's and idle writes wait for it; `owed_write_first` writes 2 MiB of the other entry while the owed copy waited before the fix and nothing after.
Under load on this Windows PC (`cpu-resume` beside `cpu-cache`, clean builds), main 06936f48e passed the recorder case 9 of 9 and failed `prefilling_victim` once in 10 (0 taken back, 0 rows recomputed) and `cpu-cache`'s reply read again over a two-CPU split once in 10, both main's flakes. it.
**Left:** the related tests on the CPU, review, the rebase onto main.
**Gotchas:** a staged write's copy time, which sizes a turn's next pieces, is measured to the round that saw it land (`DiskTier::last_copy_ms`).

## ROCm step 3, first part: Qwen3 Q8_0 on one MI50 (2026-10-30, DDEV, branch feat/rocm-qwen3-q8 on main 7f83d159a, the coordinator's order of 2026-10-30 for the part both delivery orders need; approved by F2DEV and landing by fast-forward on a green hosted run, the speed gate open)

**Goal:** Qwen3 Q8_0 runs on one MI50 through `--device rocm:0` at the default F16 precision: the Q8_0 decode row kernel and prompt tile on block-int16 activations with F32 sums (docs/PRECISION.md), paged attention over F16 caches, the KV cache and the server path, with batch invariance from the first kernel and the collective seam kept for step 4.
**Done:** the design outline, approved by F2DEV with four changes: one documented tie rule for the 16-bit twin, reconstructed independently by the test; gfx906's 16-bit dot chosen by a device capability flag; the raw and chat-template 16k sequences against file-exact HF before merge; the row-class test either side of the tile crossover and every attention chunk split. Quantized products in the F16 class read block-int16 activations under PRECISION.md rule 4 and its frozen budget, so --dtype f16 means the same on Vulkan and ROCm.
**The twin's rule:** per block of 32, amax the largest magnitude; s = 0 where amax is in [2^-100, 2^100] and otherwise the power of two that brings amax into [1, 2); d = (amax 2^s / 32767) 2^-s and q = x 2^s (32767 / (amax 2^s)) rounded half away from zero and clamped to 32767, each division correctly rounded; a block of zeros has d = 0 and q = 0.
First kernels (renderD128): the twin, the Q8_0 row kernel and the tile pass backend-rocm (the twin is its rule through one-hot rows on both kernels, products within 1e-6 of a double sum over the twin, every decode column of 1 to 64 its column alone (below) and a prompt row the same bits in calls of 1 to 21 rows, row classes compared); Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 passes tests/baseline.py on rocm:0 at its HF bounds (top-1 6/6, NLL delta 0.0011 to 0.0124 against 0.010 and 0.020); unoptimized bench pp512 1267.5 and tg128 62.5 tok/s.
Gates on rocm:0 (commit f0dd8c25d and on): 8B Q8_0 baseline_8b.py PASS, 41 checks (gate-8b-20261030-build4); the 16k raw and chat-template sequences against file-exact HF on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 (a reference made with the quant-depth producer for its SHA-256, f16 policy, `hf_depth_top1` at 0.1): raw 510 exact, 2 accepted ties, 0 misses, chat 512, 0, 0; server.py and server_mix_check PASS.
Found on the way and fixed: hipFree unmaps a buffer queued work still names, which faulted a 16k prompt (a dropped buffer's memory now waits in graves for the work before it); serve's fitted pool overran the card, HIP rounding allocations to 2 MiB pages (`scratch_reserve`, 256 MiB and a twentieth of the free memory); a routed layer on ROCm failed in a pass (routed layers declare `Op::routed_experts`).
Tiled prompt attention (`llmx_attention_tile`), the 16k raw depth output byte for byte the chunk kernel's: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 prompt 857 to 1205 tok/s at 1929 tokens, 291 to 467 at 7482 and 143 to 242 at 16305; decode after 7482 tokens 46 to 47 tok/s.
Decode: the row kernel's early return compiled about four times slower on rows of 2048 and 4096 than a loop over the rows (47 to 11 us on 1024 x 2048), and the head wrote its logits a float a row into pinned host memory over PCIe (3.3 ms of a token); with the loop form and products into host memory formed on the device and copied whole, bench tg64 went 121 to 227 tok/s and decode after 1929 tokens 68 to 101 tok/s, bits unchanged.
The 16-bit dot (F2DEV's change 2): a dot module of the int16 kernels compiled for gfx906 alone, loaded where the build holds a code object for the device, which sets `DeviceCaps::integer_dot`; three interleaved rounds gave the tile +28 percent on pp64 (1694 to 2165 tok/s) and the row kernel -1.7 percent on tg64 (228 to 224), so the tile takes the dot and the rows keep the plain module.
Error against the HF bounds on rocm:0: Qwen3-8B Q8_0 (gate-8b-20261030-build4) continuous NLL 0.00154 against 0.01 (85 percent headroom), the windows' largest 0.00219 against 0.02 (89 percent), top-1 6/6 and top-5 overlap 5/5 in every case; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 top-1 6/6 and NLL deltas 0.0011 to 0.0124, the tightest 0.0124 against 0.020 (38 percent headroom), rerun on the landing head after the serving gate.
The 16k sequences against file-exact HF are run on the 0.6B alone: the 8B's F32 HF reference holds about 33 GB of weights and 4 GB of 16k KV and attention, and the host's 62 GiB had 12 GiB available beside production and the serving gate. The 0.6B result covers the 8B's paths, since both run the same kernels (the row kernel and tile on the block-int16 twin, the chunk and tile attention over F16 caches) with only their widths and counts changed, and backend-rocm holds the kernels at the 8B's 4096-wide rows and 128-wide heads.
backend-rocm holds every decode column of 1 to 64 generated rows, four launches of 16, to the column alone bit for bit, rows 4096 and 1280 wide, with the residual add and a group of three projections at counts either side of each launch's edge.
Every dtype on ROCm in the end (the owner's decision of 2026-10-30): f32, f16, bf16 and int8, each with Vulkan's meaning and fallback (docs/PRECISION.md, one rule per flag). Order: step 3 lands as planned, then int8 as a short step of its own before the collective, since production runs `--dtype int8`, held to Vulkan's frozen int8 budget and policy (docs/PRECISION.md, section 4) and confirmed on ROCm, then bf16 and f32 as the F32 class's full meaning. Until int8 exists the one-card screen sets ROCm's F16 class against the reference's 8-bit path; the int8 step adds the matched int8 arm beside the default one.
One-card screen (MI50 at c3:00.0, default clocks, three interleaved rounds, medians; until ROCm has int8 its F16 class meets the reference HIP build's 8-bit path): Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 pp512 / tg128 llmx ROCm 2432 / 195, reference HIP 6975 / 325, llmx Vulkan 8946 / 396, reference Vulkan 7379 / 296; Qwen3-8B Q8_0 llmx ROCm 210 / 55.5, reference HIP 1316 / 72.0, llmx Vulkan 843 / 78.0, reference Vulkan 906 / 58.2 tok/s. Every ROCm cell is below the reference HIP build, a speed gate open on first support.
Profile of the 8B (rocprofv3 kernel traces on that card, prof8b-20261030-0919; llmx profiled at 210.4 / 52.2 against 210.6 / 56.0 unprofiled, the reference's decode 26.3 profiled against 71.7, so its decode durations are inflated and read only as proportions):
| pp512 pass | llmx ROCm | reference HIP |
|---|---|---|
| wall | 2451 ms | 383 ms |
| quantized products | 2226 ms (90.9%), 3.8 TOPS, `llmx_q8_0_tile16` | 323 ms (84.3%), 26.0 TOPS, `mmq_gemm_repacked` |
| attention | 175 ms (7.2%) | 31 ms (8.2%) |
| activation twin / quantize | 9 ms | 13 ms |
| device idle | 2 ms | 0 ms |
| decode token (last 128 of 258) | llmx ROCm | reference HIP (profiled) |
|---|---|---|
| wall | 19.1 ms | 38.0 ms (13.9 unprofiled) |
| quantized products | 12.9 ms (71.5%), 675 GB/s of weights, 66% of the HBM peak | 15.5 ms (86.8%) |
| attention (chunk, merge, KV write) | 2.64 ms (14.7%) | 0.78 ms (4.4%) |
| norms, rope and twin | 2.33 ms (12.9%): rms norm 1.04, norm and rope 0.65, twin 0.64 | 1.54 ms (8.6%), rope fused into its norm |
| device idle | 1.11 ms (5.8%) | profiler-made |
Proposed fixes by the share each removes, each profiled before and after: the prompt product tile (90.9% of a pp512 pass, at 3.8 TOPS against the reference's 26), a register-blocked tile on the 16-bit dot; decode attention (12.5% of a token at short histories, and most of it at 16k), a kernel that does not walk 64-position tiles one block at a time for one row; the norms (12.9%), a 4096-wide row norm at 14 us and a separate twin pass, by a faster norm writing the twin; the decode products (66% of the HBM peak); the host's 1.1 ms a token.
**Left:** the open speed gate above: every one-card cell below the reference HIP build, recovered by the fixes ranked there, fix 1 (the prompt tile) built with the int8 step as one tile for both activation forms, then decode attention (32 tok/s after 16k), the norms, the decode products and the host's idle, each profiled before and after; int8 next, with the matched int8 arm against the reference's 8-bit path, then bf16 and f32.
**Gotchas:** renderD128/129 only, yielded during a serving final gate; rocprofv3 on the 7.2.1 image needs libdw installed and `ROCPROF_TMPDIR`, and slows the reference's decode about threefold.

## A tensor group's queue calls on a thread of their own (2026-10-29, DDEV, branch feat/sum-submit-thread on main 3a5e3d5bd, step 1 of the CPU-trips audit, the coordinator's DECISION of 12:36 and F2DEV's approval with four conditions, in progress)

**Goal:** a group's recording thread hands each queue call over and records on, so no device of the group waits while the calls are made.
**Measured first** (Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2, production's flags, untimed, GPUs 4-7, CPUs 4-7): each decode sum held the recording thread about 190 us, of it the two members' `vkQueueSubmit` calls about 70-80 us each, the export 7 us and the import 9 us, with the ring never full, so about 9 ms of each 14-17 ms stage pass was the host while the device had 7.9 ms of work.
**Done:** `VulkanSubmitter`, one queue thread per group, owns every member's queue (submissions, holds, a sum's calls, exports and imports in recorded order); a ticket handed out before its call is waited for there first; a failed call settles its tickets, wakes every waiter, recovers each collective's semaphores and throws once at the next hand-over; no result of a failed submission is read (`read` throws a pending failure, `raise(t)` a given-up ticket's before the logits are read in place, F2DEV's review finding, its test red before the fix and green after); a ring slot is reused only after its call and its work; the holds have their own command pool; the last collective gives the members their calls back.
vulkan-lifetime holds the order, the thread, the give-back, the failed call's wake and the failed read, and its exchange failures now surface at the next hand-over.
Prototype on 4 pinned CPUs, MTP off: one reply 34.4 to 40.3 tok/s (medians, +17%).
Timing round as production runs (unpinned, --threads 8), three interleaved repeats, each server three single 512-token replies then four at once, medians without each server's first reply: one reply raw 45.3 to 46.3 tok/s (+2.2%) and drafted 53.3 to 55.1 (+3.4%, drafts priced by measured costs, so kept drafts differ); four at once raw 128.5 to 128.5 tok/s together (level) and drafted 109.3 to 119.4 (+9%).
Per stage pass the recording thread's sum time fell from 6.3-7.2 to 4.5-5.9 ms and the device's work left after recording rose from 0.4-2.3 to 3.4-5.5 ms; stage 0's lookup waits stayed under 0.6 ms in both.
Gates: byte identity against main on the CPU, a tensor group of 2 (Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, Qwen3.6-27B MTP Q4_1), Flash-Next 2x2, the scheduler's mix with log-probabilities on 0.6B 2x2 and a layer split's split-check; CPU CTest 94/94; Radeon VII Vulkan CTest 17/17; vulkan-lifetime's new cases pass on four MI50s and its two-shot ownership and second-exchange cases at widths 3 and 4 fail the same way on main; TSan on vulkan-lifetime reports only the Mesa driver's shader-cache threads.
**Left:** the review, then landing as one commit.
**Gotchas:** the failure is given at the next hand-over on the group, which may be the next pass's when it was the last call of a pass; a hold given up after a failure ends by its bound.

## ROCm backend foundation, step 2 of docs/ROCM.md (2026-10-29, DDEV, branch feat/rocm-foundation on feat/sum-submit-thread 599c0347f (on main f7cf66e33), the owner's ruling of 2026-10-29 that ROCm starts, the plan in docs/ROCM.md, approved by F2DEV at dddec6e88 with four landing items, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

**Goal:** the optional ROCm backend's foundation: `LLMX_HAS_BACKEND_ROCM`, off by default; the HIP runtime opened at run time; devices, buffers, tickets, copies, allocation accounting and errors; the dense Qwen3 F32 ops; native failure and lifetime tests; and the tiny HF F32 model passing on `--device rocm:0`, with CPU and Vulkan unchanged.
**Done:** the design outline, approved by F2DEV with four additions; the build option and embedded kernels; the HIP runtime table; device facts in `DeviceCaps`; one refusal owner (`Backend::lacks`) for the ops a backend lacks; the backend class (stream, event tickets, staging and argument rings, first-cause errors, KV through `BlockKVStorage`, `row_class`); the dense F32 kernels; `--device rocm:N` in USAGE, help and cli.py; `rocm-runtime` and `backend-rocm`.
Q8_0 weights are read too, decoded exactly into F32 sums, since every tiny fixture carries an unused Q8_0 tensor the loader refuses a file over when no backend reads its type.
Measured on an MI50 (renderD128, gfx906): rocm-runtime and backend-rocm pass; the f32 component on `--device rocm:0` passes in the auto, mapped and direct load modes, its largest logit error 6.3e-7 against the 2e-5 HF bound and NLL error 5e-8 against 1e-5 (it skips by design with F16 caches, which backend-rocm holds to the CPU).
CPU and Vulkan unchanged: a Vulkan build of the branch passes CPU CTest 94/94, Vulkan CTest 17/17 on two MI50s, docs, dead-code and cli, and gives Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 logits and 64 greedy tokens byte-identical to main on the CPU and on Vulkan.
**Hand check:** no hosted runner has a ROCm device, so the hosted `rocm-build` job compiles the backend and runs the docs and dead-code checks over it, and the device tests run by hand on an MI50 off production's PCI roots (renderD128) at every change to the backend: `rocm-runtime`, `backend-rocm`, and `tests/run_tests.py --device rocm:0 --only f32` in the auto, mapped and direct load modes.
Rebased on feat/sum-submit-thread: `raise(t)` throws the first cause before logits are read in place (backend-rocm injects a failure at a ticket's event), and the ticket bookkeeping the Vulkan and ROCm backends both kept is one `TicketLedger` in `backend.hpp`.
F2DEV's four landing items: USAGE names the Q8_0 weights; backend-rocm waits on tickets from another thread while 3000 more are submitted; the ticket bookkeeping is one `TicketLedger`; the hosted `rocm-build` job compiles the backend (headers and compiler from AMD's repository at 7.2.1, preferred over the distribution's older HIP) and runs docs and dead-code over it.
On the rebased head the ROCm tests and f32 pass on renderD128, and a Vulkan build passes CPU CTest 94/94, Vulkan CTest 17/17 and docs, dead-code and cli, with Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 identical to the sum-submit-thread build on the CPU, on Vulkan and as a tensor group of 2.
**Left:** the hosted run at the landing head.
**How it keeps the architecture rules (the owner's directive of 2026-10-29):**
- Layers: everything is under `src/backends/rocm/` and includes only `core/`, `quant/`, `format/` and `backends/` headers; above the backends only the device factory (`backends/devices.hpp`) names it, as it names Vulkan.
- Shape: one translation unit (`rocm_backend.cpp`) as Vulkan's, the option in CMake, `cmake/llmx-config.hpp.in` and `src/config.hpp`, kernels compiled at build time and embedded as Vulkan's SPIR-V is, and device facts in `DeviceCaps`/`DeviceProfile`; kernels are chosen by what the device reports (wave width, ISA), never by vendor.
- One owner: `pci_root_of` moved from the Vulkan device into `device_profile.hpp` for both; the ops a backend may lack refuse through one default in `Backend` (F2DEV's ruling); KV blocks through the shared `BlockKVStorage`; quant, placement, dtype and state logic stay with their owners.
- Same surface: `--device rocm:N` with the one flag set, each flag honoured or refused as on Vulkan (cache types F32 and F16, dtype f32 only in this step, every load mode); no llmx environment variable.
- Docs and checks: `docs/src/backends-rocm.md` for the directory, USAGE and print_usage with cli.py's refusal tests, dead-code and docs clean, no stubs, no other project named.
- Comments: a sentence or two, ASCII, a sentence a line.
**Gotchas:** Linux only, built in the gfx906 ROCm image pinned by digest; cards on pci0000:c0 (renderD128-131), never production's roots; every other op and type is refused at load by capability, and tensor groups by `join()` returning none until step 4.

## The serving rework, step 1: holds off the reply path (2026-10-29, VDEV, branch feat/serving-holds on RDEV's feat/serving-rule 413a0328d, F2DEV's design of 2026-10-27 12:31 ("Step 2, holds off the reply path"), the coordinator's order of 2026-10-29, lands with step 2 below by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** the scheduler thread owns host state and each stage's thread is the only recorder on its devices; device work outside a pass goes to the stages' threads in formation order, and the whole-model hold (`quiet`) stays only for abort-all, recall, stop and failure.
- **Done:** `Stats::holds` (`/v1/health` `passes.since_start.holds`) counts every hold; a mark and a kept state are plain calls; a verify's retract hands its state rerun to each state stage's thread as an item (`Model::retract` with a `Defer`, `Recorder::items`), the lengths changing at once and the mark's hold going back as the history settles, and a failed item ends its request alone, its passes in flight abandoned and their other requests formed again; a timed scheduler's stage readings run on their stage's thread (`run_on`) while the other stages record, and lookup takes no hold at all.
  The embedded drafter's chain is split as F2DEV approved on 2026-10-29 at 14:58 (`Model::draft_begin`, `draft_record`, `draft_end`): begun on the scheduler thread, recorded as an item on the head stage's thread and ended by the round when it reports, its requests sitting the pass out and verifying its drafts in the next, so the scheduler thread never waits for a chain; the model's context and the chains' buffers are taken as the scheduler is made (`Model::reserve_drafting`) and counted in the fit (`Footprint::context_rows`, `drafter_cache`), so neither a chain nor a rerun allocates while a stage's thread records.
  `server-spec`'s `rerun_failure_alone`: four drafting replies two to a pass over two tensor-group stages, the 61st rerun call throwing once every request decodes beside another; it ends alone with the error and the others give their replies alone, where the previous `item_failed` ended its pass partner too.
  `server-spec`'s `steady_gap`, a sampled reply drafting alone on the Flash fixture over two tensor-group CPU stages at two passes (240 tokens from the 60th, two runs each, interleaved): with the chain waited for, token gap p50 0.060 and 0.062 ms, p99 0.189 and 0.248 ms, 14766 and 13167 tokens/s; with the chain on the head stage's thread (35 chains begun there), p50 0.065 and 0.063 ms, p99 0.209 and 0.189 ms, 12216 and 14006 tokens/s.
  The arms differ within their noise; the fixture's chain takes microseconds, so the cost of sitting a round out is measured on a device with a real model before this merges.
  `server-spec`'s `steady_holds` takes no hold between a reply's 60th and 300th token while it drafts: Q8_0 with lookup and the hybrid model with its embedded drafter, on one CPU and on a two-CPU split at two passes (280 holds before on Q8_0 with lookup).
  CTest 77 of 77 on a CPU build.
  The tier copies, F2DEV's approval of 2026-10-29, step 1 of 4: a copy to host memory (`write_back`, `keep_boundary`) takes no hold, its parts on the stages' threads with the fresh slabs they allocate and a pending record every reader settles (`Model::copy_out`, `host_settle`); `server-spec`'s `host_saves` copies donors to host memory beside a drafting reply over two CPU stages at two passes with no hold and the reply its reply alone, and with a copy's first part throwing, that copy alone lost.
  Step 2 of 4: a promotion from host memory and a fork with a boundary's state take no hold (`Model::restore_host`, `fork` with a `Defer`, `copy_in`), and a part that fails, F2DEV's ruling, is the history gone: each request holding it leaves flight and reads it again, a donor holding it is dropped (`Scheduler::history_failed`); a history still landing is forked by no other request, serves as no source and is not cancelled into a donor (`Sequence::landing`, F2DEV's note).
  `server-resume`'s host tier on two devices' threads (a layer split over backends that say they are no CPU, so the copies run on the last stage's thread and land 50 ms late): every reply its reply alone with a write-back failing and with a promotion failing, a second follow-up of the conversation beside the first while its copies land; the recorder rule now expects no copy and no allocation on the scheduler's thread.
  Steps 3 and 4: the host tier's frees and the idle growth's slabs (`Model::trim_host`, `host_yield` and `grow_slabs` with a `Defer`), the images the cache's retracts drop (`drop_media`), and the disk tier's reads, writes, proofs and streams (`Model::take_host`, `DiskTier::write_next`, `prove`, `read` and `StreamedRead` with a `Defer`) take no hold; `DiskTier::measure` takes no memory (`Model::host_bytes`); the only holds left are abort-all's, recall's, the stop's, a failed pass's, a proposer's on other stages' devices and an image's encode.
  The step gap on a real model, Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 as a layer split over two MI50s with its embedded drafter, sampled 512-token prompts and 256-token replies, the chain waited for (99663e641) against the chain on the head stage's thread (f73b60950), interleaved twice: level at 1 user (19.6-19.9 tok/s, ITL p50 48.3-49.0 ms), and at 4 users 33.8 and 33.6 against 28.8 and 27.3 tok/s, TTFT p50 6.0 and 6.2 against 8.0 and 7.3 s, ITL unchanged; a reply sitting out the pass its chain is queued in costs the passes rows.
  A KV storage's layer count is fixed when it is made and what it has backed is atomic (`BlockKVStorage::layers`, `allocated_bytes`, `peak_bytes`), since a restore now grows the storage on the device's stage's thread while the scheduler's thread reads the layer count and the accounting (the final gate's phase 1 found the race on a streamed read); the buffers, their retirement and the growth hook are touched only on the device's thread.
  A retract's mark goes back as soon as its rerun has run (`Model::release_settled`, after the retract and once a round), where it had waited for the history's next settle and kept two replies' marks from the others (RDEV's `drafts shared among four replies over two marks` in `server-passes-cpu`).
  A copy into host memory made while the idle growth's slabs are still being made on the stages' threads may take as many beside the tier's limit, given back once they land (`Cache::copy_limit`, `copies_retired`): the growth had reserved the whole tier, so a donor leaving then was refused room as held by entries in use and lost, which failed `server-passes-cpu`'s `boundary_fork_held` on Windows in 6 of 20 runs (0 of 20 on main aca246a74), and with the fix 0 of 20 there and on Linux.
  A promotion of a host copy whose save is still queued waits a round for it rather than the scheduler's thread waiting (F2DEV's ruling of 2026-10-30); `server-resume`'s host tier on two devices' threads, its copies landing 50 ms late both ways, a follow-up right after its conversation's write-back, holds that the scheduler's thread waits for no stage's work (`Stats::stage_waits`, 0); on a model that keeps a state, whose restore reads the copy's token tail on the host, the promotion also waits until the copy has retired on its devices (F2DEV's finding of 2026-10-30), every device wait of the scheduler's thread counts in `stage_waits` (`Model::wait_ticket`), and `server-resume`'s `promotion_after_write_back`, one request at a time so the donor count sends a conversation to host memory as the next request ends and its follow-up comes at once, on two devices' threads whose slab copies land 5 ms late and retire 500 ms after their submission, holds 0 waits on the dense and the hybrid model; without the promotion's wait for the copy to retire it counts the restore's wait on the hybrid one.
  The scheduler's thread still waits for a stage's work in these places, each counted in `stage_waits`: a history settling before another call on it while its rerun or restore parts run (a fork, a save or a reset of such a history), the disk tier's reads, which take their slabs on the stages' threads before the store reads into them (`Model::take_host`), and the proof of entries another build wrote, which restores the history it proves and copies the blocks it compares under such waits (`Cache::prove`).
  `server-spec`'s `chain_cases` hold a request cancelled, requests paused and a chain failing with chains queued on the head stage's thread, every other reply its reply alone.
  The chain queued as a reply's token is drawn, with a rule for when a reply sits out, was measured on 2026-10-30 (Qwen3.6-27B-MTP over two MI50s): it dropped 83 to 95 percent of chains at 1 user and gave 21.9 to 24.1 tok/s at 4 users against main's 27.9 to 28.3, so F2DEV withdrew it; the chain one pass ahead is a separate branch after the owner's decision.
  The draft columns go to the drafts the price kept, likeliest kept first (`Scheduler::order_`), where each request had taken its columns in admission order before the price: on Flash-Next 2x2 a reply admitted earlier, whose embedded drafter's later drafts it rarely keeps, took all 14 columns and the price then dropped its draft, so the reply drafting well from its own history got none (the final gate's four-reply cell, 0 to 5 verifies in about 355 steps).
  `server-spec`'s `columns_to_likelier` holds it: B keeps 119 own drafts beside A as alone, against 88 before.
  On Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 over GPUs 4-7 at the gate's flags, four replies on a warm server: two replies at 2.26 to 2.34 and 1.87 to 1.88 tokens a step (68.6 to 72.2 and 53.2 to 55.1 tok/s), against 1.02 to 1.05 for all four before; the owner's scenario is unchanged, its greedy reply 103.4 tok/s at 15 tokens a step against 103.1 before.
  Only one mark fits beside an automatic pool on that placement, so one request drafts a pass.
- **Open:** byte identity with drafting on and off on a device; the 4-user cost of a reply sitting out the pass its chain is queued in (27.4 tok/s against main's 27.9-28.3, 99663e641's 33.6-33.8), which the chain one pass ahead addresses.
  A greedy reply's chain at its verify's last-stage tail (F2DEV's design) is a change of its own after this step, judged on its measured gain.
- **Gotchas:** a stage's thread tells the round of an end by spinning on the scheduler's lock unless the scheduler thread waits for it, so every wait of the scheduler thread on a stage's thread raises `quieting_` (`run_on`, `Model::on_stage_wait`).
  The model's context lock is the last lock taken: nothing else is locked or waited for while it is held, so a chain's begin takes it only after its histories settle, whose rerun parts need it.

## The serving rework, step 2: one formation rule (2026-10-29, RDEV, branch feat/serving-rule on main 3a5e3d5bd (step 0 landed), step 2 of the serving rework plan, the coordinator's DECISION of 2026-10-29 05:52; by the owner's direction the rework's steps stack on this branch and land together; reviewed by F2DEV; lands by fast-forward on main aca246a74 as two commits, the failing test and then the change)

**Goal.** One rule forms the passes on every placement (docs/SERVER.md, The service rule): replies kept at a reading-speed objective of 8 tokens a second where the stages' measured prices allow it, prompts read in chunks the price table sizes to fit between their steps, prompts in least-remaining order with a 10 s wait bound, and the pacing modes, pieces, passes apart, short prompts, `--generating-share` and `--no-pacing` deleted.
Its failing test is SDEV's starvation case of 2026-10-29 04:08 (`prompt_beside_replies` in `server-passes-cpu`): a prompt beside four uncapped replies on a two-device split read no row, since four decoders over the passes filled every slot.

**Done.**
- The rule (`Scheduler::plan`, `form_round`, `form`): on a split the replies packed by the decode columns (`packed_passes`) and each other slot one prompt's chunk, continuing in its own pass, at S + 1 passes in flight by default; on one pass in flight the chunk rides the replies' pass.
- The gap model restated against the measured two-stage gap: a reply's pass meets a chunk at every stage, so the gap is S times a chunk and its own pass, and a chunk takes at most the gap over the stages less the replies' pass (`chunk_budget`).
- The reply objective in place of a ratio, the criterion F2DEV and XDEV agreed (2026-10-29 09:36 and 09:40) under the owner's rule that nothing is model- or topology-specific: `kReplyTokensPerSecond` = 8, a product objective; the gap is 1000 ms over 8 times the fewest tokens a step among the replies (`StepTokens`, the mean of a reply's last 8 steps, 1 until then); a chunk takes the gap over the stages less the replies' pass (`chunk_plan`).
  Where the replies' pass alone leaves nothing, the objective is unmet, the health counts it (`service.objective`), and a prompt takes a chunk only once the 10 s bound makes it due, so it still reads each bound (`replay_unmet` in `server-passes`).
- The step gap's maximum, `kMaxStepGapMs` = 500 ms (F2DEV and XDEV, 2026-10-29): a drafting reply's tokens a step widen the gap only up to it, since on the owner's scenario a greedy reply keeping 16 tokens a step was given 2000 ms and arrived in bursts 1.4 s apart; the health counts the passes it bound (`service.objective.since_start.capped`).
  At Flash's fitted prices 8 tokens a second lies between the table's ratios 3 and 4 below: the long prompt keeps about a fifth of its rate while a reply runs, and all of it between replies.
- Disk writes take only what nothing waits on (`Scheduler::write_turn`); the runtime's apart arena, `Pace`, `record_pass_within`, `stage_ready` and the fit's apart rows deleted.
- `server-passes` simulates the rule as its only formation (2000 schedules pass), a decoder beside prompt work getting a token within two laps and a round.

**Checks at the head.** The build; the server, scheduler, cache-scenario, placement and kv-cache CTests (11 of 11, `server-passes` 2000 schedules); the suite's docs, dead-code, cli and server components; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 logits, 64 greedy ids and `server_mix_check` ids with log-probabilities byte-identical to bac4ed4bd on the CPU.
The starvation test fails on main and passes here: on the CPU, one decode column a pass, the replies' packed passes first took every slot, so they now leave prompt work one (`packed_passes`), and the plan counts a reply in flight as a reply.
- Two tests moved with the rule: the fitted room of `fitted_reservation` follows the scheduler's smaller reservation, and the boundary fork's case runs on a split of two devices, since one device no longer records a stage on a thread of its own.

**Passes in flight follow the queue (2026-10-29).** With S + 1 passes always in flight, four replies alone on Flash-Next 2x2 split their rows over more, smaller passes (1211 passes for 1600 tokens against main's 802) and decoded at 28 to 36 tokens a second each against main's 36 to 37; each pass's stage split was the same (about 13 ms recording, 7.5 ms of it sum waits, 3.6 ms on the devices after).
The round now keeps a pass a stage in flight and the one more only while prompt rows and replies overlap (`passes_in_flight`): 820 passes and 34 to 39 tokens a second, level with main, interleaved twice, drafts off; one reply alone runs at 44 to 47 on all three.

A lone prompt on a split is again cut to about a 2S-th of what it lacks, at least 128 rows (`lone_slice`); beside other work the service rule's slices stand.

**A short newcomer never waits for the bound (2026-10-30).** Under an unmet objective every prompt waited for the 10 s bound, short ones included: on Qwen3.6-27B Q4_1 over two MI50s an 85-token newcomer beside eight replies took its first token at 16.4 s. F2DEV's rule: while the objective is unmet, the shortest prompt whose whole remaining cost and the replies-only pass fit within the 500 ms step gap's cap is quick and runs whole in a pass shared with the replies, every other replies' pass at most (`quick_prompt`); every other prompt keeps the bound, and before prices are measured the 16-row learning step applies.
A prompt longer than one pass is never quick, and a slice beside decode rows already priced takes what remains of the pass, so a riding prompt learns its price.
A replies' pass formed from a slot no prompt is due for takes the quick prompt too: on devices whose decode kernels hold every reply in one pass, the second and later newcomers had waited about 35 s, until the replies ended (`short_newcomer` in `server-passes-cpu`, alone on such devices, fails without it).
On Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_1 over two MI50s, eight 400-token replies and four 85-token newcomers 3 s apart, cd4ac0841 against 56dd2fec7, two and four runs: the newcomers' first token 0.93-1.76 s against 11.2-61.9 s, the replies 6.3-7.0 against 5.5-5.6 tok/s while the newcomers came, the largest reply gap 433-671 ms against 390-678 ms.

**Gotchas.** The chunk's fixed cost dominates at Flash's prices, so the prompt's share at the objective rises only as that cost falls; the objective is a code constant, not a flag.

**A tensor group's sum wait is pacing (2026-11-01).** On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 2x2 the host's wait in a sum is `VulkanBackend::open()` waiting for a free ring slot (`kRing` 16), about 86% of a decode stage's sum time, while the device already waits on its peers' semaphores; the SYNC_FD export and import cost about 1 ms a stage pass (RDEV, 2026-10-31 19:26). A probe with 64 slots (never landing; fresh servers main/probe/probe/main at production's flags, 2026-11-01 00:08 to 00:43) moved nothing beyond the run spread, under a host load of median 22.5 and max 32: a reply alone stepped at a p50 of 49 and 52 ms on main against 60 and 47 ms on the probe, a reply beside a 140k-token prompt at 205 and 137 ms on main against 124 and 121 ms on the probe, four users got 25.8 and 21.6 tok/s on main against 21.1 and 23.5 on the probe, and the llmx process's peak memory was 787 MiB on one main server (the other's was not caught) against 784 and 785 MiB on the probe. The wait is the device's queue depth showing on the host, so more slots buy nothing; a gain needs fewer submissions a sum. Data: rig `rdev/k64`.

## The encoder's products on a wide float tile (2026-10-29, branch perf/image-encode-products on main 80cbf1da0, step 2 of perf/image-encode, the owner's approval of the order and F2DEV's DECIDED of 2026-10-27 09:33, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Goal:** the vision encoder's products of BF16 weights, the larger gap to the references (their F32 SGEMM runs at about twice llmx's rate on an MI50), faster on both cards with the rows unchanged.
- **Done:** `shaders/matmul_tile_wide.comp`, a 128 by 128 tile for F32, F16 and BF16 weights, eight rows by eight columns a thread, stages of 16 k values twice buffered in shared memory and the next stage loaded as vectors during the current one, in six forms (each weight type with and without BF16 inputs), each with its float-preserving twin.
  Each output sums in ascending k with the float tile's operation, so the rows are the float tile's bits and a call may take either tile.
  An unsplit call of a float-weight type with at least 128 rows and 128 columns, whose tiles give every compute unit one at least, takes it (`wide_tile_fits`, `wide_tile_kernel`); every other call keeps its tile.
- **Measured (development, encode wall of `llmx-encode-image`, median ms, against main built the same way):** MI50 (GPU 9): 0.8B tower 1024x1024 248 to 224, Flash-Next 1024x1024 997 to 835, Flash-Next 2048x2048 8480-8800 to 7390 (the products 134 to 112, 614 to 452 and 2550 to 1747); Radeon VII: 705 to 640, 2914 to 2353 and 25100 to 22800.
  Rows bit-identical to main on both cards (both towers at 1024, Flash-Next at 2048); Qwen3.5-0.8B BF16 `logits` of a 1439-token prompt byte-identical to main on the MI50 at `--dtype auto`, `f32` and `bf16`; `backend-vulkan`, `vision` and `image` pass on the MI50.
- **The bits, forced (F2DEV's REVIEW of 09:23):** `vulkan-quantization` dispatches both tiles on the same inputs and compares every output: 30322568 outputs, none differing, in the preserving and the plain build on the Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver; and through `matmul` on each side of the compute-unit rule.
- **Tried and not kept:** a first form loading one value at a time was slower than main (Flash-Next 1024 products 843 against 630 ms); lanes along rows for conflict-free shared stores changed nothing.
- **Gate, main d34878121 against the branch, each built the same way from its own commit (encode wall, median ms, ABBA twice):** MI50 (GPU 9, RADV, host load 11 to 15): 0.8B 249 to 224 (-10%), Flash-Next 1024 1002 to 842 (-16%), Flash-Next 2048 8268 to 7593 (-8%); Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver): 704 to 639 (-9%), 2914 to 2352 (-19%), 25130 to 22780 (-9%).
  On both cards: encoder rows bit-identical to main, Qwen3.5-0.8B BF16 `logits` of a 1440-token prompt byte-identical at `--dtype auto`, `f32` and `bf16`, the forced comparison 30322568 outputs with none differing in both builds, `backend-vulkan`, `vision` and `image` pass, no scratch.
  MI50: CTest 94 of 94; the suite on the device with `--require-tools` passes every component but `raw-blocks`, which needs numpy the rig's image lacks (no device code; the hosted jobs install it), and `baseline`, skipped without its models.
- **Left:** the hosted run and F2DEV's review.
- **Gotchas:** the tile holds 128 registers and 32 KiB of shared memory, two waves a SIMD; the products reach about 7.5 TFLOPS on Flash-Next 1024 against the references' 10.9.

## Layered HF references for dense Qwen3 file-exact runs (2026-10-29)

- **Done:** `tools/gen_layered_reference.py` can stream dense Qwen3 GGUF tensors through the existing `tests/f32.py` names and `tests/spec_decode.py` decoder, calling HF's own Qwen3 forward with one module loaded at a time. File-exact metadata records the GGUF identity and decoded tensor types; it does not label checkpoint weights as the quantized file.

The original HF forward owns all math. [Version pins, retained input hashes and output identities](benchmarks/qwen3-layered-tiny-20261029.json). No model download was needed.

The intervening main change concerns Vulkan vision attention; the layered tool, generator tests and reference inputs retain their checked bytes, so the exact tiny HF evidence carries forward. The affected generator and docs checks run on this tree, with applicable hosted checks required before fast-forward. No inference runtime or numerical limit changes.

The Q2_0 integration must pin the candidate tree's `spec_decode.py` and `gen_baseline.py`; this main-tree unit case uses Q2_K, which its decoder supports. The large-file Q2 quality result remains pending. The tiny test establishes adapter equivalence, not released-model correctness.
