## The serving rework, step 0: the service record, the price table and the replay (2026-10-27, RDEV, branch feat/serving-step0 on feat/q8-short-k bac4ed4bd (on perf/image-encode-attention 509d3241b), approved by F2DEV, lands third by fast-forward, step 0 of the serving rework plan (the coordinator's sched-audit draft 3, agreed by F2DEV and XDEV, the owner's answers of 12:43), landed; steps 1 and 2 above land on it)

- **Goal:** the server under a long prompt redone as one service rule for every placement (production on 2026-10-27: a reply at 3 tok/s beside a 150k prompt read at 400-768 tok/s, prompts of 327 and 3,334 tokens at 0 rows for 106 s).
  Step 0 measures and decides without changing a generated output byte: the server records every stage's time against a measured price table, and the scheduler's simulator replays production's requests and synthetic loads under each share rule through the policy the server will run.
- **Done:** `server/service_record.hpp` (`ServiceRecord`): each recorded stage posted with `Model::stage_sent` and measured by the record's own thread; the price table and the service rule's policy in `server/policy.hpp` (`depth_band`, `PassWork`, `PriceTable`, `service_gap`, `chunk_budget`, `packed_passes`, `Share`, `next_prompt`, `charge_share`); `/v1/health`'s `service` and the live items' `queued_ms`, `first_token_ms` and `inter_token_ms` (docs/USAGE.md); `server-passes` holds the policy by hand and replays the owner's case at 20k tokens in every run, and `--replay FILE` or `--load NAME` replays the trace and the loads S1 to S7 under the candidates A0 to A7 (docs/SERVER.md, Prompt shares).
- **Unchanged by construction:** what a pass holds; the record only reads the passes the round forms, which rests on review (XDEV and F2DEV), and the byte identity below checks the output.
- **Checks:** CTest 74 of 74 on a CPU build and server-passes at 2000 schedules on the rig; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on the CPU against main 5673d3c25: logits, greedy ids, and `tools/server_mix_check.py --logprobs` ids identical; docs and dead-code pass.
- **Left:** F2DEV's review; the share rule and `mix` chosen from the replays and frozen here; step 1, the holds off the reply path, on its own branch.
- **Prices:** the replay's defaults are fitted to SDEV's profile of 2026-10-27 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, production's 2x2 placement, `bench --profile`, device time a stage): a 512-row pass took 312, 394, 504 and 598 ms at depths 10k, 50k, 100k and 150k and a 64-row pass 103 ms at 100k, so a chunk pass costs about 46 ms fixed plus 0.48 ms a row plus 4.0e-6 ms a row a token of depth; a decode step 12.0 to 13.1 ms over the same depths.
  The depth term is the indexer's scores (`kv_index_scores_tile`, 22 to 47 percent of a 512-row pass from 10k to 150k), sparse attention being flat, so the table's depth bands carry it within a row class.
- **Replays at those prices** (two stages, P = 3, 16 decode columns): the share rule moves the later prompts' first tokens (S1's 327- and 3,334-token prompts at p95 408 s oldest first, 1.0 s least remaining with a 10 s bound), but the chunk budget moves the long prompt and the replies against each other: in S1 the 150k prompt's first token at 412 s against 131 s alone and a reply's gap of 151 ms p50 at `mix` 3, 174 s and 333 ms at 6, 142 s and 700 ms at 12, since each small chunk pays the pass's 46 ms.
  At 70 percent load beside a long prompt (S5-70) every rule falls behind: the chunks' fixed cost cuts the stages' prompt rate to about 600 rows a second against 1138 alone.
- **Gotchas:** the record's thread polls `Backend::done` every millisecond while a stage waits, so a stage's time is known to about a millisecond; a pass fed in pieces is timed but not priced.
  The replay's first figures (default prices, `mix` 3, two stages of P = 3) show the gap the rule targets is not the gap a reply sees on a split: with the chunk budget `G - r` per stage, S1's replies run at a gap of 84 ms p50 against a G of 55 ms, since a reply's pass meets a chunk at both stages; the bound across stages is the service rule's to state in step 2.
## Short Q8_0 rows decode two to a subgroup (2026-10-27, DDEV, branch feat/q8-short-k on main 26f97c37d (gated on cfd195380), lever 3 part 1 of the 2x2 decode plan, design approved by F2DEV at 10:14, code approved at 13:02, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Goal:** a one-column Q8_0 decode call of rows at most 16 blocks wide (hc_up, 320 wide on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) takes the paired build: each 32-lane half of a subgroup takes its own rows, where today 44 of 64 lanes have no block. Every column keeps the bits of the build it replaces.
- **Why:** the 2x2 decode profile of 2026-10-27 (Flash UD-Q4_K_XL, int8) has the hyper-connection pair at 1.01 ms a stage, 91 calls of about 11 us; hc_up runs at 340-370 GB/s against 650-700 for the large products.
- **Done:** the build (variant 9, specialization constant 16 `HALVES`, `VulkanBackend::paired_build`) on the plain call path only, two rows a half; the decode-column comparison at Q8_0 rows 320, 448 and 512 wide, the one-column build witness for short rows, and the --isa counts of a paired build, with planted refusals; docs.
- **Probe** (GPU 9 alone, default clocks, one-column calls, 2000 warm calls, median of 7 repeats of 1000, main c004c8e3a against the build at two and four rows a half, interleaved twice; the bytes of every case identical across all arms, int8 and f16, and also at one row a half):

  | Shape (K x rows) | main int8 | paired int8 | main f16 | paired f16 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 320 x 10240 (hc_up) | 10.24 us | 7.38 us (-28%) | 11.84 us | 8.18 us (-31%) |
  | 448 x 2560 | 5.01 us | 4.47 us | 5.47 us | 4.74 us |
  | 512 x 2560 | 5.15 us | 4.60 us | 5.55 us | 4.86 us |
  | 64 x 4096 | 5.71 us | 4.23 us | 6.34 us | 4.50 us |
  | 2560 x 2560 (control, unchanged) | 12.13 us | 12.13 us | 13.53 us | 13.54 us |

  Four rows a half were slower than two at int8 (hc_up 7.72 us) and level at f16, so two are kept.
- **Gates** (main cfd195380 against the branch, both built the same way, GPUs 4-7, default clocks, CPUs 4-7,12-15): Flash UD-Q4_K_XL identity byte for byte at 2x2 int8, 2x2 auto and layer 4 int8 (the last 16 logits rows of a 3k-token prompt and 64 greedy tokens); `llmx-split-check` of Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 over two MI50s bit-identical in both arms; MI50 CTest passes but q2-k-vulkan and q3-k-vulkan, which fail on main too (a test expectation, fixed on its own branch); backend-vulkan --isa on an MI50 holds the two paired builds to their counts; the Radeon VII's vulkan CTests and --isa pass, with no paired build there; docs and dead-code pass.
- **Timing, tg32 tok/s, ABBA:** Flash 2x2 int8: main 47.53, 45.85, 47.47, 47.33 (median 47.40); branch 45.45, 48.23, 48.34, 48.78 (median 48.29, +1.9%); pp64 level. Layer 4 int8: main 51.18, 43.21; branch 45.17, 44.19, unresolved, since main alone spread 8 tok/s across two runs.
- **Left:** the rebase on main, its builds and the hosted run.
- **Also recorded here:** lever 4, the inject gates as a role of hc_down's dispatch, is parked. On the MI50 the Q8_0 decode build is the _preserve module and F32 rows keep the ordinary one, so the fused kernel's two parts differ in float controls and the fusion is refused (F2DEV, 09:57 and 10:05); it would pay only where both modules match.

## DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and DeepSeek-V4 planned (2026-10-27, branch docs/deepseek4-plan on main 53309fd3b, docs only, the owner's request of 2026-10-27, reviewed by F2DEV and XDEV, decided by the owner on 2026-10-27, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Goal:** docs/DEEPSEEK4.md: the plan for running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (`deepseek41`) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (`deepseek4`) in llmx, from the plan the owner decided on 2026-09-26, updated for the 1017 release and for what llmx gained since.
- **Done:** 1017 compared file by file with V4.1-Flash on the Hub (same configuration, tokenizer, tensor index and kernels; every weight shard new; two reference fixes, the index keys in decode and an FP8 cast of the attention output); the other project's 1017 GGUF headers read on the test machine (the files the page's provenance lists) and the upstream layout's from range reads; the big runtimes' and the fork's handling surveyed; the V4 question answered (one module, two registry entries, V4 about a quarter to a third more model work).
- **Reviews:** F2DEV (four points, cleared 07:33) and XDEV (four points, cleared 07:36), every finding taken with its evidence in the page's section 10.
- **Decisions:** the owner answered all nine on 2026-10-27 as recommended (the page's section 9): V4 too after V4.1's CPU step; both `deepseek41` layouts, the local one first; the other project's 1017 GGUF read read-only once it is finished, no download; V4.1 checked against the local file's own weights; announced whole-machine windows; the 2026-10-19 depth rules for the 16k check (a gate change); 1017's FP8 cast not emulated; the fork as the speed reference; V4-0731's UD file copied back when V4 starts.
- **Revision of 2026-11-04 (DSDEV2, branch docs/deepseek4-update on main 840b96ec7, docs only):** the owner's requirements of that day folded in (the page's section 0): Engram reuses Flash-Next's PLE, hoisted into `arch/blocks.hpp` (step 4a) and generalized there (step 4b); ROCm beside CPU and Vulkan (section 4.9, steps 9a and 9b: MXFP4 on ROCm as the backend's type work with its own gate, then the DeepSeek ops from RDEV's landing B); windows from midnight on all ten MI50s; the fork layout's Engram tensors read from the headers (`engram_wkv`, `engram_q`, `engram_k`, no convolution).
  F2DEV reviewed it alone (2026-11-04 20:16, approve with six changes), and DSDEV3 folded every point in with the page's section 10: the gate's sign at a zero dot as a mode of `signed_sqrt_gate` (DeepSeek's `copysign`; Qwen3.8's HF `sign()`, which today's op follows), one gate path for both layouts through the F32 product of `engram_q` and `engram_k`, the hash's mapped pad fill that cuts only before the start, step 4a as a hoist, step 9 split, and the reference read from the local checkpoint, pinned by its SHA-256s.
- **Left:** F2DEV's read of the folded changes, then it lands by fast-forward as one docs commit; then step 2, the reference tool, built by DSDEV3 in the environment at `/opt/claude-work/llmx-dsdev2-env` on the NVMe root pool, from a copy of the local checkpoint's code checked against its digests.
- **Gotchas:** the other project's DeepSeek files are read read-only, GGUF headers and tensors only (decision 3); V4.1 needs all ten MI50s, so its device checks run in announced whole-machine windows (decision 5); `/zpool1` stood at 299 GiB free on 2026-11-04, at the reserve.

## Vulkan AllReduce submission cost (2026-10-28, in progress)

- **Goal:** reduce the completed multi-device AllReduce cost toward the matched ROCm reference without adding a ROCm dependency. Keep the existing ordered sum, peer-buffer ownership and failure contracts.
- **Done:** recovered the isolated historical experiment from `ar-bench`, based on public main `9d00fb0a5`. Both saved HTTP loads completed 256 requests per named transport with no failures or short replies and identical prompts. Their labels lack a saved HTTP startup-mode witness, their runs were sequential and no activity monitor accompanies them, so they are historical observations, not a merge gate. At eight clients their means are 116.07 / 116.65 output tok/s (named sync files / shared timelines), while median TTFT rises from about 1.32 to 1.55 s. The user container and production remain untouched.
- **Portable experiments:** a confirmed-ticket cache and one binary source signal exported once, with a duplicated sync-file descriptor for every peer. All three arms pass the bounded Linux ticket and TP2/TP4 collective screen: 128 ring-reuse/two-waiter rounds per arm, changing inputs over four message sizes including two-shot sums, and three outstanding generations. The selected source passes the Linux MI50 native Vulkan test with three devices, 160 storage/submission checks and 52,250,032 kernel outputs checked against CPU; Windows Radeon VII native CTest passes with 135 storage/submission checks and 51,899,392 outputs. The earlier Windows test before fan-out remains historical evidence. [Cross-platform native record](benchmarks/vulkan-allreduce-cross-platform-native-20261028.json), [Windows native record](benchmarks/vulkan-submit-windows-20261028.json).
- **Verified identity and suite checks:** CPU and Radeon VII each produce 21/21 byte-identical full-vocabulary payload pairs and 448 matching greedy IDs across seven models. The Radeon original suite has 45/46 components passing; MXFP4's `VK_ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER` loader failure is retained with cause unproven. Its focused MXFP4 rerun passes 289 calls with no source or binary changes. The source/test carry from tested commit `94c1680` to hosted commit `c2ed9a0` and this landing is unchanged. [Windows CPU identity](benchmarks/vulkan-allreduce-windows-cpu-identity-20261028.json), [Radeon qualification](benchmarks/vulkan-allreduce-windows-radeon-20261028.json).
- **Verified Linux qualification:** the ordinary selected-source Vulkan suite passes 46/46 components. Focused tensor-split HF checks pass at GPU widths 2 and 4, including single-device greedy and MTP comparisons. During the suite, CPU affinity moved from 4-7 to 8-11 to avoid active quality-raw CPUs; a fresh admission audit included both jobs and passed. The original admission filter omitted quality raw, so it does not prove that job was covered by the initial check. No performance claim follows from these correctness runs. [Linux suite and tensor-split evidence](benchmarks/vulkan-allreduce-linux-device-qualification-20261028.json).
- **Timing screen:** all 24 interleaved calls retained on the same two/four MI50s, image, compiler flags and build path. The table is the mean of four per-call p50 completion times in microseconds, including final sum submission and every member's completion; readback stays outside it. A cache alone has no established gain. At TP2 the combined arm is 7.9 to 12.9 percent faster at 20/160 KiB; its larger messages improve by 5.6/0.8 percent. At TP4:

  | Bytes | Main | Cache | Cache and one export/source |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 20480 | 323.130 | 326.769 | 265.728 |
  | 163840 | 339.540 | 332.687 | 272.108 |
  | 1310720 | 715.119 | 718.911 | 685.695 |
  | 10485760 | 4109.507 | 4113.562 | 4082.646 |

  All calls have monitor coverage: 59 samples, one call flagged for unrelated CPU activity, none for other GPUs, aggregate disk or sample gaps. Unknown process CPU remains recorded. This screen has no fresh ROCm arm and establishes no real-model gate. [Pinned sources, binaries, every sample and historical limitations](benchmarks/vulkan-allreduce-resume-20261028.json).
- **Follow-up screen:** removing the cache and using close-on-exec duplicates together loses much of the combined arm's small-message gain. At TP4, main / cached dup / uncached close-on-exec means are 341.385 / 254.782 / 321.726 us at 20 KiB and 345.687 / 278.795 / 332.257 us at 160 KiB; the uncached close-on-exec arm costs 0.30 / 0.18 percent at 1.25 / 10 MiB. All twelve calls have monitor coverage, one CPU-flagged call retained. Its descriptor check passes eight exact injected failures, no leak and correct recovery after each, with 120 close-on-exec duplicates witnessed. These two simultaneous changes need the existing uncached-dup phase control before attribution. The largest phase difference is host time in sum_into (copy/barrier recording, exchange and final-sum recording); final sum submission remains about 70 us in all three arms.
- **Attribution:** two interleaved phase-control calls per arm give 20 KiB completed means of 321.464 / 253.688 / 294.293 / 295.698 us for main / cached dup / uncached dup / uncached close-on-exec. Host sum_into-time means of the per-call medians are 200.215 / 133.394 / 171.005 / 171.544 us; final submissions remain 68-72 us. These are host times, not GPU kernel times, and separate medians do not add to the total median. All eight calls have coverage and no activity flags. Strace was not used in this early screen; later syscall counts are recorded below. The measured cache/fan-out interaction, rather than close-on-exec alone, chooses the combined cache and close-on-exec candidate.
- **Selected real-model screen:** the combined cache and close-on-exec transport passes its brief ring, multi-generation, large-message and injected-FD-failure checks, then all 24 fixed TP4 calls on Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M. Every decode sample is above every main sample of its case. Four process samples per arm/case, ABBA then BAAB, each with one warmup and one measured repeat, same binary kind, image, flags, file and four MI50s:

  | Workload | Main PP tok/s | Candidate PP tok/s | Main TG tok/s | Candidate TG tok/s |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | P128 / G256, one sequence | 1109.235 | 1119.485 | 55.745 | 61.995 |
  | P4096 / G128, one sequence | 1283.633 | 1283.995 | 54.343 | 61.823 |
  | P128 / G128, four sequences | 1130.512 | 1134.150 | 213.968 | 237.260 |

  PP and TG reset independently. Single-sequence TG starts empty in each case; four-sequence TG begins after each sequence's P128 prompt, outside its timer. The bench requests active histories of 256 / 4096 / 256 tokens per sequence; its model context is read from the file. A prelaunch attempt was refused for unsupported `bench --ctx-size` and produced no performance sample; its receipt is retained separately. All 24 measured calls have monitor coverage over 205 samples: three calls flagged for unrelated CPU activity, all 24 for aggregate disk traffic including their model loads, none for other GPUs or gaps. No call was dropped; unknown process CPU remains reported. This is a before/after screen with no fresh ROCm arm yet.
- **Focused serving identity:** main and selected each pass 16 requests alone (928 output tokens), together with zero differences, and skewed with zero differences among twelve retained clients and all four planned departures handled. Four CLI replies per arm match that arm's server. The saved phase JSON files, containing IDs, log-probabilities and top-five values without timing metadata, are byte-identical across main and selected. Only owned servers were started/stopped; the test container is removed and inputs unchanged. The test duration is not a performance comparison.
- **Matched serving performance:** all 256 measured requests in four fresh ABBA servers complete with no failures, short replies or cached tokens. Two fixed samples per arm/client count, sixteen distinct deterministic requests per level, equal request manifests across blocks. Main / selected aggregate output tok/s at 1/2/4/8 clients is 43.475 / 47.977, 68.590 / 73.509, 89.025 / 96.863 and 107.634 / 110.990: gains of 10.35 / 7.17 / 8.80 / 3.12 percent. Mean time per output token improves by 11.34 / 8.84 / 9.79 / 3.33 percent. Median TTFT changes by -0.12 / +2.44 / +10.80 / +12.05 percent, and p99 by +0.03 / -3.05 / +6.70 / -10.63 percent; the throughput gain comes with a latency tradeoff at higher concurrency. All sixteen measured windows have activity coverage; three CPU-flagged windows remain included, with no other-GPU, disk or gap flags.
- **Fresh custom ROCm baseline:** four interleaved TP4 calls, selected / ROCm / ROCm / selected, on exactly the same four MI50 PCI devices and CPU set. Mean per-call p50 completed times in microseconds are:

  | Bytes | Selected Vulkan | Custom ROCm | Vulkan / ROCm |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 20480 | 268.028 | 61.977 | 4.325 |
  | 163840 | 271.463 | 93.048 | 2.917 |
  | 1310720 | 656.400 | 331.215 | 1.982 |
  | 10485760 | 3946.761 | 2307.181 | 1.711 |

  Both arms pass every end-of-run output check, use 120 warmups and 100 measured calls with constant rank inputs, and stop timing only after all ranks complete. Vulkan accumulates into an initially zero residual; the reference overwrites its output, so the benchmark checks the corresponding expected result in each arm. Native backend images differ and are pinned; before/after llmx uses the same Vulkan image. The staged reference binary, source, clean mx revision and HIP PCI mapping are verified. Four calls have full monitoring coverage, maximum sample gap 2.003 seconds; raw background activity and unknown process CPU are retained. This small runner did not define activity thresholds, so no retrospective activity flags are assigned. This establishes the current TP4 gap, not a TP2 result or an achieved target.
- **Two/four-card follow-up:** the fresh twelve-call selected / aggregate-fence / ROCm palindrome passes all four sizes on both widths, after four brief changing-input and multi-generation smoke calls. Both owned CPU correctness jobs were paused for 30.8 seconds and resumed without losing progress; all planned samples remain retained. At TP2, selected / ROCm mean p50 us is 166.855 / 34.631, 163.525 / 49.657, 290.929 / 187.111 and 1266.079 / 1279.184 across the four sizes. The separate aggregate arm retains TP2's direct peer path; its apparent 8.73 percent small-message gain is not established, given selected's 153.204 / 180.505 us sample spread. At TP4, selected / aggregate / ROCm is 268.673 / 256.523 / 62.527, 259.068 / 275.709 / 93.093, 646.370 / 656.551 / 329.115 and 3941.691 / 3946.721 / 2312.331 us. The aggregate loses 6.42 percent at 160 KiB in both samples; larger cases are flat/slower, and its 20 KiB samples vary from 243.188 to 269.858 us. It is not selected. A preworkload attempt failed because copied wrappers lost execute permission; that receipt is preserved separately, fixed with permission-preserving copies, and produced no performance sample.
- **Host cost diagnosis:** the aggregate-fence diagnostic spends about 40.15 us per TP4 20 KiB exchange: 9.71 merging, 2.50 duplicating, 13.77 importing and 14.17 cleaning up. The added work largely consumes the plausible budget of eight avoided imports; these initial clocks include first use and warmups. A separate selected-source profile resets every counter after 120 warmups and records exactly 100 calls. At TP4 20 KiB, sum-body host time is 153.32 us: 14.55 copy/barrier recording, 10.74 sum recording and 127.80 actual exchange. Exchange includes 75.82 dispatch/join and 46.34 serial imports (45.17 at 160 KiB). Preparation is below one microsecond per member. Per-rank queue clocks overlap and must not be summed. An earlier contaminated profile is retained, not interpreted as steady state; no instrumented completed time is a before/after speed result.
- **Further fixed screens:** per-recipient parallel imports pass all 48 rank/size/call checks but establish no gain: TP4 changes are -1.60 / +7.38 / +2.30 / -0.20 percent across the four sizes, with overlapping 20 KiB samples and substantial 160 KiB scatter. Batched outbound release barriers are also mixed at +3.11 / -0.76 / -2.06 / -0.01 percent. TP2's apparent 14.79 percent 20 KiB gain has no changed barrier count, while selected itself shifts against prior samples; it is not attributed to batching. Every planned sample remains. Two CPU-flagged release-screen intervals remain included; its raw TP2 other-GPU flag spans our own transition into TP4, so it does not prove unrelated GPU competition. Neither arm is adopted or sent through broad correctness gates.
- **Reference mechanics:** the pinned reference uses one kernel per rank with fine-grained peer writes and system-scope barriers, including both phases of two-shot inside the kernel. This is source-derived, not a fresh GPU trace. llmx's established Vulkan visibility contract uses submission boundaries on these cards; no mx code is copied.
- **Idle relay result:** the separate device-idle arm removes native semaphore FD exchange while retaining the FOREIGN barriers and GPU arithmetic. All twelve calls, 48 rank/size checks and four brief smoke calls pass, but it is slower: TP2 changes +4.18 / +22.27 / +12.01 / +4.88 percent; TP4 -2.57 / +10.70 / +27.25 / +4.80 percent. Completed source waits lose more overlap than the removed FD work saves. This arm is not adopted and receives no real-model or broad correctness gate.
- **Native syncobj opportunity:** the stock-libdrm probe passes reset/import/signal and snapshot controls, with all eight timed batches retained. Create/import/destroy averages 2867.85 ns per operation versus 2155.82 for reset/import. The completed-fd Signal equivalent averages 3414.60 versus 2646.80 ns. Separate traced 100-operation captures confirm 300 versus 200 ioctls, without errors. Optimistic summed CPU savings are 1.40/8.42 us for two/twelve imports, before real Mesa cache costs; they are not measured collective wall gains. Every batch has activity coverage and no threshold flags, with unknown process observations retained. Pooling is deferred; the completed private-driver timing below instead separates submission preparation from the native call. [Native probe evidence](benchmarks/vulkan-native-syncobj-20261028.json).
- **Driver CPU profile:** after 120 warmups, selected-only 20 KiB captures retain 470 / 1257 cycle samples at TP2 / TP4, with zero reported lost samples. Kernel-exclusive period weight is 89.65 / 86.93 percent; Mesa Vulkan is 5.39 / 7.41 and the helper 1.80 / 1.85. Inclusive command-submission ioctl paths account for 54.63 / 50.04 percent, inside all-ioctl 78.34 / 71.51; these overlap and must not be summed. Reservation/VM bookkeeping, rather than another FD rearrangement, is the next owner to investigate. Exclusive unresolved symbols remain 10.30 / 11.39 percent. All observed threads match the READY identity set; cache-worker weight is negligible. Sampled CPU cycles do not measure blocked waits or completed latency. Saved-data symbol resolution was repaired without repeating workloads.
- **Native syscall counts:** after 120 warmups, two 100-call 20 KiB traces pass at TP2 and TP4. Each collective makes 4 / 8 native command submissions, exactly two per rank; there are no hidden submits. Timeline payloads distinguish 4 / 8 fence-availability checks from 2 / 4 completion waits. Flags 7 include WAIT_AVAILABLE, while flags 3 wait for completion; both infinite and zero-timeout availability checks occur. Imports create and destroy 2 / 12 temporary native syncobjs per collective despite persistent Vulkan semaphore objects. Five/six CS chunks do not reveal BO count. Tracing inflates p50 completion to roughly 2.4 / 6.95 ms; syscall durations and idle-worker futex totals are diagnostic, not ordinary wall latency. Raw traces stay in scratch artifacts, with a compact decoded summary in the evidence.
- **GPU region diagnostic:** six selected-source 20 KiB calls pass with markers disabled / enabled / disabled at TP2 and TP4, and all 600 measured rank/call rows are present. Per-rank median copy plus FOREIGN release is 12.96-13.12 / 24.00-24.48 us; acquire plus ordered sum is 13.12-13.92 / 14.88-15.52 us. The same-device gap between regions is 48.48-71.68 / 92.16-94.56 us, combining peer readiness, host handoff and queue scheduling. Markers increase completed p50 by 15.05 / 9.11 percent against bracketing same-binary controls; these are diagnostic regions, not shares of ordinary completed latency. Each queue reports 64 timestamp bits at 40 ns; query reset/readback stays outside measured calls. All six windows have activity coverage and no recorded threshold flags. Unknown process CPU and one missed process remain reported.
- **Handoff diagnostic:** all six output calls and all fixed callback records pass. TP2 has no source workers: median initial entry / join tail is 0.060 / 0.080 us. TP4 records a 113.983 us dispatch span, first worker callback at 12.390 us, 7.270 us join tail and 95.993 us union of queue/export/dup spans. These are perturbed measurements: timed completed latency rises 6.36 percent at TP2 and 34.92 percent at TP4 against bracketing same-binary controls. All three TP4 windows also share one CPU-flagged monitor interval; no samples are removed. Per-rank TP4 queue medians are 24.081 / 33.921 / 25.511 / 31.701 us. The caller always takes rank zero and also rank two in 48 calls; a late caller start is not worker wake latency. This does not establish normal wall-time shares or a promised dispatcher saving.
- **Bounded active-wait rejected:** one shared-JobThreads research arm watches an atomic generation for up to 250 us before CV sleep. Same newly built binary, matching header/library/wrapper, control / active / active / control at TP2/TP4; no mixed class layouts or frozen-library overwrite. All eight calls and 32 size checks pass. TP4 mean p50 changes are +16.44 / +5.32 / -4.64 / +0.18 percent at 20 KiB / 160 KiB / 1.25 MiB / 10 MiB. Workload CPU per collective rises from 438.5 / 440.5 / 805.6 / 844.7 us to 940.6 / 951.1 / 1755.8 / 1847.6 us. Live-worker idle intervals return to sleep, worst 1.148 ms CPU during 250 ms. TP2 source stays serial; its +3.87 / +0.29 / -3.27 / +0.53 percent movement is not attributed to active waiting. Every sample remains, all eight windows have coverage and no activity flags. This arm is rejected without model or full gates; selected product is unchanged. Earlier ROCm reference timings are explicitly separate measurements.
- **Ordered hub rejected:** the tiny gather/reduce-once/broadcast probe reuses directional inboxes and the existing ordered F32 sum with keep. All twelve 20 KiB output calls pass. Ordinary all-member completion is primary: TP2 control / hub p50 is 152.506 / 168.966 us (+10.79 percent); TP4 is 260.260 / 302.442 us (+16.21 percent). A separate topology-aware completion skips the hub empty final submit and waits its producer ticket: 165.566 us at TP2 (+8.56 percent), 262.550 us at TP4 (+0.88 percent), with TP4 samples 238.349 / 286.751 us. Mean per-call p50 is 157.390 / 162.355 us at TP2 and 262.924 / 257.173 at TP4; the instrumented changes of +3.15 / -2.19 percent quantify perturbation, not a speedup. Per-rank native ac/libdrm-plus-CS call medians span 18.33-32.67 us, while BO-list construction is only 0.09-0.41 us. Mean p50 is 153.005 / 136.954 us at TP2 (-10.49 percent), both enabled samples below both controls. TP4 is 256.433 / 233.867 us (-8.80 percent), with overlapping samples, so its gain remains provisional. Every sample is retained; all eight windows have activity coverage and no flags. - **Uninstrumented local BO screen:** the same private baseline DSO and frozen four-size selected helper pass all eight calls and 32 output checks. Off/enabled mean p50 us at TP2 is 160.826/146.280, 166.475/160.815, 290.789/276.378 and 1313.809/1265.828 (-9.05/-3.40/-4.96/-3.65 percent). TP4 is 257.538/248.268, 323.290/259.423, 646.390/653.715 and 3953.053/3945.598 (-3.60/-19.76/+1.13/-0.19 percent). The TP4 160 KiB control samples are 385.501/261.078 us; its apparent large gain is not stable evidence. Tiny TP4 samples overlap. All windows have activity coverage; two CPU-flagged calls and one raw other-GPU flag remain included. The latter interval spans our own TP2-to-TP4 transition and does not establish unrelated GPU competition. Disk/gap flags are zero; unknown process CPU and one missed observation remain retained. The exact Q2 reference container resumed after a 22.545-second pause. The measured BO-removal mechanism is promising, especially at TP2, but no uniform TP4 or real-model gain is claimed.
- **Selected runtime qualification:** applicable native, CPU/device identity, device suite, Radeon, matched timing and hosted checks are complete. The Radeon suite's original MXFP4 loader failure remains recorded; its focused rerun passed without code changes, and its cause is unproven. ### Historical NVFP4 evidence (79e9d5928, 4f026d941, d86fb838b, dbfef2d36 and named earlier experiments, 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-26)

The entries below retain their original receipts and results. These entries remain tied to the source revisions and checkpoints named in their text and receipts. Any earlier current-state or remaining-work wording describes that historical checkpoint, not the train integration above; none qualifies its GPU behavior, model correctness, or performance.

- **Native F16-input checkpoint (79e9d5928 implementation, historical):** two software-assisted packing variants passed native checks but lost 38-165% on ordinary MI50 operator timing, so neither goes to model qualification. Actual F16 shared pairs avoid that loss. ## A function call's value is written by the JSON types its schema admits (2026-10-27, TDEV, branch fix/tool-arg-types on main 5e90171a8, the owner's production report through the coordinator, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** on production (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, main e9efe108b) Open WebUI 0.12.0's built-in `create_tasks` failed with "dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required" and `update_memory` with "1 validation error for UpdateMemoriesForm ... Input should be a valid list ... input_type=str": both take a list (`tasks: list[TaskItem]`, `operations: list[dict]`), and each got the list as a JSON string, since Open WebUI hands the call's arguments to the tool unchanged.
  A function-format value was JSON only where the request declared the parameter with a top-level `type` other than a string; a schema through `anyOf` or `$ref`, one with only `items`, one with no type, and a tool the request leaves out gave a string.
- **Cause, as far as it can be shown without the client's request:** Open WebUI's spec for both tools is a plain `"type": "array"` (reproduced from its own `convert_function_to_pydantic_model` and `clean_properties` with langchain-core 1.4.8's `convert_to_openai_function` in a scratch environment), and two requests to production with that spec, whole and streamed, gave real arrays.
  The failing path is then a tool the request does not declare: Open WebUI's tool search (`chat.tool_search`, an admin setting, off by default and not set by its environment here) leaves out every tool whose spec passes 400 characters, both of these among them, lists them by name and gives their schemas through a `search_tools` call, after which the model calls the tool by name.
  A value that is not strict JSON (a raw control character in a string, say) would also give a string; nothing seen points to it.
- **The change:** `chat::tool_params` reads each parameter's JSON types through `type`, `enum`, `const`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `allOf`, a `$ref` into the parameters' `$defs` or `definitions`, `properties` and `items` (`chat::schema_types`), and `chat::ToolValue` says how its value is written: as a string where it admits only strings and null; as JSON where it admits no string and the text is JSON; and where it admits a string and another type, names none, or is not declared, as JSON only where the text is an object or array. `Api::tools_of` calls it in place of its own reading.
  Compared, not copied: vLLM's Qwen3-Coder parser (v0.11.0, `qwen3coder_tool_parser.py`) takes the type from a parameter's top-level `type` alone, a missing one as a string, and returns the raw string for an undeclared tool or parameter; SGLang's `qwen3_coder_detector.py` infers a type through `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `allOf`, `enum`, `properties` and `items` (`infer_type_from_json_schema`, no `$ref`) but also returns an undeclared parameter's raw string; both fall back to a Python literal read. llmx reads references too, takes an undeclared value as JSON where it is an object or array, which a client that defers schemas needs, and reads strict JSON only.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: `chat-template`'s `ToolCallSplit` case of an array and a non-JSON value for a tool the request leaves out, and the server component's checklist call under the Qwen 3.8 template, whole and streamed, with the list declared an array, through `anyOf`, through `$ref`, by `items`, with no type and for a tool left out, and as a string under a schema that declares one. The second commit adds `chat-template`'s `tool_params` case over twenty parameter schemas.
- **Review:** F2DEV approved at 07:57 with one nit, a `static_assert` pinning the order of jmini's value types that `schema_types` names, which is in; on the point to judge, undeclared structured text taken as JSON, yes.
- **Checked** on Windows, MSVC Release builds from clean worktrees: the test commit fails on main at the left-out tool (`chat-template`) and at the array or null (`server`), and the change passes both. On the change before its rebases onto 98112a916 and 5e90171a8 (b7e50e78b; only STATUS conflicted), CTest passes 75 of 75 and the CPU suite with `--require-tools` 45 of 45 components. Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 greedy, three raw and three chat prompts of 128 tokens on 4 threads, gives the same text and ids as main dd4163407 (both arms built the same way, numerics 20f06a7c07a3fb37).
- **Left:** the hosted run at the landing head; then production can take it as a preview.
- **Gotchas:** an undeclared string parameter whose text is a JSON object or array now becomes that object or array; the request did not say it is a string, and a list is what a client that leaves the schema out was seen to need.

## The encoder's attention in FlashAttention-2's shape (2026-10-27, branch perf/image-encode-attention on main 26f97c37d, step 1 of perf/image-encode, the owner's approval of the order of VDEV's SUMMARY of 09:31 and its CORRECTION, F2DEV's DECIDED of 09:33, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Goal:** the vision encoder's non-causal attention (heads 64 and 72) in FlashAttention-2's shape in F32, faster on both cards with the same precision form; f16 staging becomes the default form only if it is faster on the MI50.
- **Done:** `shaders/attention_flash.comp` takes the `attention_full_tile_d64` and `attention_full_tile_d72` builds: 64 query rows a workgroup, each group of eight lanes holding two rows' queries and outputs in registers, keys and values through shared memory 16 at a time, scores eight keys at a time by partial dots and a butterfly, the softmax online in F32, and each key's weight shuffled from the lane that scored it.
  Every loop is unrolled, so no private array is indexed at run time: the AMD proprietary driver spilled the old build to scratch (320 and 352 bytes) and ran the encoder's attention about three times slower on the Radeon VII than on an MI50.
  Each row's arithmetic is the old build's, so the rows are the same bits as main's on both cards (the 0.8B and Flash-Next towers at 1024x1024, and Flash-Next at 2048x2048 on the MI50).
  `shaders/attention_tile.comp` is back to its causal builds only, as before the image commit.
  `backend-vulkan` holds the rows of a call cut into dispatches to the bits of the uncut call at heads 64 and 72 (F2DEV's condition (b)).
- **Tried and not kept:** a first form with the queries in shared memory and each lane scoring whole keys (two keys a lane a tile) gave the Radeon VII the same gain but was 2 to 4% slower than main on the MI50 in encode wall time, being bound by its shared-memory reads; fetching the next key tile into registers during the current one cost the MI50 about 4% at 2048x2048; 128-thread workgroups, 8- and 32-key tiles and 128-row tiles were slower or needed 58 KiB of shared memory; f16 staging of Q, K and V in shared memory (the f16 form) was 3 to 18% slower on the MI50, since the widening costs more than the halved reads save there, so the default keeps F32; unrolling the old build's loops kept its bits and took 1 to 3% off on the MI50 but left the Radeon VII's spill.
- **Gate, main 26f97c37d against 92753011f, each built the same way from its own commit:** encode wall of `llmx-encode-image`, median ms, interleaved main, branch, branch, main twice, three encodes a run.
  Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver, Windows): 0.8B tower 1024x1024 1314 to 747, Flash-Next 1024x1024 5094 to 2911, Flash-Next 2048x2048 60700 to 25100.
  MI50 (GPU 9, RADV, a host load of 14 to 16 from other work, so the runs drift; ABBA pair means): 0.8B -0.7%, Flash-Next 1024 -1.9%, Flash-Next 2048 -2.0%; quieter single rounds before the rebase gave -1.6%, -1.8% and -4%.
  Driver statistics: no scratch on either driver (8192 and 9216 bytes of shared memory, against 12288 and 13312 with 320 and 352 bytes of scratch on the Radeon VII before).
  Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `logits` of a 1468-token prompt, whose rows take the causal tile, byte-identical to main on both cards.
  Correctness on both cards: `vision` (0.8B file-exact 8.75e-5 on the MI50, 8.58e-5 on the Radeon VII, bound 1.18e-4), Flash-Next's tower against HF float64 (9.05e-6 and 6.39e-6, bound 1.95e-5; main's figures, since the rows are main's bits), `image` and `backend-vulkan` pass; CTest 94 of 94 on the MI50 build.
- **Left:** the hosted run and F2DEV's review.
- **Gotchas:** the encoder's attention runs over patches, four per output token, so its rate is about 5.5 TFLOPS on the MI50 (40% of F32 peak) on main and here alike.

## A message boundary kept on a split whose prompt continues (2026-10-27, branch fix/boundary-retire on main dd4163407, LDEV's FINDING of 2026-10-27 02:26, in progress)

- **Why:** every cut turn on production logged "the message boundary a request asked for was not kept (its history has no state kept once its pass retired, at 0)", so an edit or a regenerate of the last message after a cut read the whole cut prompt again (95k to 212k tokens). The scheduler marked the request when it formed the pass whose slice ends at the boundary, and the first of the request's passes to retire spent the mark: on a split a long prompt continues in consecutive passes, so the pass of the slice before retired first, before the boundary's checkpoint was the sequence's.
- **Done:** `Request::boundary_kept_` is the boundary's position, the end of the slice whose pass keeps it, in place of a flag (F2DEV's decision of 2026-10-27 02:27); retire asks for the boundary only on the pass whose rows end there, and the proof's path reads the same position. A second loss stood behind it: the boundary's copy to host memory is refused for a sequence in flight ("inference: a copy to host memory of a sequence in flight", twice in production's log of 2026-10-27), and a continued prompt's next slice was in flight when the boundary's pass retired; so no slice continues while a boundary's pass is in flight (`Scheduler::continues`), one pipeline bubble a prompt that asks for a boundary.
- **Audit** (the owner's rule of 2026-10-16: every path where passes in flight retire out of order and a decision taken at a pass's formation could be spent by an earlier pass's retirement, read at main d1525c6e9):

  | Decision | Taken | Consumed | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | the message boundary's state (`boundary_kept_`) | formation, the slice ending at it | retire of the first pass of the request | same bug, fixed here |
  | the boundary's copy to host memory (`Cache::keep_boundary`) | the boundary pass's retire | `Model::copy_to_host`, refused while a later slice of the sequence is in flight | other: a second loss on the same path, fixed here by not continuing past a boundary in flight |
  | the follow-up checkpoint (`keep_at_`) and any `BatchEntry::keep` | formation | that pass's own last-stage commit (`Pass::kept`, `stage_commit`) | safe: held by the pass |
  | a proof's state (`prove_at_`) | formation | `Cache::prove`, only once `seq_.in_flight()` is false | safe |
  | a boundary over rows restored unproved | formation | the same retire as the boundary, now at its position | safe with the fix |
  | a verify's mark and drafts (`verify_`) | formation | `settle_verifies` of the same slot; a decoding request is in one pass at a time | safe |
  | a slice's ticket under the interleaved rule (`slice_ticket_`) | each stage of the slice's pass, the latest slice overwriting | the next slice's formation | safe |
  | a cancel, a job's completion and its donor, parking and pausing | none at formation | each waits for `seq_.in_flight()` to be false | safe |
  | sampling and a request's end | the wanting rows of a pass | that pass's retire | safe |
  | rows read again, `reached_`, the restore's first pass and a turn's change timing | none | any retire, as counts or the first pass's time | other: counts and timings, no rows kept or lost |
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: `server-passes-cpu`'s boundary on a split whose prompt continues (AGENTS, Tests).
- **Left:** CTest, Qwen3-0.6B byte identity against main, the hosted run.

## Dashboard startup status consumer (2026-10-27, branch feat/dashboard-startup-status)

- **Goal:** show the server's bounded `/v1/health` startup and failure record while preserving ready telemetry and inference-rate semantics.

## Short prompts beside a long one (2026-10-26, branch feat/short-prompts on main ac940c059 (the landing stack: fix/disk-digest-stop, then fix/image-encode-live), the plan in docs/SERVER.md cleared by F2DEV and XDEV and decided by the owner on 2026-10-26, landed on public main at e9efe108b as two commits)

## A lookup table keeps its hot rows in host memory under the one host budget (2026-10-26, branch feat/lookup-row-store on main 8632074e8, step 1 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 9, the owner's decisions of 2026-10-26, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Goal:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's per-layer table (26.8 GiB, read from its file under `--lookup-storage file`) keeps the rows it has read in host memory, so a row read before is copied from memory and never read from the file again; CACHE-PLAN section 9 measured the rows' cost at 0.14 s of a fresh 2048-token prompt on production's cell and projects about 0.1 s from a 2 GiB store.
- **Done:**
  - `WeightRows` holds a store of hot rows (`hold`): an arena of host pages committed as slots fill, an open-addressing index of {row id, slot} at load 3/4 with backward-shift deletion, and CLOCK, one reference byte a slot. A read looks in the store first, inside the table's read task and under its mutex, reads only the missing rows, and puts them in the store once every read has succeeded, referenced so a read gives up older rows before its own. `store_bytes_for` is the store's real allocation, which the fit counts once with the read windows (`host_bytes`, in place of `staging_bytes`).
  - One host budget, `--host-cache-bytes`, split by one function (`infer::host_shares` in `model/place.hpp`): the rows first, at most half of it and at most the rows of 1.5M tokens (`kRowStoreTokens`, about 2.4 GiB for Flash) and of the table, the server's evicted prefixes the rest; without the flag the budget is half the free host memory, and 0 keeps neither. Placement gives each table read from its file its share by its bytes a token, a table that reaches its cap leaving the rest to the others (`hold_rows`), a table on the devices none, and a host whose budget has no room for the rows none. The server's default, the disk tier's check, the turns' line and the start line take the prefixes' share (`Model::lookup_store_bytes`); the start line gives both.
  - Help and docs: USAGE, SERVER, DISK-TIER, QWEN38-FLASH, AGENTS and the source pages.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing to build on main, which has no store: `weight-rows` (the store's real bytes and the slots a size holds; a held table's rows; on POSIX, with the file rewritten between reads, a held row read from memory, the store kept to its slots with a read's own rows kept and older ones given up by CLOCK, every row read from the file once it holds none, nothing published by a failed read), `placement` (the shares, a table held whole, at half the budget, none for 0, none on the devices and none on a host without room, the store counted once by the fit, and two tables sharing the rows by their bytes a token within their caps, a capped table's rest going to the other) and `server-passes` (the prefixes' default within their share).
- **Measured, warm** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL at production's served flags without a disk tier, the pool then at 95% and below the tier's floor, GPUs 4-7 and CPUs 4-7,12-15 at default clocks, 2026-10-26 16:37-18:15 UTC; main f61c8ca75 at `--host-cache-bytes` 4 GiB against 64c8f0a4a's code at `6843408384`, both servers' start lines giving 4096 MiB to the prefixes, the branch's also 2430 MiB to the rows; blocks fixed in advance, servers m b b m m b b m, each on text no other server read: 16 fresh 2048-token prompts to warm, 12 measured, 3 replies of 256 greedy tokens streamed, and twice a 4096-token conversation pushed to the host tier by 17 others and its follow-up; s8/rsg):

  | Server median | main | branch | change | A-A spread |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | fresh 2048-token prompt | 2.364, 2.355, 2.326, 2.364 s | 2.333, 2.334, 2.330, 2.320 s | -0.98% (0.023 s) | 0.038 s |
  | follow-up from the host tier (4032 reused) | 0.383, 0.393, 0.378, 0.387 s | 0.379, 0.379, 0.377, 0.375 s | -1.9% | 0.015 s |
  | reply, server-logged tok/s | 39.1, 58.5, 39.4, 44.4 | 46.3, 52.7, 52.7, 61.0 | +17% | 19.4 tok/s |
  | reply inter-token p99 | 110, 50, 79, 84 ms | 46, 84, 83, 112 ms | level | 60 ms |

The conversion had ended before the gate, so the ZFS cache served the table's rows faster than in the profile of 13:41-14:08 (0.14 s), which the 4% projection rested on.
  - Replies follow each text's draft acceptance (accepted drafts arrive together, so some medians of the inter-token gap are 0.1 ms), so the reply rows hold no arm effect either way.

  | Server median | main | branch | change | A-A spread |

## A held queue's wait ends by the device's clock (2026-10-26, branch fix/vulkan-hold-bounded on main dd4163407, F2DEV's DECIDED of 20:36 and REVIEW of 23:25, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** a device of a placement over several held between submissions with a submission waiting on a `VkEvent` that only the next submission or a 100 ms watchdog thread set. A process killed with SIGKILL ran neither, so its last hold waited until the driver's 10 s job timeout reset the ring: every test server killed on a tensor pair reset all four cards, and on one MI50 a `generate` over `vulkan:0,cpu` killed mid-reply reset its ring both times, against none for the same command on `vulkan:0` alone.
- **Done:** the hold is a dispatch of `shaders/hold.comp`, one invocation spinning until a release counter reaches its sequence or 100 ms of the device's clock (`clockRealtime2x32EXT`, VK_KHR_shader_clock's `shaderDeviceClock`, counted at the timestamp period) pass; the next submission's `prepare` writes the counter, the watchdog thread and the events are gone, and a device without `shaderDeviceClock` keeps no hold and says so. The counter sits in device-uncached host memory where the device offers it (VK_AMD_device_coherent_memory) and is read with `atomicAdd(released, 0)`: on the Radeon VII a `coherent volatile` load never saw the host's write, every hold running to its bound, and on the MI50 a load saw it only at the next submission's start. Since that rests on behaviour the specification does not promise, the first hold set up is released once it is spinning, 10 ms after its submission with the queue's earlier work done and no submission after it, and a device on which it ends by its bound (the word after the counter takes the sequence of a hold its bound ended) keeps no hold and says so.
  - `vulkan-lifetime`, 1000 holds released by the next submission, from the host's write to the hold's end: MI50 (RADV) p50 0.068 ms, p99 0.113 ms, max 0.170 ms; Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver) p50 0.14 ms, p99 0.35 ms, max 0.45 ms. 300 holds given back with no work after them, the release followed by a submission since the atomic alone took up to 3 ms at the tail on the MI50: MI50 p50 0.041 ms, p99 0.054 ms; Radeon VII p50 0.10 ms, p99 0.32 ms. A hold never released ends at 100.0 to 100.1 ms on both, so the tick rate is right. The setup failing at its timeline and at its counter's memory cleans up on both.
  - Failing first by hand, as no hosted runner has a GPU and the fault shows only in the kernel log after a process dies: `tools/kill_check.py` on one MI50 over `vulkan:0,cpu --layer-shares 1,1`, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, 3 kills 20 s into a reply. At main 458f45fda, 3 ring timeouts on that card, one a kill, each with "device wedged, but recovered through reset"; at the branch, none.
- **Left:** the timing gate F2DEV set, interleaved against main at default clocks: (a) Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.6-27B Q8_0 tg256 at depth 512 on one MI50 and two, (b) Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on 2x2 with production's flags, the reply gaps at 1, 4 and 16 users and a 16k prompt beside a reply, (c) clocks during a split decode and idle after it, (d) the Radeon VII; the kill check on a 2x2 pair; CTest, docs, dead-code and the hosted run.
- **Gotchas:** the spin is one wave issuing an atomic about every microsecond; its cost against the CP's event wait is what gates (b) and (c) measure. A hold given back with no submission after it ends at once as well, since the atomic needs no cache invalidation.

The `mapped` run was stopped by SIGTERM after 11 minutes, the cards clean.

| **to listening** | **527.6** | |

## Server startup plan (planned, 2026-10-26, SDEV, reviewed by F2DEV and XDEV, decided by the owner: steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 built in that order, 4a in the update script, 6 after the code is measured, 4b parked)

Each step on its own branch, measured on production's cell against main as above; seconds are measured where a scratch run took them and marked estimated otherwise.
1. **The fit counts a shard's bytes without listing its runs.** `shard` describes a member's shard by its rows, row bytes and spans, and `footprint` takes a shard's bytes from that description; while `shard::runs` still exists a test holds its byte count equal to the description's over every supported axis and width. Measured 338.7 s to 5.2 s, the rest being the settle's 20 reads of free memory; the fit's results unchanged. Gate: the model tier (placement and fit identical on the CPU and a device, the suite, one timing round).
2. **More reads in flight in the stream.** The ring's readers and slots from 2 and 4 to 8 and 16 as the stream's constants, a measured default and no probe of the disk, the piece kept at 16 MiB and a load of few pieces still taking no more slots than pieces. Its host cost is 256 MiB of pages for the load's duration where it is 64 MiB today; neither is charged by the fit, since the ring is made after the model is built and freed before the server reads the host memory it sizes its host tier by. Measured 174.7 s to 82.4 s on this pool. That nothing is lost where the disk keeps up is still to be shown: the 1M-record copy read 3057 MB/s with 2 jobs and 2972 with 8, so the Radeon VII and a single NVMe disk are timed cold and warm before it lands, with no loss beyond the loader's spread. Gate: `load-progress` and the loader's timing on both machines.
3. **Construct and the stream on step 1's description.** Construct and the stream keep about 126M runs of 32 bytes, about 4 GB of host memory through the load (estimated), for rows the stream packs anyway; moving them onto step 1's description takes construct from 12 s to about 1 s (estimated) and the memory with it, and `shard::runs` goes once nothing reaches it, with step 1's test. Measured first when its branch starts.
4. **The digest once per file.** (a) Production carries `digests/` into each new `--disk-cache-dir` (the update script, no code): 514 s and 103.7 GiB of reads gone at every update after the first. A carried digest is still taken only where the file's absolute path, size, modification time and inode match, so a moved or replaced file is read again. (b) Parked behind 4a, since with digests carried the digest runs once a new file, after listening: the digest reading its pieces through the readers, around the cache where the file system takes direct reads and through it where it refuses them (`format::DirectUnavailable`, as the loader's `open_reader` falls back), with one hash owner, `format::file_sha256`, never a second SHA loop. About 97 s on this pool (estimated from fio's 1147 MB/s); that it spares the ARC the measured churn is not measured. It would follow VDEV's stop flag (fix/disk-digest-stop). Not proposed: hashing the load's own reads, which would read the 26.8 GiB table during the load as well and tie the disk tier's identity into the loader, for a gain only on a cold cache.
5. **`/v1/health` during startup.** The server listens before loading and answers `/v1/health` with HTTP 503 and a body of `"status":"starting"`, the `server` and `requests` objects in their shapes and a `startup` object (`started_unix`, `elapsed_s`, `phase`, and `phases` in order, each with its state, its seconds and, where known, completed and total bytes, an unknown total missing rather than guessed), so a readiness check on 200 keeps its meaning; once the model is published it answers 200 with `"status":"ok"` as today and keeps the record. Every other route refuses with 503 in the native error shape until then. The digest's and the adoption's progress go under `reuse.disk.now`, the disk tier's own phases. The phases are this timeline's: devices, metadata, fit, allocate, weights (bytes, a file each), vision, ready; then digest and adopt. The loader reports its phases through its one progress callback; the server owns the early listener and serves a synchronized snapshot, the CLI renders the same phases, and the server holds no load logic. A stop during startup exits promptly with the listener closed, and a failed load exits nonzero with its error, its health saying so until then, both tested in `tests/server.py`. XDEV's agent builds the dashboard side on its own branch, with its collector (`tools/health_dashboard/server.py`) taking a validated starting body on 503, which it refuses today, other 503s and errors still failures and starting samples kept out of the rate history, held by its own collector tests (XDEV, 20:43).
6. **For the owner: 16K records only where the table is.** The table's random 90-byte rows want 16K records (docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 9); the rest reads 3 GB/s at 1M records against 1.1 GB/s at 16K with 8 readers. A shard set re-split so the table is a file of its own on the 16K dataset, the rest on a 1M-record dataset, would take the stream to about 30 s, bound by the uploads (estimated), and a cold digest to about 80 s. It is a file move, so the owner's decision, and needs no llmx change, the shards being symlinks today.

With steps 1 and 2 a start measured 101.8 s to listening against 527.6, and with 4a no digest at an update; with step 3 about 91 s (estimated), with step 6 about 45 s (estimated).

## A refusal the reference generator's test provokes prints nothing (2026-10-26, branch fix/refusal-stderr on main f61c8ca75, tests only, the coordinator's order of 2026-10-26, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** `reference-generator` checked `iq3-s --threads 2` refused without taking stderr, so every suite run printed "run_tests.py: error: iq3-s uses fixed synthetic raw blocks and one thread; only --output-dir applies" into its log, where it reads as a failure.
