## A stop ends the disk tier's model digest (2026-10-26, branch fix/disk-digest-stop on main 8632074e8, the image gate's leg 4 finding, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** `DiskTier::close` joined the thread that reads every model file's SHA-256 before the store exists, and nothing stopped that read, so a server stopped within minutes of a start with uncached digests (a new disk directory or new model files) waited for the whole hash: the image gate's Flash-Next server, on a fresh disk directory, outlived `docker stop -t 120` that way with shards 2 to 4 still being read.
- **Done:** `format::file_sha256` and `cached_file_sha256` take a stop flag checked between 64 MiB pieces, which `close` sets before the join; the starter then prints that there is no disk cache. `server-resume`'s `disk_stop_digest` grows the model file to 64 GiB of holes and requires a server stopped half a second after the start to stop within 10 s with no tier made, where it took 94 s before (on POSIX; Windows prints that it does not check). Under `--disk-cache-keep` a flush that finds the store not made yet writes nothing and does not wait out its 20 s bound (F2DEV's ruling of 20:31), held by the same case under keep. `file-reader` holds the stop itself: a stop set before the call and one set while a 2 GiB file of holes is read each end it with "was stopped before its end" and cache nothing, and the next call reads it whole and caches it.
- **Landed:** public main `d1525c6e9`, after all seven jobs in [hosted run 40426623853](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/40426623853) passed.

## A request encoding an image shows in the live items (2026-10-26, branch fix/image-encode-live on the image branch e46e72e90, the owner's ask through the coordinator, lands after the image branch by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Goal:** on production a request encoding an 11844-row image (1082 pieces, 56 s) was missing from `/v1/health`'s `requests.live.items` while `requests.now.active` said 1, so the dashboard showed nothing and the encode looked hung. A request alone at its image ran every piece in one scheduler round, and the live items refresh only at a round boundary.
- **Done:** a pending poll ends a lone request's run of pieces (`encode_piece`'s `more`), so the next boundary refreshes the items; a request at an image without rows is in phase `encode` with `image`: its index and count, its rows, the pieces run of the encode's and the milliseconds since it began (`Cache::encode_progress`, 0 of 0 in 0 ms while another image holds the encoder), the shape XDEV agreed at 18:50 with the time he asked for; `ImageSteps` carries its piece count. `image-cache`'s `encode_live` polls a lone 400-piece encode and requires the item with its pieces and its time rising (docs/SERVER.md, health).
- **Landed:** public main `ac940c059`, after [hosted run 40431875660](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/40431875660) passed at that exact commit.
- **Gotchas:** a poll costs a lone encode one round's break, about one a second from the dashboard; a job's encode stays out of the items, as jobs do.

## A lookup table read from its file reads on its own readers in every load mode (2026-10-26, branch fix/lookup-rows-reader on main 7300e94ac, the owner's decision of 2026-10-26, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** under `--load-mode auto` and `mapped` the loader gave a table read from its file a second source, a view over the payload's mapping, which `WeightRows::start` copied a row at a time on the stage's thread; only `direct` reached the table's readers that read ahead on 16 threads.
  Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's table (`per_layer_token_embd`, IQ4_NL, 90-byte rows, 26.8 GiB, 16 random rows a token) is larger than production's 16 GiB ARC, so a fresh prompt waited on its cold rows one page fault at a time: production's flags gave fresh 2048-token prompts 331-415 tok/s against 951 for the warm bench (`lw/pc5`).
  A probe of 8192 random rows of the table read 5.8-6.1K rows/s on one thread and 35-42K rows/s on 16, flat to 128 (`s8/rowprobe*`).
- **The change:** the loader gives the table its file reader in every mode, buffered in `auto` and `mapped` and direct in `direct`, and maps the payload in `auto` only for weights a host reads in place. `WeightRows`' memory source and its memory copy go, so a table has one source and one read path.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: `qwen4exp-model`'s loader checks require a table read from its file to hold no share of the payload's mapping under `auto` and `mapped`. `weight-rows`, `placement` and `qwen4exp-model` build their tables over files.
- **Checked:** the test commit fails on main ("loader: auto reads its lookup table through the mapping") and passes here, with its 3 HF cases on the CPU in every load mode. CTest `load-progress`, `weight-rows`, `placement`, `arch-qwen4exp`, `qwen4exp-graph` and `kv-selection` pass, as do the `docs` and `dead-code` components. Greedy ids equal main's on the tiny Flash fixture on the CPU in `auto`, `mapped` and `direct` (3 prompts of 12 tokens), and on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on 2x2 (int8, 24 tokens after 3930 tokens of real text).
- **Measured** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, production's serve flags, GPUs 4-7 and CPUs 4-7,12-15 at default clocks, main 7300e94ac against 965a00472 built the same way, servers main, fix, fix, main, each given four fresh 2048-token prompts at max_tokens 1, `lw/rft`): main 334-360 tok/s with a time to first token of about 5.9 s, the fix 881-898 tok/s with 2.3 s.
  Another project's model conversion held about 45 GiB of host memory and read and wrote the pool for the whole round, at times leaving the ARC at 2-3 GiB, so these figures are measured under that load; a block on a quiet host is a record that follows.

## One owner for making a file durable (2026-10-26, branch fix/file-sync-owner on main 7300e94ac, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Goal:** the disk store flushed with plain `fsync`, so on macOS a cache entry, a claim's identity write and a claimed file could sit in the drive's cache after the store reported them durable, while `FileWriter::sync` used `F_FULLFSYNC`. One owner in `core/file_sync.hpp` gives both the strongest call per platform.
- **Done:** the failing test came first: `disk-store` requires a write and a claim to flush through the owner (`core::sync_calls`), which the store's own `fsync` did not. `FileWriter::sync` and `DiskStore` now call `core::sync_handle`, `core::sync_file` and `core::sync_directory`; the store's two private variants and the writer's platform branches are gone. The macOS branch cannot run on the Linux and Windows runners, so the test holds the routing and the branch is read in review.
- **Left:** a macOS run of `disk-store` and the hosted run.
- **Gotchas:** the file is named out of the numerics fingerprint with an allow line for `file_writer.hpp`. The fingerprint still moves with this change, because editing `src/format/file_writer.hpp` and `cmake/numerics-sources.txt` changes bytes of files it covers; no file was added to it and no flush changes a byte of an entry. On Linux a claimed file and the identity file are now flushed with `fdatasync` where the store used `fsync`; the file's size is still flushed when it matters, and a directory still gets `fsync`.

## Vulkan module float controls (in progress, 2026-10-26)

- **Goal:** give each shader module one declared set of float controls and verify the words passed to module creation. Current branch `fix/vulkan-float-controls-train-20261026` is based on agreed decode stack `5eb59c0d3`, which is queued and not yet public main; NVFP4 depends on this fix. The agreed sequence is float controls, args-flush, then narrow tile, with one hosted run at the tip.
- **Train integration:** the merge conflict is resolved while retaining both `workgroup_counter` and `float_controls` members. Fourteen required-preserve table masks were added. The native metadata test failed before those masks were added; the updated build now passes, and its focused results are recorded below.
- **Done:** the native regression confirms that repeated glslang execution-mode declarations lose the earlier width in seven MXFP4 modules, including the integer tile. The 64-bit signed-zero/Inf/NaN requirement remains necessary: finite F32 inputs can round to infinity under BF16, and MXFP4's double recomputation must preserve exceptional products and sums.
- **Test-first checkpoint:** the fresh MSVC Release build succeeds. `vulkan-float-controls` fails all seven required 64-bit declarations on unchanged runtime code, while each module retains both required 32-bit declarations. The native test and generated-module hashes are in [the receipt](benchmarks/vulkan-float-controls-test-first-20261026.json). This intentional failing-test commit precedes the fix and is not merge-ready.
- **Implemented:** the kernel table declares both ordinary and preserved modules' controls. `kernel_module` checks each required device property, preserves complete embedded modules without copying, and adds missing mode widths and capabilities before creation. The four shader sources generating the seven affected modules no longer repeat mode ids. All seven compiled shader blobs remain byte-identical to the failing build; only the missing creation-time metadata is added.
- **Prior-base focused evidence:** the focused build, device runs and checks below were measured on the earlier `ab3ecbb5d` base with shared fix `e44e59efe`, not on current main `0dee47685`. The fresh MSVC and GCC Release builds checked 488 prepared module selections and 392 missing-property refusals; all 20 repaired selections from each compiler passed `spirv-val` for Vulkan 1.2. On each GPU, 244 intercepted creation calls carried the declared modes, while separate real MXFP4 execution passed 577 cases (1166678 outputs on Radeon VII and 703574 on MI50). Windows buffer, docs and dead-code checks and Linux CPU MXFP4/buffer checks passed. [The evidence](benchmarks/vulkan-float-controls-focused-20261026.json) retains source/binary hashes and the Linux wrapper failure caused by its missing validator executable; the exact Linux output was then validated locally, without rebuilding. The changed control requirement and its references were reviewed across project Markdown, with the source-owner, build, CI and user-facing descriptions updated.
- **Prior-base model and native evidence:** on the earlier `ab3ecbb5d` base with shared fix `e44e59efe`, matched archived-source Release builds passed 24 CPU and 24 Radeon VII cells against main: dense tied, dense untied, MoE and the pinned released Qwen3-0.6B MXFP4 file, each at F32/F16/BF16 with F32/F16 KV. Full-vocabulary outputs matched byte for byte for 65 batched prompt positions, 65 token-by-token history positions and 64 greedy continuation positions; reply ids and matrix-path records also matched. [The receipt](benchmarks/vulkan-float-controls-model-identity-20261026.json) pins the source archives, binaries, model files and every output. This is main/candidate identity, not independent HF or performance measurement. All 16 Radeon native Vulkan CTests passed on that prior base. These results do not establish current-main identity.
- **Train-base delta and remaining checks:** agreed base `5eb59c0d3` includes routed MoE operation and Q8 decode-kernel changes, so the old metadata and operator evidence must be rechecked for applicability. Against main `0dee47685`, paired archived builds and capture tools are complete, but no identity or timing run was performed. The older `e44e59efe` device suite and CI run `40251521604` are still running and do not qualify this train base. Final-base build, identity, device checks and matched timing remain pending; the hosted run is planned at the train tip. No old-base result is claimed as final-base qualification.
- **Prior-base review follow-up:** F2DEV approved the shared owner and requested that an unsupported-control refusal name its kernel. The helper now takes the kernel id and the missing-property checks require that exact name. Its fresh full MSVC build and native metadata test passed on the earlier base. All 20 repaired module selections remain byte-identical to the validated focused build. Numerical limits are unchanged.
- **Train-parent focused checkpoint (before NVFP4 merge):** fresh MSVC product and native builds passed on the decode-stack integration. Before the 14 table declarations, the native test refused the merged module metadata; afterwards, 522 prepared selections and 420 missing-property refusals passed across the parent fix's eight masks over three properties. The Radeon VII driver accepted all 261 selected modules, and docs/dead-code checks passed. [The replay receipt](benchmarks/vulkan-float-controls-train-replay-20261026.json) preserves the failure, logs, source hashes and binary identities. Module creation does not establish pipeline acceptance or numerical execution. This parent checkpoint does not validate the current NVFP4 merge; its paired model, device-suite, timing and hosted checks remain pending.
- **Gotchas at that checkpoint:** the missing declaration is proven, but no MXFP4 numerical failure has yet been demonstrated. Do not remove the device requirement or weaken numerical limits. NVFP4's private control repair has since been replaced by this shared owner in the private train integration above; public landing and its GPU/model qualification remain pending.

## A pipelined prompt records each stage that waits on its devices on a thread of its own (2026-10-25, branch feat/stage-threads on main 9df63df36, change 1 of the prompt-path PROPOSAL of 13:10 after the timeline of 14:44, F2DEV's review of 15:24, one owner of a stage's thread with the server after the coordinator's stop of 17:05 and my DESIGN of 17:12, in progress)

- **Why:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL at pp2048 on 2x2 runs at 720 tok/s, 2.85 s, with each card busy 1.18-1.31 s of it (main 8e84e4c4f, `lw/pprof`).
  - A timeline of the measured phase (a temporary, uncommitted print of `bench --profile`'s timestamps, `lw/tline`) splits each card's span of 2.11 s:
    - 0.43 s before submissions that wait on the peer member at the 192 tensor-group sums;
    - on stage 0, 0.35 s before the next slice's `embed`;
    - on stage 1, 0.47 s waiting for stage 0's next slice;
    - 0.03 s inside submissions.
  - `Model::prefill` recorded every stage on the calling thread, step t taking stage s of chunk t - s. A grouped stage's recording waits at each of its 48 exchanges a slice, and a stage past the first waits for its rows (`receive`), so each stage's recording held every other stage's.
  - Layer 4's cards are busy 99% of their spans, so its 1.78 s is the pipeline's fill alone.
- **What lands:**
  - `Model::run_chunks` takes a prompt's chunks through a pipelined split. A stage that waits on its devices (`stage_waits`) records on a thread of its own, while the calling thread begins, prepares and commits every stage and records the rest, as the scheduler's stages already are (`prepare_pass_stage`, `record_pass_stage`, `commit_pass_stage`).
  - Stage s takes chunk c once its chunk c - 1 is committed, once stage s + 1 has committed chunk c - 2 (whose handoff buffer chunk c reuses), and stage 0 once the last stage has committed chunk c - S (whose pass slot it reuses).
  - A round takes each stage ready at its start once, the first stage first, as a step of the software pipeline did, so a placement without such stages runs the same order as before.
  - A failure on any stage stops the others at their current chunk before the prompt's transaction is undone.
  - `prepare_stage` and `record_stage` are the one place a stage is prepared and recorded: `run_stage`, the pass API and `run_chunks` call them, and `group_stage` goes.
  - `infer::StageLanes` (`model/stage_lanes.hpp`) is the one owner of a stage's thread, for `run_chunks` and the server alike: a lane's thread steps its caller's policy while ready holds and otherwise sleeps under the caller's mutex for as long as the policy's idle allows, and destruction stops and joins every lane.
  - The scheduler's `Recorder` is now its lane's policy: ready while a pass or a pass apart is posted, its step one `record`, its idle the timed slices settled every millisecond while any is out. Its `cv` and `quit` are the lane's.
  - The scheduler loses its own thread, quit flag, wait loop and joining destructor, and keeps its pacing, shares, holds, background gaps and timed slices unchanged, so the server records exactly what it recorded before.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: `placement` runs the pipelined prompt, its decode, a continued prompt, `score`, a two-sequence pass and the failure rollback again with backends that play devices (`FailingCpu::plays_device`), over two and three stages.
  - Every stage past the first must have submitted from no thread but its own, and the prompt must give one backend's bits.
  - A failure on the last stage's thread must leave every storage at the history, the first stage being at the failing chunk at least.
  - CTest passes 70 of 70 on Windows at b6d262fee. With the lanes, `placement`, `server-passes`, `server-passes-cpu`, `server-resume` and `server-resume-cache` pass on Windows.
- **Measured** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, int8, f16 KV, `--lookup-storage file` on the 16K-record copy, GPUs 4-7 with 8-9 idle at default clocks; main 8e84e4c4f against b6d262fee, interleaved main, new, new, main; `lw/sg`):

| | Main | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| 2x2, `bench --p 2048 --n 8 --r 2`, pp2048 tok/s | 721.9, 722.0 | 932.4, 932.2 (+29.1%) |
| Layer 4, the same | 1151.6, 1151.8 | 1152.2, 1151.0 (level) |
| 2x2, `generate` after 3930 tokens of real text, prompt tok/s (one run each) | 285.2 | 752.4 |
| Layer 4, the same | 959.3 | 945.0 |

  - The greedy ids, 24 tokens after that prompt, are equal to main's on 2x2 and on layer 4.
  - The branch's first 2x2 run (932.4 tok/s) overlapped DDEV's correctness legs on the machine and is kept, flagged; its twin read 932.2. The binaries were `llmx 0.1.0+g8e84e4c4f382 numerics 1ac17687c6f1ab07` (main) and `llmx 0.1.0+gb6d262fee0e7 numerics 55643a80739d943c` (the branch).
  - On real text, 2x2's file reads of the lookup table for each slice overlap the other stage's recording too, hence more than the bench's gain.
  - Layer 4 lost nothing to the host before, so its pair is level.
  - The peer waits at the tensor-group sums, about 0.43 s a card at pp2048, are the next join (my RESULT of 14:44).
- **What reaches production:** the server already recorded each waiting stage on a thread of its own (production's 2x2 serves with two passes in flight), so served prompts take the same recording as before, now through the shared lanes. The CLI's prompt path (`generate`, `chat`, `bench`, drafting's prefill) is what gains.
- **Left:** the gate the coordinator set at 17:05, on the lanes' head:
  - CLI greedy-ids identity against main on 2x2 and on layer 4;
  - `tools/server_mix_check.py` on a split, ids equal to main's;
  - one CLI pp2048 pair and one served-prompt figure on 2x2 against main;
  - the hosted run;
  - F2DEV's review of the lanes.

## A routed integer tile of few entries takes a narrow build (2026-10-25, branch feat/routed-narrow, change 2 of the prompt-path PROPOSAL, design approved by the reviewer at 18:02, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** a routed prompt spreads its entries over the experts, and the integer tile took them in runs of 64 columns.
  Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 512-row slice routes 10 picks a row over 512 experts, about 10 entries an expert, so most of each tile's columns were empty.
- **What lands:**
  - The integer tile gets a narrow build of 16 columns, variant 2 of its id (`_narrow`, specialization constant 8, `NARROW`, in `matmul_tile_q.comp`). Each thread keeps its rows by 4 columns in the same k order, so a column gives the 64-column build's bits.
  - `routed_call` takes it, at the tall height (the short one for a type with one integer module), where a call's entries are at most `kNarrowCols` (16) times the experts it can touch, and groups the entries in runs of 16.
  - No flag: the threshold is the build's own width.
- **Tests:** `backend-vulkan`'s `check_routed_narrow` routes 200 rows over 64 experts, one expert taking 40 entries so its runs cross 16, then 600 rows repeating them, on Q4_0, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K and Q6_K in int8 and f16.
  The first call must take the narrow build and the second the 64-column one, by name where the device has timestamps, and the 200 rows' entries must be the same bits in both.
  It must fail on the base by the build's name. A device whose profile takes the float tile, the Radeon VII among them, skips it by name.
  The test also prints the time per entry of a routed Q4_K product at Flash's expert shape.
- **Gate** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, `--dtype int8`, f16 KV, ubatch 512, MI50 GPUs 4-7 at default clocks):
  - On GPU 4, `check_routed_narrow` passes (10 calls) with every routed build named `_narrow` and the bits equal.
  - The printed Q4_K occupancy: 657 ns an entry at 512 rows over 512 experts (10 an expert, narrow), against 282 at 2048 rows (40 an expert) and 265 and 184 with the same picks over 80 experts.
  - `bench --p 2048 --n 8 --r 2`, main 8e84e4c4f against the branch on 6d6f0897d, interleaved main, new, new, main:

| Placement | Main pp2048 tok/s | Narrow pp2048 tok/s | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2x2 | 722.2, 718.2 | 794.9, 791.8 | +10.2% |
| layer 4 | 1109.6, 1118.1 | 1274.1, 1270.8 | +14.2% |

  - tg8 is level within its noise (2x2 43.6 and 42.4 against 42.8 and 42.4; layer 4 44.5 and 43.3 against 44.3 and 43.1): decode runs never take the tile.
  - The main arm lacks 6d6f0897d's six vision-encoder commits, which no Flash path runs, so the landing round below builds both arms on the same base.
- **Landing timing round** against main 14010059a, both arms built from detached checkouts, the same model and flags, GPUs 4-7 on cores 4-7, interleaved main, new, new, main:

| Placement | Main pp2048 tok/s | Narrow pp2048 tok/s | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2x2 | 722.2, 721.5 | 794.9, 794.8 | +10.1% |
| layer 4 | 1139.0, 1118.9 | 1278.2, 1271.9 | +12.9% |

  - tg8 is level. Another job's builds ran on other cores during two of the 2x2 cells (721.5 and 794.9), each within 0.1% of its partner, so the block was not repeated.
- **Left:** the Radeon VII takes the float tile, which gets the same change afterwards under the same rule and test (the reviewer's ANSWER of 18:02).

## The indexer keeps each complete group's pooled key (2026-10-25, branch feat/index-pool on feat/index-scores, part 1 of the indexer DESIGN of 01:13 with C2DEV's amendments of 02:17 and 03:58, lands by fast-forward as two commits after parts 3 and 2)

- **Why:** `kv_index_pool` pooled every complete group of a history again at every pass: 2.54 ms a decode stage of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 2x2 at a 155648-token history (2026-10-24 profiles), against 0.21 at 8k.
- **What lands:**
  - A QSA layer's auxiliary blocks keep, after their token rows, one row of the index width for each complete group of the layer's compression (`LayerPlan::kv_pool`, `kv_alloc`'s `auxiliary_pools`, `BlockKVStorage::auxiliary_pool`).
  - `select_kv` pools only the groups its own rows complete and reads every earlier group's kept row, on the CPU (`pool_view`) and on Vulkan (`pool_view`, `pooled_row` in `views.glsl`), with the same arithmetic as before, so the values are the same.
  - A caller that writes a pooled layer's rows without selecting them pools them with the new `Backend::pool_kv`: qwen4exp's MTP context rows do.
  - Retracted rows complete their group again when they are written again, a fork at a whole block shares the kept rows, and host copies and disk files carry them with the block. The disk description names the pools, so files of builds without them are not adopted.
  - Nothing moves a token's position after it is written. A change that would, such as a sliding window kept in place, must drop or recompute the rows (`BlockKVStorage`'s comment).
- **Memory** (C2DEV's amendment 1): 128 bytes a position on each QSA layer beside the 512 of the raw key.
  - On Flash with f16 sides that is about 5% of a token's KV.
  - On a 2x2 member, which holds 6 QSA layers' head-split K and V (1024 B) and whole raw keys (512 B), 768 against 9216 bytes a token, 8.3%.
  - So production's 2x2 pool of 655616 tokens becomes about 605200 where KV is what fills the cards.
  - The fit at production's flags on 2x2 in the gate: 926400 KV tokens with the three parts against 1003584 on main 07facf1b6 (-7.7%), and 47744 against 51712 for the 16 state checkpoints.
- **Tests:** `kv-selection` holds the rows to being kept on whatever backend it is given: `pool_kv` over rows completing group 2 writes that row alone, and a selection after group 0's kept row is replaced by one the query favours takes group 0, where pooling it again from its raw keys would take group 5.
  `kv-selection` and `sparse-attention` pool the rows they write before the rows they select, as the passes would; `arch-qwen4exp`, `qwen4exp-mtp` (its MTP block's QSA layer, a verify retracted inside a group and a prompt in slices against a fresh sequence, bit for bit) and `qwen4exp-graph` pass unchanged on the CPU.
  `llmx-qwen4exp-model-test` reads each HF case's prompt in consecutive passes in flight over the two-CPU split (C2DEV's amendment of 03:58), so the QSA layer on the second stage pools a group two slices share in the later pass: the last slice's rows and the decode step must be the bits of the same slices run one after another, and within the HF bound of the sliced and follow-up logits.
- **Device checks:** `vulkan-index`, `kv-selection --device vulkan:0`, `sparse-attention --device vulkan:0`, `qwen4exp-mtp --device vulkan:0` and `backend-vulkan` pass on the Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver 26.5.2 at this head, and on an MI50 under RADV at the gate's build.
- **Gate** (the three parts together; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, int8, f16 KV, `--lookup-storage file`, GPUs 4-9 at default clocks; main 07facf1b6 against the three parts built at b79bad34e, whose product code is this head's before the rebase on main; `lw/idx` on the test machine):
  - Greedy ids, 24 tokens after real-text prompts of 7745, 64075 and 152425 tokens on 2x2 and on the six-card layer split: equal to main's in all six cells. The 64075-token prompt ends at once on both builds, and the six-card 152425 after 5 tokens. The scores keep their bits by the tests above, so the selections and the logits do too, and no long-context check of changed numerics is due.
  - Decode after a depth on 2x2, tg32 in tok/s, the builds interleaved main, new, new, main:

| Depth | Main | Three parts |
|---|---|---|
| 8192 | 33.67, 33.62 | 33.80, 34.25 |
| 65536 | 26.43, 25.70 | 32.83, 32.06 |
| 155648 | 20.67, 20.58 | 31.26, 31.07 |

  - Level at 8192, +24% at 65536 and +51% at 155648. The three parts' bench reads its ids over the whole vocabulary (bench-ids) and main's below 1000, so the new arm reads more of the table from the file; the gain is if anything understated.
  - The profile at 155648, a decode token on the first device: `kv_index_select` 4.43 ms against `kv_index_select_wide` 0.51, `kv_index_scores` 2.56 against `kv_index_scores_tile` 0.66, `kv_index_pool` 2.54 against 0.018; device time 23.4 against 15.3 ms a token.
  - The generate runs' prompt rates differ by more than the indexer, since main there predates phase 4 and each main run warmed the ARC for the new one, so they are not quoted as its gain.
- **Landing timing round** against main 8e84e4c4f (9df63df36's product code), 2x2, `bench --p 32 --n 64 --r 2 --depth D`, the 16K-record copy, GPUs 4-7, interleaved main, new, new, main:

## The indexer scores a tile of groups a workgroup (2026-10-25, branch feat/index-scores on feat/index-select, part 2 of the indexer DESIGN of 01:13 with C2DEV's amendments of 02:17 and 03:58, lands by fast-forward as two commits after part 3)

- **Why:** `kv_index_scores` took a workgroup per (row, group), four heads of a 256-lane tree each with eight barrier steps: 2.56 ms a decode stage of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 2x2 at a 155648-token history (2026-10-24 profiles).
- **What lands:** `kv_index_scores_tile` (`score_rows`) takes 8 groups a workgroup, one to each 32-lane group of its subgroups (two to a 64-lane subgroup, whose shuffles stay in their half).
  Each (group, head) dot keeps the old kernel's sum: lane l holds slots l + 32c, the tree's steps k = 128, 64 and 32 add within the lane and k = 16 to 1 across lanes by shuffle, each add the same pair in the same order, the products and adds `precise` so nothing contracts where shared memory used to prevent it; the slots past the head's width are +0.0 and the step k = 128 adds them, as the 256-slot tree does.
  `kv_index_scores` is removed with its kernel id (C2DEV's amendment of 03:58): the test's host reference now holds its sum.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on part 3's head: `vulkan-index` computes the 256-slot tree on the host in F32 in the old kernel's order, built with `-ffp-contract=off` as backend-group is, and holds every score bit for bit, subnormal cases only on a device that keeps F32 subnormals; it also requires the scoring to dispatch `kv_index_scores_tile` with no fused float multiply-add in its ISA, which the old kernel's dispatch fails.
  A row of 524296 groups in 65537 tiles meets the reference too (F2DEV's request of 11:35): past 65535 workgroups the scoring takes its tiles in more than one dispatch, which a device whose width limit is 65535 does; RADV and the AMD proprietary driver both report 2^32 - 1, so on the MI50 and the Radeon VII it is one dispatch.
  At the first commit the old kernel met the reference on all 360 scorings and 942660 scores on the Radeon VII, subnormal ones included, so the reference is that kernel's sum; the tiled kernel meets it on the Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver 26.5.2 and on the MI50 under RADV, with 0 fused float multiply-adds in its ISA on both.
- **Measured** (device time a call over one row of Flash's indexer, 4 heads 128 wide, old kernel against tiled):

| Groups | MI50 old | MI50 tiled | Radeon VII tiled |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1025 | 0.046 ms | 0.033 ms | 0.023 ms |
| 4096 | 0.103 ms | 0.041 ms | 0.028 ms |
| 16384 | 0.344 ms | 0.094 ms | 0.059 ms |
| 38912 | 0.794 ms | 0.185 ms | 0.119 ms |

  4.3 times less on the MI50 at 155648 tokens; the old kernel was not timed on the Radeon VII, since the first commit's run stops at the dispatch check.
  A first form of a tile of 16 groups a workgroup, its dots in shared memory, was slower than the old kernel (1.16 ms at 38912 groups), and one of a thread a dot with its partials indexed at run time slower still (1.64 ms); both kept the bits.
- **A hand check:** as part 3's, `vulkan-index` runs by hand on the MI50 and the Radeon VII.
- **Gate and landing:** as part 3's, the gate run on the three parts together and recorded in part 1's block, landing by fast-forward with them.

## The indexer's selection over many workgroups (2026-10-25, branch feat/index-select on main 14010059a, part 3 of the indexer DESIGN of 01:13 with C2DEV's amendments of 02:17 and 03:58, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** at a 155648-token history a decode stage of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 2x2 spent 4.43 ms a token in `kv_index_select`, one workgroup a row running eight radix passes and a chronological scan over 38912 groups, of 8.4 ms that the indexer grows from 8k (2026-10-24 profiles, `castagna/run/out2`, `out3`).
- **What lands:** from the device profile's `select_wide_from` groups (4096 by default, measured on the MI50; 5120 on the Radeon VII) `select_rows` takes `kv_index_select_wide`, five dispatches over slices of 1024 groups: three histograms of 11, 11 and 10 bits of the raw score bits, each workgroup taking the digits found before it from the histograms before, a count of each slice's greater and equal scores, and an emission placing each slice after the slices before it.
  The ids are the one-workgroup selection's by construction: the same kth-largest bits and rank left within them, equal bits to the earlier group, raw-bit order (NaN above +inf, -0 above every positive score), and no score read past a row's visible groups.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: `vulkan-index` gives both selections chosen scores and holds them to the contract's selection, and holds the wide one to five dispatches, which main's single dispatch fails.
  Scores of five levels, NaN of both signs, +inf, -0, +0, the smallest subnormal and 1, or spread; equal top scores either side of a slice boundary; 1023-1025, 2047-2049, 5000 and 38912 groups; budgets taking 512, 4 and all groups; compressions 4 and 1; earlier rows seeing fewer groups, their stale scores left large: 144 selections, 2001264 ids equal.
- **Measured** (MI50, GPU 9, a diagnostics backend's device time a call over one row, 512 groups taken):

| Groups | One workgroup | Wide (5 dispatches) |
|---|---|---|
| 1025 | 0.068 ms | 0.162 ms |
| 2048 | 0.093 ms | 0.166 ms |
| 4096 | 0.155 ms | 0.161 ms |
| 8192 | 0.322 ms | 0.158 ms |
| 16384 | 0.605 ms | 0.159 ms |
| 38912 | 1.385 ms | 0.149 ms |

  The wide selection is a floor of five dispatches, about 30 us each with the digits taken again in each workgroup, so the crossover is near 4096 groups (16384 tokens at Flash's compression of 4); it takes 9.3 times less at 155648 tokens.
  On the Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver 26.5.2 one workgroup takes 0.087 ms at 4096 groups against the wide selection's 0.104, and 0.112 against 0.103 at 5120, so its profile switches at 5120 (C2DEV's amendment 1); at 38912 groups 0.695 against 0.103.
- **A hand check:** `vulkan-index` needs a Vulkan device and no hosted runner has one, so it runs by hand on the MI50 and the Radeon VII; on a device that times no dispatches it skips the dispatch count and the times.
- **Gate and landing:** the gate ran on the three parts together and is recorded in part 1's block, with the clean pair at 2048 against main (+1.6% tg64, +1.2% pp32); the three parts land by fast-forward, part 3 first.

## A dispatch reads only its own slot's arguments (2026-10-26, branch fix/vulkan-args-flush on the float controls c6182eb70 over the decode stack 5eb59c0d3, F2DEV's finding of 2026-10-25 23:40 and DECISION of 23:50, the coordinator's DECISION of 23:43, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **The bug:** `args()` writes a call's table into the open ring slot's arena, which the slot resets when it reopens after waiting for its own submission alone. Attention's merge, pool_view's and score_rows' loops and select_rows' five wide stages bound one table in several dispatches, so a chunk flush between two of them left the later dispatch in the next slot reading the earlier slot's arena, which the host could overwrite once it had gone round the ring while that dispatch was unfinished.
- **The fix:** each of those dispatches takes its own copy of its table, and the comment at `args()` states that a dispatch reads only its own slot's arena.
- **Test:** `vulkan-lifetime` replaces the push of descriptor sets, forces the flush after a sync with 0 to 15 single adds before attention on a decode row whose 600-token history splits and before select_rows' wide stages, and requires no binding of another slot's arena, that some count put the op's dispatches in different slots, and each output the bits of the run without adds. On the Radeon VII it fails on the test commit alone (attention's merge one foreign binding, the wide stages ten) and passes with the fix, every output the bits of the run without adds.
- **Reach:** the copies change no arithmetic and no kernel; the merge's table is copied once a layer when a history splits, a few hundred bytes. The index selection's loops past the workgroup limit are fixed alike but not reached by a test.
- **Gates (on the Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver, Windows):** CTest 90 of 90 on the fix at this base, vulkan-lifetime failing on the test commit and passing on the fix; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 greedy, a 993-token wikitext prompt and 64 tokens, auto and int8, the same output and ids on main ab3ecbb5d and the fix at that base but for the load timing line; docs and dead-code. Owed as a landing condition: the Vulkan CTests on an MI50 under RADV, armed on this code, and the hosted run.

## The trimmed-donor check reads the donors on the scheduler's thread (2026-10-25, branch fix/trims-donor-timing on main 14010059a, tests only, the coordinator's work order on F2DEV's ANSWER of 19:10)

- **Goal:** `server-resume`'s `trims_finished_donor` failed twice on the hosted Windows job (runs 40205143633 and 40213243850) with "the reply's reasoning left out: the donor holds 5 blocks, against 4", and never on a desktop (10 of 10 at main and at image step 4).
- **The cause, the test's timing and not the scheduler:**
  - The check served one request at a time, so the job its next turn starts waits while `other` decodes its 1900 tokens.
  - Once `other` ends, its history takes the one donor's place, so the trimmed donor goes and the job reads from row 0. In passing runs it starts as "rows 0 to 640", as in the failing ones.
  - The test's thread gave the ids and then polled the donors every millisecond, so it had to run inside `other`'s decode, about 0.1 to 0.2 s at 9000 to 17000 tokens a second.
  - The log of 40213243850 shows the job starting only after `other` ended, as the round's admission requires (`Cache::follow_up` starts a job only while `active.size() < max_seqs_` and nothing waits). So no job ran beside the seat holder.
  - The eviction line in that log ("a history of 256 tokens left the devices with no copy: 64.0 MiB ...") is a message of an earlier case that passed. It is printed in passing runs too.
  - A 500 ms sleep of the test's thread after submitting `other` gives the hosted failure, word for word, on a desktop.
- **The fix:** the next turn's ids are given at `other`'s first retiring pass and the donors read at each later one, on the scheduler's thread (`Scheduler::on_retire`). So both fall while `other` holds the seat, however the test's thread is scheduled.
  The expectations are unchanged: four, seven, two and seven blocks.
- **Checks:** at the fix, `llmx-server-resume-test cpu-cache` passes on a desktop, and passes again with the same 500 ms sleep of the test's thread.
- **Left:** the hosted run.

## Weights cannot be taken from a temporary model (2026-10-25, branch fix/gguf-weights-temporary on main 6d6f0897d, from the routed-step test fault F2DEV closed at 15:15, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **The hazard:** `infer::gguf_weights` returns views into the `gguf::GGUFModel` it reads, so weights taken from a temporary model point at freed memory once the statement ends; a CPU backend adopts host memory in place, so a model built on them reads that memory. An unlanded routed-step test did this on `tiny_qwen_moe(2, 128)` and saw logits change from run to run and a crash, which a model kept alive never showed (0 of 20 runs differing at 1 and 16 threads in f32, f16 and bf16, by the CLI and in-process).
- **The fix:** an overload for a const rvalue model is deleted beside `gguf_weights` in `src/model/arch/registry.hpp`, and beside `vision_weights`, whose views point into an mmproj file the same way, so a call on a temporary, const or not, does not compile; the two test sites the compiler named, `heterogeneous_saved_fits` in `tests/placement.cpp`, which read only sizes, and the tied-head read in `tests/model_validation.cpp`, whose temporary outlived its call, now name their models.
- **Test:** none fails, since the compiler refuses the call; no product path took weights from a temporary.
- **Gates:** on main 6d6f0897d, built with CMake (Release, Vulkan on) and `build.bat`; CTest passes on the CPU, 71 of 71, with the Vulkan tests left out since nothing they reach changed; docs and dead-code pass; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on the CPU, `logits --last 16` batched and `--per-token` and `generate --temp 0 -n 64` in f16, int8 and f32, byte-identical to main built the same way. On main 9df63df36, before the rebase moved only the patch's context, the whole CPU suite passed, all 43 components. The hosted run to come.

## Sizes, token counts and durations with unit suffixes (2026-10-25, branch feat/size-suffixes on main 14010059a, the owner's decisions of 2026-10-25, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Goal:** `serve` takes sizes as `4g` or `100gib` and token counts as `256k`, so a command line need not carry `107374182400` or `262144`.
- **Done:** one reader, `scaled_number` in `src/cli/main.cpp`, behind `bytes_arg` (`--host-cache-bytes`, `--disk-cache-bytes`, `--disk-cache-floor`), `count_arg` (`-n`, both `--ctx-size`, `--kv-tokens`, `--ubatch`, `--moe-stream-from`, `--last`, bench `--p`, `--n`, `--depth`) and `seconds_arg` (`--disk-cache-max-age`, unchanged in behaviour).
  Sizes are binary and case-insensitive (b, k/kb/kib, m/mb/mib, g/gb/gib, t/tb/tib); counts take k (1024) and m (1048576); fractions are exact, need a suffix and must come out whole.
  `--host-cache-bytes` no longer truncates silently past `size_t`, and an overflowing duration says it is too large.
  Tests: `cli-output` (`number_readers`) and `tests/cli.py`; docs: help page, USAGE, DISK-TIER, OPERATING, `docs/src/cli-main.md`.
- **Left:** the hosted run at the landing head.
- **Gotchas:** the flag names keep `-bytes`; `--draft-max`, `--chunks`, `--top`, `--size`, `--r` and `--seqs` stay plain numbers since they are not counts of tokens; durations stay lowercase because `M` and `m` would differ.

## Layer-split shares by stage time, parked as fine-tuning (2026-10-25, no branch, a record only)

- **What was proposed:** with a four-device layer split of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL at equal shares (12 layers a stage, `--dtype int8`, ubatch 512, MI50s at default clocks), a pp2048 profile put stage 0 at 1015.9 ms of kernel time against 954.2, 866.5 and 879.1 ms on the others. Shares of 11,12,13,12 would have moved the bottleneck to about 954 ms, about -6% on prefill against a ceiling of -8.6% at perfect balance.
- **Why it is parked:** rearranging layers trims the slowest stage's share of the same work; it is not a speed improvement, and the owner parked it. The discriminating run (devices permuted, the 11,12,13,12 split timed) was not made.
- **What the profile says instead** (the same run, kernel timestamps summed per device):
  - Each stage's span is 85 to 99% kernel time; the rest is idle waiting for the previous stage's handoff (6.4, 94.6, 174.4 and 138.0 ms). No submission waits on a peer, no kernel polls, and gaps inside submissions total 3 ms a stage, so host recording does not limit a layer-split prefill.
  - The whole difference between the stages is in the routed tiles: the Q4_K gate and up products take 294.0, 242.7, 190.8 and 197.6 ms by stage and the Q5 down products 140.9, 144.4, 104.6 and 100.8 ms, on the same shapes and types, while every other kernel is level across stages within a few ms. That points at how full the tiles run, which depends on how a layer spreads its entries over the experts; the routed integer tile's narrow build (branch feat/routed-narrow) is aimed at that occupancy.
  - The wall time of the profiled pp2048, 1782 ms, is the bottleneck stage's 1016 ms of kernels and about 660 ms of pipeline fill and drain, three slices of the other stages after the last chunk leaves the first: 4 chunks over 4 stages.

## Fused routed step (2026-10-25, branch feat/moe-step on feat/q8-one-col, item B1b of item B's decode stack, plan approved by the reviewer with amendments, in review)

- **Goal:** a decode pass's routed layer ran 6 to 12 dispatches (Qwen3-30B-A3B Q8_0 6; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M 11; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL 11 and a copy), each at least the 3.6 us dispatch floor on the Radeon VII; item B fuses whole sublayers into the fewest dispatches the data allow, each fused kernel giving exactly the unfused kernels' bits.
- **The op:** `Backend::moe_step` (`MoeStep`, `MoeShared`) is a routed layer's feed-forward block; its base runs today's calls in today's order, so the CPU and any device without a fused build compute what they computed, and `blocks::moe_step` is its one caller, from qwen3 (qwen3moe), qwen35 (qwen35moe) and qwen4exp.
  `blocks::routed_experts`, `swiglu`'s row gate and `join`'s `add` are gone with their callers; qwen4exp's `clear_rows` became `Backend::repeat_row`, which the base op and the tensor-group injection share.
  The arena changed: the routed and the shared expert's rows now live at once, the shared after the routed in the g, u and act slots, so qwen4exp's feed-forward slots are `k * ff + ff_sh` floats a row where they were the wider of the two, and qwen35's the wider of a dense layer's and `k * ff + ff_sh`; arch-qwen35's slot expectation follows, and the fit and exact-arena tests (arch-qwen35-fit, model-validation) pass unchanged since they derive their figures from the plan's slots.
- **The fused path (`vulkan_moe.hpp`, `docs/src/backends-vulkan.md`):** four dispatches for every fused combination: D1 the router's and row gate's F32 rows with routing by the last workgroup, D2 the routed and shared gate and up rows as roles of one dispatch, D2b the SiLU products and the shared expert's sigmoid gate with one twin, D3 the routed down rows joined in slot order and the shared down rows added after, `(y + s) + d`.
  It takes decode rows alone (up to 64, each routed call on the per-entry row kernels), f16 or int8 on an integer-dot profile, and the combinations of the routed layers of Flash UD-Q4_K_XL (Q4_K, Q5_1, Q8_0 shared), 35B-A3B Q4_K_M (Q4_K, Q6_K, Q4_K and Q6_K shared) and 30B-A3B Q8_0 (D2 and D2b are then the routed row kernel and `silu_mul` themselves), in the builds `row_plan` and A1's `one_column_build` give the unfused calls; everything else takes the base.
  The fused kernels include the bodies of B1a's row kernels in functions of their own and the functions the standalone kernels now call: `moe_route.glsl` (the routing, a row per quarter of 64 lanes), `moe_combine.glsl`, `silu_mul.glsl` and `sigmoid_mul.glsl`.
- **Float modes:** D2 and D3 take the `_preserve` builds of the row families they embed, as those kernels do on a preserving device; D1 and D2b stay ordinary like the F32 row kernel, `moe_route`, `silu_mul` and `sigmoid_mul`.
  The combine is the one fold across modes: the ordinary `moe_combine` compiled to v_mul for slot 0 and unfused v_mad for the rest on the AMD driver, which a preserving module cannot emit, so `moe_combine.glsl` writes it out (slot 0's product is the sum, each later product rounded, then added) and `moe_combine` gains a `_preserve` module, a separable piece (`moe_combine.glsl`, the `moe_combine_preserve` entry and its table entry).
  On normal inputs its preserving module gives the ordinary module's bits (vulkan-quantization, 46800 outputs); against main it changes only subnormal intermediates on a preserving device, which it now keeps as the CPU does.
- **The counter:** the plan's counter on the Vulkan memory model was dropped: glslang 16.4 emits no NonPrivatePointer or MakePointer operands under that model, for `nonprivate` or `queuefamilycoherent` buffers and shared variables alike, so its barriers did not order the shared flag that tells a workgroup it is last, and subgroups 1 to 3 of the last workgroup intermittently exited without routing; backend-vulkan's `check_moe_step` caught it at Flash's widths, 2 and 3 rows.
  D1 uses the GLSL450 model: coherent buffers, `memoryBarrierBuffer`, a device-scope atomic and `barrier()`, which the SPIR-V shows as Coherent decorations, a Device-scope AcquireRelease|UniformMemory barrier and a device-scope atomic; the last workgroup resets the counter, which is zero between calls.
  The named need is what the routing needs: subgroups of 32 or 64 lanes (`missing_counter_need`), refused by name in vulkan-buffer, a device without it taking the base.
- **Tests** (descriptions in AGENTS.md, Tests): backend-vulkan holds the dispatch count, every output of the op against its base op bit for bit (2370156 values over the three combinations at their files' widths and at small widths with 60 to 1000 experts, f16 and int8, with zero, 1000-scaled, 1e-30, 1e-20 and NaN rows and -0 residuals), every token at 1 to 64 tokens and over 200 random steps against the token alone (51011 columns), and 1125 row-class pairs.
  Under `--isa` every fused build's float multiplies and adds, less those of its build without the row products (`ROLES`, constant 14, built by a diagnostic backend), are whole copies of its component one-column builds': 22 of 22 builds on the Radeon VII.
  D1's component is `matmul_row_f32_only`, the row kernel built for the F32 family alone, which only a diagnostic backend makes, and D1 compiles its row body for that family alone too.
  Both carried the Q8_0 family's code before, which D1 never runs: `moe_build` fuses only an F32 router and row gate. On an MI50 under RADV the same `moe_step_route_s1` build failed the screen by 7 multiplies and 7 multiply-adds.
  RADV had unrolled that branch's per-column scale over 8 columns in D1 and kept one column-picking block in `matmul_row_f32`, while the F32 path matched block for block. The reviewer's decision of 2026-10-25 22:55 removed the code rather than allowing for it.
  backend-group holds the base op to the calls written out (`tests/moe_step.hpp`); arch-qwen35 and qwen4exp-mtp count one step a pass per routed layer of qwen35moe, qwen3moe and Flash models with no routed op outside it; vulkan-quantization holds the combine's preserving module to the ordinary one and its subnormal sums to the CPU's (kept) and to 0 (the ordinary module); vulkan-buffer holds the counter's need.
  `tests/dead_code.py`'s shader rule now counts a define tested in a shared include as set where another source including it sets it, and a default as overridden by a shader that defines it before including the file, so the fused kernels inherit the row kernels' family tests and hooks without listed findings.
- **Per-call device time, Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver 26.5.2, default clocks, integer dot forced through the test hook), synthetic weights at each file's routed shapes, three rounds of 100 calls each arm per cell, medians, the empty-dispatch floor 3.56 to 3.78 us:**
  Every cell's outputs equal between the arms; the figures sum the dispatches' device times, so the gaps between dispatches, which the fused step also saves, are not in them.
  The machine ran its user's processes throughout (system CPU up to 79 percent, a game client and a browser), recorded beside each round.

  | 30B-A3B Q8_0 | int8 | 2 | 201.9 | 198.2 | -1.9% |
  | 30B-A3B Q8_0 | int8 | 4 | 359.3 | 354.2 | -1.4% |
  | 30B-A3B Q8_0 | int8 | 8 | 679.7 | 685.5 | +0.9% |

  Gains at 1 token are 21 to 36 percent on Flash and 35B-A3B and 2 to 3 percent on 30B-A3B, whose step D2 leaves unfused; three cells at 8 tokens lose 0.9 to 1.9 percent with overlapping ranges.
  Two causes show in the kernels' times: D2 computes the shared expert a token at a time in the one-column build, where the unfused grouped call reads its weights once for all tokens in a wide build, and D1's last workgroup routes 8 rows in two rounds where the unfused routing takes 8 workgroups.
- **B2:** B2, the hyper-connection mix's up projection taking the SiLU's dispatch, was dropped: on an MI50 its four-dispatch form lost 3.2 to 19.7 us a mix at 1, 2, 4 and 8 tokens in f16 and int8 (+5 to +23 percent), against the 5.7 to 7.2 us the SiLU dispatch costs; the activation-load macros B1a added for it (`XQ2_AT` and the rest) are plain array reads again, every kernel module's SPIR-V unchanged.
- **Modules against the B2 tree:** the Radeon VII legs run on the B2 tree count for this top because every embedded module the two builds share is the same: a fresh Release Vulkan build of B2's head 143cb7087 and one of this branch's change commit 244ade235 give 296 modules with equal SHA-256, the four `stream_up_q8` builds (plain, `_i8`, `_preserve`, `_i8_preserve`) exist only in B2, and none exists only here or differs; B2's own build directory `build-vk5`, last built from a working tree before that head, also holds four stale `stream_mix_up` modules of the dropped three-dispatch kernel.
- **Left:** it is the top of the decode stack (part one, A1, B1b) and lands with it by the reviewer's 16:34 decision, measured by the stack's gate, which is its own; measured follow-ups, each held to these figures: the shared expert's rows in a wide build for several tokens, the routing over several workgroups at many rows, and the paired epilogue, whose gain is at most D2b's 7.5 to 9 us a call.

## One-column Q8_0 decode builds by row width, rows and activations (2026-10-25, branch feat/q8-one-col on feat/elementwise-preserve, item A1 of item B's decode stack after probe A0, approved by the reviewer, in progress)

- **Goal:** a one-column call of the Q8_0 decode kernel (`matmul_vec_q8.comp`, the 16-bit and 8-bit builds alike) takes the build its shape and activations favour, by one rule whose numbers sit in the device profile, every column's bits unchanged.
- **The change:** the one-column chunk has three builds: variant 1 of two rows and one step (`matmul_vec_q8_1col`, `matmul_vec_q8_i8_1col`, the build it had), variant 7 of one row and four steps loaded ahead (`..._1col_1row`) and variant 8 of two rows and two steps (`..._1col_2step`), in `vulkan_kernels.hpp`. `one_column_build` (`vulkan_matmul.hpp`) gives rows narrower than the profile's `q8_decode_narrow_below` variant 1; wider rows take variant 7 below the knee of their activations' width, counted in the output rows a dispatch computes, its projections' rows together and, routed, times its entries, and from it variant 8 over 8-bit activations and variant 1 over 16-bit ones. The reduction forms come from the profile as before.
  `q8_decode_narrow_below` is 1024 on both profiles; the 8-bit knee `q8_decode_two_rows_from` is 2560 on the Radeon VII (and by default) and 4096 on the MI50 under RADV; the 16-bit knee `q8_decode_one_row_below_16bit` is 1280 on the Radeon VII, 1024 on the MI50 and 1024 by default, provisionally until the f16 sweep (gitea probe/a0-f16) runs on an MI50.
  Cost: `kVariants` goes from 7 to 9, two more empty pipeline slots for every kernel, since pipelines are built on first dispatch; the Q8_0 decode kernels compile up to three one-column pipelines a dtype where the base compiled one, each only once a call takes it.
- **The 8-bit rule, from probe A0's one-column int8 calls on both cards** (each build's column bits equal to the default's in every cell):
  - Narrow rows (320 and 640 wide) lose with the one-row build on both cards, 11 to 39 percent on the Radeon VII and 6 to 20 percent on the MI50, and with two rows of two steps on the Radeon VII, 3 to 14 percent; the old two rows and one step is the fastest of the three there on the Radeon VII and within 3.4 percent of the fastest on the MI50 (two rows and two steps, 9.94 against 10.28 us at 320x10240).
  - Wider rows: the one-row build gains 13 to 31 percent below 2560 output rows on the Radeon VII and 2 to 22 percent below 4096 on the MI50, where the half-block order makes it the same build as one row and one step.
  - The knee on the MI50: the one-row build and two rows of two steps are within 1.7 percent everywhere above 3072 rows, the one-row build ahead on rows 2560 wide and the other on rows 4096 wide and wider. Over the 22 wider shapes 4096 gives the smallest total time (1133.8 against 1135.9 us at 16384) and the smallest worst loss against the fastest of the three, 1.1 percent at 2560x5120, against 1.7 percent at 17408x5120 with a knee of 16384; the mean loss is 0.15 percent at both.
  - No simpler rule holds every measured shape within 1 percent of the fastest of the three on both cards: without the narrow build the narrow rows lose 3 to 14 percent on both cards; without two rows of two steps, the old build above the knee, the Radeon VII loses up to 5.6 percent on 15 shapes; without the one-row build the small products lose 13 to 23 percent; and without a knee, the one-row build on every wider shape, the Radeon VII loses up to 16 percent at the head. The rule as built leaves the MI50 3.4 percent behind the fastest at 320x10240, 1.2 percent at 320x2560 and 1.1 percent at 2560x5120, and the Radeon VII at most 0.8 percent (6144x2560).
- **The 16-bit rule.** The 16-bit twin is twice the 8-bit one's bytes, and A0 swept int8 alone, so the MI50 round r29 found the one-row build 5 to 17 percent slower in f16 at 1280 to 3072 rows (6144x1280 17.81 against 15.19 us, 2560x3072 16.56 against 14.78, 3072x2560 15.30 against 14.57) while 3 to 13 percent faster up to 640 rows (2560x256, 2560x320, 2560x512, 2560x640, 10240x320). The extended A0 probe on the Radeon VII gives the same in f16: the one-row build 4 to 25 percent faster up to 1024 rows and slower from 1280 on most shapes 2560 to 6144 wide, two rows of two steps up to 9 percent faster on rows 4096 wide and wider but up to 6 percent slower on rows 2560 wide (us, the f16 cells; every build's bytes equal the default's in all 1220 cells of both dtypes):

## Preserving elementwise modules and a twin writer of multiplies and adds (2026-10-25, branch feat/elementwise-preserve on refactor/row-bodies, part one of item B's decode stack, the writer's third form approved by the reviewer at 16:17)

- **Goal:** item B fuses the steps between preserving row products into those products' kernels, so those steps must already compute in the products' float mode; and a twin must be one function of its floats in every module, since a twin dropped from the twin table is requantized by `quantize_x`.
- **The change:** `silu_scaled`, `mix_streams` and `inject_streams` gain preserving builds (`shaders/float_controls.glsl`), selected as the Q8 row consumers' are, where the device reports both preservation properties.
  `xquant.glsl` takes the twin's scale and reciprocal from correctly rounded multiplies and adds alone (`xq_div`, `xq_rdiv`), in place of a float division, whose lowering differs between modules on the AMD proprietary driver and is wrong for huge divisors in RADV's preserving modules, and of an fma, which RADV does not fuse (docs/VULKAN.md, Kernel notes).
- **Done:** the test commit (`vulkan-quantization`: subnormals kept where preserving and flushed otherwise, each module against a double reference, every twin word against the host's run of the writer's arithmetic, the two producers in the activation-range check) fails on d87cf26fa at the twin check and passes with the change on the Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver 26.5.2) and on an MI50 (Mesa 25.0.7, RADV), where the writer's fma form failed on one block's scale because RADV does not fuse an fma.
  - Quotients: 41943040 on the host in the CTest `twin-quotients`, which the hosted jobs run (the reviewer's 14:54 condition 1), every significand at both levels for the scale, within one unit of the IEEE quotient, and at 32767, 127 and 1 for the reciprocal, within two.
  - Cost on the Radeon VII, per call against d87cf26fa, three interleaved runs: the twin writers 0 to 5 percent slower at 1 to 4 rows and up to 16 percent at 16 rows of 10240 with the 8-bit twin, `quantize_x`'s lane writer 25 to 33 percent at 512 rows and its word writer 1 to 16 percent; `silu_scaled`, `mix_streams` and `inject_streams` at 512 rows of Flash's 4 x 2560 30, 11 and 15 percent, the IEEE division of their preserving modules among it. The writer's three earlier forms, long division, an fma remainder and integer remainders, cost more or relied on a fused fma (docs/VULKAN.md, Kernel notes).
  - Twins: 147456 of 147456 words equal to the host's run of the writer's arithmetic on each card, through `quantize_x` and through the twin `silu_scaled` keeps, in both modules; the activation-range check fails 0 on both cards, where the first writer failed 115 with the preserving `silu_mul` on RADV.
  - Double reference, mean error in units in the last place of each result, or of a sum's mean term magnitude, preserving against ordinary: Radeon VII `silu_scaled` 0.407 against 0.501, `inject_streams` 0.478 against 0.504, `mix_streams` 0.373 against 0.371; MI50 0.501 and 0.501, 0.485 and 0.485, 0.345 and 0.384, RADV lowering a normal division alike in both modules.
  - Subnormals: 160 results kept as the CPU keeps them on the preserving backend and 160 flushed on the ordinary one, on both cards.
  - RADV's envelope (docs/PRECISION.md, section 3): wrong preserving quotients only for divisors past 6e30, true values below 1e-29, inside the reviewer's 1e-28 bound.
- **Left:** it lands with the decode stack (part one, A1, B1b) by the reviewer's 16:34 decision, and the stack top's gate measures it: HF error and headroom per family on both cards, the 16k raw and chat-template checks against file-exact HF, one interleaved timing round against main on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 2x2 and layer 4 and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, `--isa` on both cards and the hosted run. Its checkpoint figures above are not that gate.
- **Gotchas:** a twin check needs peaks the producer keeps in the ordinary range, so `silu_scaled`'s twin is checked on its own blocks; F32 rows keep the ordinary row module, so a subnormal case of a consumer reading F32 rows says nothing about preservation.

## Row kernel bodies as includes (2026-10-25, branch refactor/row-bodies on refactor/vulkan-split 4ab05bffe, item B1a, approved by the reviewer, no behaviour change)

- **Goal:** item B fuses decode sublayers into fewer dispatches, and a fused kernel must compute each row with the unfused kernel's bits; the row kernels' bodies become text both include, so the row arithmetic has one owner (B1b's routed step builds on it).
- **The change:** `matmul_row.comp` keeps its `main`, a workgroup's projection, rows, columns and stores, and includes `matmul_row.glsl` (its bindings, push and specialization constants and per-family helpers), `matmul_row_one.glsl` (the one-row builds' body, every family) and `matmul_row_two.glsl` (the Q4 and K-quant families' two-row body) where their text stood.
  `matmul_vec_q8.comp` keeps its bindings, `main` and stores and includes `matmul_vec_q8.glsl` (its helpers) and `matmul_vec_q8_one.glsl` (its body: both layouts, the TREE and subgroup reductions).
  Each body hands a sum to a store macro its kernel defines (`ROW_STORE`, `ROW_STORE2`, `VEC_STORE`, `VEC_TREE_STORE`), so stores stay with the callers, and `matmul_row.glsl` takes `LLMX_ROW_PROJ`, `LLMX_ROW_Y` and `LLMX_ROW_PUSH`, which B1b's fused kernels set.
  The bodies are included text rather than GLSL functions, so the kernels' preprocessed tokens are those they had: a function returning its sums would move the stores and change the code.
- **Proof, on the Radeon VII (AMD proprietary driver, default clocks), both arms built the same way in fresh MSVC Release directories from detached worktrees at 6807750e6 and at the change:**
  - All 266 generated kernel modules are byte-identical SPIR-V, the 87 builds of the two row kernels among them.
  - `llmx-backend-vulkan-test --isa` passes in both arms and its 141 dumped kernel disassemblies are byte-identical, the 62 row-kernel and Q8_0 decode builds among them.
  - Identity: the four tiny fixtures' `llmx-model-logits` files and `logits --then-ids` with and without `--per-token` on the CPU and vulkan:0 in f16 and int8, and Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M `logits --last 16` and `generate --temp 0 -n 64` on vulkan:0 in f16 and int8, 64 files, byte-identical.
  - CTest passes; `tests/dead_code.py` and `tests/docs_check.py` report no finding against the list.
  - Per-call device time of a decode routed step (the base sequence of B1's `moe_step`) on synthetic weights at the routed layers' shapes of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M and Qwen3-30B-A3B Q8_0 (types, widths, experts and picks), integer dot forced, three interleaved rounds per arm, medians: every cell within -2.6 to +3.3 percent, with the same output hashes; with identical modules on both sides this is the run-to-run spread, and the empty-dispatch floor read 3.55 to 3.94 us across the rounds.
    The machine ran other users' processes throughout (system CPU 17 to 43 percent, a game client and a browser), recorded beside every round.

## Vulkan backend split into headers by concern (2026-10-25, branch refactor/vulkan-split on main 8e84e4c4f, approved by the reviewer, move only)

- **Goal:** `vulkan_backend.cpp` was one file of 5155 lines holding every concern of the backend; each concern gets one owner, so later features (fused decode kernels first) add their host code to the right header and only a declaration to the class.
- **The change:** the backend stays one translation unit; `vulkan_backend.cpp` keeps the `VulkanBackend` class with its construction, queue, submissions, diagnostics and the elementwise, norm, state, gather and embedding ops, and includes nine headers (`docs/src/backends-vulkan.md` lists what each holds).
  - Before the class: `vulkan_device.hpp` (loader, entry points, `Device`, device needs), `vulkan_kernels.hpp` (the kernel table, weight formats' kernels, row and decode builds, write sets) and `vulkan_buffer.hpp` (`VulkanBuffer`, padded F32 rule, table views, `VulkanKVStorage`), each moved verbatim.
  - After the class: `vulkan_memory.hpp`, `vulkan_dispatch.hpp`, `vulkan_twins.hpp`, `vulkan_matmul.hpp`, `vulkan_attention.hpp` and `vulkan_collective.hpp` define 84 members out of line, each body and its comment moved verbatim; the class keeps each one's declaration where its definition stood, with its default arguments and `override`, and the definition is `inline VulkanBackend::name(...)` without them.
  - Nothing else changed but what a split needs: the anonymous namespace closes after the class and reopens for the public functions, the moved block of declarations loses the blank lines between neighbours, and one comment that said "this file" now says "the backend".
  - `tests/dead_code.py`'s shader check reads the kernel table in `vulkan_kernels.hpp` and the dispatches in every backend source; four docs that named `vulkan_backend.cpp` for a moved function name its header.
- **Proof:** the Vulkan backend's object file, built in fresh MSVC Release directories at 8e84e4c4f and at the change, holds the same 8665 sections as a multiset, each byte for byte with the same relocations by symbol name, once the anonymous namespace's and the lambdas' hashed names are read as one; only the section order, the section checksum table and the debug section naming the source path differ.
  On the Radeon VII (vulkan:0), Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M `logits --last 16` and `generate --temp 0 -n 64`, and the four tiny fixtures' `llmx-model-logits` files and `logits --then-ids` with and without `--per-token`, are byte-identical, 28 of 28 files.
  CTest from the fresh change build passes, 83 of 83 (a first run beside the docs and dead-code checks timed out `vulkan-quantization` at 120 s, which takes 25 s alone in both arms), and `tests/dead_code.py` and `tests/docs_check.py` report no finding; the `--linked` dead-code check runs only on Linux and was not run.
- **Left:** reviewer's review and the queue; the moved code reorders sections in the binary, which can shift timing by the layout band AGENTS.md describes without changing an instruction.

## The linked dead-code check reads objects by their path inside the build (2026-10-25, branch fix/dead-code-src-path on main fc6f53415, F2DEV's finding of 07:42, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **The bug:** `tests/dead_code.py --linked` took every object whose full path held `/src/` as built from `src/`, so from a checkout under such a path (a container mounting the tree at `/src`) every test's objects counted and their functions were reported: 131 spurious `linked-test-only` findings on main there, none at a clean path, where the hosted Vulkan job runs.
- **The fix:** `product_objects` reads the path inside the build's `CMakeFiles`, where CMake keeps an object under its target's directory by its source's path, and takes those under `src/`.
- **Test:** the dead-code self-test builds a tree under a path holding `src/` with a test's object and a product's and requires only the product's; the first commit fails on main, the function missing.
- **Gates:** to run: docs and dead-code, the linked check at a path holding `/src/` and at a clean one, and the hosted run.
