## Room counted once (2026-10-19, branch feat/room-once on step1b/legs 84e6ff9da, item 7 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, step 3, lands by fast-forward as two commits after step1b/legs)

- **Why:** the scheduler's ledger (`reserved_`) added each request's whole reservation and each donor's whole blocks, so blocks a fork shares with its donor were counted twice: a conversation past half the pool could not keep two holders (N1, S1's root) and a donor forked by an edit was consumed for room, its rows past the fork lost (N14).
- **The change (the DESIGN of 13:28, F2DEV's DECISION of 13:31):** one count of the device's room in `reuse.hpp`. `room()` is each pool's free blocks in the model less what the running requests promised and have not taken (`need_` less what their sequences hold, a pass's prepared blocks among them, so a request in flight counts at what its pass took). `Model::freed(set)` (history.hpp) says what a set of sequences frees together, from the pool's own references, blocks and checkpoint slots. `make_room` takes the free blocks and a `Gain` asked of the cumulative victim set, never victim by victim, and gives back only a donor that frees nothing beside the other victims, the order otherwise unchanged. `reserved_`, its eleven add and sub sites, `Donor::blocks`, `donor_blocks()` and `Streaming::need` are gone. `Stats::reserved` keeps its name with the true count (taken or promised) and `donor_blocks` is what only donors and streams hold, both as `note_room` last found them. Marks stay outside, the host and disk tiers' room untouched.
- **One more change the count needed:** of donors sharing as much with a request, `best_donor` takes the newest. A request no longer consumes a donor it shares whole, so two donors of one conversation can stand, the older inside the newer, and a job forking the older found no room the newer could give; the newer, a fork of the older, holds all it holds.
- **Tests:** the failing commit flips the scenario's two expectations to held: a turn's donor beside its job past half the pool, and a donor forked by an edit losing no row (the next turn reusing all 1152 on the synthetic model, its split and the hybrid model, where it was 896 and 768). `kv-cache` holds `Model::freed` against the pool on one pool and two, `arch-qwen35` a checkpoint's slot a fork shares, `server-passes` the set gain by hand beside its simulation (whose ledger shares nothing, through an adapter), donors still taken oldest first where the newer alone would do, and a donor that frees nothing beside the others given back. step1b's room-for-all and room-for-four legs are unchanged.
- **Witnesses the count moved, in the change's commit:** `server-resume`'s request whose donor went with part of its history kept, and its twin beside a donor holding its reply as prompt rows, now take their step at 512 tokens with the setup's donor (its one unshared block the gain), so A's step pauses B at 532 and the resume recomputes 404 rows, not 384, still forking the first block alone. The two stop cases of item 14 (`stop_keeps_job`, `stop_keeps_request`) no longer take the donor over, since a fork sharing every block of its donor frees nothing by consuming it: they keep that shape, the donor beside the job or the request, and each runs again as the only holder (F2DEV's REVIEW of 14:41), on the synthetic model, where three other turns ending at three requests at once make the donor count drop the turn's donor while the job reads or the request replies, the stop then held at a pass and the restart required to fork the 512 tokens only the job or request held. With the stop's parking reverted locally each lone case fails, the restart forking 256; the hybrid model is not used for them, as a job there parks at the checkpoint it forked, which the dropped donor's host copy also holds. The test's gate lets attention calls go one at a time (`HeldAttention::hold_until`), so the stop is taken at the first held call after the scheduler's counts show the donor dropped, not after a time.

## Prompt pieces cut by time at depth (2026-10-18, branch feat/piece-time, item 3 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** a piece is a layer's part over all the pass's rows, so at depth a ubatch's attention piece grows with the history (305 ms at S8's depth, 61 ms at 40k), and a reply beside a long prompt waits for whole pieces; and a job's grant was priced by a forgetting mean of a whole pass's time over every row in it, decode rows included, so every grant beside replies overran on production (3 of 3).
- **The change (F2DEV's rule of 11:44, XDEV's conditions of 12:02, F2DEV's decisions of 18:23, 19:00 and 20:20 after the first 27B gate):** each stage keeps its last passes fed in pieces' rows and longest pieces (`StagePace::search`, from the recorder's `End`, the passes apart between pieces left out) and the prompt and history end it measured (`piece_of`, `piece_end`); under the automatic rule, beside generated rows, the next slice of that prompt at that depth is those rows times `kPieceMs` (50 ms) over that time, in steps of `kPieceStep` (16), at least one and at most a ubatch, the least over the stages (since replaced by the fit below), and any other slice, a new depth, starts at one step (`piece_cut`). A round with a cut slice has the generated rows go apart (`cut_now`), so every cut pass is fed in pieces and measured: a probe the replies rode, as small slices are, was never measured, and the cut then stayed at one step. ## The slow write's two arms independent of the runner (2026-10-18, branch test/capped-write-wait, tests only, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** both arms of `cache-scenario`'s slow write failed on macOS. The capped arm (fix/turns-kept's run 39135787891, "1 waits, 0 at their bound"): its 100 ms bound is seen only at the scheduler's next look, which on a slow runner came after the write, whose pieces the store held 200 ms each, had ended. The uncapped arm (feat/restore-ms's run 39156576100, "1 waits, 1 at their bound"): a wait for a donor's write follows the write's rate only once that write has begun (`waits_for_room` reads the write in flight); the other request arrived before this runner had begun it, so the wait had only its 100 ms constant, as the line "left the devices with no copy ... not yet whole on disk" 154 ms in shows.
- **The change:** the capped arm's store holds each piece five minutes, so the write is in flight at any look a running scheduler makes and the wait is counted at its bound; the uncapped arm's holds each piece five seconds, and the other request is submitted once the history's write is under way (`Stats::disk_in_flight`), so the wait follows the write's rate whatever the runner. Both checks stay on counts; the stop cancels the capped write, so neither case takes long.
- **Held by:** the legs four copies at once on Windows, every run passing in 59 s; CTest; the hosted run of github gate/capped-write-wait.

## Turns at the pool's edge only where the history is kept (2026-10-18, branch fix/turns-kept, item 2 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** production's reply of 2026-10-17 was "paused 20 times, 0 taken back, 67456 tokens recomputed"; the request line counts a turn given up as a pause. `Scheduler::yields` gave a turn up on the host tier's size, not on whether the copy could be made, so where the host had no memory for the copy's slabs the history was lost and every change of turn recomputed the other request's history. Pauses for growth alone did not repeat in any variant tried (docs/CACHE-PLAN.md, item 2).
- **The change:** `host_room` in `server/reuse.hpp` is the one plan of whether a copy is kept, which `write_back` executes and `yields` asks: the room it releases, in write_back's order (superseded copies, entries on disk, boundaries, unreturned copies for an unreturned donor, the oldest), or why not (larger than the tier, an unreturned donor refused, the room still short once every entry it may release is gone, or no host memory for the slabs it takes anew, `Model::host_fresh` with the slabs the releases free over `Model::host_admits`). A copy short of room or of the host's memory now releases nothing, where it released entries and then failed in `save_host`, and `yields` keeps the edge for either (F2DEV, 2026-10-18 10:16). A turn kept for want of memory is counted (`Stats::turns_without_memory`, `pressure.since_start.turns_without_memory`) and its run said as it starts and as it ends, at a turn given up or where none waits.
- **Tests:** `server-resume`'s turns only where the history is kept, the first commit, failing on main 185e64592 (2 turns given up, 4324 rows recomputed, against none and at most 1700); with the change, without the memory 0 turns, 996 rows recomputed on the Q8_0 model and 1408 on the hybrid one (one growth pause), with it 2 turns and 100 and 0 rows, as on main.
- **Checked, Windows, MSVC:** the build, CTest 49 of 49, the `server` and `threads` components, `docs`, `dead-code`.
- **XDEV's review of 10:18 and 10:39:** (1) an entry released while its disk write is in flight parks its slabs (`release_entry`), so `host_room` credits it no idle slab, only the limit it leaves (`parks`, the one condition both read); (2) a tier still short after every release the plan may make answers room, which also covers an in-flight read counted in the tier's bytes; (3) the slabs are read as `alloc_host` takes them, idle slabs past the limit freed before fresh ones are admitted and the memory they give back counted (`Model::host_copy_fits` over `detail::copy_slabs`, which `alloc_host` now uses too), with `kv-cache`'s case of one slab a device, two idle on the second, at a limit of two. Not cased beyond that: (1) and (2) need a copy's disk write or a read held across a turn under constrained memory, which the one-backend disk-free case does not reach.
- **Not cased:** the answer "room" needs entries the plan may not release to hold the tier during a turn: a boundary is pinned only inside an admission and a copy is promoted only inside `promote`, neither of which spans `grow`, and a disk read's source is pinned while a state read alone runs, which a case would have to hold in flight across a turn; no cheap case reaches it, so it is held by `host_room`'s one rule for `write_back` and `yields`.
- **Follow-up (F2DEV, 10:16):** one shared eligibility predicate for `host_room` and `release_written`, `drop_oldest_bound` and `drop_oldest_host`, which today restate who may be released.
- **Left:** the gate (host logic and its hosted run; the 27B leg of the plan's gate, the waiting reply's time to first token beside the older's tokens a second, turns, pauses and recompute with the host's free memory below one copy, by the gate runner), F2DEV's review.

## The device pool apart from the request limit (2026-10-17, branch feat/kv-pool, item 1 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, in progress)

- **Goal:** serve's pool sized apart from a request's limit (docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 7), so production's long chat and a client's task both stay on the cards.
- **Done (built, the CPU tests green on Windows):** serve's `--ctx-size` is a request's limit (at most the model's context, refused past it once the file is read, exit 1) and `--kv-tokens` the pool; without it `PlacementRequest::kv_auto` sizes the pool to every whole block the devices' free memory holds, searched up to `kv_search_bound` with the drafter and its first mark in the fit, the checkpoints' quarter rule on that pool, and keeps the model's context with the reason in the start line where a device's free memory is the host's (`Backend::memory_is_host`, the CPU's) or unknown, or no KV grows; `Scheduler::request_limit` is the one rule of what a request holds, taken once by the scheduler and by `default_host_cache` and `no_turns`, and `/v1/health` gives it as `server.request_tokens`; the suite's and tools' pool uses moved to `--kv-tokens` (`tools/server_mix_check.py` and `tools/long_context_check.py` take `--kv-tokens` for the server pool); docs (USAGE's three readings, SERVER, OPERATING, KV-CACHE, SPECULATIVE's amendment, the source pages). The implementation DESIGN of 07:37, F2DEV's review of 08:01 (the host-memory predicate, the limit computed once), XDEV's block-id bound of 10:41 and F2DEV's approval note of 08:34 (the suite's servers at the model's context through `common.pool_args`, the settle skipped where a device's memory is unknown, the start wait in USAGE) and XDEV's Vulkan point of 11:36 (an integrated or CPU Vulkan device's memory counted as the host's by its type, `host_memory_device`, held by `vulkan-buffer`) are in.
- **Tests:** `placement` (the automatic budget on a device, unknown memory, the CPU, a split with a host-memory stage, the search bound's edges), `arch-qwen35-fit` (the drafter's two numbers on the hybrid with checkpoints by number; it fails with the drafter left out of the automatic fit), `cache-scenario` (a limit below the context beside a larger pool, a pool below the limit, a kept entry read back at a pool of twice the context), `server` (the limit and `request_tokens` through `/v1/health`, the refusal past the context).
- **Left:** the gates (server and placement host tier: CTest, the suite on the CPU and a device, Qwen3-0.6B identity against main, the hosted run; the full-load gate of the default on the 27B; the no-code figures from the gate runner, `--ctx-size 524288` against 262144, folded in).
- **Hosted run 39019022210 at 2e4ca1408:** the Vulkan job's `cache-scenario-production` found the cut turn's 384 leading rows neither reused nor explained: the read of them reached its bound (the tiny model's recompute time) before it ended on that runner, and the request computed them, as P2 allows, while the classifier had no way to tell a failed restore; the change does not reach that turn (its limit and pool are as on main). The scheduler now counts such waits (`Stats::disk_wait_timeouts`, `reuse.disk.since_start.wait_timeouts`), the request keeps the rows its own read covered (`Request::restore_late`), the scenario classifies those rows alone as failed restore (XDEV's recheck of 06:29: a timeout of another request's read, or rows past the read's end, stay unexplained, held by made-up witnesses); the cut turn's expectation took them as held until the scenario's reads stopped timing out (below), and is strict again.
  XDEV's recheck of 06:49: the kinds are disjoint, a row a loss explains being evicted and never also a failed restore (witness: [0, 128) lost and a read reaching its bound at 256 give 128 evicted, 128 failed, 128 unexplained), and a wait's rows are those of the read that started, which is the shorter whole path where a state read alone found no host room; no test reaches a state on disk higher than its blocks (the `alone` branch of `Scheduler::prefetch`), so that endpoint is held by construction, not by a witness. XDEV asked again (08:22) for one where a fixture reaches it; the attempt (a 300-token conversation on disk, its 700-token next turn's boundary at 384 written and its history kept off disk by the disk tier's cap) needs a cap between the files of a state and of a history segment, which the test cannot read before the scheduler is made: the model's host sizes are whole 64 MiB slabs, and the disk tier writes a history as the segments past what it holds.
- **Hosted run 39105265337 at d050984e0:** the Windows job's `cache-scenario-production` met the same timeout, the cut turn's 384 rows classified as failed restore and so P1 broken. The scenario's test-only read bound (`DiskOptions::read_wait`, `Scheduler::read_until`) went to test/stabilize-main with main's other flaky tests, and this branch keeps its own leg's use of it (the pool past the context) and the strict P1 and P5; a read reaching its bound is P2's case, `server-resume`'s read past its bound, which here also requires the wait counted and the rows kept on the request and, at XDEV's request (08:22), takes its bound from the test's read wait (100 ms) rather than the measured prompt rate, and the classifier's witnesses map those rows to failed restore.
- **Gotchas:** the automatic default follows free device memory at start, so a production start passes the measured `--kv-tokens`; the flags' landing refuses a `--ctx-size` above the context, retiring the no-code line; a dense model has no embedded drafter in the tree, so its automatic budget reserves nothing beside the fit and the drafter's two-number case is the hybrid's.

## The cache scenario's write waits bounded only against a hang (2026-10-18, branch test/first-write-hang, tests only, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** feat/kv-pool's hosted run 39135787656 failed on macOS in `cache-scenario` with "first write: the other request's history written within a minute": the first-write case's store holds each 4 MiB 3 s, and a slow runner's queue of writes passed the minute the test gave it, though the case asserts counts and not time.
- **The change:** the first write's and the slow write's waits for the disk tier and for the other request's history go through `within` with ten minutes, a bound only a hang reaches; `within_a_minute` is `within` at a minute. Nothing they assert changes.
- **Held by:** the legs five copies at once on Windows, every run passing; CTest; the hosted run of github gate/first-write-hang.
## A failed host copy drains only what it recorded (2026-10-18, branch fix/fork-own-tickets, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** `Model::fork` with a state and `Model::restore_host` synced every device on a failure, safe only while no other thread records on any of them; the server's hold gives that, but nothing in the model says so, and a future caller has the same trap (F2DEV's follow-up to the boundary fork, devlog 2026-10-18 06:10).
- **The change:** one helper, `Model::drain_recorded`, which both call on a failure: a device they submitted on waits on that ticket, one they recorded on without submitting submits and waits, synced alone should that fail, and a device they never touched is left alone.
- **Tests:** `arch-qwen35`'s failed fork with a state, the first commit, failing on main 30baef845 ("synced a device it never copied to"): three devices, the mixers on two and the feed-forward parts on the third, each mixer device failing its submission in turn; the copies retire, the third is not synced, the slot comes back and the fork then succeeds. The failed restore's case now holds the copies retired, not the syncs, the first device submitting once either way.
- **Left:** the gate (model code: CTest, the suite on the CPU and a device, Qwen3-0.6B identity against main, the hosted run), a review.

## The write waits' cap by recomputing made the test's (2026-10-18, branch test/stable-write-wait, tests and a test-only option, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** `cache-scenario`'s write slower than the wait's constant failed on hosted Windows and macOS runners (runs 39120957649 and 39124055276, "1 waits, 1 at their bound, the next turn reusing 1024"): a wait for a save is capped by recomputing its rows at the measured prompt rate, about 0.5 s on the test's slowed CPU, which a slow runner's write of the history could pass.
- **The change:** `DiskOptions::recompute_row_ms`, for tests, replaces the measured prompt rate where it caps a wait for a save (`waits_for_room`); the slow write and the first write cap it at 50 ms a row, about a minute, so the wait follows the write's rate whatever the runner, and a second arm of the slow write caps it at 1 us a row, so the same wait reaches its bound, is counted and the reply is still the fresh model's.
- **Held by:** `cache-scenario` (the legs) five times at once on Windows, every run passing; CTest; the hosted run of github gate/stable-write-wait.

## The host pool gives idle memory back in runs said once, and takes none ahead in between (2026-10-18, branch fix/host-give-back-line, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** after production's restart at 11:16 on 2026-10-17 the server said "N MiB of idle host memory given back, the host being short of memory" every second (64 to 832 MiB a time): the host's free memory fell below the pool's reserve while it adopted 1302 kept entries through the file cache, and between two looks the idle growth took slabs again (it was armed again at the first look that gave nothing back), which the next look gave back.
- **The change:** after idle slabs go back the pool takes none ahead until the host has gone `kHostQuiet` (30 s) without a give-back, and a run of give-backs is said once as it starts and once with its total and length as it ends (`host_pressure`).
- **Tests:** `server-resume`'s host pool under pressure: after one slab went back the host has room again at once, and no slab may be taken ahead within three seconds; on main three were. The first commit adds the check, failing on main.
- **Checked:** see the REVIEW-REQUEST; the gate is CTest and the server component.

## Main's tests made deterministic and the hosted limits raised (2026-10-18, branch test/stabilize-main, tests, a test-only option and the workflow, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** ci/vulkan-job-limit's hosted run 39110189068, whose change only raised limits, failed on main's tests in two places. The Vulkan job's `server-passes-cpu`: the boundary fork beside a paced prompt waited for a pass taken between a prompt's pieces, which the automatic rule, deciding by this runner's times, never took in 60 seconds. The ubuntu and UBSan jobs' `cache-scenario-production`: the cut turn's read reached its bound, the tiny model's recompute time of 384 rows, a few milliseconds, before the runner's disk gave it, so P5 broke. Before that, the landing run of main 185e64592 (run 39103232546) had its Vulkan job ended at 25 min 3 s by its 25-minute limit with every step already passed (build 6.7 min, backend tests 11.2, test on the CPU 2.3, linked dead code 4.5), its Linux CPU job took 19 min 48 s of its 20, and fix/host-give-back-line's run 39106474409 had that job ended at 20 minutes in its suite.
- **The change:**
  - `timeout-minutes` 40 for the Vulkan job and 30 for the Linux CPU job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, with their lines in docs/CI.md.
  - `DiskOptions::read_wait`, for tests, replaces the recompute estimate as a read's bound through one helper, `Scheduler::read_until`, which both read starts in `prefetch` call; the scenario's four legs that read from disk wait up to 60 s, so no turn depends on the runner's disk, and P1 and P5 stay strict. A read reaching its bound stays `server-resume`'s read past its bound.
  - The boundary fork case runs with a fixed share, under which a pass beside another request is fed in pieces whatever the runner's times (`Scheduler::form`'s rule), and drives the overlap by the device's state: once a stage's thread has submitted, until the edit's first token, every stage submission holds the queue 200 ms and every call of the scheduler's thread first waits up to 500 ms for one, so a call outside the stages' hold meets a held queue every time and one inside it never does.
- **Held by:** the boundary fork case on ae5add311's code (main with the fork outside the hold) fails in each of three runs, 3 calls meeting the held queue of 11 the scheduler's thread made, and passes in each of three with the hold, each run beside four others of the binary; CTest on Windows; the hosted run of github gate/stabilize-main.

## A message boundary's state is forked under the stages' hold (2026-10-17, branch fix/boundary-fork-hold, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** production (2a0221627, Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 over a tensor group of two MI50s, automatic pacing) lost its device at 11:15:54 UTC and was restarted: an edit forked a message boundary whose state was read from disk while a prompt was read in pieces on the stage's thread; `admit` called `Model::fork` with the state outside `quieted()`, its copy met the Vulkan guard ("a call on a backend whose queue a submission holds"), and the fork's failure path synced every device from the scheduler's thread, flushing the command buffer the stage's thread was recording and submitting on a queue another thread used, so the context was lost.
- **The change:** `admit` forks with a state through `quieted()` (`scheduler.hpp`), so the copy, and a failed copy's drain, run with every recorder at a piece boundary. Every other call the scheduler's thread makes on the stages' devices was checked: the copies to and from host memory, the disk tier's reads, writes and proofs, keep, retract, mark, the drafter's chain and the device timings already go through the hold; `reset`, `release_host`, `wait_host`, the disk tier's settling and writes of host copies only wait for tickets or touch host memory; the fork without a state and `make_sequence` record nothing; the pass calls are the recorders' protocol. XDEV's b6ef3ad85 (a failed host restore drains its copies) is the same drain, which is safe only under the hold, as `promote` calls it.
- **Tests:** `server-passes-cpu`'s boundary fork beside a paced prompt, on a device that counts a call meeting a queue a submission holds: one such call in each of three runs on main, none in five with the change. The first commit adds it, failing on main.
- **Reviewed:** XDEV approved the runtime change (devlog 2026-10-17 14:56 and 14:58 on its clock); at its suggestion the test takes the passes between a prompt's pieces as a growth since the long prompt came, not the counter since start.
- **Checked:** see the REVIEW-REQUEST; the gate is the server host tier and the case on two MI50s as a tensor group with automatic pacing.

## Health device topology integration (2026-10-18, branch feat/health-topology-land-20261018; lands by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** Integrate the realized model placement health payload so the dashboard can show actual backend groups and layer stages.
- **Done:** Integrated topology commit `53c6b6854` on base `25a542856` as `f0d8266e6`. The model owns the realized placement snapshot; health adds topology while retaining `requests.live`, and the dashboard renders it with an older-server fallback. The immutable topology JSON is serialized once when `Api` is constructed, avoiding layer traversal and JSON construction on each health poll.

## Validation follows the changed behavior (2026-10-17, lands by fast-forward)

Static dashboard changes use focused browser checks; documentation changes use the docs and dead-code checks. Neither requires unrelated HF or inference performance runs. Runtime and numerical changes retain their applicable gates. Follow-up fixes rerun affected checks and record retained evidence with its revision and intervening delta. AGENTS.md owns the gate policy; docs/CI.md explains the existing hosted workflow and skipping its unrelated matrix for documentation/static-UI-only pushes.

## Live per-request operational counters (2026-10-17, landed and deployed 2026-10-18)

- **Goal:** Give the monitoring dashboard bounded per-request prompt and generation work counters from which it can derive live rates without reading request text or scheduler-owned state from another thread.
- **Done:** `Request` owns its retired prompt count beside existing successful retirement accounting. Live published counts use existing generated history only at a safe round boundary. Health requests a coalesced snapshot under its existing lock; the scheduler copies at most 64 records at its next natural boundary without an extra lock or analytics wakeup. Health exposes `requests.live` with actual monotonic sample time, bounded totals, phases and opaque IDs, active requests before paused and queued requests. Snapshots refresh on demand at natural scheduler boundaries; the first poll may be empty or stale, and browser rates require two distinct sample times for the same ID. Idle polling does not advance sample time, and empty request sets clear cached records before waiting. Prompt recomputation can count again. The implementation removes per-token analytics increments and unconditional snapshot locking, scans and clock reads; a demand check, retired-prompt addition and bounded requested copying remain.
- **Landing and gates:** API commit `3b2a701b70bb082fdc4b9b85e7ce8624d06a3269` landed on GitHub main. Hosted run [39063827631](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/39063827631), attempt 2, passed. Attempt 1's six successful jobs and one pre-existing cache-scenario failure are retained; the Vulkan retry [117497391920](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/117497391920) passed all 53 CTests, the CPU suite and linked dead-code checks. The cache timeout-reporting change at `4eae` is separate and is not in this release. The exact clean Release binary was built from the Vulkan-enabled configuration with no GPU exposed to the builder, CPU affinity 2,3 and a 6 GiB limit: SHA256 `2279c26a0da9710dbd3edc78f1a882c97899d55fa87145d33ae8ee4524a6bc90`, version `llmx 0.1.0+g3b2a701b70bb numerics 888d8972bfd4898b`. Final docs/dead-code checks passed (0 docs findings of 21 planted; 5 known code findings of 18 planted). The hosted test head `68a7df405` differs from landing head `3b2a701b` only by documentation changes; runtime, tests, fixtures, configuration and build inputs are unchanged.
- **Production:** Deployed `3b2a701b` on 2026-10-18 after the readiness gate returned four real tokens. The deployed binary and dashboard HTML match the release hashes above and `4b61deafeea3bf20524656668f1e2754e728334ebc3643a14d6cf20863be940b`; the previous server container remains available for rollback, and the existing Python collector (`096f5315-b8bd-43d5-9aef-dd9aed438331`) was preserved. At that deployment, health did not expose `topology`; the subsequent topology rollout recorded above supplies it. A bounded post-deploy observation confirmed the live schema and collected six distinct runtime sample timestamps with no polling errors or reset. Four positive aggregate generation-rate observations ranged from 37.074 to 50.1 tokens/s, but the HTTP response ID could not be correlated to a scheduler request ID, so other requests may have contributed; these are not attributed per-request rates or a performance claim. No prompt or response text was retained.
- **Measured, API checkpoint on Windows CPU:** [Matched overhead evidence](benchmarks/request-live-overhead-20261017.json) compares clean detached `b6ef3ad85` and `8d4c5f2db` builds of Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, with 2-second health polling and without health polling. All 32 cells are retained: 31 succeeded, one was interrupted at the frozen 30-minute cap; a separately pinned continuation ran only the one never-started cell. Eight polled pairs and seven unpolled pairs are complete; the interrupted cell and its successful partner remain explicitly unpaired. All available successful requests have exact prompt/token identity, with zero actual mismatches; eight identity groups lack the interrupted condition, and absence is not a mismatch. The 16 polled cells show no observed counter-bound or monotonicity violations. With polling, paired mean output-throughput changes are +1.68% at one request and +5.81% at four, but paired ranges span roughly -10% to +17% with substantial observed CPU/disk/GPU activity. No demonstrated slowdown outside the observed noise, no speedup or zero-overhead claim, and no strict sub-percent bound; these measurements cover the API checkpoint, not the combined landing binary or GPU throughput.
- **History:** The initial API revision passed `server-passes-cpu` (356244 checks) and focused synthetic HTTP checks; the initial combined head `ad0b6eefc` passed all 49 CTests, four Qwen3-0.6B reply/logit identity cases and the MI50 server component. Its hosted TSan run found ten races in the test harness's shared check counter, not the runtime; callbacks were changed to collect their own count and first error and check after joining. The corrected tree and final landing gates above supersede the earlier pending status. The production-shaped cache timeout also reproduced on the pre-API scheduler; that failure remains recorded and is not counted as an API pass.
- **Markdown review:** Compared all 110 tracked Markdown files with the clean pre-update `3b2a701b` tree after normalizing checkout line endings; only this `STATUS.md` changed and the other 109 hashes are unchanged. Rechecked this API block against the local release, production rollout and live-observation JSON; build identity, deployed HTML hash, retained rollback/collector, missing topology payload and the uncorrelated aggregate rates match those records.
- **Gotchas:** Paused requests do not count against the queue limit, so exported records need their own fixed cap. Counters describe retired prompt work and published tokens; requests that start and finish between polls may not appear because the endpoint exposes no completed-request history. Zero inference overhead cannot be promised. The dashboard exposes no request text or token IDs, and no GPU performance claim is made.

## Restore-host submission failures drain borrowed copies (2026-10-17, branch fix/restore-submit-final, lands by fast-forward after final-head gates)

- **Goal:** A `restore_host` submission could throw after one or more devices had queued copies from `HostHistory` slabs. Because submission was outside the existing failure handler, those queues could still borrow slabs after the failed restore released its checkpoint slot.
- **Done:** The regression first reproduced the failure; the fix moves the final per-device submit loop into the existing restore transaction's `try`, whose catch synchronizes every backend before unwinding. `arch-qwen35` injects a submit failure on each device of a two-device split, checks all queued and open copies are drained and the checkpoint slot returned, then retries, releases the host slabs after retirement, and compares continuation logits with a fresh prompt. The unfixed build fails the new drain assertion; the fixed build passes all 808 architecture/Qwen35 checks and focused CTest. The active goal/done/left/gotchas block was missed before implementation and is recorded here after the fix; this does not claim the process rule was followed.
- **Measured gates:** At baseline `2a0221627` and fix `c898d4177`, matched Release Vulkan builds, Linux CTest 53/53 (including 808 regression checks), all 28 device-suite components and all eight dense/hybrid CPU/GPU F32/F16-cache identity cells pass. The device suite reaches real dense host promotion (960 reused tokens, CLI-equal replies) and hybrid pause/promotion. Windows CTest passes 49/49; the CPU suite's two sandbox failures pass unrestricted reruns. Hosted CI passes all seven jobs at c898. One monitored ABBA timing block gives mean prefill/decode changes of -0.0163%/+0.7402% on dense Q8 and -0.0308%/+0.0058% on hybrid Q8, with peer GPUs active and no performance-improvement claim. Exact versions, hashes, absolute timings, activity and limits are in [the gate record](benchmarks/restore-submit-drain-20261017.md).
- **Final-head validation:** The branch integrates unchanged runtime/test changes onto docs-only main `3b70f5e4f`. This requires a fresh build, full CTest and hosted CI at the integrated head before fast-forward landing; the hosted result is attached to that commit. The measured c898 results above cover their named binaries and do not substitute for final-head checks. No new model-qualification claim is made.
- **Gotchas:** A submit can fail on a later device after earlier queues accepted work; a throwing backend may also retain open copies. Keep every backend synchronized before the host slabs or failed sequence storage can be released. See `docs/src/model-history.md` and `tests/arch_qwen35.cpp`.

## Tokenizing a long chat takes a tenth of the time (2026-10-16, branch fix/tokenize-speed, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** after fix/message-ends a cut costs one render and one tokenize of the whole conversation, and the owner saw one core at 100 percent during it. Measured on a 159-message conversation under the Qwen3.8 template of the chat fixture, cut from tests/data/wiki.test.raw (4114542 bytes, 954025 ids, 480 special tokens), Qwen3's tokenizer, on the Windows development machine: `encode` took 943 to 956 ms, of which 366 to 382 ms comparing every byte against all 26 special tokens and 591 to 606 ms running BPE on 854644 words of which 20389 are distinct.
- **The change, in `bpe::Tokenizer::encode` alone:** the scan for a special token looks only at a byte one begins with (`special_lead`, filled as the tokenizer is made), and the text between special tokens is taken as one range; a word merged once in a call is not merged again (a map local to the call, so concurrent connections share nothing and need no lock). The ids are the same by construction: BPE gives a word the same ids wherever it stands, and a special token can only begin at a byte one begins with.
- **Measured, same machine and conversation, two runs of five encodes each:** 943 to 958 ms before, 95 to 105 ms after, the same ids (FNV hash b945fc0893991e8b both). Threads and ids kept across turns were weighed in the design (devlog 2026-10-16 08:47, F2DEV's review 08:59) and left out: the tokenizer sits below the backends' pool, and kept ids need state across requests.
- **Tests:** `tokenizer-encode`, new: `encode` against the encode it replaced, written out in the test, on a vocabulary with merges and six special tokens: each piece alone, special tokens at the start, the end and side by side, a `<` that begins none, specials cut short at the text's end, and 50 texts of up to 4000 random pieces, a word beside every neighbour (87 checks); a memo keyed on the word's first byte alone fails it. The `tokenizer` component's goldens (Qwen3 and qwen35) and `chat-template` hold the real vocabularies. No test can fail on the unchanged code, since the change keeps every id: there is one commit.
- **Checked, Windows, MSVC, on the CPU:** see the REVIEW-REQUEST. The tier's gates (CTest, the CPU suite, Qwen3-0.6B identity against main, the hosted run) are the gate runner's at the head that lands.

## A cut finds its messages' ends in a few renders and never answers 500, and the time to first token counts it (2026-10-16, branch fix/message-ends, lands by fast-forward)

- **Two causes in one function, `Api::message_ends`:**
  - **Slow first token on long chats.** The end tokens place each message's end only where they number the messages, and on the Qwen 3.8 templates a conversation without a system message renders one more, the system block of reasoning instructions the template adds (the coordinator's finding on production, 2026-10-16: k messages render k + 1 end tokens). So every cut turn of such a chat rendered and tokenized the conversation up to each message, which grows with the square of the chat: 37 to 39 s before admission on each turn of a chat of 158 messages, 401408 tokens, cut to about 119000, where one whole render and tokenize takes 1.5 s. The request line said 1.2 to 2.0 s to first token, since it counted from admission.
  - **A 500 on a cut.** Where the count differs, as when a run of tool results shares one end token, the per-message render of the system message alone makes the Qwen 3.5 templates and the official 3.6 and 3.8 templates raise "No user query found in messages.", which escaped `Api::fit` as a 500.
- **The fix:** the template's own end tokens are counted once, from a render of the leading system message and one user message (`message_ends`), so the scan places every message's end where it numbers the messages and those, as on the Qwen 3.8 templates with or without a system message. Where it still does not, `first_kept` asks for only the ends it needs (`MessageEnds`, `context_cut.hpp`): the ends grow with the messages, so its two candidates, the first turn start that leaves at most the room and the steps' first start past the start before it, are found by halving, at most 2 (log2(messages + 1) rounded up + 1) + 2 ends, each a render of the conversation up to that message as text, counted in the prompt's ids whose text lies within it, with no tokenizing; a render takes 11 ms on a 4 MB, 1.1M-token conversation of 159 messages on the Windows development machine, where tokenizing it takes 703 ms. A part the template refuses ends at the last end token before the next part's end, or with that part. The cut's line says how many renders placed the ends.
- **The time to first token:** a request carries when its connection read it (`Request::received_`, passed to `Scheduler::submit`), so the request line gives `ms preparing` (reading to submission: the render, the tokenizer and a cut), `ms queued` and `ms to first token` from the reading, and the compatible routes' `timings` give `prepared_ms`. `/v1/health` reports no time to first token, so it has nothing to change.
- **Tests:** `context-cut`: `first_kept` against the walk over every end it replaced on 20000 random conversations, each asking for at most the bound; a conversation of 4096 messages cut by steps of 64 rows asking for at most it; a refused part placed by the end tokens and rendered once. `server`, `check_message_ends`, on the synthetic reasoning model whose end of text is now a control token in the prompt (`f32.write_model`'s `control`), `--ctx-size 128 --context-overflow shift`: a template writing a system block of its own where the conversation has none, with and without a system message, cut with its ends placed in 1 render; a template that raises without a user message and writes no end tokens, each cut reply and prompt those of the kept messages sent alone; one whose tool results share an end token, whose cuts and prompts equal those of the same template without the raise; a chat of 238 messages cut with its ends placed in 11 renders; and the request line's and `timings`' times. The tests commit, on the unfixed code, fails with "(2, 500, {'error': 'No user query found in messages.'})", and `context-cut` does not compile there, `MessageEnds` not existing.
- **For a measurement on production's shape:** the cut line's renders and the request line's `ms preparing` time the cut on the long chat; a test server on the test machine needs no card for it.
- **Checked, Windows, MSVC, on the CPU:** see the REVIEW-REQUEST. The tier's gates (CTest, the CPU suite, Qwen3-0.6B identity against main, the hosted run) are the gate runner's at the head that lands.

## The compatible routes refuse what they cannot honour, and gain the additive penalties and min_p (2026-10-15, branch fix/api-silent-fields on main 8d40bc52f, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** an audit found the compatible routes silently ignoring fields a client sends. The owner decided that a field llmx cannot honour is refused with a 400 naming it, a field with a harmless default stays ignored, and llmx's sampling defaults (temperature 0.8, top-k 40, top-p 0.95) are kept with the difference from OpenAI's documented.
- **Done:**
  - `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty` (-2 to 2, OpenAI's definitions) and `min_p` (0 to 1) are `infer::Sampling` fields with their ranges beside the others, so the server and the CLI refuse the same values. The flags are `--presence-penalty`, `--frequency-penalty` and `--min-p` on `generate` and `chat`; `serve` has no sampling flags, a request carries them.
  - The additive penalties come off a generated token's score after the multiplicative `penalty` and before the temperature (presence once, frequency once for each time). `min_p` is applied last, after top-k and top-p, as HF and other runtimes order them: the nucleus is measured on the top-k set as without `min_p`, then the ranking's tail below `min_p` times the likeliest weight is dropped. At 0, 0 and 0 no path changes.
  - `Api::refuse_unsupported` (compatible routes only) refuses `tools` other than an empty list, `tool_choice` other than "none", `response_format` other than text, `logit_bias` other than an empty object, `best_of` other than 1, `echo` true, `suffix`, `reasoning_effort`; `n` other than 1 was already refused, and a `prompt` array of several entries now says so. `logit_bias` is refused, not implemented: it needs its own flag and a per-token table, and the brief left it optional. The `tools` and `tool_choice` refusals are the ones the tool-calling branch removes.
  - An assistant message whose content is null or absent and which has `tool_calls` renders as an empty content (the calls are not rendered); the role `developer` renders as `system`.
  - The stop text was in the reply on the compatible routes (checked on main: `qr</th` for a stop of `</th`, as `/v1/generate` and the CLI print it). `StopTrim` now cuts it from the compatible routes' text, whole and streamed, holding back only the end of the text that is a proper prefix of a stop text; the scheduler is unchanged. Known limits: the stop text's tokens stay in `usage.completion_tokens`, in the logprobs and in the `text_offset`, and `/v1/generate` and `/v1/chat` keep the stop text as before (the native contract and the CLI print it).
  - `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is `timings.cache_n`, in the whole reply and in the streamed usage chunk.
- **Tests:** the first commit fails on main (the sampler test does not compile without the new fields; `tests/server.py` `check_api_fields` fails at its first range check). The sampler test holds hand-computed draws for each penalty, the order of the penalty before the temperature, min_p against the temperature and against top-k and top-p; `check_api_fields` holds every refusal and every ignored field, the three fields' ranges and neutral identity on the server and the CLI, min_p 1 equal to greedy at temperature 1.5, a penalty changing a greedy repeat, null content, the developer role, the stop text whole and streamed on both routes, and the cached count. The real-model paused-prefill case compared the compatible text with the CLI's including the stop text; it now holds the CLI's text to start with the reply's text and the stop text.
- **Identity with main at the neutral values (Windows, MSVC, CPU):** `generate` on the synthetic F32 model (two prompts, greedy and seeded, with and without top-k, top-p, repetition penalty and `--ignore-eos`) and on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 (greedy, greedy with penalty 1.2, seeded, seeded with top-k 0, top-p 0.9 and penalty 1.1), main's binary, this branch's, and this branch's with the three flags given as 0, byte-identical stdout.
- **Not done:** no timing round; the sampler's full-vocabulary path gains one comparison a weight (`cut`), which is not on the prefill path and is not measured. No device run; the change is host code. The Linux and hosted runs are the gate runner's.
- **Checked, Windows, MSVC, CPU only:** see the REVIEW-REQUEST for what ran.

## Tool calling on the chat routes, steps 2 to 5: tools in the request, the reply's calls parsed and streamed, one call a reply on request (2026-10-16, branches feat/tool-calls-reply and feat/tool-calls-single, stacked on fix/api-silent-fields and step 1)

## `--drafter` is an ordered list of sources, so a drafter can run alone (2026-10-13, branch feat/drafter-list on main b9ce43ef9, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** a drafter that runs a model always stood behind the reply's own history, with no way to run the MTP block alone, which measuring a drafter by itself and a reply whose history misleads both need.
- **The rule, one for every value:** `--drafter` is `off` or a comma-separated list of sources tried in the order given: `lookup`, `embedded` or a drafter file. `embedded` and `PATH` are the model drafter alone (this changes their meaning from the combined form), `lookup,embedded` and `lookup,PATH` are what they did between lookup-first and this change, `lookup` and `off` do not change.
- **Done:** `drafter_sources` in `cli/main.cpp` reads the list with `core::comma_list` once, for `drafts_flag` and `bench_drafter`; `Drafts::lookup_first` is true when lookup stands ahead of a model source and `Drafts::attach` passes it to the proposer where it passed `true`, so `spec.hpp`, `generate` and the scheduler are unchanged, and a mark is `--draft-max` + 1 rows for every source as on main. feat/own-draft-depth, which cuts a mark by the list again (the history's longer draft only behind lookup), rebases over this later.
- **Refused where the line is read (usage error, status 2, nothing on stdout):** an empty entry, a source twice, `off` beside another source, two sources that run a model, lookup behind a model drafter (the text gives `lookup,embedded`), and in `bench --model` lookup anywhere. A file's kind and `serve`'s refusal of a draft model stay at load with their texts.
- **Seen:** `/v1/health` `drafting.sources` lists the sources in the flag's spelling (empty without a drafter), and the serve start line ends with `, drafting lookup,embedded` after the checkpoints.
- **Migration:** `--drafter embedded` and `--drafter PATH` are now the drafter alone; production's flag becomes `lookup,embedded` to keep what it ran, which is the coordinator's with the owner told. No warning is printed for the old meaning. USAGE advises `lookup,embedded` as the usual form, from the Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 measurement on one MI50 and a tensor group of two (no loss beyond the spread on any reply kind, +17.3 and +21.4 percent on code edits), and states those cards and that model.
- **Tests:** `cli` and `cli-output` hold each refusal by its reason and the state a second `--drafter` replaces; `qwen35` and `drafters` run `embedded`, `lookup,embedded` and `lookup,PATH` byte-equal to drafts off, greedy and seeded, and on a prompt whose greedy pick repeats its start check `lookup,embedded` takes own-history drafts, `embedded` none, and the sources in health. The tests commit fails on the unchanged code (the refusals pass through as file errors, `cli-output` does not compile).
- **Not measured:** pure `embedded` against c27fb5fa6 (its `embedded` was pure) on tokens a pass and a second on one MI50 is the gate runner's cell, not run here; nor were the forms run on the 27B.

## The cache's moves in one file (2026-10-13, branch step2/reuse, step 2 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** the plan's later steps give the cache one question for reuse and one ranking of what stays, and they cannot while the functions that decide are scattered among the round's code. This step gathers them and changes nothing else: no behaviour, no signature, no call site, no lock scope.
- **Done:** 63 member functions of `Scheduler`, 987 lines, are defined in `src/server/reuse.hpp` out of the class, which `scheduler.hpp` includes after it, as `runtime.hpp` does with the model's `history.hpp`. Each keeps its declaration in the class where it stood. They are the host tier's slabs, the device donors' lookups, slots and drops, message boundaries, host entries, the one place a move is said and counted, the disk tier's side and the restores from disk with their wait. `scheduler.hpp` goes from 3692 lines to 2746.
- **What stays in the scheduler:** the round, the passes, pacing, sampling, drafting, and the requests' and jobs' lifetimes (`enter`, `admit`, `grow`, `pause`, `park`, `finish`, `hand_jobs`, `yield_jobs`, `follow_up`, `complete_jobs`), the ledger `make_room` reads (`donor_blocks` and `holders`, which step 3 replaces together), and the copies held behind passes.
- **What the plan had and this step does not do:** the containers (`donors_`, `host_`, `bounds_`, `disk_reads_`) and their types stay declared in `Scheduler`. A data member leaves its class only through a base or a member struct, which renames call sites or moves the order of construction and destruction, so it is not a pure move; the plan's text is corrected to say the holders follow when the functions have shrunk to its two.
- **How it is held to be a pure move, in place of a failing test, which a change of no behaviour has none of:** a script kept out of the tree reads the scheduler's file before and the two files after and holds them to five rules. Each definition's comment and body are the old lines in order, four columns to the left; its head is the old head with `inline` and `Scheduler::` added, `static` and default arguments left on the declaration, and the one nested return type qualified; the declaration left in the class is the old head with a semicolon; every other line of `scheduler.hpp` that is not blank is unchanged and in order, with nine marker comments and the one include added; and `reuse.hpp` holds nothing but its frame and the definitions. It finds 63 of 63 for each rule, and a changed body line, a changed line outside the moved ranges, a changed declaration and an added function are each found when planted.
- **Behaviour:** `cache-scenario`'s 501 server lines are identical before and after once the wall times in them are masked, and its 132 report lines are identical but for one counter, in the three runs of each build compared whole, on both models and both placements. The counter is `donors consumed` in the line of turn 6 (B), on the synthetic model on one CPU and over two: it reads 1 or 2 from run to run on the build before the move as on the one after (seen over 17 runs of each build at an earlier head of this branch, 2 in six of them before and in one after), so the scenario has one outcome that depends on the test's thread against the scheduler's, which is the test's to settle and not this change's. The count of checks in its last line also differs from run to run on either build, since the test polls while it waits.
- **Dead code:** the name check reads an out-of-class definition as it does the model's: a member declared in the class and defined in `reuse.hpp` that nothing names is found as `unused`, and one only a test names as `test-only`, both planted and both found.
- **Checked, Windows, MSVC, on the CPU:** a fresh build with the Vulkan backend, CTest 50 of 50, the suite's `docs`, `dead-code` and `server`. The tier's gates are run on the test machine at the head that lands.
- **Reviewed:** the design by the stand-in gating reviewer before it was built; its verdict on the code at the landing head is a condition of landing.

## The cache's moves said and counted in one place, and the plan's scenario (2026-10-13, branch step1/scenario, step 1 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** the cache and the context are planned as one thing (`docs/CACHE-PLAN.md`, approved on 2026-10-13, in this change). Its first step makes every move of a conversation's cache visible and gives the plan one scripted scenario every later step must keep green. No behaviour changes: lines printed and counters only.
- **One function:** `Scheduler::moved` says and counts each move by kind (`server::Move`, 27 kinds). The lines operators and tests already read keep their text and go through it; the moves that said nothing now have lines: a job starting, giving way (with what it held, the state it had kept and why no request took it over), being handed over, and the rows a job or a consumed donor alone held. The disk tier's outcomes are taken where its completions are, never on an I/O thread: a write counts once its file is published in the index, a read has one outcome, and a file leaving the index carries the tier's own reason (`DiskTier::Gone`).
- **Health:** `reuse.moves.since_start.<kind>` and `reread.since_start.rows_released`; `docs/SERVER.md`, The cache's moves, lists every kind with its line, and `docs/USAGE.md` the two fields.
- **The scenario, CTest `cache-scenario`:** a chat of 24 turns through the scheduler on the synthetic Q8_0 model and the hybrid one, each on one CPU and over two, a pool and context of 2048 tokens: turns below and past half the pool with another conversation's request arriving at the read-ahead job's pass, two edits, and two cuts by the product's own rule with turns after each. Every reply is its reply on a fresh model. Each turn's rows are classified against a ledger the test keeps itself, and rows a restore point should have held that no reported move explains fail it.
- **What it shows today, recorded as expectations with their witnesses (none fixed here):** past half the pool a turn's donor is consumed by its own job, and the job, giving way to another conversation's request, takes 896 rows with it that the next turn computes again, on every placement; a donor consumed by an edit's fork loses its rows past the fork, 384 computed again by the conversation's next turn; a job gives way to requests that would fit after a donor's eviction (3 of 4 jobs below half the pool on the synthetic model, 1 on the hybrid one); on the hybrid model an edit reuses 640 of 768 rows, the state at its message thinned out of host memory; and on the hybrid model over two CPUs a host tier of 1 GiB, taken in whole slabs a device, keeps no state at a message boundary, so edits and cuts reuse nothing, which the server now says where it was silent. Held: a cut falls at the same message turn after turn, and the turns after a cut reuse.
- **The failing commit:** the scenario with the counters present and zero fails at its first witness, "leg B's witness: 1 jobs gave way, 0 rows reused and 0 evicted, against 1, 0 and 896": the rows are computed again and nothing the server reports says why.
- **How a shortfall is explained:** by a loss the server reported of that prompt's own history, compared row for row, and of rows or a state inside the shortfall. The test takes each loss with its history through `Scheduler::on_move`, a hook on the one reporter, set before the run as `on_retire` is; no record of events is kept in the server. On made-up losses the classifier refuses another history's loss, a loss of other rows, and none.
- **Quiescence, what the test waits for:** before each step that is not meant to meet a job, it waits until every read-ahead job asked for so far has finished (`Stats::reprefills`). A job that gave way starts again whenever nothing waits, and whether it has is the scheduler thread against the test's; without the wait the next step met it or not from run to run. The product has no race there: both orders are valid, and the scenario pins one so its counts are the same on every run. Where the script wants a job alive, the arrival is submitted from the scheduler's thread as the job's pass retires.
- **Split in two, and why:** the legs that need a disk tier in this test are not in this change: a restart over kept files, two followers of one history on disk, a history the host tier cannot keep, and many users at the cap. They follow as a tests-only change, with the disk directory helper moved out of `server-resume` into the shared harness, before the plan's step 3 for many users at the cap, which holds the room count, and before step 6 for the rest. They were split off so the reporter and the scenario's first legs could be reviewed as soon as they showed what the plan had not expected.
- **Time:** 12 to 15 s for the four placements together on the Windows development machine and 18.5 to 19.1 s on the test machine over twenty runs in a row (about 2 s each for the synthetic model's two, the rest the hybrid model's). The hosted jobs give no time a test; by `server-resume`, which took 235 s on the test machine and 298 s on the hosted macOS runner, the slowest hosted job should take about 25 s. The limit is 120 s.
- **Checked, Windows, MSVC, on the CPU:** the build, CTest, the suite's `docs`, `dead-code` and `server`. The tier's gates are run on the test machine at the head that lands.
## The fit cases of the qwen35 module are a CTest of their own, their two groups side by side (2026-10-13, branch test/fit-cases, tests only, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** a placement that falls short of its whole request waits five quiet seconds for its device's memory to settle, and `arch-qwen35` runs those placements one after another, which is nearly all of its time; a branch that added more of them passed the test's 120-second limit on a hosted macOS run. Its review asked for the fit cases as a test of their own with their waits side by side, as a tests-only change.
- **What changed:** `llmx-arch-qwen35-test` takes `fit` or `models` and runs both without an argument. CTest `arch-qwen35` runs `models` with its limit at 60 seconds; the new `arch-qwen35-fit` runs `fit`, the checkpoint fit and the drafting fit on a thread each, with a limit of 240. No case is removed or changed, and nothing under `src/`.
- **Measured** (a Windows desktop, one run each): the fit cases 50.6 s (22 checks), the rest 0.3 s (792 checks), the whole binary without an argument 50.8 s. The test before the change was not timed on this base here; the hosted runs give its time on each runner.
- **Not done:** the fit has no seam to shorten its wait and none was added, since a seam only tests use is what the dead-code rule refuses; the checkpoint fit's own placements still wait in turn and could be overlapped the same way, a placement a thread.

## One count of what leaves memory with no file (2026-10-13, branch fix/lost-restore-points, lands by fast-forward)

- **The gap:** beside a disk tier, `reuse.disk.since_start.lost_before_written` counted a host copy dropped unwritten and a donor too large for the host tier, and nothing else. A boundary's state dropped unwritten, a donor refused host room because the copies there were in use, and a donor whose copy failed for want of host memory left no count, though each is something a later request could have forked and no file kept.
- **What it counts now, in one sentence:** restore points released while no file holds them, a complete history or a boundary's state that a later request could have forked.
- **Where:** `Scheduler::lost`, called at the release owner: `drop_host` (a copy neither superseded nor read through host memory, as before), `drop_bound` (a state with no file) and `write_back`'s three ways of keeping nothing (larger than the tier, refused the room of copies in use, the copy failing), each unless the donor's files are whole on disk. Beside a disk tier and while the server runs, as before.
- **Never counted:** a superseded copy or donor, a newer one of its conversation standing for it; a donor consumed by the request that forks its rows, which does not pass `write_back`; a boundary thinned on a server without a disk tier; anything released as the server stops.
- **One name:** `Stats::host_unwritten` is `Stats::lost_before_written`, the health field's name, which does not change. The line a donor larger than the tier prints stays.
- **Operators:** the figure can read higher than before on the same load, since it now includes boundaries and uncopied donors; `docs/USAGE.md` and `docs/OPERATING.md` say what it holds.
- **Test:** `server-resume`, the hybrid model on one CPU, a host tier of exactly one conversation's copy and a disk tier whose writes pause three seconds after a chunk, so no file is whole. A 700-token conversation with a boundary at 256, then another conversation's request: the copy takes the boundary's room, 1 lost. The first conversation's follow-up promotes its copy and reuses 640; the other's donor is refused that copy's room, 2 lost. On a host with no memory and no boundary, the donor's copy fails, 1 lost. That arm's host is short of memory from the server's start: set only before the other request, the seam raced an idle round that takes slabs the copy then finds idle, which failed the case on three hosted configurations. The failing commit, which holds the rename alone: "0 lost before the other conversation, 0 after it with 0 boundaries and 1 host copies held, 0 at the end, 640 tokens reused by the follow-up, 0 files on disk, against 1 lost with the boundary, then 2 with the donor refused room, and 640 reused".
- **Not covered by a case of its own:** the exclusions above. Their code is unchanged: a superseded donor returns from `write_back` before anything is counted and a consumed one is not passed to it; the counts the case holds are exact, so nothing else on its path adds one.
- **No assertion added to an existing case for the superseded exclusion:** the cases that drop a superseded donor or copy either run without a disk tier, where nothing is counted, or, as the superseded history on disk does, drop one whose files are whole on disk, which is not counted with the exclusion removed either, so an assertion there would hold nothing.
- **Checked, Windows, MSVC, on the CPU:** the build, CTest, the suite's `docs` and `dead-code`. The tier's gates are run on the test machine at the head that lands.

## A reply's own history is drafted ahead of a model drafter (2026-10-12, branch feat/lookup-first, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** the match profile of 2026-10-11 (Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M on the CPU, greedy, 30 prompts in six kinds, 10338 reply positions) found that where the last 8 tokens of a prompt and its reply so far occur earlier in them, the tokens that followed are wrong at the first 4 percent of the time, against 16 percent for a match of 3 and 45 for a match of 1, and that such a match covers 79 percent of the positions of code edits and under 3 percent of prose. The draft cost profile of 2026-10-12 put a draft row of the embedded drafter at 4 to 7 ms on Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0. A server had one drafter, so a reply that copies its prompt paid for a chain to draft what its own history holds.
- **The rule** (`spec::lookup_first`, [SPECULATIVE](SPECULATIVE.md), section 8): ahead of a proposer that runs a model, the embedded drafter or a draft model, a request whose history holds such a match drafts the tokens after its latest occurrence, up to the drafts it may take, and is left out of the proposer's batch that round; a match that reaches the history's end goes on into its own draft. `--drafter lookup` and `off` are unchanged, and nothing drafts where no drafter was asked for.
- **An acceptance a source** (`spec::Record`): a verify counts for the source that drafted it, so a resting drafter does not stop a history that convinces and lookup's misses never rest the drafter. The pass price charges a chain's steps only for the requests a chain drafts for, weighs each depth with the chain and without it, so a chain too dear for its own requests does not take a history's drafts with it, and cuts a history's draft to the one depth the pass takes.
- **Output:** the verify and `infer::accept` are untouched, so ids, draws, log-probabilities and ends are those of the run without drafts.
- **What a round pays to look, measured** (`spec` prints it): a walk of a history with no such match, 21 microseconds at 32768 tokens and 167 at 262144, and the scheduler's copy of the history 3 and 50, on a desktop CPU with tests running beside it; about half a percent of a 31 ms pass at 262144 tokens. No source position is kept between rounds for that.
- **Where it applies:** `spec::Embedded` and `spec::DraftModel` stand behind lookup only where made so, which `Drafts::attach` did for `generate`, `chat` and `serve` until feat/drafter-list made it follow the `--drafter` list (lookup first only); made without it, as the tests make the embedded drafter, each drafts alone as before.
- **Seen:** `generate --verbose` prints `own drafts kept:` under `drafts kept:` where the history gave any, and `/v1/health` gives `drafting.since_start.own_history`.
- **Measured** (Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 on one MI50 and on a tensor group of two, the match profile's 30 prompts in six kinds, 400 tokens a reply, greedy, `--draft-max 3`, through `generate`; main b783743a4 against this change at f44c02fdc built the same way from detached trees, default clocks; two rounds interleaved and a third of the prose kinds; the machine ran other work throughout, load above 8 at the start of most runs, so every figure is flagged and none was discarded). Generation tokens a second, the mean of a cell's runs:

  | placement | kind | main, off | main, lookup | main, embedded | this change, embedded | reference with its MTP |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | one MI50 | code edit | 22.5 | 55.2 | 54.8 | 64.3 | not run |
  | one MI50 | code question | 22.5 | 24.3 | 41.8 | 41.8 | not run |
  | one MI50 | document quote | 22.3 | 28.7 | 47.8 | 49.0 | not run |
  | one MI50 | free chat | 23.4 | 23.4 | 41.2 | 41.3 | not run |
  | one MI50 | structured | 22.5 | 35.2 | 51.2 | 51.4 | not run |
  | one MI50 | summary | 22.7 | 23.1 | 41.4 | 41.4 | not run |
  | group of two | code edit | 31.9 | 78.1 | 73.7 | 89.5 | 48.3 |
  | group of two | code question | 31.6 | 33.8 | 54.8 | 55.4 | 37.0 |
  | group of two | document quote | 31.4 | 40.4 | 64.0 | 66.4 | 44.7 |
  | group of two | free chat | 32.7 | 32.6 | 53.9 | 53.5 | 35.5 |
  | group of two | structured | 31.9 | 49.3 | 68.3 | 68.6 | 46.6 |
  | group of two | summary | 31.6 | 32.1 | 54.0 | 54.0 | 37.2 |

## The server-resume test is three CTests (2026-10-13, branch test/server-resume-split, tests only, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** `server-resume` took 297.6 and 306.4 seconds on the hosted macOS runner, and its limit was raised to 600 as a stopgap (the record below); the CPU half is nearly all of its time on a runner without a device, so splitting the CPU and device halves shortens nothing.
- **What changed:** `llmx-server-resume-test` takes `cpu-resume` or `cpu-cache` beside `cpu` and `device`, and runs everything without an argument. The CPU half is two groups: the cases up to the files-lost-between-two-servers pair (`server-resume`, `cpu-resume`) and those from the disk tier's cap case on (`server-resume-cache`, `cpu-cache`), each with a limit of 300 seconds. The device half is `server-resume-device` with 300, which reports a skip and passes where there is no device. The cut is at the point that balances the two groups, found by timing every call of a whole run; the only edit in `tests/server_resume.cpp` is in `main()`, where the hybrid model is now built before the first group so both groups see it, and no case is removed, changed or reordered.
- **Shared state:** none between cases: each builds its own scheduler, model and directory (`DiskRoot` makes a directory of its own name and a random number), and the one global is the check counter. The weights, tokenizer and hybrid model `main()` builds are read-only.
- **Measured** (a Windows desktop, CPU build, one run each, the machine busy with nothing else; an earlier pair of runs overlapped other work and is not used): the old test, `cpu`, 225 s; a first cut at the end of the hybrid cases gave 59 s and 230 s and was moved; the cut that landed gives `cpu-resume` 116 s and `cpu-cache` 92 s, `device` 0 s. The hosted runs give each test's time on each runner.
- **Checks:** the old binary ran 50 case lines of results and the two new groups together the same 50 (compared by label, one line mangled by the interleaving of stdout and stderr in both). The count of checks printed is not fixed: the old test printed 832520 to 973196 over its runs, since cases that wait poll with a check in the loop, and the groups printed 73793 and 941243 (and 89246 and 961727 at the first cut), so the sum of the new counts cannot equal the old to the unit and was not asserted.
- **Gates:** CTest, the suite's `docs` and `dead-code` components and the hosted run; the macOS job of that run shows the three times.

## The server-resume test's limit is 600 seconds (2026-10-13, branch ci/server-resume-limit, the build file only, lands by fast-forward)
